9.grammar: A past-tense verb of the basic Form I, third-person masculine singular ('he wrote/decreed'), shown by the bare -a ending. Beyond literal writing, it commonly means to prescribe or make something binding, as in a divine decree.
9.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; writing, decree, prescription

10.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
10.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

11.meaning: 'His self', 'his own being', 'himself' — the inner self, soul, or very person of a male individual. The word can denote the soul, the self, or a person's essential identity.

parts.en: genitive ending (because of the attached possessor)

11.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive 'his'. The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive (possessive) marking that appears when a noun is owned by a following pronoun; the -hi form of 'his' is used after an i-vowel.
11.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self, soul, breath of life

12.meaning: 'The mercy' — divine compassion, tenderness, and loving-kindness; the disposition to show pity and to do good to others. As a definite noun it points to mercy as a known, specific reality.
12.grammar: A definite noun ('the mercy'). The final -a is the accusative ending, which commonly marks a word as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or otherwise governed into this case. The 'l' of 'the' is pronounced as a doubled 'r' because r is a sun letter.
12.root: ر-ح-م (r-ḥ-m) — mercy, compassion, womb-like tenderness

13.meaning: He will most surely gather you (plural) together — an emphatic assurance that the addressees will certainly be assembled into one place. The doubled emphasis makes it a solemn certainty.
13.grammar: A present/future verb, 3rd-person masculine singular ('he will gather'). The prefixed la- ('surely') together with the heavy ending -nna form a double emphasis ('He shall most certainly …'), and the attached -kum is the object 'you all'.

14.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
14.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

15.meaning: 'Day' — a span of time. It denotes a day or a definite point/period of time; it links to a following word to specify which day (e.g., 'the day of …').
15.grammar: A masculine noun. Its final -i vowel is the genitive case: it typically appears after a preposition or when the word is linked to a following noun in an 'of …' relationship (as in 'the day OF …').

16.meaning: "the Resurrection" — the standing-up of all people from death to be judged; literally the act of rising or standing up.
16.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -i ending (on the feminine -t) is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ("the … OF this") or follows a preposition.

17.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
17.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

18.meaning: Doubt, suspicion, disquieting uncertainty — the kind of wavering that unsettles the heart, stronger than a passing question. It names the state of not being at rest about whether something is true.
18.grammar: A masculine singular noun shown with an -a ending and no tanwin. This is the accusative (mansub) noun governed by the negating particle la — its ism — taking a bare form to express absolute negation, conveying that the whole category is ruled out ('there is no doubt whatsoever').

19.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
19.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

20.meaning: Those who / the ones who — a plural relative pronoun (masculine) introducing a description: 'those (people) who …'.
20.grammar: A relative pronoun, masculine plural, meaning 'those who / the ones who'. It refers back to a group already in view and introduces a clause describing them. Its form is fixed and does not change for case.
20.root: — (relative pronoun; no triliteral root)

21.meaning: 'They lost', 'they have suffered loss', 'they ruined themselves' — said of a group of males who have come out as losers, forfeiting or wasting something of value, especially their own selves.
21.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -ū ending means the subject is 'they' (more than one male) and the action is presented as completed: 'they lost'.
21.root: خ-س-ر (kh-s-r) — loss, to lose, to suffer ruin

22.meaning: A noun meaning 'their own selves' or 'themselves' — the plural of 'nafs' (self, soul, person, inner self), joined to the pronoun 'their.' It commonly conveys the reflexive idea of acting upon one's own self.
22.grammar: A noun (a broken/irregular plural of 'nafs') with the attached possessive pronoun '-hum' ('their/them,' masculine plural). The -a case ending before the pronoun is accusative, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb — i.e. the self upon which the action falls.

23.meaning: Means 'so they / then they' — the connector 'so/then' joined to the standalone pronoun 'they' (for a group of males or a mixed group). It draws a consequence and then names the subject.
23.grammar: The connecting particle fa- ('so/then', drawing a result or sequence from what precedes) attached to the detached subject pronoun hum ('they', masculine or mixed plural). As a standalone pronoun it has no case ending and serves as the subject of what follows.

24.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
24.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

25.meaning: 'They believe / they have faith' — to affirm something as true with trusting inner conviction and to feel secure in it. The verb carries both believing and being at peace through that belief; in religious use it is to commit oneself in faith.
25.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb, masculine plural. The yu-…-una frame means 'they (men, or a mixed group) do' the action now or habitually. The retained final -na marks the indicative (a plain, unqualified statement) — 'they believe' — as opposed to forms where that -na drops. The verb is Form IV (amana), used intransitively here meaning simply 'to believe / to have faith'.
25.root: ا-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, trust, faith

1.meaning: And for him / and he has — the connector 'and', the preposition 'for/to', and the pronoun 'him'. Together it expresses possession or belonging ('and to him belongs …', 'and he has …').
1.grammar: A small phrase, not a verb: the connector wa- ('and') + the preposition la- ('for/to') + the pronoun -hu ('him'). The preposition with a pronoun commonly conveys having or belonging ('he has', 'belonging to him').

2.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

3.meaning: 'It dwelt', 'it became still', 'it rested / settled'. The verb covers both inhabiting a place (to dwell, reside) and growing calm and motionless (to be at rest, to settle down).
3.grammar: Past-tense verb. The final -a marks a single masculine subject ('he' or 'it') with the action presented as completed: 'he/it dwelt'.
3.root: س-ك-ن (s-k-n) — to dwell, to be still, to rest

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
4.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

5.meaning: The night — the period of darkness from sunset to dawn.
5.grammar: Prefix 'al-' = 'the' (its 'l' merges with the word's initial 'l', said al-layl). A noun for night-time. The final -i is the genitive case ending, typically used after a preposition or to link to a preceding noun ('… OF the night').

6.meaning: And the day / daytime — the period of light from dawn to sunset.
6.grammar: Prefix 'wa' = 'and'; 'al-' = 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'n', said an-nahār). A noun for the daylight hours. The final -i is the genitive case ending, typically used after a preposition or to link to a preceding noun ('… OF the day').

7.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
7.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

8.meaning: "the All-Hearing" — one who hears, perceiving all sounds completely and constantly; used as a divine name it denotes the One whose hearing is perfect and all-encompassing.
8.grammar: A definite intensive adjective/noun on the faʿīl pattern, which conveys a deep, enduring quality ('ever-hearing,' not merely 'hearing once'). The 'al-' prefix makes it definite ('the'). The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, the form a word takes when it is the subject of a sentence or a predicate/description following it.

9.meaning: The All-Knowing — one whose knowledge is complete, perfect, and all-encompassing; an intensive form stressing that knowing is an essential, constant attribute.
9.grammar: A definite noun/adjective in an intensive pattern (faʿīl) that stresses depth and permanence of the quality. The prefix 'al-' means 'the'; the final -u (ḍamma) marks the nominative case, which typically signals the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it.

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: 'Is it other than…?', 'shall (it be) other than…?' — a questioning expression built from the question particle 'is/shall?' and the word for 'other than / besides'. It challenges whether anything besides the named thing could be intended.
2.grammar: A yes/no question particle attached to the noun 'other than'. The -a ending is accusative, the case that often marks a word as a direct object or otherwise governed into this case (here the questioned object). The opening 'a-' turns the phrase into a question.
2.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — otherness, difference, being other than

3.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
3.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

4.meaning: 'Shall I take (for myself)?', 'should I adopt / take as my own?'. This verb form carries the reflexive sense of taking something to oneself — adopting, acquiring, or choosing it for oneself.
4.grammar: A present-tense verb 'I take', here opened by the question particle 'a-' ('shall I…?'). The form is the self-benefiting (reflexive) pattern, so it means taking something for oneself. The verb's bare present form (ending in -u) signals an ongoing or yet-to-happen action.

5.meaning: A guardian, protector, ally, or close supporter — one who is near and takes charge of another's affairs. Waliyy carries the sense of nearness combined with care, authority, and friendship.
5.grammar: An indefinite noun ('a protector'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the accusative case: it commonly marks the word as a direct object of a verb, or as a predicate/complement after certain verbs of 'making' or 'becoming'.

6.meaning: 'Originator', 'Bringer-into-being', 'Maker who splits forth creation from nothing'. The word names the one who first brings things into existence, cleaving them into being where there was none.

parts.en: originator / one who brings into being

6.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' noun: 'the one who originates'). The -i ending is genitive, the case that typically links the word to a following noun ('… OF …') or follows a preposition. As a doer-noun it can also take an object after it.
6.root: ف-ط-ر (f-ṭ-r) — to split, cleave, bring forth, originate

7.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
7.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

8.meaning: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
8.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.

9.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
9.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

10.meaning: 'He feeds', 'he gives food (to others)'. This verb form means to provide nourishment to someone — to cause another to eat. It describes the act of supplying food and sustenance.
10.grammar: Present-tense verb in the causative pattern ('to make eat' = to feed). The yu- prefix marks a single masculine subject ('he/it') and the bare present form signals an ongoing or habitual action: 'he feeds'.
10.root: ط-ع-م (ṭ-ʿ-m) — food, to eat, to taste

11.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
11.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

12.meaning: 'He is fed', 'food is given to him' — the passive counterpart of feeding: to be on the receiving end of being given food, to be nourished by another.
12.grammar: Present-tense passive verb. The yu- prefix marks a single masculine subject, and the internal a-vowel pattern (ṭ'ʿam rather than ṭ'ʿim) makes it passive: the subject does not feed but 'is fed'.
12.root: ط-ع-م (ṭ-ʿ-m) — food, to eat, to taste

13.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
13.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

14.meaning: 'Truly I' or 'indeed I' — the emphatic affirming particle inna ('truly, indeed, certainly'), which strengthens and confirms a statement, joined to the pronoun 'I'.
14.grammar: An emphasizing particle with an attached pronoun. 'Inna' is a particle of emphasis and affirmation that introduces a statement and lends it certainty ('it is certainly the case that…'). The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I / me') in the object form this particle requires. Together: 'Indeed I…'.

15.meaning: 'I was commanded', 'I have been ordered / instructed'. It expresses that the speaker is the recipient of a command — someone else has issued an order and the speaker is bound by it.

parts.en: passive vowel: the action was done to the subject

15.grammar: Past-tense passive verb. The -tu ending means the subject is 'I', and the opening u-vowel makes it passive ('I was commanded' rather than 'I commanded'). The action is presented as completed.

16.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
16.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

17.meaning: '(that) I be / I should be' — the verb 'to be/become' in the first person, used in a dependent sense ('that I be…', 'lest I be…'). It expresses entering into or belonging to a described state.

parts.en: be / become (stem, ending in the subjunctive vowel -a)

17.grammar: A present-tense verb 'to be/become' with the 'I' prefix (a-). The stem ends in the third root letter ن, which carries the final short vowel -a; this -a is the subjunctive ending, the form used after particles such as 'that', 'so that', or 'lest' — so it reads 'that I be / I should be' rather than the plain statement 'I am' (which would end in -u).
17.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to become, to come into existence

18.meaning: First, foremost — the one that comes before all others in time, order, or rank.
18.grammar: A noun/adjective meaning 'first', here in a form that does not take normal indefinite case-tanwīn (a 'diptote'). The -a ending is accusative, marking it as an object or, very often, as the leading term of a possessive phrase ('the first of …').
18.root: أ-و-ل (ʾ-w-l) — to be first, to return to a beginning

19.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
19.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.
19.root: — (pronoun)

20.meaning: He submitted / surrendered (himself); he gave himself over wholly, devoting and resigning himself to Allah. The verb carries the sense of entering into peace and security by total surrender — the very root of the word 'Islam.'
20.grammar: A past-tense verb, 'he submitted,' describing a completed act by a single male (or 'one who'). The final -a is the standard ending of this third-person masculine singular past form. The four-letter (causative) pattern adds the sense of actively giving oneself up to something.
20.root: س-ل-م (s-l-m) — soundness, peace, safety; to submit/surrender

21.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
21.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

22.meaning: You must certainly be / never be — an emphatic form of the verb 'to be', stressing that one truly will (or, with a negative, truly must not) be in a certain state.
22.grammar: A present-tense form of the verb 'to be', addressed to 'you' (the prefix ta-). The heavy ending -anna (nūn of emphasis) gives a strong, insistent force — 'you most certainly are/must be' — and is the standard way Arabic stresses a command or warning attached to a verb.
22.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into being

23.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
23.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

24.meaning: Those who associate partners with Allah — idolaters / polytheists who set up others alongside the one God in worship or devotion.
24.grammar: An active participle used as a noun, with 'the', in the masculine sound plural. The -īna ending marks the plural in the genitive/accusative case — the form used after a preposition or as the object of a verb.
24.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, associate, partner

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: 'Truly I' or 'indeed I' — the emphatic affirming particle inna ('truly, indeed, certainly'), which strengthens and confirms a statement, joined to the pronoun 'I'.
2.grammar: An emphasizing particle with an attached pronoun. 'Inna' is a particle of emphasis and affirmation that introduces a statement and lends it certainty ('it is certainly the case that…'). The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I / me') in the object form this particle requires. Together: 'Indeed I…'.

3.meaning: I fear, I am afraid of, I stand in awe/dread — expressing the speaker's own fear, whether dread of harm or reverent awe.
3.grammar: A present-tense verb. The a- prefix marks the doer as 'I'. The final -u ending marks the ordinary (indicative) mood, used for a plain statement of an ongoing or habitual state ('I fear / I am fearing').

4.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
4.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

5.meaning: 'I disobeyed', 'I rebelled against', 'I defied (an order)'. The verb means to go against a command and refuse obedience.
5.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -tu ending marks the subject as 'I' with the action completed: 'I disobeyed'. The stem comes from a root whose final letter is a weak letter, which surfaces here as 'ay' before the ending.

6.meaning: 'My Lord' — the Master, Sustainer and Nurturer, claimed in close personal relation by the speaker.
6.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord') with the attached pronoun -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' ending merges with the case-vowel of the noun, so a single long -ī is heard. The sense is 'the Lord who is mine'.
6.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord/master, to nurture and sustain

7.meaning: Torment, punishment, or chastisement — severe, painful suffering imposed as a penalty.
7.grammar: A singular noun. The final -a (fatḥa) marks the accusative case, the form used for a direct object of a verb, or for the first noun of a possessive pair ('the punishment of …') when that whole phrase is itself an object.

8.meaning: a day — a day, the basic unit of daytime or a twenty-four-hour span; figuratively a time or occasion.
8.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The final -in ending marks the genitive case together with the indefinite 'a/an'. The genitive is the case used after prepositions or to link this noun to a preceding word ('… of a day').
8.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — a day, a span of time

9.meaning: An adjective meaning 'great', 'immense', 'mighty', or 'tremendous' — vast in size, importance, or gravity; used of things weighty and momentous.
9.grammar: An adjective on the intensive 'faʿīl' pattern (conveying a strong, established quality), carrying the genitive indefinite '-in' (tanwīn) ending. The genitive case typically appears after a preposition or when describing/qualifying a preceding genitive noun.
9.root: ع-ظ-م (ʿ-ẓ-m) — to be great, mighty, immense; (literally) bone, hence weightiness

1.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
1.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

2.meaning: 'It is turned away', 'it is diverted / averted'. The passive verb describes something being deflected or kept away from a target — turned aside so that it does not reach.

parts.en: he / it — present/ongoing action; the doubled y reflects assimilation of a preceding particle's final letter into this prefix

2.grammar: Present-tense passive verb in a jussive (clipped) form. The prefix is the masculine 'he/it' marker, written with a doubling (shadda) because the final consonant of an immediately preceding particle has assimilated into it. The internal a-vowel makes it passive ('is averted'), and the bare consonant ending (no final vowel) is the shortened form that typically follows conditional or negating particles.
2.root: ص-ر-ف (ṣ-r-f) — to turn away, divert, dispose

3.meaning: A combination meaning 'from him / from it / about him.' The preposition denotes moving away from, departing from, or concerning a thing, and the pronoun refers to a single masculine entity.
3.grammar: A preposition with a fused object pronoun. ʿan governs the genitive and conveys separation or 'concerning.' The attached -hu marks a third-person masculine singular object ('him/it').

4.meaning: On that day / that day — pointing back to a particular past day already in view; 'a day, at that time.'
4.grammar: A time-word ('day') joined to 'idhin' ('at that time'), together meaning 'on that day.' The '-in' ('tanwīn') compensates for an understood clause ('the day when…'). The form functions adverbially, locating an event at a specific past moment.

5.meaning: A two-part connector: fa- means 'so', 'then', or 'and so', linking what follows as a result or consequence; qad before a past-tense verb intensifies it, conveying 'certainly', 'indeed', or 'already' — stressing that the action has truly and definitely occurred.
5.grammar: fa- is a connecting particle meaning 'so' or 'then', often marking a result. qad is a particle of emphasis; placed before a completed (past-tense) verb it affirms that the action has definitely or already happened. Neither part takes a case ending.

6.meaning: 'He had mercy on him', 'He showed compassion / pity toward him'. The verb is the act of mercy directed at a particular object — to treat someone with tenderness and forgiveness.
6.grammar: Past-tense verb with an attached object 'him'. The -a between stem and pronoun marks a single masculine subject ('he') with completed action; the -hu is the object pronoun 'him/it', used in this form after an a-vowel.

7.meaning: 'And that' — a connective 'and' plus the demonstrative 'that', pointing to something distant or already mentioned (masculine).
7.grammar: Connective 'and' + a masculine singular demonstrative pronoun, 'that (one)'. Demonstratives in Arabic do not change for grammatical case; the -ka element is a particle directing attention to a distant referent.

8.meaning: 'The success' / 'the triumph' — attainment of what is sought and safety from what is feared; winning, salvation, the great achievement. With the article it is 'the (true) success'.
8.grammar: A definite masculine noun. The -u ending is the nominative case, marking it as a subject or as the thing identified (e.g. 'that IS the success').
8.root: ف-و-ز (f-w-z) — to win, triumph, attain salvation

9.meaning: Clear, plain, manifest; that which makes things evident — both 'clearly apparent in itself' and 'making the truth clear to others'.
9.grammar: An active participle, 'the one that makes clear / the manifest', from a causative (form-IV) pattern, carried by the definite article al- ('the'). The final -u ending is the nominative case, the form used when the word serves as a subject or as a descriptor of such a word.

1.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
1.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

2.meaning: 'He/it touches you', 'it afflicts / befalls you'. The verb means to make contact with, and by extension for something (often harm) to reach or strike a person. The 'you' here is a single male.

parts.en: he / it — present/ongoing action; the doubled y reflects assimilation of a preceding particle's final letter into this prefix

2.grammar: Present-tense verb in a jussive (clipped) form with attached object 'you'. The prefix is the masculine 'he/it' marker, written with a doubling (shadda) because the final consonant of an immediately preceding particle has assimilated into it. The bare consonant ending of the stem (with the doubled root letter spelled out as msas) is the shortened form used after conditional particles. The -ka means 'you', addressed to one male.
2.root: م-س-س (m-s-s) — to touch, make contact, befall

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
3.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

4.meaning: 'With harm', 'with affliction / hurt'. The phrase joins the preposition 'with / by means of' to a word for harm, injury, or distress. The word is in its indefinite form: 'some harm', 'any affliction'.
4.grammar: A preposition 'with' attached to the noun 'harm'. The -in ending is the indefinite genitive: the genitive case (required after a preposition) combined with the 'an/some' nunation that marks the noun as unspecified — 'with some harm'.

5.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
5.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

6.meaning: 'Remover', 'one who uncovers / lifts away / dispels'. The word names the agent who unveils or takes away something — for instance lifting away harm or revealing what was hidden.
6.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' noun: 'one who removes/uncovers'). The -a ending is accusative, the case that commonly marks a word as a direct object or otherwise governs it into this case. As a doer-noun it can take an object after it.
6.root: ك-ش-ف (k-sh-f) — to uncover, unveil, remove, lay bare

7.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
7.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

8.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
8.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

9.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
9.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

10.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
10.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

11.meaning: 'He/it touches you', 'it afflicts / befalls you'. The verb means to make contact with, and by extension for something (often harm) to reach or strike a person. The 'you' here is a single male.

parts.en: he / it — present/ongoing action; the doubled y reflects assimilation of a preceding particle's final letter into this prefix

11.grammar: Present-tense verb in a jussive (clipped) form with attached object 'you'. The prefix is the masculine 'he/it' marker, written with a doubling (shadda) because the final consonant of an immediately preceding particle has assimilated into it. The bare consonant ending of the stem (with the doubled root letter spelled out as msas) is the shortened form used after conditional particles. The -ka means 'you', addressed to one male.
11.root: م-س-س (m-s-s) — to touch, make contact, befall

12.meaning: Good, better, that which is beneficial — goodness itself, and by comparison 'more good / better'; also wealth or any benefit regarded as good.
12.grammar: A noun/comparative ('good' or 'better') carrying a prefixed preposition. The prefix bi- means 'with'; the final -in is the indefinite genitive (nunation), showing no 'the' and the genitive case taken after a preposition.
12.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — goodness, that which is good or preferable

13.meaning: A two-part phrase: the connector 'then / so' plus the standalone pronoun 'he / it,' used to point back and resume with 'then he…' or 'so it…'
13.grammar: The connector 'fa' ('then/so') plus the detached subject pronoun 'huwa' ('he/it'), 3rd-person masculine singular. Both are indeclinable, with no case ending; the pronoun typically begins or emphasizes a statement about 'he/it.'

14.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
14.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

15.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
15.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

16.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
16.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
16.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

17.meaning: All-powerful, fully able, ever-capable — possessing complete and effective power to do whatever is willed; one whose ability never falls short.
17.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, which stresses a deep, abiding quality ('thoroughly able'). The final -un is the indefinite nominative (nunation) — the doubled-n shows no 'the', and the -u base vowel marks the nominative case, used when the word is a subject or a predicate ('… is all-powerful').

1.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
1.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

2.meaning: 'The Subduer', 'the Overpowering / Dominant One' — the one who has total mastery and irresistible power over all, holding everything beneath His control.
2.grammar: A definite active participle (a 'doer' noun: 'the one who overpowers'). The -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject of a sentence or a word standing as the main topic/predicate.

3.meaning: 'Above / over / on top of.' An adverb of place meaning the higher position relative to something else; it can also mean 'superior to' or 'beyond.'
3.grammar: An adverb of place that is normally attached to a following noun ('above …'). Its fixed -a ending is the form such place-words take when they govern the noun that follows them.
3.root: ف-و-ق (f-w-q) — to be above, surpass, exceed

4.meaning: 'His servants / His slaves / His worshippers' — ʿibād are those who serve and worship; with the attached pronoun it denotes the servants belonging to Him (Allah), i.e., humankind or His devotees.
4.grammar: A plural noun with an attached possessive pronoun '-hi' ('his/His'). The -i vowel is the genitive case, typically appearing after a preposition or in a possessive ('of') link; the pronoun names the one to whom the servants belong.

5.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
5.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

6.meaning: The All-Wise — one possessing perfect wisdom, who puts everything in its right place and acts with flawless judgment; can also carry the sense of one who decrees and decides soundly.
6.grammar: A definite noun/adjective in an intensive pattern (faʿīl) stressing the depth and constancy of the quality. The prefix 'al-' means 'the'; the final -u (ḍamma) marks the nominative case, which typically signals the subject of a sentence or a describing predicate.
6.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge wisely, to be wise

7.meaning: 'The All-Aware', 'the Well-Acquainted' — the one possessing thorough, intimate knowledge of the inner reality of things, fully informed of what is hidden as well as what is open.
7.grammar: A definite intensive adjective (a 'one who is deeply X' pattern: thoroughly aware). The -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject of a sentence or a word standing as the main topic/predicate.
7.root: خ-ب-ر (kh-b-r) — knowledge, inner acquaintance, being informed

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: 'Which?', 'what?', 'which one (of several)?'. A question word used to ask which member of a class or group is meant. It can also serve as 'whatever / whichever'.
2.grammar: An interrogative noun ('which?'). The -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks a word as the subject or the main topic of its clause. It normally connects to a following noun naming the group being asked about.

3.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
3.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
3.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

4.meaning: Greater, bigger, more grave — the comparative/superlative 'more great' or 'greatest'.
4.grammar: An elative on the afʿal pattern, expressing 'more/most great'. Such forms are diptotes, so they take -u (without nunation) in the nominative; the -u marks it as a subject or predicate ('is greater').

5.meaning: 'A testimony / witnessing / attestation' — the act or content of bearing witness: giving evidence about something one knows to be true, or formal certification of a fact.
5.grammar: A feminine singular noun, indefinite. The -an ending (written on the tied tā’, hence -tan) is the accusative with 'tanwīn': it marks the word as 'a testimony' (no 'the') and signals that the noun typically functions as the direct object of a verb or otherwise stands in the accusative.

6.meaning: 'Say!' — a command to utter or declare something aloud, addressed to a single male.
6.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to one male: 'say!'. Its natural form ends in a silent consonant (qul), but here a short -i vowel is added simply to smooth pronunciation before a following word that begins with a connecting sound; it carries no case meaning of its own.

7.meaning: 'Allah' — the proper name of the One God, the unique Divine Being worshipped as Creator and Lord. It is a name without plural or gender, referring to Allah alone.
7.grammar: The proper divine name. The final '-u' is the nominative ending, which typically marks the word as the subject of a verb or the thing being described/identified. As a unique name it takes no indefinite nunation.

8.meaning: A witness — one who sees and observes directly and can testify to what is true; also carries the sense of an ever-watchful observer.
8.grammar: An intensive descriptive noun (pattern 'faʿīl') meaning one who witnesses fully and constantly. The '-un' ending is nominative and indefinite: the nominative typically marks the subject or predicate ('is a witness'), and the final 'n' sound marks it indefinite.

9.meaning: 'Between me' — the spatial or relational word 'between' joined to 'me'. It marks the point or interval that lies on the speaker's side of a relationship between two parties.
9.grammar: The adverb/noun 'between' with the attached pronoun 'me'. 'Between' takes a following word in the genitive (linked-to) relation, and the -ī ending is the attached pronoun meaning 'me/my'.
9.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

10.meaning: 'And between you' — the connector 'and' joined to 'between', joined to 'you' (a group). It marks the point or interval lying on the side of the addressed party.
10.grammar: 'And' + 'between' + the attached pronoun 'you (plural)'. The -kum ending is the attached pronoun for a group being addressed ('you all'). The -a vowel before it is the fixed form 'bayna' takes when carrying a pronoun.
10.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

11.meaning: A verb meaning 'and it has been revealed / and it was inspired' — passive, expressing that a divine communication has been sent down or conveyed into someone from Allah, without naming the giver. The wa- is a connector ('and'). The content of inspiration is received, not initiated by the one it reaches.
11.grammar: Past-tense passive verb, third-person masculine singular ('it was revealed'). The initial vowelled hamzah plus the internal vowelling (ū…i) marks the passive voice — the grammatical subject is the thing revealed, while the revealer is left unstated. The final -a is the standard past-tense ending. The prefixed wa- means 'and'.
11.root: و-ح-ي (w-ḥ-y) — to reveal, inspire, convey by inspiration

12.meaning: 'To me / toward me.' It joins the preposition ilā, meaning 'to / toward,' with an attached first-person 'me,' expressing motion or direction toward the speaker.
12.grammar: A preposition meaning 'to / toward' with the attached pronoun 'me.' The base preposition is ilā, ending in a long vowel (written with alif maqsūra, ى). When the 'me' pronoun attaches, that final long vowel turns into yāʾ and merges with the pronoun's yāʾ, giving a doubled, stressed -ayya — the whole word reading ilayya, 'to me.'
12.root: — (preposition)

13.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
13.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

14.meaning: The Qur'ān — literally 'the Recitation' or 'that which is read aloud'; the name of the revealed Scripture, understood as something recited.
14.grammar: A definite verbal noun ('the recitation') used as a proper name. The final -u is the nominative case, the ending that typically marks the subject or the thing being identified.
14.root: ق-ر-ا (q-r-ʾ) — to read, recite, gather together

15.meaning: A purpose-phrase meaning 'so that I may warn you (plural)' — combining a 'so that / in order to' particle with a verb of warning addressed to a group. To warn here is to alert people to a coming danger or accountability so they may take heed.
15.grammar: A 'so that' particle (li-) attached to a present-tense Form IV verb in the first-person singular ('I warn'). The first-person marker is a hamzah carrying a damma (ʾu-), which distinguishes it from the interrogative a- and from the Form I first-person prefix. Because of the purpose particle, the verb takes a subjunctive -a ending (the mood of intention/result: 'in order that I warn'). The attached -kum is the object 'you', addressing more than one person.
15.root: ن-ذ-ر (n-dh-r) — to warn, caution, give notice of danger

16.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
16.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

17.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
17.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

18.meaning: A verb meaning 'it reached / attained / arrived at' — to extend to and make contact with a point, person, or limit, whether a message reaching hearers or a thing arriving at its end. It conveys completion of arrival.
18.grammar: Past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it reached'). The plain stem with the final -a marks completed past action and a masculine singular doer.
18.root: ب-ل-غ (b-l-gh) — to reach, attain, convey to its destination

19.meaning: A charged question-opener meaning roughly 'Is it really the case that you (plural)…?' — a questioning particle fused with an emphasis particle (inna, 'indeed/truly') and 'you'. It poses a question while underscoring the claim being questioned, often with a tone of astonishment or challenge.
19.grammar: An interrogative prefix a- ('do/is it that…?') joined to the emphasizing particle inna ('indeed'). Inna places the noun or pronoun following it (its ism) in the accusative; here that is the attached -kum ('you', plural), which functions logically like the subject of the statement but stands formally in the accusative. The combination both asks and stresses, and the -kum addresses a group.
19.root: — (particles; no root)

20.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (plural) bear witness / testify' — to affirm and attest to something as true, often solemnly, on the basis of knowledge or conviction. It carries the weight of standing as a witness.
20.grammar: An emphatic prefix la- ('surely') on a present-tense verb, second-person masculine plural. The ta- prefix marks 'you', and the -ūna ending marks masculine plural in the indicative ('you all do testify'). The la- adds insistence: 'you surely do testify'.
20.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — to witness, attest, be present as witness

21.meaning: An emphatic particle meaning 'that' (as in 'I know that...') or 'indeed/surely.' It introduces a statement and gives it certainty and emphasis, presenting what follows as an established fact.
21.grammar: An emphatic particle that introduces a noun-clause ('that...'). It puts the following noun into the accusative case and lends the whole statement a sense of certainty and assertion. It typically comes after verbs of knowing, saying, or informing.

22.meaning: With, together with, alongside — indicating company, accompaniment, or being in the same place or time as another.
22.grammar: A preposition of accompaniment ('with, alongside'); grammatically it is an adverbial of place/time (ẓarf) that governs the genitive. It is placed before a following noun to put one thing in the company of another, and that following noun stands in the genitive. The -a is its fixed ending.

23.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
23.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

24.meaning: A noun meaning 'gods / deities' — the plural of ilāh, objects taken as worthy of worship besides Allah. It denotes claimed divine beings in general.
24.grammar: A plural noun, indefinite ('gods'), in the accusative case marked by tanwīn. The word ends in a tā' marbūṭah, which is normally silent in pause but is pronounced as -t- when a case-vowel and tanwīn follow it; combined with the accusative tanwīn this is sounded as -tan, so the full ending is ālihatan (not a bare -an). The accusative typically marks a noun as the object of a verb or the focus of certain particles.
24.root: ا-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, that which is worshipped

25.meaning: 'Another / other' — a feminine word for one that is different from, or additional to, one already mentioned; a second or further (feminine) one.
25.grammar: A feminine singular adjective/noun meaning 'other, another', the feminine counterpart of ākhar. It ends in a fixed long -ā (alif maqṣūra) and does not change its ending for case; it commonly describes or stands for a feminine noun such as 'a group/party'.
25.root: أ-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be later/other; that which comes after or differs

26.meaning: An imperative command meaning 'Say!' or 'Speak!' — a direct order to one person to utter or declare something.
26.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a single male. The bare, vowelless ending (the silent stop on the final 'l') marks it as a direct order: 'you, say!' It is built from the verb 'to say' with the weak middle letter dropped, leaving the short, clipped command form.
26.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, to speak, to utter

27.meaning: 'Not' — a particle of negation. Depending on context it denies a present fact, forbids an action, or rules something out ('do not / there is no').
27.grammar: A negating particle, 'not / no'. It is used to deny or prohibit — negating present-tense statements, expressing 'there is no...', or, with a command form, forbidding an action ('do not...').

28.meaning: A verb meaning 'I bear witness / I testify' — a first-person affirmation attesting to the truth of something from one's own knowledge or conviction, carrying solemn personal commitment.
28.grammar: Present-tense verb, first-person singular ('I testify'). The initial vowelled hamzah marks the speaker 'I', and the final -u is the indicative ending used for a plain present-tense statement.
28.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — to witness, attest, be present as witness

29.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
29.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

30.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
30.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

31.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
31.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

32.meaning: A god / an object of worship — a being taken as a deity and worshipped. As an indefinite noun it means 'a god' in the general sense.
32.grammar: A singular noun. The -un ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a god') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate.
32.root: أ-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, worship, being a deity

33.meaning: One / single and unique — denoting oneness: a single individual, undivided and without partner or plurality.
33.grammar: An adjective/numeral meaning 'one.' The -un ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite and in the nominative case, the case typically used for a subject, predicate, or a descriptor agreeing with such a noun.

34.meaning: An emphatic self-declaration meaning 'and indeed I (am)…' — the connector 'and' joined to inna ('truly/indeed') bearing the first-person 'I'. It introduces a statement about oneself with strong assertion.
34.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') plus the emphasis particle inna ('indeed'), to which the first-person pronoun is attached. An -n- buffer (nūn al-wiqāya) is inserted before the pronoun, giving -nī ('I/me'); this serves as the ism of inna, accusative in case though functioning logically as the subject. Inna lends strong assertion to the statement made about the speaker.

35.meaning: An adjective/noun meaning 'free of / quit of / disassociated from' — innocent of and having nothing to do with something, washing one's hands of it. It describes a person clear and detached from a thing, especially a wrong.
35.grammar: A descriptive noun, indefinite, with the nominative -un ending (tanwīn). The nominative typically marks the subject of a sentence or a predicate ('[someone] is free/quit'); the -un tanwīn shows it is indefinite. It is usually completed by 'of/from' something.
35.root: ب-ر-ء (b-r-ʾ) — to be free, clear, quit of; innocence, disassociation

36.meaning: A fused word combining the preposition 'min' ('from', 'of', 'about') with the relative/indefinite 'mā' ('what', 'that which'). Together: 'from what', 'about that which', 'of what'.
36.grammar: The preposition 'min' and the word 'mā' merge in pronunciation (the 'n' assimilating into the 'm'). 'min' governs a genitive, and 'mā' here functions as a relative pronoun introducing a clause ('that which …'). These are indeclinable particles without case endings.

37.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (plural) associate as partners' — to set up others alongside Allah in worship or divinity, i.e. to commit shirk by ascribing partners to Him. It denotes the act of treating something as Allah's equal or associate.
37.grammar: Present-tense verb (form IV), second-person masculine plural. The tu- prefix (with the form-IV pattern 'to make a partner') marks 'you', and the -ūna ending marks masculine plural indicative ('you all associate'). It implies an object: associating others with Allah.
37.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, partner; to ascribe partners (to Allah)

1.meaning: Those who / the ones who — a plural relative pronoun (masculine) introducing a description: 'those (people) who …'.
1.grammar: A relative pronoun, masculine plural, meaning 'those who / the ones who'. It refers back to a group already in view and introduces a clause describing them. Its form is fixed and does not change for case.

2.meaning: We gave them / We granted them — a completed act of bestowing or conferring something upon a group, done by 'We'.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb of Form IV ('to give, bestow, grant'). The suffix -nā marks the doer as 'we'. The attached pronoun -hum(u) is the object, 'them' (a group); its vowel is lengthened to -humu to ease pronunciation before the next word. Altogether: 'We gave them'.
2.root: ء-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (Form IV) to give, bring, bestow

3.meaning: The Book, the Scripture — a written revelation; the term for a divinely revealed text.
3.grammar: A definite noun ('the Book') with attached 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb.
3.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; a writing, book

4.meaning: They recognize him/it — to know something by its marks, to identify or acknowledge a thing already familiar, said of a group toward a single object.
4.grammar: A present-tense verb 'to recognize/know', with subject and object built in: the prefix ya- with suffix -ūna gives a masculine-plural 'they', and the attached -hu is the object 'him/it'. The -ūna ending marks the ongoing/indicative form; it is the lengthened -hū because a vowel precedes.
4.root: ع-ر-ف (ʿ-r-f) — to know, recognize, be acquainted

5.meaning: 'Just as / in the same way that' — a phrase of comparison joining 'like / as' to 'what', meaning 'like that which...' or 'in the manner that...'.
5.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like / as') joined to mā ('what / that which'). Together they introduce a likeness or manner — 'just as...', 'in the same way that...' — comparing one thing or action to another.

6.meaning: They recognize / know — to identify something by its signs, to acknowledge what is already familiar, said of a group.
6.grammar: A present-tense verb 'to recognize'. The prefix ya- together with the suffix -ūna marks a masculine-plural subject ('they') in the ongoing/indicative form.
6.root: ع-ر-ف (ʿ-r-f) — to know, recognize, be acquainted

7.meaning: A noun meaning 'their sons / their children' — male offspring (the plural of ibn, 'son') belonging to a group of people, marked as theirs.
7.grammar: A plural noun 'sons' carrying the accusative -a ending, followed by the attached possessive pronoun -hum ('their', masculine plural). The accusative typically marks the noun as a verb's object. The pronoun normally appears as -hum; its vowel here lengthens to -humu for smooth pronunciation before a following word.

8.meaning: Those who / the ones who — a plural relative pronoun (masculine) introducing a description: 'those (people) who …'.
8.grammar: A relative pronoun, masculine plural, meaning 'those who / the ones who'. It refers back to a group already in view and introduces a clause describing them. Its form is fixed and does not change for case.

9.meaning: 'They lost', 'they have suffered loss', 'they ruined themselves' — said of a group of males who have come out as losers, forfeiting or wasting something of value, especially their own selves.
9.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -ū ending means the subject is 'they' (more than one male) and the action is presented as completed: 'they lost'.
9.root: خ-س-ر (kh-s-r) — loss, to lose, to suffer ruin

10.meaning: A noun meaning 'their own selves' or 'themselves' — the plural of 'nafs' (self, soul, person, inner self), joined to the pronoun 'their.' It commonly conveys the reflexive idea of acting upon one's own self.
10.grammar: A noun (a broken/irregular plural of 'nafs') with the attached possessive pronoun '-hum' ('their/them,' masculine plural). The -a case ending before the pronoun is accusative, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb — i.e. the self upon which the action falls.

11.meaning: Means 'so they / then they' — the connector 'so/then' joined to the standalone pronoun 'they' (for a group of males or a mixed group). It draws a consequence and then names the subject.
11.grammar: The connecting particle fa- ('so/then', drawing a result or sequence from what precedes) attached to the detached subject pronoun hum ('they', masculine or mixed plural). As a standalone pronoun it has no case ending and serves as the subject of what follows.

12.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
12.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

13.meaning: 'They believe / they have faith' — to affirm something as true with trusting inner conviction and to feel secure in it. The verb carries both believing and being at peace through that belief; in religious use it is to commit oneself in faith.
13.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb, masculine plural. The yu-…-una frame means 'they (men, or a mixed group) do' the action now or habitually. The retained final -na marks the indicative (a plain, unqualified statement) — 'they believe' — as opposed to forms where that -na drops. The verb is Form IV (amana), used intransitively here meaning simply 'to believe / to have faith'.

1.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
1.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

2.meaning: An elative adjective meaning 'more / most wrongdoing, unjust, or oppressive' — comparing degrees of ẓulm (placing things out of their rightful place, transgression).
2.grammar: An elative (comparative/superlative) noun on the pattern afʿal, meaning 'more/most unjust'. It ends in -u (nominative), the case typical of a subject or predicate.
2.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — wrongdoing, injustice, putting something where it does not belong

3.meaning: A combination meaning 'than whoever / than one who' or 'from whoever' — the preposition min ('from/than') merged with man ('who/whoever'). It links a comparison or origin to an unspecified person.
3.grammar: The preposition min ('from', and 'than' in comparisons) fused with the relative/indefinite pronoun man ('who(ever)'). The nūn of min assimilates into the mīm of man, so min + man becomes mimman. The whole final nūn belongs to man, not to min; the kasrah on it (-i) is a liaison (waṣl) vowel added to keep two unvowelled consonants (sukūns) from meeting before the next word. Read together: mimmani, 'than/from the one who'.

4.meaning: 'He fabricated, invented, forged (a lie); he concocted falsely' — made something up and falsely attributed it, especially a lie. A verb of deliberate fabrication.

parts.en: connecting (helping) vowel for the verb pattern
past-tense 3rd person masculine singular ending '-ā' (from a weak final root letter)

4.grammar: A past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he fabricated'). It is a Form VIII (ifta'ala) verb. The final '-ā' (written as alif maqṣūra) is how the past-tense '-a' ending appears when the root ends in a weak letter (w/y). The initial 'i-' is a helping vowel that lets the consonant cluster of this pattern be pronounced.
4.root: ف-ر-ي (f-r-y) — to fabricate, forge, invent (a falsehood)

5.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
5.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
5.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

6.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
6.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

7.meaning: A noun meaning 'a lie / falsehood' — a deliberately false statement, an untruth fabricated against the truth.
7.grammar: An indefinite noun ('a lie') with the accusative -an ending (tanwīn). The accusative commonly marks the object of a verb (e.g. fabricating a lie); the -an tanwīn shows it is indefinite.
7.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie, to declare false

8.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
8.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

9.meaning: A verb meaning 'he denied / cried lies against / rejected as false' — to treat something or someone as a lie, refusing to accept it as true and openly rejecting it.
9.grammar: Past-tense verb (form II, intensive), third-person masculine singular ('he denied / rejected as false'). The doubled middle letter (kadhdhaba) gives the sense of actively declaring something false. The final -a is the past-tense ending for a masculine singular doer.
9.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie; (form II) to deny, to call a lie

10.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in / by His signs' — the preposition bi- ('with/in/by') joined to āyāt ('signs, verses, tokens') and 'His'. Āyāt are signs or proofs pointing to Allah, including revealed verses and observable signs.
10.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in/by/with') governing the plural noun āyāt ('signs'), which takes the genitive -i ending because it follows a preposition; the attached -hi means 'His'. The genitive is the case used after prepositions and to show possession ('signs OF His'). The pronoun appears as -hi (rather than -hu) in harmony with the preceding -i vowel.

11.meaning: An emphasis particle fused with a pronoun, meaning 'indeed He' or 'truly He'. The particle inna strongly affirms and certifies the statement that follows ('it is certainly the case that…'), with 'He' as its subject.
11.grammar: The emphasising particle inna ('indeed/truly') with the attached pronoun -hu ('He'). inna affirms and strengthens the whole statement and grammatically takes a following noun or pronoun as its subject. The lengthened -hū is how this pronoun is pronounced after an -u vowel.

12.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
12.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

13.meaning: A verb meaning 'he succeeds / prospers / attains salvation' — to thrive and reach what is sought while escaping what is feared; ultimate well-being and triumph, including success in the Hereafter.
13.grammar: Present-tense verb (form IV), third-person masculine singular ('he succeeds'). The yu- prefix marks 'he', and the final -u is the indicative ending for a plain present statement.
13.root: ف-ل-ح (f-l-ḥ) — to prosper, succeed, attain, be saved

14.meaning: The wrongdoers; those who do wrong, act unjustly, or place things where they do not belong. The underlying image is one who oppresses, transgresses limits, and deals unjustly with others or with themselves.
14.grammar: An active participle (the doer of the action) made definite by the prefix al- ('the'). The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural in the nominative (subject) case, the form used when the word functions as the doer of a verb or the subject of a sentence.

1.meaning: "and (on the) day" — the conjunction "and" joined to the noun for "day," a single daytime period or, more broadly, an appointed day or time of judgment/event.
1.grammar: The wa- prefix is the conjunction "and." The -a ending on the noun is accusative; on a word for "day" this frequently marks it as an adverb of time ("on the day …"), or marks it as the object of a verb.

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'we gather them / we will herd them together' — to assemble and drive a group together into one place, as in the mustering of creatures. With 'them' attached, it means rounding them up.
2.grammar: Present-tense verb, first-person plural ('we gather'). The na- prefix means 'we', and the indicative -u on the stem (naḥshuru) marks a plain present/future statement. The attached -hum is the object 'them' (masculine plural).
2.root: ح-ش-ر (ḥ-sh-r) — to gather, assemble, muster together

3.meaning: A word meaning 'all together', 'all of them', or 'the whole lot' — emphasising that no one and nothing is left out of a group.
3.grammar: A noun meaning 'all/entirety' carrying the -an ending: accusative case with tanwīn (the indefinite '-n'). This accusative form is typical of a word that comes alongside another to specify it as 'all of them, every one', describing the manner or extent.

4.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
4.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

5.meaning: A verb meaning 'we say' — the act of speaking or uttering words, in the first-person plural.
5.grammar: Present-tense verb, first-person plural ('we say'). The na- prefix means 'we'; this is a hollow verb whose middle root letter appears as a long ū (naqūlu). The final -u is the indicative ending for a plain present/future statement.

6.meaning: A compound meaning 'for those who' or 'belonging to those who'. It joins the preposition 'for/to' with a masculine plural relative pronoun ('those who'), introducing a clause that describes a group of people by something they do or possess.
6.grammar: The prefix 'li-' is a preposition meaning 'for', 'to', or expressing ownership/benefit ('belonging to'). The relative pronoun is 'alladhīna' ('those who'), but when 'li-' attaches to it the connecting hamza of 'al-' drops out and the two lām sounds merge into one doubled lām, so the form is written and read 'lilladhīna' rather than 'li-alladhīna'. 'alladhīna' has a fixed shape and does not change for case.

7.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'they associated partners / they set up partners (with Allah)' — to ascribe partners or equals to Allah, the act underlying idolatry and polytheism.
7.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb in a pattern meaning 'to make (someone) a partner'. The ending -ū marks a masculine-plural subject, 'they', so it reads 'they associated partners (with Allah)'.

8.meaning: Where / wherever. An interrogative or conditional adverb of place: it asks 'where?' or, in a conditional sense, sets up 'wherever / in whatever place'.
8.grammar: An indeclinable adverb of place fixed on a final -a; it does not change for case. It functions either as a question word ('where?') or as a conditional particle introducing a clause ('wherever'), often pairing with a following verb in the jussive mood.

9.meaning: A noun-phrase meaning 'your (plural) partners / associates' — those alleged to share with Allah in divinity or worship, the partners that a group ascribes to Him, marked as belonging to that group.
9.grammar: A plural noun 'partners' with the nominative -u ending, followed by the attached possessive -kum ('your', plural). The nominative typically marks the subject of a sentence. The pronoun normally appears as -kum; its vowel lengthens to -kumu for smooth linking before a following word.

10.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
10.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

11.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
11.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
11.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

12.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (plural) claim / allege / assert' — to make a claim, often one that is unfounded or merely supposed. It frequently carries a tone of an unproven or false assertion.
12.grammar: Present-tense verb, second-person masculine plural ('you all claim'). The ta- prefix marks 'you', and the -ūna ending marks masculine plural indicative for a plain present statement.
12.root: ز-ع-م (z-ʿ-m) — to claim, allege, assert (often without proof)

1.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
1.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

2.meaning: A negating particle, 'not', used specifically to deny that an action happened in the past, even though it attaches to a present-tense verb form. It turns 'you do X' into 'you did not do X'.

parts.en: did not (negation of a completed act)

2.grammar: An indeclinable particle that governs the verb after it, putting that verb into the jussive (clipped) mood and giving it past-time meaning. In short: lam + a present-form verb = 'did not [verb]'.

3.meaning: A short (jussive) form of the verb 'to be / to become', meaning 'be' or 'does not become / is not'. It expresses being, existing, or coming to be in a clipped form that typically follows a particle such as a negator or a command.
3.grammar: Present-tense verb with the ta- prefix marking a second-person masculine singular ('you') or third-person feminine singular ('it/she') subject. The clipped final consonant (sukun, no vowel) is the jussive/apocopated mood, the form used after negative particles ('did not / was not') or as a command or prohibition.
3.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be
