6.meaning: 'They say / they keep saying' — a present-tense verb of speaking: to say, utter, or assert in words.
6.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'), from a hollow (middle-vowel) root. The ya- prefix marks the 'they/he' class, the -ū marks the masculine plural subject, and the -na ending signals the ordinary (indicative) present, 'they are saying.'

7.meaning: 'for indeed they …' — a connective 'for/so' joined to an emphatic particle that strongly affirms what follows, plus the pronoun 'they'. The combination introduces a firmly stressed statement about a group.
7.grammar: The particle 'inna' gives strong emphasis ('indeed, truly') and grammatically takes a following noun or pronoun in the accusative; here that is the attached -hum ('they', masculine plural), which serves as its subject. The leading 'fa' connects the clause to what precedes ('and so / for').

8.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
8.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

9.meaning: A verb meaning 'they call (you) a liar / they reject (you) as false,' with the object 'you.' The intensive pattern conveys persistent or emphatic denial — treating someone or their message as untrue.

parts.en: they (the prefix marking a third-person subject)
to charge with lying / reject as false (intensive)
plural marker, with the -na of the ongoing/present

9.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb in an intensive pattern (the middle letter carries a doubling shadda, strengthening the sense to 'charge with lying'), third-person masculine plural. The yu- prefix marks 'they,' and -ūna marks a plural subject and an ongoing or repeated action. The attached -ka is the object, 'you' (one male).
9.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie; in this pattern, to call a liar, deny as false

10.meaning: But; however; rather. A particle of correction or contrast that cancels or qualifies a preceding statement and introduces what is actually the case.
10.grammar: A connective wa- ('and') joined to the emphatic particle lākinna. Lākinna belongs to the 'inna family: it governs the noun that follows it, putting it in the accusative case, and adds a sense of firm contrast — 'but in fact …'.

11.meaning: The wrongdoers — those who do wrong or injustice; literally those who put things out of their rightful place, transgressing limits and harming themselves or others. The root sense is darkness.
11.grammar: 'al-' is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'ẓ', doubling it). The stem is an active participle ('one who wrongs') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the object/genitive form of the sound masculine plural, marking the word as an object of a verb or governed by a preposition.
11.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — darkness; wrongdoing, injustice

12.meaning: 'With/in the signs of…' — the preposition bi- joined to a plural noun meaning 'signs', 'tokens', or 'verses': evidences that point to a truth beyond themselves.
12.grammar: bi- is a preposition meaning 'with/in' and always takes the genitive. āyāt is a sound feminine plural; its -i ending here is genitive, the case required after the preposition, and it typically also links to a following noun ('signs OF …').
12.root: ء-ي-ي / ء-و-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, mark, or token

13.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
13.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

14.meaning: A verb meaning 'they knowingly reject / deny / repudiate.' Its distinctive sense is denying something one inwardly recognizes to be true — rejection against better knowledge.

parts.en: they (the prefix marking a third-person subject)
plural marker, with the -na of the ongoing/present

14.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb, third-person masculine plural. The ya- prefix marks 'they,' and -ūna marks a plural subject and an ongoing or repeated action. The retained -na is the mark of the indicative mood, the verb's default unbroken form.
14.root: ج-ح-د (j-ḥ-d) — to deny or reject what one knows to be true

1.meaning: "And indeed / and most certainly" — combines 'and' with the emphatic 'la-' and the particle 'qad'; before a past-tense verb 'qad' affirms that the action has definitely and already happened, reinforced into 'and indeed it surely did'.
1.grammar: The conjunction 'and' plus the emphatic 'la-' ('surely') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' stresses that the act is real and completed ('has indeed happened'); together they form a strong oath-like affirmation. These are function words and are not inflected.

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'she/it was called a liar, was denied, was rejected as false.' It is the passive of the intensive 'to charge with lying' — the action is undergone rather than performed.

parts.en: to be charged with lying / be rejected as false (passive)

2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in the passive voice and intensive pattern; the middle letter carries a doubling shadda and the internal vowels (u–i) mark it as passive, so the subject receives the action. The ending -at marks a third-person feminine-singular subject ('she/it was …'), viewed as a completed action.
2.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie; in this pattern, to be called a liar / denied

3.meaning: Messengers — the plural of 'messenger': those sent with a commission to convey a message; in religious usage, prophets sent with revelation.
3.grammar: A plural noun. The final '-un' (tanwīn ḍamma) is the indefinite nominative: it marks 'messengers' (no 'the') and signals that the word is functioning as a subject or naming a thing rather than being possessed or governed by a preposition.
3.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send, dispatch a message

4.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
4.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

5.meaning: 'Before you' (in time or place): the period or position prior to a single person — that which comes earlier or stands in front, relative to one addressee.
5.grammar: The adverb/noun qabl ('before, prior') with the attached pronoun -ka ('you', a single male). The -i ending on qabl is genitive, the case regularly taken after a preposition (such as min, 'from before') and when a noun is linked to a following possessor; here it is linked to the pronoun 'you' ('before-you').
5.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, be before; priority, what comes first

6.meaning: A verb meaning 'so/then they were patient, they bore it steadfastly,' prefixed with 'so/then.' Patience here is steadfast endurance — restraining oneself and holding firm through hardship.

parts.en: they (masculine-plural subject ending; the final alif is silent)

6.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb led by the connector fa- ('so/then,' often showing sequence or result). The ending -ū marks a third-person masculine-plural subject ('they'), viewing the action as completed. The written final alif after the wāw is silent.
6.root: ص-ب-ر (ṣ-b-r) — to be patient, endure, restrain oneself

7.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
7.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

8.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
8.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

9.meaning: A verb meaning 'they were called liars, were denied, were rejected as false.' It is the passive plural of the intensive 'to charge with lying' — the people undergo the rejection rather than perform it.

parts.en: to be charged with lying / be rejected as false (passive)
they (masculine-plural subject ending; the final alif is silent)

9.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in the passive voice and intensive pattern; the middle letter carries a doubling shadda and the internal vowels (u–i) mark it as passive, so the subjects receive the action. The ending -ū marks a third-person masculine-plural subject ('they were …'). The written final alif is silent.
9.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie; in this pattern, to be called liars / denied

10.meaning: 'And they were harmed / hurt / persecuted' — a passive completed-action verb meaning to be subjected to harm, injury, or persecution, with 'they' as those harmed.

parts.en: were harmed, hurt (Form IV passive stem)

10.grammar: A connective wa ('and') on a Form IV perfect (completed-action) verb in the passive voice ('were …-ed'). The internal vowelling marks it as passive; the suffix -ū marks a masculine plural subject ('they'). So: 'they were harmed'.
10.root: أ-ذ-ي (ʾ-dh-y) — to harm, hurt, injure, cause suffering

11.meaning: A particle meaning 'until, up to the point that,' or 'so that.' It marks an end-limit in time, place, or purpose — the boundary at which something culminates or the goal toward which it moves.
11.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It introduces an end-point or goal; when followed by a verb it can express purpose or result ('until' / 'so that').

12.meaning: A verb meaning 'it/he came to them, reached them, arrived to them,' with the object 'them.' The root sense is coming or arriving at a destination.

parts.en: them / to them (attached object pronoun, masculine plural)

12.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it came'), with a weak final root-letter showing as the long -ā. The attached -hum is the object pronoun, 'them' (a male group). The action is viewed as completed.
12.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come, arrive, reach

13.meaning: A noun meaning 'our help, our aid, our victory.' The root denotes coming to someone's assistance and granting triumph, here joined to the pronoun 'our.'
13.grammar: A noun with the attached pronoun -nā ('our'). The -u before the pronoun is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the subject of a verb or sentence.
13.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, aid, grant victory

14.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
14.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

15.meaning: A noun/participle meaning 'one who changes / alters / replaces.' It names the doer of changing — a substituter who exchanges one thing for another.

parts.en: one who … (prefix forming an active doer-noun)

15.grammar: An active participle (a doer-noun) from the intensive pattern, with the mu- prefix that marks 'the one who does' the action. The final -a is the accusative case ending, the form a noun takes as the object of a verb or after certain particles (such as 'there is no …').

16.meaning: A noun meaning 'the words / utterances / decrees,' prefixed with 'for/to.' Beyond ordinary speech it can denote Allah's words, commands, and decisive decrees. It is the plural of 'word.'

parts.en: genitive ending (because of the preceding preposition)

16.grammar: A sound feminine plural noun governed by the attached preposition li- ('for / to'). The final -i is the genitive case ending — the form sound feminine plurals take after a preposition or when linked to a following noun ('… of …').
16.root: ك-ل-م (k-l-m) — to speak; hence a word or utterance

17.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
17.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

18.meaning: "And indeed / and most certainly" — combines 'and' with the emphatic 'la-' and the particle 'qad'; before a past-tense verb 'qad' affirms that the action has definitely and already happened, reinforced into 'and indeed it surely did'.
18.grammar: The conjunction 'and' plus the emphatic 'la-' ('surely') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' stresses that the act is real and completed ('has indeed happened'); together they form a strong oath-like affirmation. These are function words and are not inflected.

19.meaning: It came to you / reached you — a completed arrival of something reaching a person (one male).
19.grammar: A past-tense verb, 'he/it came', whose final -a vowel is the inherent third-person masculine singular inflection built into the verb form itself (not a separate piece). The attached pronoun -ka ('you', one male) is the object reached — 'it came to you'.
19.root: ج-ي-ء (j-y-ʾ) — to come, arrive, reach

20.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
20.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
20.root: — (preposition)

21.meaning: A noun meaning 'tidings, news, an account of weighty import,' prefixed with 'of/from.' It denotes significant information or a report of consequence, not mere trivial news.

parts.en: the third root-letter (hamza) carrying the genitive ending (because of a preceding preposition)

21.grammar: A noun in the genitive case. The three root-letters are n-b-ʾ; the final hamza (ʾ) is the third radical, and the -i upon it is the genitive case ending — the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a following noun ('… of …').
21.root: ن-ب-أ (n-b-ʾ) — to inform; hence weighty news or tidings

22.meaning: "the messengers / the ones sent" — the definite plural of mursal, a passive participle meaning 'one who is sent'; it denotes those commissioned and dispatched, i.e. the divine messengers.
22.grammar: A definite masculine sound plural passive participle ('the sent ones'). The -īna ending is the accusative/genitive (object or after-preposition) form of the masculine plural, as opposed to -ūna which would mark the subject form.

1.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
1.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

2.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

2.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

3.meaning: A finite past-tense verb meaning 'it became great/weighty/burdensome' — that something grew large, heavy, hard to bear, or oppressive to the heart. Often used of a matter felt as overwhelming or intolerably difficult.
3.grammar: A perfect (past-tense) verb, 3rd-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The intransitive vowel pattern (-u- in the middle) indicates an inherent quality — it 'is/became' great rather than acting on something. The final -a is the standard ending of this past-tense form.

4.meaning: "upon you / to you / against you" — the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over') with the 'you' pronoun, carrying senses of resting upon, being directed to, or bearing upon someone.
4.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base ʿalā shifts to ʿalay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -ka means 'you' (second-person masculine singular). Prepositions themselves take no case ending.

5.meaning: A verbal noun meaning 'their turning away / their aversion / their rejection' — the act of averting oneself from something and refusing to face or accept it, attributed to 'them'.
5.grammar: A verbal noun (the action named as a thing) from Form IV, carrying the sense of deliberately turning oneself away. The -u ending marks the nominative case (the word as subject or naming-form). The attached -hum ('their') is in the possessive/genitive role, owning the action: 'the turning-away of them'.
5.root: ع-ر-ض (ʿ-r-ḍ) — to present, turn aside, set oneself athwart; here, turning away

6.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'then if / so if.' It joins a clause to what precedes (fa-) and introduces a hypothetical condition (in, 'if').
6.grammar: A compound of two particles. Fa- means 'then/so,' connecting to a prior statement. In means 'if,' setting up a condition whose outcome follows. The final -i is a helping vowel added to the normally vowel-less in to ease pronunciation before the next word; it carries no grammatical case meaning.

7.meaning: A finite past-tense verb meaning 'you were able / you had the power or capacity' — to possess the strength, means, or ability to do something.
7.grammar: A perfect (past-tense) verb of Form X (the 'ista-' pattern, often meaning to seek or find within oneself a capacity). The suffix -ta marks the doer as 2nd-person masculine singular ('you'). It frequently opens conditional statements ('if you are/were able…').
7.root: ط-و-ع (ṭ-w-ʿ) — willing obedience, capacity, being able

8.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
8.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

9.meaning: A finite present/future verb meaning 'you seek / strive after / desire to obtain' — to actively pursue or want to attain something.
9.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb of Form VIII, meaning to seek out or strive for. The ta- prefix marks 2nd-person masculine singular ('you'). The final -a (written here on the weak final letter as -iya) is the subjunctive mood, which typically appears after particles meaning 'so that / in order to / that' and signals purpose or dependence on a preceding word.
9.root: ب-غ-ي (b-gh-y) — to seek, desire, strive after

10.meaning: A noun meaning 'a tunnel / an underground passage / a burrow' — a hole or channel dug through or beneath the ground.
10.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The -an ending (tanwīn) marks both indefiniteness ('a tunnel') and the accusative case, the form a noun takes when it is the object of a verb. It is pronounced with a final '-n' sound that is not written as a separate letter.
10.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — to pass through / tunnel; also spending and hypocrisy share this root via the idea of an outlet

11.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
11.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
11.root: — (particle)

12.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
12.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').
12.root: أ-ر-ض (ʾ-r-ḍ) — earth, land, ground

13.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
13.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

14.meaning: A noun meaning 'a ladder / a stairway / a means of ascent' — something by which one climbs upward.
14.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The -an ending (tanwīn) marks indefiniteness ('a ladder') together with the accusative case, the form used when the noun is a verb's object. The final '-n' sound is spoken but not written as a letter.
14.root: س-ل-م (s-l-m) — soundness, safety; by extension a means of ascent (ladder)

15.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
15.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

16.meaning: The sky or heaven — the canopy overhead; the expanse above the earth, also that which is elevated or raised over something. With the definite article it means 'the sky / the heaven'.
16.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'), in the genitive marked by the -i ending. (The 'l' of al- assimilates in sound into the following 's', a 'sun letter', though it is still written.) The genitive -i ending typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').

17.meaning: A finite present/future verb meaning 'so that you bring/come to them' — to come bearing something to people, here joined with 'them' as the ones approached.
17.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb meaning 'to come / bring'. The fa- prefix means 'so that / then' and carries the sense of a result or purpose; the ta- prefix marks the doer as 2nd-person masculine singular ('you'). The verb stands in the subjunctive mood (final -a), expected after such a result/purpose particle. The attached -hum ('them') is the object reached.

18.meaning: With a sign — by means of an indicative token, miracle, or evidentiary proof that points to a truth.
18.grammar: The prefix bi- means 'with / by means of' and always pulls the following noun into the genitive. The final -in (tanwīn) is the indefinite genitive: 'with a sign', the ending required after this preposition and marking the noun as indefinite ('a', not 'the').
18.root: أ-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — sign, mark, token; a verse of scripture

19.meaning: 'and if' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle 'if'. This particular 'if' (law) introduces a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact condition: 'if (such-and-such had been the case)…', often implying it was not.
19.grammar: A conjunction plus a conditional particle. wa- means 'and'. law is a non-changing particle (no case ending) that sets up a supposition, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('… then certainly …').
19.root: — (particles; no triliteral root)

20.meaning: A past-tense verb 'he willed / he wished / he so desired'. It denotes an act of will or volition bringing something about.
20.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third person masculine singular ('he'). The bare stem with no suffix is the basic 'he did' form. Its subject and object are typically supplied by context.
20.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — to will, wish

21.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
21.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
21.root: — (proper divine name)

22.meaning: A past-tense verb introduced by an emphatic particle, meaning 'He would surely have gathered them / brought them together'. The combination expresses the strongly affirmed outcome of an unfulfilled condition.
22.grammar: A perfect (past-tense) verb, 3rd-person masculine singular ('he'), with final -a as its standard ending. The prefixed la- is an emphatic particle ('surely, certainly') that commonly answers a hypothetical 'if', stressing that the result would definitely have occurred. The attached -hum ('them') is the object gathered.
22.root: ج-م-ع (j-m-ʿ) — to gather, collect, bring together

23.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
23.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
23.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

24.meaning: The guidance; the right leading and true direction (with the definite article, 'the Guidance').
24.grammar: A definite verbal noun: the prefix al- means 'the'. It ends in a long -ā (from a weak-final root), an ending that does not change for case. It denotes the abstract reality of right guidance, made specific and definite by 'the'.
24.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead rightly, show the way

25.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
25.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

26.meaning: You must certainly be / never be — an emphatic form of the verb 'to be', stressing that one truly will (or, with a negative, truly must not) be in a certain state.
26.grammar: A present-tense form of the verb 'to be', addressed to 'you' (the prefix ta-). The heavy ending -anna (nūn of emphasis) gives a strong, insistent force — 'you most certainly are/must be' — and is the standard way Arabic stresses a command or warning attached to a verb.
26.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into being

27.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
27.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

28.meaning: 'The ignorant ones' — those marked by jahl: ignorance of the truth, or the reckless, unrestrained conduct that springs from it. It describes people who act without knowledge or proper self-control.
28.grammar: A definite active participle ('the ignorant ones'): 'al-' is 'the', and jāhil is the doer-noun 'one who is ignorant'. The -īna ending is the masculine sound-plural in its accusative/genitive form, used when the word is an object, follows a preposition, or completes a verb like 'to be'.
28.root: ج-ه-ل (j-h-l) — ignorance; rash, unrestrained behaviour

1.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
1.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

2.meaning: A finite present/future verb meaning 'he/it responds / answers / accepts an appeal' — to give a favorable reply to a call, prayer, or request.
2.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb of Form X (the 'ista-' pattern), conveying responding to or answering a call. The ya- prefix marks 3rd-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The final -u marks the indicative mood — the plain, fact-stating form used when the verb is not governed by a particle of negation, purpose, or condition.

3.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
3.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

4.meaning: They hear / listen to — to perceive by hearing, and often to give heed to what is heard.
4.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form I). The 'ya-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks the third-person masculine plural ('they'). The '-ūna' (with final 'n') is the indicative form, marking a plain ongoing or habitual action.

5.meaning: A plural noun with two prefixes, meaning 'and the dead' — those who have died; lifeless ones, as opposed to the living.
5.grammar: A plural noun preceded by the connector wa- ('and/but') and the definite article al- ('the'). It follows a fixed (non-changing) plural pattern ending in a long -ā, so its case is not shown by a final vowel; the ending stays the same whether subject or object.

6.meaning: A finite present/future verb meaning 'He raises them / brings them back to life / sends them forth' — to resurrect or dispatch, joined with 'them' as those acted upon.
6.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb, 3rd-person masculine singular ('He'). The ya- prefix marks that subject. The attached -hum ('them') is the object raised; the final -u here is a helping vowel added so that '-hum' joins smoothly to a following word. The base sense covers both raising the dead and sending someone forth on a mission.
6.root: ب-ع-ث (b-ʿ-th) — to raise up, resurrect, send forth

7.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
7.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

8.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
8.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

9.meaning: 'To Him' or 'toward Him' — the preposition expressing direction or endpoint ('to / toward') combined with a pronoun referring to a single masculine person, indicating motion or attention directed at him.
9.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base 'ilā shifts to 'ilay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -hi is the third-person masculine singular object of a preposition, 'him'; its -i vowel is the form the pronoun takes after the 'ay' sound.

10.meaning: 'They are returned / brought back.' A passive form: the subjects do not act but are themselves caused to return to someone, conveying that all will ultimately be brought back to Allah.
10.grammar: A present-tense passive verb. The vowel pattern (yu-…-a-) makes it passive: the subject is acted upon ('are returned') rather than acting. The -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they') in the indicative mood used for plain statements.
10.root: ر-ج-ع (r-j-ʿ) — to return, go back, bring back

1.meaning: And they said — to utter or declare in speech, with the action presented as completed by a group.
1.grammar: The prefix 'wa-' means 'and'. 'qāla' is the past-tense verb 'to say'; the '-ū' suffix marks a completed action done by 'they' (a masculine or mixed group). The stem shown here ('qālu') carries only the stem vowel before the suffix, with the plural '-ū' supplied by the separate ending. Past tense, so the speaking is presented as already finished.

2.meaning: A particle of urging or exhortation meaning 'why not …?' — used to press for or demand that something be done, and sometimes to express a wish, often with a tone of reproach ('why does … not happen?').
2.grammar: An indivisible particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ). Although written as one form, it is not built up from the conditional 'if' plus a negation; in this prompting usage it is a single fixed particle meaning 'why not?' / 'if only.' Followed by a verb it presses for that action. (Note: in a different construction the same form can mean 'were it not for,' but that is a separate usage.) It is a particle and takes no case ending.

3.meaning: A past-tense passive verb meaning 'it was sent down / caused to descend' — something made to come down (typically revelation), with an intensive nuance of being sent down gradually or fully.
3.grammar: A perfect (past-tense) passive verb of Form II (the doubled-middle pattern, which adds intensity or gradualness), 3rd-person masculine singular. The vowel shape 'nuzzila' (u–i) marks it as passive: the subject is the thing acted upon, with the doer unnamed ('it was sent down'). The final -a is the standard past-tense ending.
3.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down; (sending down)

4.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
4.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

5.meaning: A sign, token, or mark — and especially a 'verse' of revelation. It denotes a clear indicator that points to a deeper truth: a miracle, a proof, or a portion of revealed text.
5.grammar: A feminine noun in the nominative case with tanwīn (the -un ending), marking it as indefinite ('a sign') and typically the subject or doer of a sentence. The nominative shows it is acting or being identified rather than acted upon.

6.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
6.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

7.meaning: A phrase meaning 'his Lord'. 'Lord' (rabb) denotes the Master, Owner, Sustainer, and Nurturer who creates, provides for, and governs — far richer than a mere title; here joined to 'his'.
7.grammar: The noun 'Lord' with the genitive -i ending followed by the attached pronoun -hi ('his'). The genitive case appears because the noun is linked to a preceding word ('… OF his Lord') or follows a preposition. The lengthened -hī reflects how this pronoun is pronounced after an -i vowel.
7.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, nurturing, ownership, sustaining and bringing to completion

8.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
8.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

9.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
9.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

10.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
10.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

11.meaning: An active participle meaning 'able / capable / having power and determining control' — one who possesses the power to do a thing and to measure it out as He wills.
11.grammar: An active participle (a doer-noun, 'one who is able') on the 'fāʿil' pattern. The -un ending (tanwīn) marks indefiniteness together with the nominative case — the naming form used for a subject or predicate. The final '-n' sound is pronounced but not written as a separate letter.
11.root: ق-د-ر (q-d-r) — power, ability, measuring out / decreeing

12.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on, upon, over,' and by extension 'against' or 'incumbent upon.' It can mark something resting on top of, an obligation laid on someone, or being set over/above something.
12.grammar: An indeclinable preposition (its form never changes). It governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case, and conveys location 'on/upon,' or figuratively duty or opposition ('against').
12.root: — (preposition; no triliteral root)

13.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
13.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

14.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he sends down (gradually/repeatedly), he bestows' — the intensive form often implying sending down in stages or in abundance, used of revelation or grace.
14.grammar: A present-tense verb with a single masculine subject ('he'); the yu- prefix marks third-person masculine singular, and the final -a shows the subjunctive mood — used after particles like 'that' or 'so that.' The doubled middle letter (form II) intensifies the action, suggesting sending down little by little or copiously.

15.meaning: 'A sign' — a token, mark, or proof that points to something beyond itself; a miraculous indication, a lesson, or an evidence. (The same word also denotes a verse of the Qur'an.)
15.grammar: An indefinite noun. The '-an' ending (accusative with 'tanwīn', the doubled final 'n' of indefiniteness) typically marks the noun as the direct object of a verb, or as the thing one is being made or named, and signals 'a / an' rather than 'the'.

16.meaning: A connective particle 'but / however / yet' used to correct or contrast with what precedes, here with emphasis. It introduces a clause that sets the record straight against an expectation.
16.grammar: A contrastive conjunction ('but, however') joined by 'wa' ('and'). This is the heavy, emphatic form 'lākinna', which governs the noun after it into the object ('-a') case and adds force, like saying 'but in fact …'. It rebuts or qualifies a preceding statement.
16.root: — (no triliteral root; a compound particle of exception/contrast)

17.meaning: A noun phrase meaning 'most of them / the greater part of them' — the larger portion of a group.
17.grammar: An elative/comparative noun ('more/most, the greater number') on the 'afʿal' pattern. The -a ending marks the accusative case, the form used when the word is a verb's object. The attached -hum ('them') is in the possessive role, completing the sense 'the most of them'.

18.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
18.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

19.meaning: They know, have knowledge, are aware. Expresses ongoing or habitual knowing held by a group of males (or a mixed group).
19.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending means 'they' (a group of males). The full -ūna ending (rather than a shortened -ū) marks the indicative mood, signaling a plain statement of fact: 'they (do) know.'
19.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; knowledge

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
2.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

3.meaning: A noun meaning 'a moving/walking creature / a beast / any living thing that treads the earth' — broadly, any animal that moves along the ground.
3.grammar: A singular indefinite feminine noun (originally an active participle, 'one that moves/treads'). The ending -tin combines the feminine marker (tā' marbūṭa) with tanwīn showing indefiniteness and the genitive case — the form typically used after a preposition or in a possessive link ('… of …'). The final '-n' sound is spoken but unwritten.
3.root: د-ب-ب (d-b-b) — to move/creep/walk gently along the ground

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
4.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

5.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
5.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

6.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
6.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

7.meaning: A noun meaning 'a bird / a flying creature' — a winged animal that flies.
7.grammar: A singular indefinite noun (an active participle in form, 'one that flies'). The -in ending (tanwīn) marks indefiniteness with the genitive case — the form a noun takes after a preposition or in a possessive ('… of …') link. The final '-n' is pronounced but not written as a separate letter.

8.meaning: A finite present/future verb meaning 'it flies / takes to the air' — moving through the air on wings.
8.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb, 3rd-person masculine singular ('it/he'), marked by the ya- prefix (here written doubled because it links closely to the preceding word). The final -u marks the indicative mood — the plain, fact-stating form used when no particle of negation, purpose, or condition governs the verb.

9.meaning: A prepositional phrase meaning 'with its two wings' — by means of the pair of wings belonging to it.
9.grammar: A noun in the dual (exactly two) carrying an attached possessive, governed by the preposition bi- ('with / by means of'). The dual form 'janāḥay-' is the case used after a preposition or as an object (its dual ending appears as -ay rather than -ā). The attached -hi ('its/his') is in the possessive role; its vowel is -i because it follows the -ay ending.

10.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
10.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

11.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'communities / nations / peoples' — groups of beings bound together as distinct collectives, each a community in its own right.
11.grammar: An indefinite plural noun (plural of 'umma', a community or nation). The -un ending (tanwīn) marks indefiniteness ('communities') together with the nominative case — the naming form used for a subject or predicate. The final '-n' sound is pronounced but not written as a letter.
11.root: أ-م-م (ʾ-m-m) — community, nation; a way/path followed in common

12.meaning: A noun phrase meaning 'the likes of you / ones similar to you' — peers or counterparts resembling the people addressed.
12.grammar: A plural noun ('likenesses, equals', plural of 'mithl') with an attached pronoun. The -u ending marks the nominative case — the naming form for a subject or predicate. The attached -kum ('your / you') stands in the possessive role, giving 'the likes of you'.
12.root: م-ث-ل (m-th-l) — likeness, similarity, resemblance

13.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
13.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

14.meaning: A verb meaning 'we fell short, we were neglectful, we squandered or failed in our duty.' It conveys negligence — falling below what was required and letting an opportunity or obligation slip away.

parts.en: to neglect / fall short / be remiss

14.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in an intensive pattern (the doubled middle letter strengthens the sense). The ending -nā marks a first-person plural subject: 'we' did this, viewed as a completed action.
14.root: ف-ر-ط (f-r-ṭ) — to fall short, neglect, let slip

15.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
15.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

16.meaning: 'The Book / the Scripture' — a written record or revealed scripture; literally that which is written.
16.grammar: The definite article al- with the noun kitāb ('book, scripture'), itself a verbal noun from 'to write.' The -i ending is genitive, typically marking the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a preceding noun.

17.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
17.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

18.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
18.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
18.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

19.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
19.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

20.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
20.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

21.meaning: 'Their Lord' — the base 'rabb' means Lord, Master, Sustainer: the one who owns, nurtures, governs, and brings to maturity. As a divine title it conveys Allah as Creator and Sustainer of all.
21.grammar: The noun 'rabb' ('Lord, Sustainer') with the attached pronoun '-him' ('their'). The '-i' before the pronoun is the genitive case, the form used after a preposition or, as in a possessive linkage, to show belonging ('of/their').
21.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, master, sustain; lordship

22.meaning: A finite present/future passive verb meaning 'they are gathered / mustered / brought together' — herded or assembled into one place, with the doer unnamed.
22.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) passive verb, 3rd-person masculine plural. The prefix vowel 'yu-' marks it as passive ('they are gathered', doer unstated). The ending -ūna marks a masculine-plural subject ('they') in the indicative mood — the plain, fact-stating form kept when no particle of purpose or negation shortens it. The word often carries the sense of being assembled for judgment.
22.root: ح-ش-ر (ḥ-sh-r) — to gather, herd together, muster

1.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

2.meaning: They denied / they cried lies; they declared (something or someone) to be false. An intensive verb meaning to reject as a lie, to disbelieve and brand untrue — directed by a plural 'they'.

parts.tr: kadhdhab (doubled dh; simplified transliterations may write 'kadhab')
parts.en: denied / branded as lies (past stem, intensive)

2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in an intensive pattern (to treat as false, to repeatedly deny). The middle radical carries a shadda (doubling), which is exactly what marks this as the intensive form: kadhdhab- (not the simple kadhab-). The ending -ū marks the doers as 'they' — a plural, grammatically masculine group, so the whole reconstructs to kadhdhabū. Note that simplified transliterations sometimes omit the doubling and write 'kadhabū', but the doubled dh is essential to the form. The perfect tense denotes a completed action.
2.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie; in this form, to call a lie, to deny as false

3.meaning: By/in Our signs. Āyāt is the plural of āya — a sign, token, or evidence. Signs are pointers that indicate a greater reality. With the prefixed particle and pronoun it means 'with/in Our signs'.
3.grammar: A plural noun preceded by the preposition bi- ('with, in, by'), which requires the following noun to take the -i (genitive) ending. The attached -nā means 'our' when joined to a noun. The genitive here is governed by the preposition.

4.meaning: Deaf — unable to hear; the plural describing a group who cannot hear. Figuratively it can describe those unresponsive to guidance or unwilling to listen.
4.grammar: A plural adjective/noun in the indefinite nominative, marked by the -un ending (tanwīn). The nominative -un ending typically marks the subject of a sentence or a basic descriptive statement ('[they are] deaf').

5.meaning: A plural noun joined by 'and', meaning 'and dumb / mute ones' — those unable to speak.
5.grammar: An indefinite plural adjective/noun ('mute ones', plural of 'abkam'), preceded by the connector wa- ('and'), here written doubled because it binds closely to the preceding word. The -un ending (tanwīn) marks indefiniteness and the nominative case — the naming form for a subject or predicate. The final '-n' is pronounced but unwritten.

6.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
6.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

7.meaning: Darknesses, layers of gloom; the manifold states of being deprived of light, whether literal or as a figure for ignorance and error.
7.grammar: A definite sound feminine plural noun ("the darknesses"). The -i ending here is genitive — the case taken by this plural after a preposition (the -āt plural shows genitive with -i rather than the -a it would take in the accusative). The al- prefix makes it definite ("the").
7.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — darkness; also wrongdoing and injustice

8.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
8.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

9.meaning: A finite present/future verb meaning 'he/it wills / wishes / desires' — to want or choose that something be.
9.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb, 3rd-person masculine singular ('he/it'), marked by the ya- prefix (written doubled because it links to the preceding word). It stands in the jussive mood — the shortened form a verb takes after a conditional particle ('if/whoever…'), so its outcome hangs on a condition. The jussive is shown by the dropping of the indicative -u (not by any added vowel). The final kasra (-i) written under the hamza is only a supporting/connecting vowel, added to ease pronunciation into the next word; it is a spelling/sound aid, not a mood ending.

10.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
10.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

11.meaning: A finite present/future verb meaning 'He leaves him to stray / lets him go astray / sends him off the path', joined with 'him' as the one affected.
11.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb of Form IV (causative — to cause or allow straying), 3rd-person masculine singular ('He'), marked by the yu- prefix. The stem shows the jussive/shortened form (the doubled root letters are split as -ḍlil-), the clipped ending used after a conditional particle, so the meaning depends on a preceding 'if/whoever'. The attached -hu ('him') is the object left to stray.
11.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, go astray, be lost; (to lead astray)

12.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
12.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.
12.root: — (pronoun/particle; no triliteral root)

13.meaning: A verb meaning 'He wills, wishes, or so chooses' — to want and intend something by sovereign decision. The root denotes willing and desiring as an act of the will.
13.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('He'). This is a hollow verb (the weak letter sits in the middle of the root, with hamza as the strong final radical). In the jussive/conditional mood the medial long vowel is shortened (giving 'yashaʾ' rather than 'yashāʾ') — the form taken after 'if' or in a conditional clause.

14.meaning: A verb meaning 'he makes/places/renders/appoints (him).' The root conveys setting something in a place or assigning it a state or role; with two objects it can mean 'to render X into Y.' The attached 'him/it' is what is being placed or transformed.
14.grammar: A present/jussive verb. The ya- prefix marks a single masculine 'he' as the doer. The bare ending (no final -u) reflects the jussive/short form rather than the indicative, often after a conditional or particle that shortens the verb. The suffix -hu is the direct object 'him/it.'
14.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, place, set, or appoint

15.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
15.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

16.meaning: 'A path / road / way'. It denotes a clear, open road that one travels — often used figuratively for a course of life or conduct.
16.grammar: The '-in' ending (tanwīn) marks the word as indefinite ('a path / some way') and in the genitive case. The genitive typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').

17.meaning: 'Straight / upright / undeviating' — describing something that runs true without bending or wandering; applied to a 'path' it means a direct, correct way that leads soundly to its goal.
17.grammar: An active participle (a describing word, 'straight/upright') from a verb meaning 'to be/become straight'. It is indefinite, and the -in ending is the genitive with 'tanwīn'. As a describing word it normally follows and agrees with the noun it modifies, matching that noun in being indefinite and in the genitive case.

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: A compound expression literally 'have you (all) considered / do you see?' It is an interrogative used rhetorically to make an audience reflect: 'tell me — what do you think?' The form combines the question particle, the verb 'to see/consider,' a 'you' subject, and a 'you' addressee pronoun.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb fronted by the question particle a-. The -ta ending marks 'you' (masculine singular) as the one who saw/considered. The added -kum (plural 'you') functions as an ethical/addressee pronoun reinforcing the appeal — roughly 'tell me, all of you.' The whole serves as a rhetorical 'what do you think?'

3.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
3.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

4.meaning: A verb meaning 'it/he came to you (all).' The root conveys coming or arriving; with an object pronoun it means something reached or befell the addressees.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it came'), shown by the bare stem with no subject suffix. The attached -kum is the object 'you (plural),' so the subject came to or reached the addressees.

5.meaning: A noun meaning 'punishment, torment, chastisement' — painful suffering imposed as a penalty.
5.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject or doer of a sentence (the thing performing or undergoing the main action) and is the noun's basic citation form.

6.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
6.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

7.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
7.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

8.meaning: A verb meaning 'it/she came to you (all).' Same coming/arriving sense as its masculine counterpart, but feminine, agreeing with a feminine subject such as 'the Hour' or 'punishment.'
8.grammar: A past-tense verb. The stem 'ata-' carries the meaning 'came'; the suffix -t is the feminine third-person singular marker, so the subject is 'she/it' (feminine). The attached pronoun is 'you (plural)' as object; its vowel surfaces as -kumu (the usual -kum lengthened to ease pronunciation before a following word).

9.meaning: A noun meaning 'the Hour' — a moment or short span of time. In its weighty sense it names the Last Hour, the appointed time of resurrection and final reckoning. Built with the definite article 'the.'
9.grammar: A definite noun (the 'l' of al- assimilates into the following 's,' doubling it). The final -u is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the subject of a verb or sentence.
9.root: س-و-ع (s-w-ʿ) — relating to an hour, a moment, or a span of time

10.meaning: 'Is it other than…?', 'shall (it be) other than…?' — a questioning expression built from the question particle 'is/shall?' and the word for 'other than / besides'. It challenges whether anything besides the named thing could be intended.
10.grammar: A yes/no question particle attached to the noun 'other than'. The -a ending is accusative, the case that often marks a word as a direct object or otherwise governed into this case (here the questioned object). The opening 'a-' turns the phrase into a question.
10.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — otherness, difference, being other than

11.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
11.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

12.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (all) call upon, invoke, summon, or pray to.' The root spans calling out, naming, inviting, and supplicating — especially calling on someone for help.
12.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix with the -ūna ending marks 'you all' (masculine plural) as the doers. The final -na is the indicative marker, signalling an ongoing or habitual action (a complete, non-shortened present-tense verb).
12.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, invoke, summon, pray

13.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
13.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

14.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
14.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
14.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

15.meaning: The plural of 'ṣādiq': 'truthful ones', 'those who speak the truth', 'the sincere and reliable'. It describes people whose words and conduct match reality.
15.grammar: 'ṣādiq' is an active participle ('one who is truthful'). The '-īna' ending is a 'sound' masculine plural marker; the '-ī-' form (rather than '-ū-') signals that the noun is functioning as an object or is governed by a preposition/particle, while the '-na' completes the plural ('the truthful ones').
15.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — truthfulness, sincerity, to speak truly

1.meaning: A particle of retraction meaning 'rather,' 'no, but,' or 'nay' — it cancels or sets aside what was just said and shifts to a corrected or contrasting statement that follows.
1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it never changes form). Its function is to redirect the discourse: it dismisses a prior idea and introduces what is actually the case.

2.meaning: An emphatic stand-alone object pronoun: 'Him (and Him alone).' The particle 'iyyā' exists precisely to carry an object pronoun out in front for emphasis or exclusivity, and the attached -hu means 'him/it.'
2.grammar: A special construction that lets an object pronoun stand on its own, usually for emphasis or to single something out ('Him alone'). The attached -hu is the third-person masculine singular object pronoun ('him/it'). As a particle base, iyyā itself takes no case ending.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (all) call upon, invoke, summon, or pray to.' The root spans calling out, naming, inviting, and supplicating — especially calling on someone for help.
3.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix with the -ūna ending marks 'you all' (masculine plural) as the doers. The final -na is the indicative marker, signalling an ongoing or habitual action (a complete, non-shortened present-tense verb).
3.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, invoke, summon, pray

4.meaning: A verb meaning 'so/then he uncovers, removes, lifts away, or discloses.' The root conveys stripping off a covering — hence removing a hardship or laying something bare. The prefixed 'fa-' adds 'so/then/and then.'
4.grammar: A present-tense verb with the connective particle fa- ('so/then') in front. The ya- prefix marks 'he' as the doer; the final -u is the indicative ending, marking a plain, ongoing or future action (the full, non-shortened present form).

5.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
5.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

6.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (all) call upon, invoke, summon, or pray to.' The root spans calling out, naming, inviting, and supplicating — especially calling on someone for help.
6.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix with the -ūna ending marks 'you all' (masculine plural) as the doers. The final -na is the indicative marker, signalling an ongoing or habitual action (a complete, non-shortened present-tense verb).
6.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, invoke, summon, pray

7.meaning: 'To Him' or 'toward Him' — the preposition expressing direction or endpoint ('to / toward') combined with a pronoun referring to a single masculine person, indicating motion or attention directed at him.
7.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base 'ilā shifts to 'ilay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -hi is the third-person masculine singular object of a preposition, 'him'; its -i vowel is the form the pronoun takes after the 'ay' sound.

8.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
8.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

9.meaning: A past-tense verb 'he willed / he wished / he so desired'. It denotes an act of will or volition bringing something about.
9.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third person masculine singular ('he'). The bare stem with no suffix is the basic 'he did' form. Its subject and object are typically supplied by context.

10.meaning: 'And you forget' or 'while you neglect' — to let something slip from the mind, to be heedless of or disregard it.
10.grammar: Begins with 'wa-' ('and/while'). The prefix 'ta-' marks a 2nd-person present-tense verb, and the '-awna' ending makes the subject a masculine plural 'you all.' Because this root ends in a weak letter (a defective verb), the plural ending surfaces as '-awna' rather than the usual '-ūna'; it is still the indicative form, signalling a plain factual/ongoing statement.
10.root: ن-س-ي (n-s-y) — to forget, neglect, be heedless

11.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
11.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

12.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (all) associate (something) as a partner.' The root means to make something a partner or share; in religious usage it is to set up partners alongside Allah, the opposite of pure monotheism.
12.grammar: A present-tense verb of the form that means 'to make a partner.' The tu- prefix plus -ūna ending marks 'you all' (masculine plural) as the doers. The final -na is the indicative marker, signalling an ongoing or habitual action (the complete, non-shortened present).
12.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, associate, take a partner

1.meaning: "And indeed / and most certainly" — combines 'and' with the emphatic 'la-' and the particle 'qad'; before a past-tense verb 'qad' affirms that the action has definitely and already happened, reinforced into 'and indeed it surely did'.
1.grammar: The conjunction 'and' plus the emphatic 'la-' ('surely') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' stresses that the act is real and completed ('has indeed happened'); together they form a strong oath-like affirmation. These are function words and are not inflected.

2.meaning: We sent / dispatched. From the causative verb meaning to send forth or commission, especially the sending of messengers; with 'We' as the subject.
2.grammar: Past/perfect verb in the causative (form IV) pattern meaning 'to send', 1st person plural ('we'). The suffix -nā is the subject ending 'we' on a completed action. The perfect tense presents the sending as accomplished and complete.

3.meaning: "to / towards" — a preposition marking the end-point, goal, or direction of a movement or extent ("up to," "as far as," "toward").
3.grammar: An indeclinable preposition; it has no case ending of its own and always governs a following noun in the genitive case.

4.meaning: A noun meaning 'nations, communities, or peoples' — the plural of 'umma,' a group bound together as one community.
4.grammar: A plural noun. The ending -in is genitive and indefinite (the doubled 'nunation' marking 'some, an indefinite'). The genitive case typically follows a preposition or links the noun to a preceding noun (the 'of' relationship), and the -in shows it is indefinite ('some communities').

5.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
5.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

6.meaning: 'Before you' (in time or place): the period or position prior to a single person — that which comes earlier or stands in front, relative to one addressee.
6.grammar: The adverb/noun qabl ('before, prior') with the attached pronoun -ka ('you', a single male). The -i ending on qabl is genitive, the case regularly taken after a preposition (such as min, 'from before') and when a noun is linked to a following possessor; here it is linked to the pronoun 'you' ('before-you').
6.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, be before; priority, what comes first

7.meaning: A verb meaning 'so/then We seized, took hold of, or gripped them.' The root conveys taking firmly; with 'fa-' it adds 'so/then,' and the seizing often implies seizing with punishment.
7.grammar: A past-tense verb with the connective fa- ('so/then') in front. The -nā ending marks 'we' as the doers; the suffix -hum is the object 'them.' So the whole says 'so we seized them.'

8.meaning: A noun meaning 'adversity, hardship, misery, or distress' — especially affliction in one's outward circumstances such as poverty or loss. The prefixed 'bi-' adds 'with/by.'
8.grammar: A noun carrying the preposition bi- ('with/by') and the definite article al- ('the'). The final -i is genitive, the case regularly required after a preposition; here it follows bi- to mean 'with the hardship.'

9.meaning: 'And hardship / affliction' — harm, injury, or suffering that touches the body or circumstances (such as illness or loss). Joined by 'and'.
9.grammar: The connector wa ('and') plus a definite feminine noun on the faʿlāʾ pattern, denoting an intense condition (grievous harm or suffering); the article's 'l' is assimilated into the following sun letter 'ḍ'. The final -i is the genitive case, taken after a preposition or as the second term of a possessive construction.

10.meaning: 'So that they may / perhaps they will.' A particle expressing hope, expectation, or purpose, fused with the pronoun 'them'; it introduces a hoped-for or intended outcome.

parts.en: perhaps / so that / in hope that

10.grammar: The particle laʿalla ('perhaps, in the hope that, so that') with the attached pronoun -hum ('them'), which serves as its subject. Laʿalla belongs to a family of particles that put a following noun or pronoun in the accusative; -hum is that fixed object form. It conveys hope or an intended purpose rather than certainty.

11.meaning: A verb meaning 'they humble themselves, plead earnestly, or beseech with lowliness.' The root conveys submissive, urgent supplication — abasing oneself and imploring.
11.grammar: A present-tense verb of the reflexive/intensive pattern (doing something to or for oneself — here lowering oneself in entreaty). The ya- prefix with -ūna ending marks 'they' (masculine plural). The final -na is the indicative marker for an ongoing or habitual action.
11.root: ض-ر-ع (ḍ-r-ʿ) — to humble oneself, plead, beseech
