10.grammar: A present-tense verb with a third-person masculine singular subject ('it/he') marked by the ya- prefix; the -u vowel signals the indicative mood (a plain statement of fact). The attached -nā is the object 'us,' giving 'it harms us.' The doubled middle letter reflects the root's geminate (doubled) consonant.

11.meaning: 'And we are turned back / we are made to turn back' — a passive verb of 'to return/turn back,' so the subject is caused to revert or be sent back rather than doing the returning by choice.

parts.en: verbal stem (passive): be turned back / be returned

11.grammar: A present-tense verb in the passive voice, joined by 'and.' The nu- prefix marks a first-person plural subject — 'we' — and its u-vowel signals the passive ('we are turned back' rather than 'we turn back'). The final -u is the indicative mood, used for plain statements. The doubled middle consonant reflects the geminate root.
11.root: ر-د-د (r-d-d) — to return, turn back, send back

12.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on, upon, over,' and by extension 'against' or 'incumbent upon.' It can mark something resting on top of, an obligation laid on someone, or being set over/above something.
12.grammar: An indeclinable preposition (its form never changes). It governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case, and conveys location 'on/upon,' or figuratively duty or opposition ('against').
12.root: — (preposition; no triliteral root)

13.meaning: 'Our heels' — the plural of 'heel' (the back of the foot) with the possessive 'our' attached. Figuratively the back part, the rear; to turn 'on one's heels' is to retreat or revert backward.
13.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun with the possessive suffix -nā ('our'). The -i vowel before the suffix is genitive, the case a noun takes when something is possessed by what follows or when it comes after a preposition — here marking 'our heels.'
13.root: ع-ق-ب (ʿ-q-b) — heel; what comes behind, follows after, the consequence

14.meaning: After; following in time or order — the point or moment subsequent to something.
14.grammar: An adverb of time functioning much like a preposition ('after'). It is fixed in the accusative form ending in -a, and is normally followed by a noun in the 'of' relationship, giving 'after (the) …'.
14.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — afterness, that which comes later; distance/remoteness

15.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
15.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

16.meaning: 'He guided us' — a past-tense verb of guiding, showing the right way, or leading aright, with the object 'us' attached. The root denotes guidance and right direction.
16.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb with a third-person masculine singular subject built into it — 'he.' The long final -ā belongs to a weak-ending root (its last letter is a vowel-like letter). The attached -nā is the object 'us,' so the whole means 'he guided us.'
16.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance, to guide, to show the right way

17.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
17.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

18.meaning: like the one who / as the one who — a comparison particle joined to a relative pronoun, introducing a single masculine person being likened to something: 'like him who…'.
18.grammar: The ka- prefix is a particle of comparison meaning 'like' or 'as'. Attached to it is the relative pronoun 'the one who / which', which is masculine singular and introduces a following descriptive clause.

19.meaning: 'It/he has lured him away / enticed him' — a verb (in the Form X istafʿala pattern) meaning to entice, tempt, or cause someone to fall headlong after vain desire, with the object 'him' attached. The root sense is falling/plunging downward, hence being drawn away by craving.

parts.en: Form X (ista-) pattern marker (prefix): to seek/deem/elicit
verbal stem: lure away after desire / cause to plunge

19.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in the Form X (istafʿala) pattern. Form X is not the causative; it typically conveys seeking something or treating/deeming a thing to have a quality. With this particular verb (istahwā) it means to lure someone away so that they follow their caprice and plunge after desire. The -t ending marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('she/it'), and the attached -hu is the object 'him' — 'it lured him away.'
19.root: ه-و-ي (h-w-y) — to fall/plunge; desire, craving, caprice

20.meaning: The satans / devils — the plural of 'shayṭān', a rebellious, malevolent being (from a root sense of being remote from good or burning with rebellion) who tempts and leads astray; with the definite article.
20.grammar: Definite ('al-') broken (internal) plural. The final '-u' ending is the nominative case, the form used when the word is the subject or doer of an action ('the devils ___').
20.root: ش-ط-ن (sh-ṭ-n) — to be far/remote (from good); rebellious, devil

21.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
21.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
21.root: — (particle)

22.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
22.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

23.meaning: 'Bewildered, confused, wandering at a loss' — describing one who is dazed and disoriented, not knowing which way to go. It is a descriptive form denoting a state of perplexed wandering.
23.grammar: A descriptive noun/adjective of the faʿlān pattern, which conveys an ongoing state or condition (here, perplexity). The final -a is the accusative case, the form often used for a circumstantial description ('… while bewildered') or the object of a verb; this pattern does not take indefinite nunation.
23.root: ح-ي-ر (ḥ-y-r) — to be perplexed, confounded, at a loss

24.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
24.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

25.meaning: 'Companions, associates, people of (something)' — the plural of a word for one who keeps company with or belongs to a thing. The phrase 'aṣḥāb of X' commonly means 'the people/folk of X' or 'those who possess/are bound to X.'
25.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun. The final -un (nunation) marks it indefinite, and the -u vowel is the nominative case — the form for a subject or a thing being named or stated to exist.
25.root: ص-ح-ب (ṣ-ḥ-b) — companionship, to accompany, keep company

26.meaning: 'They call him / invite him' — a present-tense verb of calling, summoning, or inviting, with the object 'him' attached. The root covers calling out, summoning, and inviting toward something.

parts.en: verbal stem + 'they' (masculine plural) ending: they call

26.grammar: A present-tense verb with a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'), marked by the ya- prefix together with the -ūna ending; the full -ūna form signals the indicative mood, used for plain statements. The attached -hu is the object 'him' — 'they call him.'
26.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, summon, invite

27.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
27.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

28.meaning: 'The guidance' — right direction, the showing and following of the true path; being led aright. As a verbal noun it names the very thing of guidance itself.
28.grammar: A definite verbal noun: the article al- ('the') makes it specific — 'the guidance.' The word ends in a fixed long -ā (written as a weak final letter), so its case does not change with a visible vowel; it stays the same in form regardless of grammatical position.
28.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance, to guide, to show the right way

29.meaning: 'Come!' (to more than one person, or with the sense 'come to us') — a command to approach or come forward. The base verb means to come or arrive.
29.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to someone, built on the verb 'to come.' Its initial vowel is a helping (connecting) vowel that lets the consonant cluster be pronounced. The attached -nā means 'us,' giving the sense 'come to us.'
29.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come, to arrive, to bring

30.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
30.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

31.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
31.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

32.meaning: Guidance; right direction and true leading — being shown and set upon the correct way (construct form, 'guidance of …').
32.grammar: A verbal noun ending in a long -ā from a weak-final root. Its form (without the article and ending in -ā) commonly serves as the first term of a possessive phrase ('the guidance OF …'). It names the abstract idea of being rightly guided.
32.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead rightly, show the way

33.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
33.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

34.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
34.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

35.meaning: The guidance; the right leading and true direction (with the definite article, 'the Guidance').
35.grammar: A definite verbal noun: the prefix al- means 'the'. It ends in a long -ā (from a weak-final root), an ending that does not change for case. It denotes the abstract reality of right guidance, made specific and definite by 'the'.
35.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead rightly, show the way

36.meaning: 'And we have been commanded / ordered' — a passive past-tense verb of commanding, so the subject receives the command rather than gives it. The root denotes ordering, commanding, and affairs/matters.

parts.en: verbal stem (passive past): were/have been commanded

36.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in the passive voice, joined by 'and.' The internal u-i vowelling marks the passive ('were commanded' rather than 'commanded'), and the -nā ending is the first-person plural subject — 'we' — so it means 'we were/have been commanded.'
36.root: ا-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — to command, order; affair, matter

37.meaning: 'That we submit / so that we surrender (to Allah)' — a verb (in the giving-over form) meaning to submit oneself, surrender, and commit wholly; the root sense of yielding in peace and safety. The very word 'Islam' derives from this.

parts.en: so that / in order to (purpose marker)

37.grammar: A present-tense verb in the causative/devotional (afʿala) pattern preceded by li- ('so that, in order to'), which expresses purpose. Because of this li-, the verb takes the subjunctive mood, shown by the final -a vowel (instead of -u). The nu- prefix marks the subject 'we' — 'so that we submit.'
37.root: س-ل-م (s-l-m) — soundness, peace, safety; to submit/surrender

38.meaning: 'To/for the Lord' — the preposition 'to/for' joined to rabb, a richly loaded term meaning the Lord, Master, Owner, Sustainer and Nurturer who creates, sustains, and brings to maturity all He governs.
38.grammar: The prefix 'li-' is a preposition ('to/for') that places the following noun in the genitive. Accordingly rabb takes the -i (genitive) ending, marking it as governed by the preposition and typically standing in construct with a following noun ('Lord OF …').

39.meaning: The worlds, all created realms — the totality of beings and peoples; in 'Lord of the worlds,' the whole of creation across all its kinds.
39.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the worlds') with 'al-' ('the'). The '-īna' ending marks a masculine sound plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) form — the form used after a preposition, in an 'of' linkage, or as a direct object.
39.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; a 'world' as a sign by which the Creator is known

1.meaning: A two-part connector: 'and that.' The 'wa' joins what precedes, and 'an' is the subordinating particle 'that,' which introduces a following verb-clause (often steering it into the subjunctive) — used to report or quote a command, statement, or purpose.
1.grammar: The conjunction wa- ('and') plus the particle an, a subordinator meaning 'that' which heads a clause and commonly puts a following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood (often expressing purpose, intention, or reported speech). It is a particle and does not itself take a case ending.

2.meaning: 'Establish! / set up firmly / keep up' (addressed to more than one person) — a command to make something stand upright, perform it properly, and maintain it steadfastly. The root revolves around standing and uprightness.

parts.en: verbal stem: establish / set up / keep up

2.grammar: An imperative (command) verb in the causative (afʿala) pattern, meaning to make something stand / establish it. The -ū ending directs the command to a masculine plural audience — 'you all, establish!' This pattern carries the active sense of setting something up and keeping it firmly in place.
2.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; uprightness, establishing

3.meaning: The ritual prayer (ṣalāh): the prescribed formal worship of standing, bowing, and prostrating before Allah at appointed times. As a verbal noun it also carries the underlying sense of calling upon, supplicating, and blessing.
3.grammar: A definite feminine noun. The -a ending is accusative: it generally marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon, e.g. that which is established or performed), or the object of certain particles.

4.meaning: 'And be mindful of Him / guard yourselves in awe of Him' — a command to have taqwā: a God-conscious reverence that makes one shield oneself from wrongdoing out of awe of Allah. With 'Him' attached as object. The root sense is to guard, shield, and protect oneself.

parts.en: verbal stem: be wary/mindful of, guard yourselves against (in reverent awe)

4.grammar: An imperative (command) verb of the iftaʿala pattern (which here conveys guarding oneself), addressed to a masculine plural audience by the -ū ending — 'you all.' The attached -hu is the object 'Him.' The whole conveys the command to hold protective, reverent God-consciousness toward Him.
4.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, shield, protect; hence taqwā (reverent mindfulness)

5.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
5.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

6.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
6.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

7.meaning: 'To Him' or 'toward Him' — the preposition expressing direction or endpoint ('to / toward') combined with a pronoun referring to a single masculine person, indicating motion or attention directed at him.
7.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base 'ilā shifts to 'ilay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -hi is the third-person masculine singular object of a preposition, 'him'; its -i vowel is the form the pronoun takes after the 'ay' sound.

8.meaning: 'You all will be gathered / assembled / mustered' — to be brought together into one place, as a crowd is rounded up. The root is strongly associated with the gathering of all people for the Day of Resurrection.
8.grammar: A present/future-tense passive verb ('to be gathered'). The tu-…-ūna frame marks a masculine plural addressee ('you all') as the ones acted upon, with the action ongoing or yet to come. The retained final -na indicates the verb is in its base (indicative) state.

1.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
1.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

2.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

3.meaning: 'He created' — to bring into being, to originate and shape something that did not exist before, from the root denoting creation and the fashioning of things from nothing.
3.grammar: Past tense, third-person masculine singular ('he'), completed action ('he created'). This is a form I verb of the CaCaCa pattern. The masculine singular 'he' here is the unmarked (zero-suffix) form — there is no separate person ending; the final -a is the inherent stem vowel of the base pattern, not a person or tense suffix.

4.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
4.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

5.meaning: 'and the earth' — the ground, land, or the planet earth; the world we stand upon, often paired with the heavens to mean all of creation.
5.grammar: A feminine noun, prefixed with 'and' and 'the.' The -a ending is accusative, the case typically marking the object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or a noun governed by certain particles.

6.meaning: 'With the truth / by means of what is true and right.' Combines the preposition 'with/by' and 'the truth' — that which is real, established, correct, and rightfully due, as opposed to falsehood.
6.grammar: A noun governed by the attached preposition bi- ('with/by'). The -i ending is the genitive case, which is required after a preposition; here it links 'the truth' to 'with', giving 'with the truth'.
6.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, reality, that which is established and due

7.meaning: "and (on the) day" — the conjunction "and" joined to the noun for "day," a single daytime period or, more broadly, an appointed day or time of judgment/event.
7.grammar: The wa- prefix is the conjunction "and." The -a ending on the noun is accusative; on a word for "day" this frequently marks it as an adverb of time ("on the day …"), or marks it as the object of a verb.

8.meaning: 'He says' or 'he is saying' — the act of speaking or uttering words. The imperfect tense conveys an ongoing, habitual, or present/future action.
8.grammar: Imperfect (present/future) verb, third person masculine singular. The ya- prefix marks 'he', the stem qūl carries the meaning 'say', and the final -u is the indicative ending, signalling a plain factual statement (as opposed to a subjunctive -a or jussive sukūn used after certain particles).

9.meaning: The command 'Be!' — an order to come into existence, the creative imperative by which a thing is summoned into being.
9.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to one person: 'Be!' It is the shortened command form of the verb 'to be/become,' with the bare, vowel-less ending typical of a singular order.
9.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into existence

10.meaning: 'And it is / and it comes to be' — a verb of being and coming-into-existence, expressing that something exists or takes place. It is the present form of the core 'to be / to become' verb.

parts.en: and so / then (connector showing result or sequence)
verbal stem: be / become / come to exist

10.grammar: A present-tense verb of 'being,' joined by fa- ('and so, then') which often marks a result or what follows next. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('it/he'), and the final -u is the indicative mood, used for plain statements — 'and so it is / comes to be.'
10.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to become, to come into existence

11.meaning: 'His word / His saying / His speech' — that which is said or uttered; a statement, decree, or speech, with the possessive 'His' attached.
11.grammar: A verbal noun ('a saying, an utterance') carrying the possessive suffix -hu ('His'). The -u vowel before the suffix is the nominative case, the form a noun takes when it is the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified — 'His word.'
11.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak; a saying, word

12.meaning: 'The truth / the reality; what is right, real, and rightfully due.' A weighty noun meaning that which is firmly true and real, as opposed to falsehood; it also carries the senses of a rightful claim, a duty owed, and justice. With the article it denotes 'the Truth' in a definite, absolute sense.
12.grammar: A definite noun: the prefix al- ('the') plus the stem. The final -u ending is the nominative case, typically used for the subject of a sentence or for a word identifying what something is (as in 'X is the truth').
12.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, reality, rightness; that which is established and rightfully due

13.meaning: 'And for Him / and to Him belongs' — the preposition 'for/to' expressing belonging or possession, joined with the pronoun 'Him.' It conveys that something belongs or is due to Him.
13.grammar: A small phrase: the connector 'and' plus the preposition la- ('for, to, belonging to') with the attached pronoun -hu ('Him'). The construction 'la- + pronoun' expresses possession or entitlement — 'and to Him belongs …' / 'and for Him is …'

14.meaning: 'The kingship / sovereignty / dominion' — al-mulk is rule and royal authority itself, the power and right to govern.
14.grammar: A definite noun with the article al- ('the'). The -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject of a sentence (the thing that 'is' or does something).

15.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
15.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
15.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

16.meaning: It is blown / breathed into — a passive verb meaning that air or breath is forced into something, especially the blowing of a horn or trumpet to produce a sound.
16.grammar: Present-tense passive verb, 3rd person masculine singular: 'it is blown.' The yu- prefix with the inner vowel pattern marks the passive (the action is done to the subject, not by it). The final -u is the indicative ending, used for a simple statement of fact rather than a command or negation.
16.root: ن-ف-خ (n-f-kh) — to blow, breathe, or puff air into

17.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
17.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

18.meaning: The horn or trumpet — the great horn that is sounded; also the natural sense of a horn-shaped instrument blown to summon or signal.
18.grammar: Definite noun ('the trumpet'). The al- prefix means 'the.' The final -i is the genitive case ending, which typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship.
18.root: ص-و-ر (ṣ-w-r) — form, shape; here a horn or trumpet

19.meaning: Knower — the active participle 'one who knows,' describing someone characterized by knowledge. Applied to Allah it conveys the One who fully knows all things.
19.grammar: Active participle (a noun describing the doer), masculine singular: 'a knower / knowing one.' The long vowel after the first letter is the participle pattern. The final -u is the nominative case ending, typically marking the subject of a sentence or a noun standing on its own.
19.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; knowledge

20.meaning: The unseen / the hidden realm — that which lies beyond perception and human knowledge: the realm and matters concealed from the senses, known fully only to Allah.
20.grammar: A masculine noun with the definite article al-. The final -i is the genitive ending, which marks the word as following a preposition or as the second term in a possessive link ('… of the unseen').
20.root: غ-ي-ب (gh-y-b) — to be absent, hidden, beyond perception

21.meaning: And the witnessed / the seen — joined by 'and,' this is the realm of what is visible, present, and openly perceived; the opposite of the hidden or unseen. (The word also carries the senses of testimony and witnessing.)
21.grammar: 'and' + definite feminine noun. The wa- prefix means 'and,' al- means 'the.' The final -i is the genitive case ending, typically appearing after a preposition or in an 'of' linkage with a preceding noun.
21.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — to witness, be present, testify

22.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
22.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

23.meaning: The All-Wise — one possessing perfect wisdom, who puts everything in its right place and acts with flawless judgment; can also carry the sense of one who decrees and decides soundly.
23.grammar: A definite noun/adjective in an intensive pattern (faʿīl) stressing the depth and constancy of the quality. The prefix 'al-' means 'the'; the final -u (ḍamma) marks the nominative case, which typically signals the subject of a sentence or a describing predicate.
23.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge wisely, to be wise

24.meaning: 'The All-Aware', 'the Well-Acquainted' — the one possessing thorough, intimate knowledge of the inner reality of things, fully informed of what is hidden as well as what is open.
24.grammar: A definite intensive adjective (a 'one who is deeply X' pattern: thoroughly aware). The -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject of a sentence or a word standing as the main topic/predicate.
24.root: خ-ب-ر (kh-b-r) — knowledge, inner acquaintance, being informed

1.meaning: 'And when / and at the time when' — the connective 'and' joined to a word that points to a past moment or circumstance ('when'), introducing the recollection of an event or situation.
1.grammar: A connective particle plus a time-word. The wa- prefix means 'and'. 'Idh' is an invariable adverb pointing to a definite time in the past ('when, at the moment that'); it has no case ending and typically introduces a clause recalling a past event.

2.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
2.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

3.meaning: A proper noun: Abraham (Ibrāhīm), the patriarch and prophet, exalted as an upright monotheist and 'friend of Allah'.
3.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin. The -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence. Because it is a foreign proper name, it is 'diptote' — it does not take the indefinite 'n' sound (tanwīn) that ordinary nouns would.

4.meaning: To / for his father — the noun 'father' attached to a possessive 'his' and preceded by the preposition 'to/for.'
4.grammar: Preposition + noun + possessive pronoun. The li- prefix means 'to' or 'for.' 'Father' is one of a small group of nouns that show case with a long vowel: the -ī here reflects the genitive required after the preposition. The attached -hi means 'his' (its 'i' vowel harmonizes after the preceding -ī).

5.meaning: Āzar — a proper name (a personal name).
5.grammar: A proper name. It is a 'diptote' — a name that takes the -a ending in place of the usual genitive -i (such names do not take the final 'n' sound and use -a for both accusative and genitive). It has no case-marking 'the' and no triliteral verbal root.

6.meaning: Do you take / adopt for yourself? — a questioning verb built on 'to take and keep something as one's own,' i.e. to adopt or set up something for oneself, voiced as a question.
6.grammar: Question particle + present-tense verb, 2nd person masculine singular: 'do you take (for yourself)?' The a- prefix turns the statement into a yes/no question. The ta- prefix marks 'you' (masculine singular). The 'for oneself' sense belongs to this particular verb's meaning rather than being a feature of the verb form. The final -u is the indicative ending, marking a plain (here, questioning) statement.

7.meaning: Idols — carved images or statues set up to be worshipped.
7.grammar: Plural noun, indefinite ('idols'). The pattern is a broken (irregular) plural of the singular 'idol.' The final -an is the accusative indefinite ending (the 'tanwīn' adds the -n sound for 'a/some'), typically marking the object of a verb.

8.meaning: A noun meaning 'gods / deities' — the plural of ilāh, objects taken as worthy of worship besides Allah. It denotes claimed divine beings in general.
8.grammar: A plural noun, indefinite ('gods'), in the accusative case marked by tanwīn. The word ends in a tā' marbūṭah, which is normally silent in pause but is pronounced as -t- when a case-vowel and tanwīn follow it; combined with the accusative tanwīn this is sounded as -tan, so the full ending is ālihatan (not a bare -an). The accusative typically marks a noun as the object of a verb or the focus of certain particles.
8.root: ا-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, that which is worshipped

9.meaning: 'Truly I' or 'indeed I' — the emphatic affirming particle inna ('truly, indeed, certainly'), which strengthens and confirms a statement, joined to the pronoun 'I'.
9.grammar: An emphasizing particle with an attached pronoun. 'Inna' is a particle of emphasis and affirmation that introduces a statement and lends it certainty ('it is certainly the case that…'). The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I / me') in the object form this particle requires. Together: 'Indeed I…'.

10.meaning: He showed you / caused you to see — to make someone perceive or behold something, whether with the eye or the understanding; addressed to a single 'you'.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he showed'), of the 'form IV' causative pattern ('to make someone see'). The attached -ka is the object pronoun 'you' (a single male). So the form means 'he caused you to see / he showed you', presented as completed.

11.meaning: And your people — the noun 'people / folk' (a community or kinsfolk) joined by 'and' and attached to the possessive 'your.'
11.grammar: 'and' + noun + possessive pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and.' The -a ending on the noun is the accusative case, which typically marks the object of a verb. The attached -ka means 'your' addressed to a single male.
11.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, arise; a people who stand together

12.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
12.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
12.root: — (particle)

13.meaning: Means 'straying / error / being lost' — wandering off the right path, the opposite of guidance, whether literally losing one's way or going astray in belief and conduct.
13.grammar: An abstract noun: 'straying / error.' The -in ending is the genitive with 'tanwīn' (the -n marking it indefinite) — the case a noun takes after a preposition or in a possessive link, e.g. 'in an error.' The long -ā- belongs to this noun-pattern.
13.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, go astray, lose the way

14.meaning: Means 'clear / plain / making manifest' — something that is evident in itself and also makes other things plain, leaving no ambiguity.
14.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' noun) from a pattern that often carries the sense 'making clear' as well as 'being clear.' The -in ending is the genitive with 'tanwīn' (the -n marking it indefinite), the form taken after a preposition or when describing a genitive noun — i.e. it agrees with a preceding indefinite noun in the genitive ('a clear …').
14.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — to be clear, distinct; to make evident

1.meaning: 'And likewise / and in the same way / and thus' — a connective phrase pointing back to a manner just mentioned and saying 'in that very way…'. Built from 'and' + 'like' + 'that'.
1.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'; the prefix ka- means 'like/as'; 'dhālika' is the demonstrative 'that' (pointing to something distant or already mentioned). Because ka- acts like a preposition, the word after it stands in the genitive, though the demonstrative 'dhālika' keeps a fixed form and shows no visible case change. The whole means 'and just like that / and thus'.

2.meaning: We show / cause to see — a verb meaning to make someone behold or perceive something, to display it to their sight or understanding. (Built on the verb 'to see' in its causative form: 'we make [someone] see.')
2.grammar: Present-tense causative verb, 1st person plural: 'we show / we make see.' The nu- prefix means 'we' and signals the causative form (making someone do the action of seeing). The verb ends in a long -ī because its final root letter is a weak (vowel-like) letter; this form expresses an ongoing or general action.
2.root: ر-ا-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see, perceive; (causative) to show

3.meaning: The proper name Ibrāhīm (the Prophet Abraham).
3.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin. The -a ending here serves for both accusative and genitive because the name is a diptote — a class of nouns that refuses tanwīn (no -an/-in) and uses a single -a for these two cases. So this one -a covers 'Ibrāhīm' whether as an object or as 'of Ibrāhīm'.

4.meaning: Dominion / sovereign kingdom — the absolute realm and rule over something; vast ownership and command. The form intensifies the plain word for 'kingdom,' conveying grand and total dominion.
4.grammar: An intensive noun built from 'kingship,' conveying grand and total dominion. The final -a is the accusative case ending, which typically marks the object of a verb.
4.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — to own, rule; kingship, dominion

5.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
5.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

6.meaning: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
6.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.

7.meaning: And so that he may be — 'and' plus a purpose particle ('so that') plus the verb 'to be,' expressing the intended result that someone come to be in a certain state.
7.grammar: 'and' + purpose particle + present-tense verb of being, 3rd person masculine singular: 'and so that he may be.' The wa- means 'and'; the li- means 'so that / in order that' and puts the verb into the subjunctive. The ya- prefix marks 'he.' The final -a is the subjunctive ending used after 'so that,' expressing purpose or an intended outcome rather than a completed fact.
7.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, exist, come to pass

8.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
8.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

9.meaning: Those who are certain — people of firm, sure conviction; ones who attain settled certainty and inner assurance, free of doubt.
9.grammar: Definite active participle, masculine plural ('the ones who are certain'). The al- means 'the.' The base is the participle of a causative verb meaning 'to attain certainty.' The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (oblique) case, typically used for the object of a verb or after a preposition.

1.meaning: A connector meaning 'then, when' — it joins to what came before ('then/so') and sets up a 'when…' clause whose outcome follows. It frames a moment: 'and then, at the point when…'.
1.grammar: A compound of the connecting particle fa- ('then/so', linking to the preceding statement) and lammā, a particle meaning 'when' that introduces a past circumstance and leads the listener to expect a following result clause.

2.meaning: It covered over / grew dark over — a verb meaning that something concealed or enveloped another in darkness, the way nightfall wraps and hides things from view.
2.grammar: Past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular: 'it covered / grew dark over.' The doubled middle letter is part of the root. The final -a marks a completed action done by 'he' or 'it.'
2.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal, veil in darkness

3.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
3.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

4.meaning: The night — the period of darkness from sunset to dawn.
4.grammar: Definite noun ('the night'). The al- means 'the' (its 'l' blends into the following letter, doubling it). The final -u is the nominative case ending, typically marking the subject of a sentence.

5.meaning: He saw / perceived — a past-tense verb of seeing, beholding with the eye, and by extension realizing or perceiving.
5.grammar: Past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular: 'he saw.' The action is completed and done by 'he.' Because the final root letter is weak (vowel-like), the ending appears as a long -ā rather than the usual short vowel.

6.meaning: A star — a luminous heavenly body; also more broadly a planet or bright point of light in the sky.
6.grammar: Noun, indefinite ('a star'). The final -an is the accusative indefinite ending (the 'tanwīn' adds the -n sound for 'a'), typically marking the object of a verb.

7.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
7.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

8.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
8.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

9.meaning: 'My Lord' — the Master, Sustainer and Nurturer, claimed in close personal relation by the speaker.
9.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord') with the attached pronoun -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' ending merges with the case-vowel of the noun, so a single long -ī is heard. The sense is 'the Lord who is mine'.
9.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord/master, to nurture and sustain

10.meaning: A connector meaning 'then, when' — it joins to what came before ('then/so') and sets up a 'when…' clause whose outcome follows. It frames a moment: 'and then, at the point when…'.
10.grammar: A compound of the connecting particle fa- ('then/so', linking to the preceding statement) and lammā, a particle meaning 'when' that introduces a past circumstance and leads the listener to expect a following result clause.

11.meaning: It set / disappeared — a past-tense verb describing a star or celestial body sinking below the horizon and vanishing from sight.
11.grammar: Past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular: 'it set / disappeared.' The final -a marks a completed action done by 'he' or 'it.'
11.root: ا-ف-ل (ʾ-f-l) — to set, sink down, vanish (of a heavenly body)

12.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
12.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.
12.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, uttering

13.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
13.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

14.meaning: I love / like — a present-tense verb of loving, holding dear, or being fond of something.
14.grammar: Present-tense verb, 1st person singular: 'I love.' The u- prefix marks 'I' (and signals the verb's causative/transitive form). The doubled final letter belongs to the root. The final -u is the indicative ending, marking a plain statement of fact.
14.root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b) — to love, hold dear, be fond of

15.meaning: Those that set / vanish — things that sink below the horizon and disappear, such as stars and other celestial bodies that fade from sight.
15.grammar: Definite active participle, masculine plural ('the ones that set'). The al- means 'the.' The base is the participle 'one that sets/vanishes.' The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (oblique) case, typically used for the object of a verb or after a preposition.
15.root: ا-ف-ل (ʾ-f-l) — to set, sink down, vanish

1.meaning: A connector meaning 'then, when' — it joins to what came before ('then/so') and sets up a 'when…' clause whose outcome follows. It frames a moment: 'and then, at the point when…'.
1.grammar: A compound of the connecting particle fa- ('then/so', linking to the preceding statement) and lammā, a particle meaning 'when' that introduces a past circumstance and leads the listener to expect a following result clause.

2.meaning: He saw / perceived — a past-tense verb of seeing, beholding with the eye, and by extension realizing or perceiving.
2.grammar: Past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular: 'he saw.' The action is completed and done by 'he.' Because the final root letter is weak (vowel-like), the ending resolves to a long -ā rather than a short vowel.

3.meaning: The moon — the moon that lights the night sky.
3.grammar: Definite noun ('the moon'). The al- means 'the.' The final -a is the accusative case ending, typically marking the object of a verb.

4.meaning: Rising / emerging in brightness — an active participle describing a heavenly body that is breaking forth and coming up shining over the horizon.
4.grammar: Active participle (a describing noun), masculine singular and indefinite ('rising'). The long vowel after the first letter is the participle pattern. The final -an is the accusative indefinite ending (the 'tanwīn' adds the -n sound), a form often used to describe the state or condition of something.
4.root: ب-ز-غ (b-z-gh) — to break forth, rise and shine (of a celestial body)

5.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
5.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

6.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
6.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

7.meaning: 'My Lord' — the Master, Sustainer and Nurturer, claimed in close personal relation by the speaker.
7.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord') with the attached pronoun -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' ending merges with the case-vowel of the noun, so a single long -ī is heard. The sense is 'the Lord who is mine'.
7.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord/master, to nurture and sustain

8.meaning: A connector meaning 'then, when' — it joins to what came before ('then/so') and sets up a 'when…' clause whose outcome follows. It frames a moment: 'and then, at the point when…'.
8.grammar: A compound of the connecting particle fa- ('then/so', linking to the preceding statement) and lammā, a particle meaning 'when' that introduces a past circumstance and leads the listener to expect a following result clause.

9.meaning: It set / disappeared — a past-tense verb describing a star or celestial body sinking below the horizon and vanishing from sight.
9.grammar: Past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular: 'it set / disappeared.' The final -a marks a completed action done by 'he' or 'it.'
9.root: ا-ف-ل (ʾ-f-l) — to set, sink down, vanish (of a heavenly body)

10.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
10.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

11.meaning: An emphatic conditional opener combining an oath-like emphasis with 'if' — roughly 'most certainly, if (such-and-such happens)…', strongly stressing the condition and the response that follows.
11.grammar: Two particles fused together: an emphatic la- that signals a coming oath or strong assertion, plus in ('if') introducing a condition. Together they set up an emphatic 'if… then surely…' construction. Neither has a case ending; particles do not inflect.
11.root: — (particles)

12.meaning: The particle 'lam', a negating word used to push a verb into the past: it means 'did not' / 'has not'. Though it sits before a present-tense verb form, it negates the action as something that did not happen.
12.grammar: 'lam' is a negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb but gives it past meaning ('did not …'). It also puts that verb into the shortened (jussive) form. 'lam' itself carries no ending.

13.meaning: He guides me / may He guide me — the verb 'to guide, to lead aright on the path' with an attached object 'me,' i.e. to be shown the right way.
13.grammar: Present-tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular, with an attached object pronoun: 'he guides me.' The ya- prefix marks 'he.' The verb's final weak letter is dropped before the ending (a shortened form often used in requests or after certain particles). The -nī ending is the object 'me' (the inserted 'n' protects the verb's ending before the pronoun).
13.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead rightly, show the way

14.meaning: 'My Lord' — the Master, Sustainer and Nurturer, claimed in close personal relation by the speaker.
14.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord') with the attached pronoun -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' ending merges with the case-vowel of the noun, so a single long -ī is heard. The sense is 'the Lord who is mine'.
14.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord/master, to nurture and sustain

15.meaning: An emphatic first-person declaration: 'I will most certainly be / become.' It joins the verb 'to be/become' with a heavy emphasis particle, expressing a vowed or solemnly affirmed future state of the speaker.
15.grammar: Built on the verb 'to be/become' in the imperfect, with the a- prefix marking the first person singular ('I'). The opening la- (emphatic laam) together with the doubled -nna (the 'heavy' emphatic nuun) form the emphatic-future construction, giving the force of a solemn oath or firm resolve ('I shall assuredly be'). This construction carries a future-assertive sense, not a simple present; the -nna ending also overrides the normal mood vowel, fixing the verb in this emphatic shape.
15.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, coming to be, existing

16.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
16.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

17.meaning: 'The people / the folk' — a collective noun for a community, nation, or group of people regarded as a body. Often it carries the nuance of one's own people or a particular group sharing a trait.
17.grammar: A collective noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final '-i' is the genitive ending, which typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of …' relationship.
17.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand/rise; a people, community

18.meaning: Those who have gone astray — people who have strayed from the right path, lost their way in error, or wandered from the truth. It describes a group characterised by being misguided.
18.grammar: A definite active participle in the masculine plural, meaning 'those who stray / the astray ones'. The -īna ending marks the masculine sound plural in the accusative or genitive case, i.e. it functions as an object or follows a preposition (the corresponding subject form would be -ūna). The al- means 'the'.
18.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to go astray, lose the way, err

1.meaning: A connector meaning 'then, when' — it joins to what came before ('then/so') and sets up a 'when…' clause whose outcome follows. It frames a moment: 'and then, at the point when…'.
1.grammar: A compound of the connecting particle fa- ('then/so', linking to the preceding statement) and lammā, a particle meaning 'when' that introduces a past circumstance and leads the listener to expect a following result clause.

2.grammar: Past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular: 'he saw.' The action is completed and done by 'he.' Because the final root letter is weak (vowel-like), the ending appears as a long -ā rather than the usual short vowel.

3.meaning: The sun — the blazing daytime luminary.
3.grammar: A feminine noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -a is the accusative ending, which generally marks the noun as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or the subject of certain particles.

4.meaning: Rising into view, breaking forth and shining — said of a heavenly body as it ascends and beams brightly.
4.grammar: An active participle (one doing the action) in its unitary feminine form بَازِغَة ('one rising/shining forth'); the split is only for display, since the tā marbūṭa belongs to the participle itself and supplies the feminine marker. The final -an is the accusative with indefinite 'nunation,' which generally marks it as an object or, often, a descriptive state ('as something rising').
4.root: ب-ز-غ (b-z-gh) — to break forth, rise and shine (of a luminary)

5.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
5.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

6.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
6.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

8.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

9.meaning: Greater, bigger, more grave — the comparative/superlative 'more great' or 'greatest'.
9.grammar: An elative on the afʿal pattern, expressing 'more/most great'. Such forms are diptotes, so they take -u (without nunation) in the nominative; the -u marks it as a subject or predicate ('is greater').

10.meaning: A connector meaning 'then, when' — it joins to what came before ('then/so') and sets up a 'when…' clause whose outcome follows. It frames a moment: 'and then, at the point when…'.
10.grammar: A compound of the connecting particle fa- ('then/so', linking to the preceding statement) and lammā, a particle meaning 'when' that introduces a past circumstance and leads the listener to expect a following result clause.

11.meaning: It set / went down and disappeared — said of a celestial body sinking below the horizon and vanishing from sight.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb. The base 'afala' means 'it set.' The added -t marks a feminine singular subject ('she/it'), so the whole means 'she/it set.' Past tense presents the action as completed.
11.root: أ-ف-ل (ʾ-f-l) — to set, sink, disappear (of stars or sun)

12.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
12.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.
12.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, uttering

13.meaning: 'O my people!' — a vocative call: 'people' (one's own community/folk) addressed directly, with 'my' attached. A speaker uses it to summon and appeal to his own community.
13.grammar: The particle yā- is the vocative ('O …'), used to call or address someone. The final -i here is the remnant of the possessive 'my' (the fuller -ī), commonly shortened to -i in direct address, so the whole means 'O my people!' The case ending proper is suppressed because the noun is being called, not used as subject or object.
13.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise; a people who stand together

14.meaning: 'Truly I' or 'indeed I' — the emphatic affirming particle inna ('truly, indeed, certainly'), which strengthens and confirms a statement, joined to the pronoun 'I'.
14.grammar: An emphasizing particle with an attached pronoun. 'Inna' is a particle of emphasis and affirmation that introduces a statement and lends it certainty ('it is certainly the case that…'). The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I / me') in the object form this particle requires. Together: 'Indeed I…'.

15.meaning: An adjective/noun meaning 'free of / quit of / disassociated from' — innocent of and having nothing to do with something, washing one's hands of it. It describes a person clear and detached from a thing, especially a wrong.
15.grammar: A descriptive noun, indefinite, with the nominative -un ending (tanwīn). The nominative typically marks the subject of a sentence or a predicate ('[someone] is free/quit'); the -un tanwīn shows it is indefinite. It is usually completed by 'of/from' something.
15.root: ب-ر-ء (b-r-ʾ) — to be free, clear, quit of; innocence, disassociation

16.meaning: A fused word combining the preposition 'min' ('from', 'of', 'about') with the relative/indefinite 'mā' ('what', 'that which'). Together: 'from what', 'about that which', 'of what'.
16.grammar: The preposition 'min' and the word 'mā' merge in pronunciation (the 'n' assimilating into the 'm'). 'min' governs a genitive, and 'mā' here functions as a relative pronoun introducing a clause ('that which …'). These are indeclinable particles without case endings.

17.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (plural) associate as partners' — to set up others alongside Allah in worship or divinity, i.e. to commit shirk by ascribing partners to Him. It denotes the act of treating something as Allah's equal or associate.
17.grammar: Present-tense verb (form IV), second-person masculine plural. The tu- prefix (with the form-IV pattern 'to make a partner') marks 'you', and the -ūna ending marks masculine plural indicative ('you all associate'). It implies an object: associating others with Allah.
17.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, partner; to ascribe partners (to Allah)

1.meaning: 'Truly I' or 'indeed I' — the emphatic affirming particle inna ('truly, indeed, certainly'), which strengthens and confirms a statement, joined to the pronoun 'I'.
1.grammar: An emphasizing particle with an attached pronoun. 'Inna' is a particle of emphasis and affirmation that introduces a statement and lends it certainty ('it is certainly the case that…'). The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I / me') in the object form this particle requires. Together: 'Indeed I…'.

2.meaning: I have turned / directed (something, especially the face or self) toward a goal — to set one's orientation firmly in a chosen direction.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb in an intensive pattern (doubled middle root letter), conveying deliberate, thorough directing or turning. The -tu ending marks the first person singular ('I') as the doer of a completed action.
2.root: و-ج-ه (w-j-h) — face, direction, to turn toward

3.meaning: My face / myself: literally the face — the front of the head — and by extension one's whole self, one's very being or the direction of one's attention and devotion; here bound to 'my'.
3.grammar: A noun with the attached possessive pronoun -ya ('my'). The -i vowel before it is the genitive case ending, the case that typically appears after prepositions or when one noun is possessed by/linked to another ('… of …'); the possessor 'my' is what governs it here.

4.meaning: 'to / for the One who…' — a preposition fused with a relative pronoun, introducing a clause that identifies someone by what they do ('the one who…').
4.grammar: The preposition li- ('to/for') joined to the masculine singular relative pronoun 'alladhī ('the one who/which'). A relative pronoun links to a following clause that describes its referent. Being a fixed particle, it does not change its ending for case.

5.meaning: He originated / brought into being from nothing — to create by splitting open and fashioning anew, an act of fresh, foundational creation.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb, third person masculine singular ('he…'), presenting the act as completed. With no added subject suffix, the doer is simply 'he.'
5.root: ف-ط-ر (f-ṭ-r) — to split open, originate, bring into being

6.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
6.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

7.meaning: 'and the earth' — the ground, land, or the planet earth; the world we stand upon, often paired with the heavens to mean all of creation.
7.grammar: A feminine noun, prefixed with 'and' and 'the.' The -a ending is accusative, the case typically marking the object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or a noun governed by certain particles.

8.meaning: 'Upright in faith, naturally inclined to pure monotheism' — one who turns away from all false worship toward sincere devotion to the one Allah; a term for steadfast, primordial monotheistic faith.
8.grammar: A singular indefinite noun/adjective (an intensive 'faʿīl' pattern). The -an ending is accusative plus nunation: it marks indefiniteness ('a/an') and the accusative case, the form used for an object, a descriptive term, or a circumstantial state ('… as one upright in faith').
8.root: ح-ن-ف (ḥ-n-f) — to incline away (from error) toward pure monotheism

9.meaning: A compound: the connective 'and' joined to the particle mā. The particle mā is highly versatile — it can mean 'what / whatever' (introducing an indirect question or a relative clause, 'that which'), or it can function as a negation ('not'). Context determines which sense applies; the core idea is an open, unspecified 'what(ever)' or a flat denial.
9.grammar: Two indeclinable particles, so there is no case ending to mark. The wa- prefix is the simple connective 'and', linking what follows to what precedes. Mā itself does not change form: it serves either as an interrogative/relative ('what, that which') or as a negating word ('not').

10.meaning: I — the standalone pronoun used to declare or emphasize the speaker himself as the one in view.
10.grammar: A detached first-person singular pronoun ("I"). Being an independent pronoun, it has a fixed form with no case ending; it is used to state or stress who the subject is.

11.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
11.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

12.meaning: Those who associate partners with Allah — idolaters / polytheists who set up others alongside the one God in worship or devotion.
12.grammar: An active participle used as a noun, with 'the', in the masculine sound plural. The -īna ending marks the plural in the genitive/accusative case — the form used after a preposition or as the object of a verb.
12.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, associate, partner

1.meaning: 'and he disputed/argued with him' — to engage someone in contention, each side pressing its case against the other, with an attached object 'him.'
1.grammar: A past-tense verb in the mutual/reciprocal pattern, meaning to dispute back-and-forth with someone. Prefixed wa- means 'and.' The verb is third person masculine singular ('he…'), and the suffix -hu ('him') is its object — the person argued with.
1.root: ح-ج-ج (ḥ-j-j) — to argue, present a proof, dispute

2.meaning: 'his people / his folk' — the community, kinsfolk, or nation belonging to him.
2.grammar: A noun meaning 'people/community' with the attached pronoun -hu ('his') marking possession. The -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the noun as the subject — the one performing the action.

3.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
3.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

4.meaning: 'Do you (all) dispute with me?' — a question challenging a group who are pressing an argument against the speaker.
4.grammar: Opens with the question marker a- ('do…?'). The verb is in the mutual-argument pattern, present tense, second person masculine plural ('you all dispute') shown by the tu-…-ū frame. The doubled -nn- is an emphatic/connective element binding the verb to the object pronoun -ī ('me').
4.root: ح-ج-ج (ḥ-j-j) — to argue, present a proof, dispute

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
5.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

6.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
6.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

7.meaning: 'And indeed / while already' — the word 'wa' ('and, while') joined to 'qad', a particle that, before a past-tense verb, stresses that the action has certainly and already happened.
7.grammar: A connective 'wa' ('and', or circumstantial 'while') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' emphasizes completion and certainty ('has indeed already…'); with a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes' or 'may'.

8.meaning: 'He has guided me' — to have shown the right way and led correctly, with the speaker as the one guided.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb, third person masculine singular ('he guided'). The suffix -ni is actually two morphemes: the 'protective nuun' (nuun al-wiqaaya), which shields the verb-ending from the object pronoun, plus the first-person object 'me' (the yaa, here dropped in pronunciation). Together they give 'he guided me.'
8.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead rightly, show the way

9.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
9.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

10.meaning: I fear, I am afraid of, I stand in awe/dread — expressing the speaker's own fear, whether dread of harm or reverent awe.
10.grammar: A present-tense verb. The a- prefix marks the doer as 'I'. The final -u ending marks the ordinary (indicative) mood, used for a plain statement of an ongoing or habitual state ('I fear / I am fearing').

11.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
11.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

12.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (plural) associate as partners' — to set up others alongside Allah in worship or divinity, i.e. to commit shirk by ascribing partners to Him. It denotes the act of treating something as Allah's equal or associate.
12.grammar: Present-tense verb (form IV), second-person masculine plural. The tu- prefix (with the form-IV pattern 'to make a partner') marks 'you', and the -ūna ending marks masculine plural indicative ('you all associate'). It implies an object: associating others with Allah.
12.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, partner; to ascribe partners (to Allah)

13.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
13.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

14.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
14.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

15.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
15.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

16.meaning: '(that) he wills / wishes' — to will, intend, or so desire that a thing comes about.
16.grammar: A present-tense verb, third person masculine singular ('he wills'). The final -a is the subjunctive ending, which typically appears after particles meaning 'that/so that/until,' giving the sense 'that he should will.'

17.meaning: 'My Lord' — the Master, Sustainer and Nurturer, claimed in close personal relation by the speaker.
17.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord') with the attached pronoun -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' ending merges with the case-vowel of the noun, so a single long -ī is heard. The sense is 'the Lord who is mine'.
17.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord/master, to nurture and sustain

18.meaning: A thing; something or anything. With a negation it commonly amounts to 'nothing at all.'
18.grammar: A singular masculine noun, indefinite ('a thing'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative, often used here as an object or an adverbial 'in any respect / at all.'

19.meaning: '(it) extended / encompassed / was vast enough for' — to be wide, spacious, or ample; to take in or embrace something fully within one's capacity. It conveys all-embracing breadth.
19.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it encompassed'). The final -a marks the completed action of a single masculine subject ('he/it did encompass / extend over').
19.root: و-س-ع (w-s-ʿ) — to be wide, spacious, to encompass

20.meaning: 'My Lord' — the Master, Sustainer and Nurturer, claimed in close personal relation by the speaker.
20.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord') with the attached pronoun -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' ending merges with the case-vowel of the noun, so a single long -ī is heard. The sense is 'the Lord who is mine'.
20.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord/master, to nurture and sustain

21.meaning: All, every, the whole of — totality. When followed by a singular it means 'every (one)'; when followed by a definite plural or whole it means 'all of.'
21.grammar: A noun of totality, almost always joined to a following noun in the genitive ('every … / all of …'). The final -a is the accusative case, the form used when the word functions as an object of a verb.
21.root: ك-ل-ل (k-l-l) — wholeness, totality

22.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
22.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
22.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

23.meaning: Knowledge — that which is known; firm, certain awareness and understanding.
23.grammar: An abstract noun, 'knowledge.' The final -an is the accusative with indefinite 'nunation,' commonly marking the noun as a direct object, or as a specification ('in respect of knowledge').

24.meaning: 'Then will you not…?' — a rhetorical opener combining 'then/so,' a question, and a negation, used to prompt reflection ('do you then not…?').
24.grammar: A cluster of particles, not a noun or verb: the question marker 'a-' ('?'), the connector 'fa-' ('then/so'), and the negator 'lā' ('not'). Together they form a rhetorical question expecting agreement — 'will you then not…?' It has no case or tense ending of its own.

25.meaning: 'you (all) take heed / call to mind' — to reflect, remember, and let a reminder sink in so as to be admonished by it.
25.grammar: A present-tense verb of the reflective (Form V) pattern, 'to keep reminding oneself, take heed.' Note the two ta- letters: the first ta- is the present-tense second-person prefix (the person marker, 'you'), while the second ta- belongs to the verb's pattern itself. The plural-and-indicative suffix -ūna (here split as -ū…-na) marks the masculine plural ('you all') in the plain present/future ('you take heed').
25.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, mention, call to mind

1.meaning: A phrase: 'and how…' — 'how?' is a question word asking about the manner, way, or state of something; with the connector 'and' prefixed.
1.grammar: An interrogative ('how?') asking about manner or condition, preceded by the connector 'wa' ('and'). This question word is invariable — it does not change for case — and it always carries a fixed '-a' ending. It can express genuine inquiry or astonishment.

2.meaning: I fear, I am afraid of, I stand in awe/dread — expressing the speaker's own fear, whether dread of harm or reverent awe.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb. The a- prefix marks the doer as 'I'. The final -u ending marks the ordinary (indicative) mood, used for a plain statement of an ongoing or habitual state ('I fear / I am fearing').

3.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
3.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

4.meaning: 'you (all) associated / set up partners' — to ascribe a partner or co-equal to Allah, i.e. to commit polytheism.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb in a causative pattern ('to make something a partner/sharer'). The suffix -tum marks the second person masculine plural ('you all') as the doers of a completed action.
4.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, associate, take a partner

5.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
