5.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

6.meaning: You fear, dread, or apprehend — to be afraid of something or to anticipate a feared outcome.
6.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, second person masculine plural ('you all'). The ta- prefix marks 'you', and the -ūna ending marks a plural subject in the indicative mood, typically describing an ongoing or general action ('you (all) fear').

7.meaning: 'That you …' — a particle anna ('that, indeed') fused with the pronoun 'you,' used to introduce an emphasized statement as the content of a thought, knowledge, or speech ('… that you …').
7.grammar: The particle anna introduces a subordinate noun-clause ('that …') and adds emphasis; it puts the following subject in the accusative. The attached pronoun -kum ('you,' masculine plural) is the accusative subject of that clause. Together: 'that you (all) …'

8.meaning: 'you (all) associated / set up partners' — to ascribe a partner or co-equal to Allah, i.e. to commit polytheism.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb in a causative pattern ('to make something a partner/sharer'). The suffix -tum marks the second person masculine plural ('you all') as the doers of a completed action.
8.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, associate, take a partner

9.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
9.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
9.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

10.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
10.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

11.meaning: A negating particle, 'not', used specifically to deny that an action happened in the past, even though it attaches to a present-tense verb form. It turns 'you do X' into 'you did not do X'.

parts.en: did not (negation of a completed act)

11.grammar: An indeclinable particle that governs the verb after it, putting that verb into the jussive (clipped) mood and giving it past-time meaning. In short: lam + a present-form verb = 'did not [verb]'.
11.root: — (particle; no triliteral root)

12.meaning: He sends down — to send something down from a higher place to a lower one, gradually or in stages. The intensive form suggests a sending-down by degrees.
12.grammar: A present-tense verb in the intensive 'fa''ala' pattern (sending down by degrees), third-person masculine singular ('he'). The vowelless final -l marks the jussive mood — the form used after certain particles (such as those for negation of the past or conditions), giving e.g. 'he did not send down' or 'let him send down'.
12.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down; to send down

13.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
13.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

14.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
14.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

15.meaning: Authority, sanction, or compelling proof — power or warrant given to back something up, whether kingly authority or a decisive argument. 'Sulṭān' is authorizing power or evidence.
15.grammar: A single noun ('authority') carrying the accusative indefinite ending -an (tanwīn al-naṣb). This one ending does two things at once: the -a marks the accusative case (typically the direct object of a verb), and the final -n sound (nunation) shows the noun is indefinite ('an authority / any warrant'). The nunation is a diacritic on the case vowel, not a separable suffix, so the word stays one undivided token.

16.meaning: 'so which / then which one?' — an interrogative asking to single out one item from among options, introduced by a connecting 'so/then.'
16.grammar: The prefix fa- means 'so/then,' linking to what precedes. 'Ayyu is the interrogative 'which one (of)?', normally followed by a noun in the 'of' (genitive) form. Its -u ending is the nominative, typically marking it as the subject of the question.

17.meaning: 'the two groups / the two parties' — two distinct camps or factions, named as a pair.
17.grammar: A noun 'group/party' with the definite article al-. The -ayni ending is the dual ('two of them') in its oblique form — the shape a dual noun takes as an object or after a preposition or in an 'of' relationship.
17.root: ف-ر-ق (f-r-q) — to separate, divide; a group split off

18.meaning: An adjective meaning 'more entitled, having a better/greater right, more deserving' of something.
18.grammar: A comparative/superlative adjective on the afʿal pattern, meaning 'more/most entitled'. The final -u is the nominative case ending, the form used when the word serves as the subject or as a predicate describing the subject.
18.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, just claim, what is due

19.meaning: 'with / to security' — the state of being safe, secure, and free from fear, governed by a preceding preposition.
19.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with/in') attached to the noun 'security' with the article al-. The final -i is the genitive ending, the case regularly required after a preposition.
19.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — to be safe, secure, to trust

20.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
20.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

21.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
21.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
21.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

22.meaning: A verb addressed to a group: 'you (all) know', 'you have knowledge', 'you are aware'. From the root meaning 'to know'.
22.grammar: The 'ta-' prefix marks a present/future verb addressed to 'you'. The '-ūna' ending marks a masculine plural subject and is the full 'indicative' form, signalling an ongoing, factual statement ('you (all) do know'), as opposed to the shortened '-ū' used after certain particles.

1.meaning: Those who / the ones who — a plural relative pronoun (masculine) introducing a description: 'those (people) who …'.
1.grammar: A relative pronoun, masculine plural, meaning 'those who / the ones who'. It refers back to a group already in view and introduces a clause describing them. Its form is fixed and does not change for case.

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
2.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

3.meaning: 'And not' — the conjunction wa- ('and') joined to lam, a particle that negates a verb and pushes its meaning into the completed past ('did not …').
3.grammar: A connector wa- ('and') plus the negative particle lam. Lam negates a following present-tense verb but turns its sense into the past: 'has not / did not …'. It also causes that verb to take the jussive (clipped) ending.

4.meaning: '(that) they confuse / mix up / cloak' — to obscure something by blending it with what doesn't belong, dressing truth in falsehood.
4.grammar: A present-tense verb, third person masculine plural ('they…'), shown by the ya-…-ū frame. The plain ending vowel has dropped (leaving -ū with a silent spelling alif), which signals a subjunctive/jussive mood — the form taken after particles like 'that,' 'not yet,' or in conditions.
4.root: ل-ب-س (l-b-s) — to clothe, cover, obscure, confuse

5.meaning: 'their faith / their belief' — the trusting acceptance and inner conviction held by them.
5.grammar: A verbal noun, 'faith/belief,' with the attached pronoun -hum ('their') marking possession. The -a ending is the accusative, typically marking the noun as the direct object — the thing acted upon.
5.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — to be secure, trust, believe

6.meaning: 'with wrongdoing / with injustice' — with putting things out of their right place: injustice, oppression, or wrong, governed by a preceding preposition.
6.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with') attached to the noun 'wrongdoing.' The ending -in is the genitive with indefinite 'nunation' ('with some wrong'); the genitive case is required after a preposition.
6.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — to wrong, oppress, put out of place; darkness

7.meaning: 'those / those ones' — a demonstrative pointing to a group of people or things at a distance ('those there').
7.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those.' The -ka element adds the sense of pointing to something farther off (as opposed to 'these' near at hand). Being a fixed pronoun, it keeps one form regardless of case.

8.meaning: To them / for them — the preposition li- ('to, for') joined to the pronoun 'them'. It expresses that something is directed toward, belongs to, or is for the benefit of a group.
8.grammar: The preposition li- ('to/for') combined with the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). When li- takes a pronoun its vowel becomes 'la-'. The final -u here is a connecting vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word; it carries no case meaning of its own.

9.meaning: Security / safety — the condition of being safe and free from fear or danger.
9.grammar: A noun, 'security,' with the definite article al-. The final -u is the nominative ending, which typically marks the word as the subject of a sentence — the thing that 'is' or does.
9.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — to be safe, secure, to trust

10.meaning: 'While they / and they' — the word 'wa' (here 'while' or 'and') joined to the standalone pronoun 'hum' ('they'), referring to a masculine plural group.
10.grammar: A connective 'wa' — often circumstantial 'while' — plus the independent subject pronoun 'hum' ('they'), used for a masculine plural group. As an independent pronoun it usually stands as the subject of a following statement.

11.meaning: '(those who are) rightly guided' — people who have accepted guidance and are travelling the right path.
11.grammar: An active participle (one in a state of being guided) in the masculine plural. The -ūna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the nominative — the form used when such a plural is the subject or a predicate ('they are the rightly guided').
11.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead rightly, show the way

1.meaning: And that; and that one. 'Tilka' is a demonstrative pointing to something distant or notable ('that' / 'those'), prefixed with 'and'. It singles out and draws attention to a thing set apart.
1.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') joined to a feminine demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' or 'those'. As a demonstrative it is fixed in form (it does not change for case) and serves to point out and identify something at a distance.

2.meaning: 'Our argument / our proof' — an argument, proof, or decisive piece of evidence brought forward to establish a case or defeat an opponent's claim, with the attached pronoun 'our'.
2.grammar: A feminine noun carrying the attached pronoun '-nā' ('our'). Its final tāʾ marbūṭa, normally a soft '-a', is sounded as a full '-t-' once a suffix follows; the '-u' on it is the nominative ending, the case used for the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified ('it is …').
2.root: ح-ج-ج (ḥ-j-j) — to argue, to bring proof; (also pilgrimage)

3.meaning: 'We gave it' — to hand over, grant, or bestow something upon someone, with both the giver ('we') and the thing given ('it') built into the single verb.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb. The '-nā' ending marks the doer as 'we'; the attached '-hā' is the object 'it/her' (referring to a feminine or non-human thing). So the form means 'we gave it'.
3.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (form IV) to bring, to give

4.meaning: The proper name Ibrāhīm (the Prophet Abraham).
4.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin. The -a ending here serves for both accusative and genitive because the name is a diptote — a class of nouns that refuses tanwīn (no -an/-in) and uses a single -a for these two cases. So this one -a covers 'Ibrāhīm' whether as an object or as 'of Ibrāhīm'.

5.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
5.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

6.meaning: 'His people / his folk' — the community, tribe, or nation to which a person belongs, with the attached pronoun 'his'.
6.grammar: A noun with the attached pronoun '-hi' ('his'). The '-i' ending is genitive: it typically marks the word as the object of a preposition or as linked to a preceding noun ('… of …'). The pronoun appears as '-hi' (rather than '-hu') because of this genitive '-i'.
6.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise; a people who stand together

7.meaning: 'We raise / We lift up' — to elevate something or someone in rank, degree, or standing; ongoing or repeated action.
7.grammar: A present-tense verb. The 'na-' prefix means 'we', and the '-u' ending marks the plain indicative (an ongoing or habitual 'we raise / we keep raising').
7.root: ر-ف-ع (r-f-ʿ) — to raise, to lift, to elevate

8.meaning: "degrees / ranks / levels / steps" — the plural of daraja, a step or grade in an ascending scale; it denotes ranks, levels, or stages of elevation.
8.grammar: A feminine plural noun (the -āt ending marks sound feminine plural). The final -in (with nunation/tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('degrees, ranks') and in the accusative/genitive case — the form used as an object or after a preposition.
8.root: د-ر-ج (d-r-j) — step, grade, to ascend by degrees

9.meaning: A versatile word meaning 'who / whoever / the one who.' It can ask a question ('who?') or introduce a clause ('whoever does…'), referring to persons.
9.grammar: An indeclinable particle/pronoun with a fixed form (it does not change for case). Used for rational beings ('who'), functioning either as an interrogative ('who?') or as a conditional/relative ('whoever, the one who').

10.meaning: 'We will / We wish' — to will, want, or choose for something to be; expresses volition.
10.grammar: A present-tense verb. The prefix means 'we'; the '-u' ending marks the plain indicative ('we will / we wish'). Its nūn carries a shadda (doubling) because the preceding connector 'man' ('whoever') merges into it, so it is sounded '-nn-'.
10.root: ش-ي-أ (sh-y-ʾ) — to will, to wish, to want

11.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
11.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

12.meaning: 'Your Lord' — the noun 'Lord' (Master, Sustainer, Owner, the One who nurtures and brings to completion) combined with 'your'. 'Rabb' carries the linked senses of ownership, authority, and ongoing care that raises a thing to its perfection.
12.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive. The -a ending is accusative, which typically marks the word as a direct object or governed element. The attached -ka means 'your', addressed to a single male.
12.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, nurturing care, ownership and mastery

13.meaning: All-Wise: possessing perfect wisdom — placing everything in its right place with flawless knowledge, judgment, and purpose. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's consummate wisdom.
13.grammar: A masculine singular adjective/intensive noun on the faʿīl pattern, expressing a deep, settled quality of wisdom. The final -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite and nominative — the case used for a subject or, very often, a predicate describing the doer ('[He is] All-Wise').
13.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, to be wise

14.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'All-Knowing / fully aware' — one whose knowledge is complete, deep, and all-encompassing; as a divine attribute it denotes Allah's perfect knowledge.
14.grammar: An intensive adjective (the pattern faʿīl conveys 'thoroughly, abundantly'). The ending -un is the indefinite nominative — the nominative case marks it as the subject or the quality being affirmed, and the -n (nunation) signals 'a / an', i.e. indefinite. So it reads '(is) all-knowing'.

1.meaning: 'And We bestowed / granted' — to give freely as a gift or favour, with no expectation of return, prefixed with 'and'.

parts.en: bestowed, granted as a gift (past stem)

1.grammar: A past-tense verb prefixed with 'wa' ('and'). The '-nā' ending marks the doer as 'we', giving 'and we bestowed'.
1.root: و-ه-ب (w-h-b) — to give freely, to bestow as a gift

2.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
2.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

3.meaning: Isaac (Isḥāq) — the proper name of the prophet, son of Abraham.
3.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin. It is a 'diptote', meaning it takes the '-a' ending for both the accusative (direct object) and genitive cases and never takes nunation ('-an').

4.meaning: The proper name 'Jacob' (Yaʿqūb), the prophet, joined to the conjunction 'and.'
4.grammar: Conjunction 'wa' (and) prefixed to a proper name. The final -a is the accusative/genitive ending; as a foreign (non-Arabic) name it is 'diptote,' taking -a for both those cases and never taking nunation (the -n sound).

5.meaning: A word meaning 'each one,' 'every one,' or 'all (of them)' taken individually — it singles out every member of a group. Here it stands in the indefinite, pointing to 'each' as the object or focus.
5.grammar: A noun of totality ('each / every'). The ending -an is the accusative with indefinite (tanwīn) marking; the accusative typically flags the word as the object of a verb or otherwise governed, and the doubled-n sound (tanwīn) shows it is indefinite ('a/an, some').

6.meaning: 'We guided' — to show the right way, lead aright, or direct toward the truth; past action with 'we' as the doer.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb. The '-nā' ending marks the doer as 'we', giving 'we guided'.
6.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, to lead rightly, to direct

7.meaning: A compound: 'and Nūḥ' — the connective 'and' joined to the proper name Nūḥ (the Prophet Noah).
7.grammar: The wa- prefix is the connective 'and'. The -an ending marks the accusative case, typically the direct object of a verb. Although a proper name, Nūḥ takes regular tanwīn (-an) because it is short and fully declinable, rather than the restricted (diptote) endings of many foreign names.

8.meaning: 'We guided' — to show the right way, lead aright, or direct toward the truth; past action with 'we' as the doer.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb. The '-nā' ending marks the doer as 'we', giving 'we guided'.
8.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, to lead rightly, to direct

9.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
9.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

10.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'before / beforehand / previously,' pointing to a moment or state that precedes something else in time. When used with the final vowel -u (qablu), it stands cut off from an explicit following noun, conveying 'before(hand)' or 'previously' in an absolute sense — the thing it is 'before' is understood rather than stated.
10.grammar: An adverb of time. The final -u ending here is the indeclinable (mabnī) form taken when the word is severed from a following genitive: rather than 'before X,' it means 'before(hand)' on its own, with the reference point left implicit.
10.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to come before, precede, be in front; to receive/accept

11.meaning: 'And from / and out of / and among.' A connector 'and' joined to the preposition 'from,' which marks origin, source, a starting point, or 'some of' a larger whole.
11.grammar: Two particles: the connector 'wa-' ('and') and the preposition 'min.' 'Min' indicates origin or source ('from'), a starting point, or partition ('some of'). Particles do not change their endings.

12.meaning: 'His offspring / his descendants' — the line of children and posterity issuing from a person, with the attached pronoun 'his'.
12.grammar: A noun with the attached pronoun '-hi' ('his'). Its final tāʾ marbūṭa, normally a soft '-a', is sounded as a full '-t-' once a suffix follows; the '-i' on it is genitive, used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun ('… of …'), and the pronoun appears as '-hi' because of it.
12.root: ذ-ر-ر / ذ-ر-أ (dh-r-r / dh-r-ʾ) — to scatter, to multiply (offspring); progeny

13.meaning: The proper name Dāwūd (David), the prophet and king known for his psalms, his judgment, and his kingship.
13.grammar: A proper name (of foreign, non-Arabic origin). Names of this kind are diptotes: they do not take case-tanwīn, and their accusative and genitive both show a single -a ending. The -a here marks the word as an object or as the noun governed by a preposition rather than carrying full case inflection.

14.meaning: A linking phrase 'and Solomon' — joining the proper name of the Prophet Sulaymān with 'and'.
14.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') plus a proper name. It ends in -a and is a 'diptote' — a noun that does not take full case endings, so it shows -a (not -un/-in) and no nunation; this single -a form serves for both the object and after-a-preposition roles.

15.meaning: A linking phrase 'and Job' — joining the proper name of the Prophet Ayyūb with 'and'.
15.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') plus a proper name. The name ends in -a and is a 'diptote' — a noun that resists full case endings, so it shows -a (not -in) and takes no nunation; this -a form covers both the object and after-a-preposition roles.

16.meaning: 'And Joseph (Yūsuf)' — the proper name of the prophet, son of Jacob, prefixed with 'and'.
16.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin prefixed with 'wa' ('and'). It is a 'diptote': it takes the '-a' ending for both the accusative and genitive cases and never takes nunation.

17.meaning: 'And Moses (Mūsā)' — the proper name of the prophet, prefixed with 'and'.
17.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin prefixed with 'wa' ('and'). It ends in a fixed long '-ā' (written as alif maqṣūra) and so shows no visible change for case.

18.meaning: A linking phrase 'and Aaron' — joining the proper name of the Prophet Hārūn with 'and'.
18.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') plus a proper name. It ends in -a and is a 'diptote' — a noun that does not take full case endings, so it shows -a (not -un/-in) and no nunation; this -a form covers both the object and after-a-preposition roles.

19.meaning: 'And likewise / and in the same way / and thus' — a connective phrase pointing back to a manner just mentioned and saying 'in that very way…'. Built from 'and' + 'like' + 'that'.
19.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'; the prefix ka- means 'like/as'; 'dhālika' is the demonstrative 'that' (pointing to something distant or already mentioned). Because ka- acts like a preposition, the word after it stands in the genitive, though the demonstrative 'dhālika' keeps a fixed form and shows no visible case change. The whole means 'and just like that / and thus'.

20.meaning: 'We reward / We requite' — to repay or recompense someone for their deeds, whether with good or with due consequence.
20.grammar: A present-tense verb. The 'na-' prefix means 'we'. The stem ends in a long '-ī' (a weak final root letter); in the plain indicative this final '-ī' is what is heard, giving 'we reward'.
20.root: ج-ز-ي (j-z-y) — to repay, to recompense, to requite

21.meaning: 'The doers of good / those who act with excellence and beauty'. It denotes people who do what is good and do it well — acting righteously, generously, and with sincerity, as if conscious of being watched by Allah.

parts.en: good-doers / those who excel in doing good

21.grammar: A definite plural active participle (the 'doer' form of the verb 'to do good'). The prefixed al- means 'the'. The ending -īna marks a sound masculine plural in the object/oblique state — the form used when the noun is a direct object or follows a preposition. It refers to male (or mixed) persons characterized by the action.
21.root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — to be good, beautiful; to do well and excellently

1.meaning: 'And Zechariah (Zakariyyā)' — the proper name of the prophet, prefixed with 'and'.
1.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin prefixed with 'wa' ('and'). It ends in a fixed long '-ā' and so shows no visible change for case.

2.meaning: 'And John (Yaḥyā)' — the proper name of the prophet, prefixed with 'and'.
2.grammar: A proper name prefixed with 'wa' ('and'). It ends in a fixed long '-ā' (written as alif maqṣūra) and so shows no visible change for case.
2.root: ح-ي-ي (ḥ-y-y) — to live; the name is Arabic in form, linked by the grammarians to this root

3.meaning: The proper name 'Isa' (Jesus), prefixed with 'and'. It refers to the prophet Isa, son of Maryam.
3.grammar: A proper noun joined by the connector 'wa' ('and'). The name ends in a long ā (written with the dagger alif) and is indeclinable, so it does not change its ending for case; it simply names the person.

4.meaning: 'And Elijah (Ilyās)' — the proper name of the prophet, prefixed with 'and'.
4.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin prefixed with 'wa' ('and'). It is a 'diptote': it takes the '-a' ending for both the accusative and genitive cases and never takes nunation.

5.meaning: A noun meaning 'all,' 'each,' 'every,' or 'the whole.' It denotes totality — that the entirety of a group or thing is included.
5.grammar: A noun in the nominative case with 'tanwīn' (the -un ending), which marks it as indefinite and as the subject or doer of a sentence. Standing alone with tanwīn it carries the sense 'everyone / all of them' as an independent subject.

6.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
6.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

7.meaning: The righteous, upright, and morally sound ones — people who are good, virtuous, and act rightly, putting things into proper order. Plural and referring to people.
7.grammar: A definite noun/adjective ('al-' = 'the') in the sound masculine plural. The -īna ending marks the plural in its accusative/genitive (object or 'of/from') form — the form used as a direct object or after a preposition; the parallel subject form would be -ūna.
7.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — soundness, righteousness, setting things right

1.meaning: And Ismāʿīl (Ishmael), the proper name of the prophet, son of Ibrahim; preceded by the connector 'and.'
1.grammar: The connector 'wa-' ('and') joined to a proper name of non-Arabic origin. As a 'diptote' foreign name, it takes a single -a ending for both the object (accusative) and possessive/after-preposition (genitive) roles, and it does not take nunation.

2.meaning: 'And Elisha (al-Yasaʿ)' — the proper name of the prophet, carrying the definite article 'al-', prefixed with 'and'.
2.grammar: A proper name prefixed with 'wa' ('and') and carrying the definite article 'al-' ('the') as part of the name. With the article attached, it declines as a fully regular noun: the '-a' shown here is the accusative (direct-object) ending, while in the genitive it would instead take '-i'.

3.meaning: A linking phrase 'and Jonah' — joining the proper name of the Prophet Yūnus with 'and'.
3.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') plus a proper name. It ends in -a and is a 'diptote' — a noun that does not take full case endings, so it shows -a (not -un/-in) and no nunation; this single -a form serves for both the object and after-a-preposition roles.

4.meaning: 'And Lot (Lūṭ)' — the proper name of the prophet, prefixed with 'and'.
4.grammar: A proper name prefixed with 'wa' ('and'). Unusually for a foreign name, it is treated as fully declinable here: the '-an' ending marks the accusative case (the direct object) together with nunation ('-n').

5.meaning: 'And all / each one' — referring comprehensively to every member of a group, 'each and every.'
5.grammar: 'And' + the totality-word kull ('all/each'). The '-an' (nunation) is the accusative indefinite ending, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon). Standing alone with nunation, kull means 'each one / all of them.'

6.meaning: "We favoured / We gave preference / We caused to excel" — built on the intensive verb meaning to give one thing precedence or superiority over another, to bestow extra favour; 'we preferred / we made excel'.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb in the 'we' form. The doubled middle consonant (Form II) makes the root sense of 'bounty/excess' transitive and intensive: 'to make excel, to favour'. The suffix -nā marks the subject as 'we' (first-person plural).

7.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
7.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
7.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

8.meaning: The worlds, all created realms — the totality of beings and peoples; in 'Lord of the worlds,' the whole of creation across all its kinds.
8.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the worlds') with 'al-' ('the'). The '-īna' ending marks a masculine sound plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) form — the form used after a preposition, in an 'of' linkage, or as a direct object.
8.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; a 'world' as a sign by which the Creator is known

1.meaning: 'And from / and out of / and among.' A connector 'and' joined to the preposition 'from,' which marks origin, source, a starting point, or 'some of' a larger whole.
1.grammar: Two particles: the connector 'wa-' ('and') and the preposition 'min.' 'Min' indicates origin or source ('from'), a starting point, or partition ('some of'). Particles do not change their endings.

2.meaning: 'Their fathers / their forefathers' — male ancestors and forebears, with the attached pronoun 'their'.
2.grammar: An irregular ('broken') plural of 'ab' ('father') with the attached pronoun '-him' ('their', referring to males). The '-i' before the suffix is genitive — used after a preposition or to link to a preceding noun ('… of …') — and the pronoun is '-him' rather than '-hum' because of it.

3.meaning: 'And their descendants / their offspring' — the lines of progeny issuing from people, plural, with the attached pronoun 'their'.
3.grammar: The sound feminine plural of 'dhurriyya' ('offspring'), prefixed with 'wa' ('and') and carrying the pronoun '-him' ('their'). The '-i' before the suffix marks the genitive (after a preposition or linking to a preceding noun); for the sound feminine plural this same '-i' also serves as the accusative ending.
3.root: ذ-ر-ر / ذ-ر-أ (dh-r-r / dh-r-ʾ) — to scatter, to multiply (offspring); progeny

4.meaning: 'And their brothers' — male siblings or, more broadly, kinsmen and brethren, with the attached pronoun 'their'.
4.grammar: A plural of 'akh' ('brother'), prefixed with 'wa' ('and') and carrying the pronoun '-him' ('their'). The '-i' before the suffix is genitive — used after a preposition or to link to a preceding noun ('… of …') — and the pronoun is '-him' rather than '-hum' because of it.

5.meaning: 'And We chose / selected them' — to pick out, single out, and elect someone as specially favoured, with 'we' as the doer and 'them' as the chosen.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb prefixed with 'wa' ('and'). The '-nā' ending marks the doer as 'we', and the attached '-hum' is the object 'them', giving 'and we chose them'.
5.root: ج-ب-ي (j-b-y) — to collect, to gather; (form VIII) to pick out, to elect

6.meaning: 'And We guided them' — to show the right way and lead aright, with 'we' as the doer and 'them' as those guided.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb prefixed with 'wa' ('and'). The '-nā' ending marks the doer as 'we', and the attached '-hum' is the object 'them', giving 'and we guided them'.
6.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, to lead rightly, to direct

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
7.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

8.meaning: 'A path / road / way'. It denotes a clear, open road that one travels — often used figuratively for a course of life or conduct.
8.grammar: The '-in' ending (tanwīn) marks the word as indefinite ('a path / some way') and in the genitive case. The genitive typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').

9.meaning: 'Straight / upright / undeviating' — describing something that runs true without bending or wandering; applied to a 'path' it means a direct, correct way that leads soundly to its goal.
9.grammar: An active participle (a describing word, 'straight/upright') from a verb meaning 'to be/become straight'. It is indefinite, and the -in ending is the genitive with 'tanwīn'. As a describing word it normally follows and agrees with the noun it modifies, matching that noun in being indefinite and in the genitive case.

1.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
1.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

2.meaning: Guidance; right direction and true leading — being shown and set upon the correct way (construct form, 'guidance of …').
2.grammar: A verbal noun ending in a long -ā from a weak-final root. Its form (without the article and ending in -ā) commonly serves as the first term of a possessive phrase ('the guidance OF …'). It names the abstract idea of being rightly guided.
2.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead rightly, show the way

3.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
3.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

4.meaning: 'He guides / leads on the right way' — to show someone the correct path, direct them rightly, or lead them to a goal, whether literally or in matters of belief and conduct.
4.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: the ya- prefix means 'he'. The verb ends in a long -ī (a weak final letter); in this indicative form the long vowel stands in place of the usual -u mood marker, still conveying a plain, ongoing statement ('he guides').
4.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance, showing the way, leading rightly

5.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
5.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

6.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
6.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

7.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he wills, he wishes, he chooses' — to want or intend something by one's own decision.
7.grammar: A present/ongoing action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular, and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('he wills'), as opposed to a command or a verb governed by 'that.'
7.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing; the root behind 'thing' (shayʾ)

8.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
8.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

9.meaning: 'His servants / His slaves / His worshippers' — ʿibād are those who serve and worship; with the attached pronoun it denotes the servants belonging to Him (Allah), i.e., humankind or His devotees.
9.grammar: A plural noun with an attached possessive pronoun '-hi' ('his/His'). The -i vowel is the genitive case, typically appearing after a preposition or in a possessive ('of') link; the pronoun names the one to whom the servants belong.

10.meaning: 'and if' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle 'if'. This particular 'if' (law) introduces a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact condition: 'if (such-and-such had been the case)…', often implying it was not.
10.grammar: A conjunction plus a conditional particle. wa- means 'and'. law is a non-changing particle (no case ending) that sets up a supposition, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('… then certainly …').

11.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'they associated partners / they set up partners (with Allah)' — to ascribe partners or equals to Allah, the act underlying idolatry and polytheism.
11.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb in a pattern meaning 'to make (someone) a partner'. The ending -ū marks a masculine-plural subject, 'they', so it reads 'they associated partners (with Allah)'.
11.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — sharing, partnership, associating partners

12.meaning: 'Would surely have come to nothing / been rendered void' — of deeds or efforts: to be nullified, lost, and stripped of all reward.

parts.en: came to nothing, was rendered void (past stem)

12.grammar: A past-tense verb with the emphatic prefix 'la-' ('surely / indeed'), which commonly answers a condition ('if … then surely …'). The '-a' ending marks a third-person masculine singular doer ('he/it came to nothing').
12.root: ح-ب-ط (ḥ-b-ṭ) — to come to nothing, to be void, to be fruitless

13.meaning: From them; away from them; concerning them. The preposition ʿan conveys moving away from, departing from, or 'on behalf of / concerning', combined with the pronoun 'them'.
13.grammar: A preposition joined to the attached pronoun -hum, 'them' (referring to a group, grammatically masculine plural). The preposition ʿan basically signals separation or removal ('away from'), and can also mean 'about/concerning' or 'on behalf of' depending on usage.

14.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
14.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

15.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
15.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
15.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

16.meaning: 'They do / they work, they act' — a present-tense verb of doing and working, covering deeds and actions carried out by a group.
16.grammar: Present/imperfect verb. The ya-…-ūna frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (do).' The -ūna ending also marks the indicative mood, the plain statement form, as opposed to command or negated-future forms.
16.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

1.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those' — pointing to people or things that are distant or already known. It singles out a group ('those ones', 'it is those who').
1.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. It is fixed in form (no case endings). The -ka element signals distance/remoteness, pointing to something far off or notable. It can refer to people of either gender.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: We gave them / We granted them — a completed act of bestowing or conferring something upon a group, done by 'We'.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb of Form IV ('to give, bestow, grant'). The suffix -nā marks the doer as 'we'. The attached pronoun -hum(u) is the object, 'them' (a group); its vowel is lengthened to -humu to ease pronunciation before the next word. Altogether: 'We gave them'.
3.root: ء-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (Form IV) to give, bring, bestow

4.meaning: The Book, the Scripture — a written revelation; the term for a divinely revealed text.
4.grammar: A definite noun ('the Book') with attached 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb.
4.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; a writing, book

5.meaning: And sound judgment, wise discernment, and the authority to decide rightly between matters. The noun denotes wisdom in the sense of correct judgment, governance, and ruling — the ability to put things in their proper place.
5.grammar: The wa- prefix means 'and'; the al- prefix means 'the'. The final -a is the accusative ending, which typically marks the word as the object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or a noun governed in that case.
5.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, decide wisely, rule

6.meaning: And prophethood — the office and dignity of being a prophet, one chosen by Allah to receive revelation and convey His message. The noun names this divinely bestowed mission and rank.
6.grammar: The wa- prefix means 'and'; the al- prefix means 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the following 'n', shown by the doubling). The word ends in tā marbūṭa (ة), the feminine noun ending, which itself carries the case vowel; here it bears the accusative -a, so it is pronounced -ta. The accusative typically marks the word as the object of a verb or a noun governed in that case.
6.root: ن-ب-ء (n-b-ʾ) — news, tidings; whence 'prophet' as bearer of news from Allah

7.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
7.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

8.meaning: To disbelieve, to reject faith; to deny the truth and to be ungrateful, covering over and refusing what is true.
8.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'). The final consonant carries no vowel (jussive form), an ending that typically appears after conditional or commanding particles and gives the sense 'whoever/if … disbelieves'.
8.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover over; to disbelieve, reject, be ungrateful

9.meaning: with it / by it — a preposition meaning 'with' or 'by means of' joined to a pronoun referring to a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing.
9.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition meaning 'with', 'by', or 'by means of'. The attached -hā is an object pronoun meaning 'it' or 'her', referring to something feminine in gender. Together they mean 'with it' or 'by means of it'.

10.meaning: These / those — a plural demonstrative pointing to a group of people or things. Its core sense is the near demonstrative 'these', but it is very commonly rendered 'those' in translation when the group it points to has already been described or named rather than being physically present.
10.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, used for a group of either gender. Its base value is near-deixis ('these'), built from an attention-drawing prefix 'hā-' ('lo!, here') plus the base 'ulāʾi'. In practice it is often translated 'those' when the referent is already mentioned or understood rather than literally nearby. Its form is fixed and does not change for grammatical case; it points to a group rather than naming it.

11.meaning: A two-part connector: fa- means 'so', 'then', or 'and so', linking what follows as a result or consequence; qad before a past-tense verb intensifies it, conveying 'certainly', 'indeed', or 'already' — stressing that the action has truly and definitely occurred.
11.grammar: fa- is a connecting particle meaning 'so' or 'then', often marking a result. qad is a particle of emphasis; placed before a completed (past-tense) verb it affirms that the action has definitely or already happened. Neither part takes a case ending.

12.meaning: 'We have entrusted / appointed in charge' — to commit something to someone's care, assign them responsibility for it, or appoint them as its guardian.

parts.en: entrusted, put in charge, appointed as guardian (past stem)

12.grammar: A past-tense verb of the intensive ('doubled-middle') pattern that carries the sense of entrusting or appointing. The '-nā' ending marks the doer as 'we', giving 'we entrusted / we appointed'.
12.root: و-ك-ل (w-k-l) — to entrust, to rely upon, to appoint as agent

13.meaning: with it / by it — a preposition meaning 'with' or 'by means of' joined to a pronoun referring to a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing.
13.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition meaning 'with', 'by', or 'by means of'. The attached -hā is an object pronoun meaning 'it' or 'her', referring to something feminine in gender. Together they mean 'with it' or 'by means of it'.

14.meaning: 'A people, a folk, a community' — a group of human beings bound together, often by kinship, tribe, or shared standing.
14.grammar: An indefinite collective noun. The -an ending (accusative with tanwīn, the 'n' sound) marks it as the object of an action.
14.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a standing group, people

15.meaning: A negating verb meaning 'they are not'. It is the masculine-plural form of laysa, a special Arabic verb that negates a statement in the present — asserting that some quality or condition does NOT apply to the subject. The 'they' is a masculine group of people.

parts.en: is not / are not (negating verb; the lām carries a shaddah from assimilation with a preceding word)

15.grammar: Laysa is a defective verb (fiʿl nāqiṣ), one of the 'sisters of kāna' (akhawāt kāna), not a particle. Like its sisters it raises a subject to the nominative and puts its predicate in the accusative, but its meaning is to negate a present-tense statement ('X is not Y'). The -ū ending marks a masculine plural subject — 'they (are) not'. The doubled lām (shaddah) here reflects assimilation of a preceding consonant onto the lām and is part of the pronounced form لَّيۡسُوۡا.
15.root: ل-ي-س (l-y-s) — non-being / negation of a present state

16.meaning: with it / by it — a preposition meaning 'with' or 'by means of' joined to a pronoun referring to a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing.
16.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition meaning 'with', 'by', or 'by means of'. The attached -hā is an object pronoun meaning 'it' or 'her', referring to something feminine in gender. Together they mean 'with it' or 'by means of it'.

17.meaning: '(as) disbelievers / rejecters' — those who cover over and reject faith. Built on the active participle kāfir (one who disbelieves), here in the plural, and introduced by the prefix bi- which often attaches to the disclaimed predicate after a negating verb.

parts.en: in / as (prefixed particle, often reinforcing a negated predicate)

17.grammar: Kāfirīna is a sound masculine plural participle. The -īna ending is the plural form used in the accusative/genitive (object or governed position); after the particle bi- the word stands in the genitive. The prefix bi- ('in/as') frequently introduces the very predicate that a negating verb denies.
17.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover over, conceal; hence to reject/disbelieve

1.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those' — pointing to people or things that are distant or already known. It singles out a group ('those ones', 'it is those who').
1.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. It is fixed in form (no case endings). The -ka element signals distance/remoteness, pointing to something far off or notable. It can refer to people of either gender.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: He guided, led aright, showed the way; to direct someone toward a goal or onto the right path. Of Allah, it denotes granting guidance to truth and faith.

parts.en: he (past-tense ending, with weak final letter)

3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he guided'). This is a 'defective' verb whose third root letter is a weak letter, so the final syllable appears as a long -ā (written with alif maqṣūra ى). The past tense states a completed action. With no attached subject pronoun, it simply means 'he/it guided'.
3.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance, showing the right way

4.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
4.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

5.meaning: A built-up word meaning roughly 'so by their guidance'. It joins a connector 'so/then', the particle 'by/with', the noun hudā ('guidance' — being shown the right way), and the attached pronoun 'their'. Hudā denotes right guidance: being directed onto the correct path.

parts.en: so / then (connector showing result or sequence)

5.grammar: After the preposition bi-, the noun hudā stands in the genitive ('by/with … guidance'). The attached pronoun -hum means 'their'; its final vowel appears as -humu (rather than -hum) to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a connecting hamza. The fa- prefix links this to what precedes as a consequence.

6.meaning: A command meaning 'follow (the right example); take as a model'. From the verb iqtadā, which means to follow someone's lead or pattern, to emulate. Addressed to a single male.

parts.en: follow / take as an example (command stem)

6.grammar: This is a singular masculine imperative ('you — follow!'). The base command would end in -i; the added silent hāʾ (hāʾ al-sakt) is attached to give the short final vowel something to rest on in pause, a recognized feature of recitation. No subject pronoun is written because the command form itself addresses 'you'.
6.root: ق-د-و (q-d-w) — to follow an example, take as a model

7.meaning: An imperative command meaning 'Say!' or 'Speak!' — a direct order to one person to utter or declare something.
7.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a single male. The bare, vowelless ending (the silent stop on the final 'l') marks it as a direct order: 'you, say!' It is built from the verb 'to say' with the weak middle letter dropped, leaving the short, clipped command form.
7.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, to speak, to utter

8.meaning: 'Not' — a particle of negation. Depending on context it denies a present fact, forbids an action, or rules something out ('do not / there is no').
8.grammar: A negating particle, 'not / no'. It is used to deny or prohibit — negating present-tense statements, expressing 'there is no...', or, with a command form, forbidding an action ('do not...').

9.meaning: 'I ask you (for)…'. A present-tense verb 'I ask/request', with the object pronoun 'you' (plural) attached. Used of asking a question or requesting something such as payment or reward.
9.grammar: The a- prefix marks a first-person singular present-tense verb: 'I ask'. The attached -kum is the object 'you (plural)'. The underlying final vowel on the verb is -u (indicative, the ordinary present-tense mood), here followed directly by the object pronoun.

10.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
10.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

11.meaning: A reward, wage, or recompense — the return earned for work or conduct, whether worldly pay or otherworldly recompense.
11.grammar: A noun meaning 'a reward.' The final '-an' (tanwīn fatḥa) marks the indefinite accusative case, the case used for the object of a verb (e.g. of 'to give'), giving the sense 'a reward.'
11.root: ا-ج-ر (ʾ-j-r) — reward, wage, recompense for what one does

12.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
12.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

13.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
13.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

14.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
14.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

15.meaning: A reminder; a remembrance or admonition that brings truth to mind — the same notion as the previous word but without 'the,' so 'a reminding / as a reminder.'
15.grammar: A noun, 'reminder/admonition,' here indefinite ('a reminder'). The closing long -ā is a fixed feminine ending that does not inflect for case; the word's role in a sentence is shown by context rather than by a final case vowel.

16.meaning: 'for / to the worlds', i.e. for all created beings and realms — all peoples, all that exists. ʿālamīn is the plural of ʿālam ('a world, a realm of creatures'); with the prefix li- it conveys benefit or direction: 'for the worlds'.
16.grammar: A sound masculine plural noun. The -īna ending is the plural used after a preposition (genitive); here governed by li- ('for/to'), so the whole reads 'for the worlds'. The li- prefix typically marks the beneficiary, recipient, or purpose.
16.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; ʿālam = a world (that by which the Creator is known)

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: 'they esteemed / assessed / gave due measure to'. Past-tense verb from qadara, whose core idea is to measure, estimate, or assign proper worth and proportion. The 'they' is a masculine group.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb. The suffix -ū marks a third-person masculine plural subject: 'they (did)'. The final written alif after the -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.
2.root: ق-د-ر (q-d-r) — to measure, determine, appraise; capacity and due proportion

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
3.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

4.meaning: Due right, just measure, rightful claim; that which is true and rightly owed — here used to mean 'as is truly its due'.
4.grammar: A noun meaning 'truth, right, due'. The final -a (accusative) often marks the object of a verb, and in a possessive phrase like this it commonly conveys the sense 'with the full right/due OF …', i.e. as something deserves to be done.
4.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, that which is due and real

5.meaning: 'his/its proper measure / worth / due estimation'. The noun qadr means the true measure, value, or rank of something — its proper standing — joined to the pronoun 'his/its'.
5.grammar: This is a possession phrase (iḍāfa): qadr is the possessed term (mudāf) and the attached pronoun -hi is the possessor (mudāf ilayh). In an iḍāfa, the possessed term takes whatever case its own role in the sentence requires, while the possessor term always stands in the genitive. The -i vowel on the pronoun (-hi, lengthened in recitation to -hī) reflects that genitive. The pronoun means 'his' or 'its', linking the measure to its owner.
5.root: ق-د-ر (q-d-r) — to measure, determine; due proportion and worth

6.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
6.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

7.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
7.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

8.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
8.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

9.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'he sent down, he caused to descend, he revealed' — used especially of Allah sending down revelation, rain, or blessings from above.
9.grammar: A completed (past) action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the -a ending marks third-person masculine singular. The form IV (causative) pattern means 'to make something come down,' i.e., to send it down.

10.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
10.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

11.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
11.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

12.meaning: 'a human being, a mortal'. Bashar denotes a human as a flesh-and-skin creature (the word is linked to the outer skin), often stressing human, as opposed to angelic or divine, nature.
12.grammar: The ending -in (tanwīn with -i) is the indefinite genitive: it both marks the noun as indefinite ('a human being') and shows it standing in the genitive, as after a preposition or in possession constructions.
12.root: ب-ش-ر (b-sh-r) — outer skin; hence humankind as skin-bearing creatures

13.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
13.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

14.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
14.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
14.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

15.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
15.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

16.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
16.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

17.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'he sent down, he caused to descend, he revealed' — used especially of Allah sending down revelation, rain, or blessings from above.
17.grammar: A completed (past) action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the -a ending marks third-person masculine singular. The form IV (causative) pattern means 'to make something come down,' i.e., to send it down.

18.meaning: The Book, the Scripture — a written revelation; the term for a divinely revealed text.
18.grammar: A definite noun ('the Book') with attached 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb.
18.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; a writing, book

19.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
19.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

20.meaning: He/it came, arrived, or came about — the act of coming into presence or of something occurring.
20.grammar: A past-tense verb with no prefix and no personal suffix, naming a completed act by a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it came'). All three letters here are root letters: jā spells the first radical plus the lengthened weak middle radical, and the final hamza (ء) is the third root consonant — not an ending. The fatḥa (-a) on that hamza is simply the past-tense vocalization for a 'he' subject sitting on the last root letter; there is no separable suffix.
20.root: ج-ي-ء (j-y-ʾ) — to come, to arrive

21.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
21.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

22.meaning: Mūsā (Moses) — the proper name of the prophet. As a name it has no Arabic root meaning; it is a non-inflecting (indeclinable) noun whose ending does not change for case.
22.grammar: A proper name ending in a fixed long -ā (written as alif maqṣūra). It is fully indeclinable (invariable): the final -ā never changes, so the word shows no case distinction at all — it looks and sounds identical whether subject, object, or possessor. (This is unlike a diptote, which still alternates between two case vowels; here there is no alternation.)

23.meaning: 'A light' — light, radiance, or illumination; that by which things become visible. Often used figuratively for guidance, clarity, and spiritual illumination.
23.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The ending -an is accusative and indefinite, the case that typically marks the object of a verb or a complement; the final -n (tanwīn) marks indefiniteness ('a light').

24.meaning: Joined to 'and': 'and a guidance' — guidance meaning right direction, the showing of the correct path, that which leads aright.
24.grammar: A noun preceded by the connector 'wa' ('and'). It is a 'defective' noun whose third root letter is a weak yāʾ, written here as a final alif maqṣūra (ى); the indefinite ending '-an' (tanwīn) sits on that final letter. Such nouns keep the same form across the nominative, accusative, and genitive cases.
24.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, show the way

25.meaning: For the people, for mankind, for humankind. The preposition 'for/to' joined to 'the people' as a collective term for human beings.
25.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('for/to') prefixed to the noun 'al-nās' ('the people'). The article 'al-' loses its 'a' sound after 'li-' and its 'l' assimilates into the noun's initial n (hence the doubled 'nn'). The -i ending is genitive, the case required after a preposition.
25.root: ن-و-س / ا-ن-س (n-w-s / ʾ-n-s) — humankind, people

26.meaning: 'you make/turn it (into something)'. A present-tense verb jaʿala ('to make, render, place, turn X into Y') addressed to a plural 'you', with the object 'it' attached.
26.grammar: The ta-…-ūna frame marks a second-person masculine plural present-tense verb: 'you (all) make'. The -ūna ending is the full indicative form (ordinary present statement). The attached -hu is the object 'it/him'.
26.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, place, appoint

27.meaning: 'parchments / sheets'. The plural of qirṭās, a sheet of writing material (papyrus, parchment, paper) on which something is written.
27.grammar: This is a 'diptote' broken plural — a noun pattern that takes no tanwīn (no -n sound). Its -a ending here serves as both the accusative (object) marker and, when it stands in the genitive, the substitute for the usual -i. The pattern qarāṭīs (faʿālīl) is the broken-plural shape.

28.meaning: 'you reveal/display it; you make it public'. Present-tense verb from abdā ('to show, disclose, bring into the open'), addressed to a plural 'you', with the object 'it (feminine)' attached.

parts.en: you (masculine plural subject ending, full indicative)

28.grammar: The tu-…-ūna frame is a second-person masculine plural present-tense verb of the 'causative' pattern (af ʿala: to make something appear). The -ūna is the full indicative ending (the -na belongs to the verb, not to the object); the attached object pronoun -hā then follows it, giving -ūna-hā. The object -hā means 'it/her' (a feminine or non-human thing).
28.root: ب-د-و (b-d-w) — to appear, become visible; (causative) to display

29.meaning: 'and you hide/conceal'. The connector 'and' plus a present-tense verb from akhfā ('to conceal, keep hidden, suppress from view'), addressed to a plural 'you'.
29.grammar: A second-person masculine plural present-tense verb of the causative pattern (af ʿala). The -ūna ending is the full indicative form ('you all conceal'). The wa- prefix simply joins it to a preceding clause.
29.root: خ-ف-ي (kh-f-y) — to be hidden; (causative) to hide, conceal

30.meaning: An adjective/noun meaning 'many', 'much', or 'numerous' — a large quantity or great number of something.
30.grammar: Adjective/noun in the indefinite accusative, marked by the final -an (nunation with fatḥa). The accusative typically marks a verb's object or an indefinite quantity, and the doubled-n sound shows the word is indefinite ('many').
30.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — to be much, many, abundant

31.meaning: 'and you were taught'. The connector 'and' plus a past-tense passive verb from ʿallama ('to teach, instruct'); in the passive it means the 'you' received instruction — were taught — without naming the teacher.

parts.en: were taught (past passive stem, intensive pattern)
you (masculine plural subject of a past verb)

31.grammar: A past-tense PASSIVE verb of the intensive pattern (faʿʿala). The inner vowel shape ʿu-lli-ma signals the passive ('was/were taught'). The suffix -tum marks a second-person masculine plural subject — here the recipients of the teaching: 'you (all) were taught'.
31.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; (intensive) to teach, instruct

32.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
32.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

33.meaning: A negating particle, 'not', used specifically to deny that an action happened in the past, even though it attaches to a present-tense verb form. It turns 'you do X' into 'you did not do X'.

parts.en: did not (negation of a completed act)

33.grammar: An indeclinable particle that governs the verb after it, putting that verb into the jussive (clipped) mood and giving it past-time meaning. In short: lam + a present-form verb = 'did not [verb]'.

34.meaning: You (plural) know, understand, or have knowledge of something — grasping a fact with certainty.
34.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix marks a second-person subject ('you'), and the -ū ending makes it masculine plural ('you all'). The short, vowelless -ū (not -ūna) is the jussive/subjunctive shape, used after particles of command, negation, or purpose ('until you know' / 'so that you know').

35.meaning: You — the standalone pronoun for a group of people ('you all', masculine or mixed). It is used for emphasis or as the subject standing on its own.
35.grammar: A detached subject pronoun meaning 'you all' (second-person masculine/mixed plural). Unlike pronoun endings attached to verbs or nouns, this word stands alone — typically to emphasize the subject or to begin an equational sentence ('you [are]…'). Its form is fixed and does not change for case.

36.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
36.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

37.meaning: Your fathers / forefathers / parents; the plural 'fathers' joined to a 'your (plural)' possessor, denoting the male ancestors or, more broadly, the parents of a group.
37.grammar: A broken plural noun ('fathers') with the attached possessor -kum ('your', addressing several people). The -u case-vowel before the suffix is nominative, typically marking the word as the doer or subject of a sentence. The ending -kum specifically addresses a group of males or a mixed group.

38.meaning: 'Say!' — a command to utter or declare something aloud, addressed to a single male.
38.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to one male: 'say!'. Its natural form ends in a silent consonant (qul), but here a short -i vowel is added simply to smooth pronunciation before a following word that begins with a connecting sound; it carries no case meaning of its own.

39.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
39.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

40.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
