4.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
4.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

5.meaning: The sky or heaven — the canopy overhead; the expanse above the earth, also that which is elevated or raised over something. With the definite article it means 'the sky / the heaven'.
5.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'), in the genitive marked by the -i ending. (The 'l' of al- assimilates in sound into the following 's', a 'sun letter', though it is still written.) The genitive -i ending typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').

6.meaning: 'water' — water in general, the fluid essential to life; also used for liquid such as rain. A basic noun for the substance of water.
6.grammar: An indefinite noun. The '-an' ending (tanwīn al-fatḥ) marks the accusative case together with indefiniteness — commonly the role of a direct object, the thing acted upon (e.g. what is sent down or brought).

7.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'so We brought out / then We brought forth' — to cause something to emerge or come out from a source.
7.grammar: A perfect (past-tense) verb in the causative (form IV) pattern, which carries the sense of 'making something come out.' The attached -nā ending marks the doer as 'we.' The prefixed fa- is a connective particle meaning 'so' or 'then,' linking what follows to what came before.

8.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
8.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

9.meaning: A noun meaning 'plant growth / vegetation / that which sprouts from the earth' — the green growing things that come up from the ground.
9.grammar: A singular noun used collectively for growing plants. The -a ending is accusative, which commonly marks the noun as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or otherwise gives it an adverbial/specifying sense.

10.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
10.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

11.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
11.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
11.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

12.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'so We brought out / then We brought forth' — to cause something to emerge or come out from a source.
12.grammar: A perfect (past-tense) verb in the causative (form IV) pattern, which carries the sense of 'making something come out.' The attached -nā ending marks the doer as 'we.' The prefixed fa- is a connective particle meaning 'so' or 'then,' linking what follows to what came before.
12.root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — going out, emerging, exiting

13.meaning: 'From it / out of it / from him'. It combines the preposition 'from / out of' with the pronoun 'it/him'.
13.grammar: The preposition min ('from / out of', indicating origin or source) with the attached pronoun -hu ('it' / 'him'), referring to a singular masculine thing or person. As object of the preposition, the pronoun is in the oblique form.
13.root: — (no triliteral root; a preposition with a pronoun)

14.meaning: An adjective/noun meaning 'green / verdant' — fresh green growth, lush and full of life.
14.grammar: A singular indefinite adjective/noun. The -an ending (written with tanwīn) marks it as both indefinite ('a green thing,' not 'the') and accusative, which typically signals a direct object or a descriptive/circumstantial term ('being green').

15.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'We bring out / We bring forth' — to cause something to emerge or be produced.
15.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb in the causative (form IV) pattern, 'to make come out.' The nu- prefix marks the subject as 'we.' The final -u ending is the indicative mood, presenting the action as a simple statement of ongoing or repeated fact.

16.meaning: 'From it / out of it / from him'. It combines the preposition 'from / out of' with the pronoun 'it/him'.
16.grammar: The preposition min ('from / out of', indicating origin or source) with the attached pronoun -hu ('it' / 'him'), referring to a singular masculine thing or person. As object of the preposition, the pronoun is in the oblique form.
16.root: — (no triliteral root; a preposition with a pronoun)

17.meaning: A noun meaning 'grain / seed / kernel' — the seed-grains of cereals and the like, used collectively.
17.grammar: A collective singular noun. The -an ending (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('grain,' not 'the grain') and accusative, the case that commonly identifies the direct object of a verb.

18.meaning: An active participle meaning 'piled up / layered upon one another / densely packed' — describing things mounted or stacked one over the other.
18.grammar: An active participle (form VI), a pattern expressing mutual or reciprocal action — here, parts piled and overlapping each other. The mu- prefix forms the 'one doing/being' the action. The -an ending marks it indefinite and accusative, often serving as a descriptive (circumstantial) term: '(being) clustered together.'
18.root: ر-ك-ب (r-k-b) — mounting, riding, layering one thing on another

19.meaning: A connector meaning 'and', joined to the preposition 'from / of', introducing a portion or origin — 'and from' or 'and among'.
19.grammar: Two particles: wa- ('and') plus the preposition min ('from, of, among'). Min normally appears as 'min', but its final vowel shifts to 'mina' when the next word begins with the definite article, simply to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.
19.root: — (particles)

20.meaning: A noun meaning 'the date-palm' — the palm tree, used collectively for date-palms.
20.grammar: A definite collective noun ('the date-palms'). The l of 'al-' assimilates into the following n (so it is pronounced 'an-nakhl'). The -i ending is genitive, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …') or follows a preposition.
20.root: ن-خ-ل (n-kh-l) — date-palm

21.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
21.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
21.root: — (preposition)

22.meaning: A noun with attached pronoun meaning 'its spadix / its pollen-sheath' — the budding flower-cluster of the date-palm from which the fruit emerges. With the suffix: 'its spathe.'

parts.en: spadix, emerging flower-sheath of the palm (stem)

22.grammar: A noun with a possessive pronoun. The -hā ending means 'its/her,' showing possession ('its spadix'). The -i vowel before it is genitive, the case taken after a preposition or when one noun is possessed by/linked to another.
22.root: ط-ل-ع (ṭ-l-ʿ) — rising, emerging, coming up (as the sun rises or a bud appears)

23.meaning: A noun meaning 'clusters / bunches (of dates)' — the hanging date-bunches of the palm.
23.grammar: A plural noun. The -un ending (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('clusters,' not 'the clusters') and nominative, the case that commonly identifies the subject of a sentence or the thing being described as existing.
23.root: ق-ن-و (q-n-w) — a cluster or bunch of dates

24.meaning: An active participle meaning 'near / close / drawing near' — describing something that hangs low and within reach, or comes close.
24.grammar: A feminine active participle ('one that is near/low'). The -at(un) combines a feminine marker with the -un (tanwīn) ending, which is indefinite and nominative — the case for the subject or a thing described as existing.
24.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, drawing close, being low/within reach

25.meaning: A noun meaning 'and gardens' — lush, walled enclosures of trees and greenery; a place of abundant growth.
25.grammar: A feminine plural noun prefixed with wa- ('and'). The -in ending (tanwīn) marks it indefinite ('gardens,' not 'the gardens') and genitive — the case taken after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of …').
25.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — covering, concealing; hence a garden whose foliage covers the ground

26.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
26.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

27.meaning: A noun meaning 'grapevines / grapes' — the plural of the grape-cluster, vines bearing grapes.
27.grammar: A plural noun (the broken plural of 'grape/vine'). The -in ending (tanwīn) marks it indefinite and genitive — the case used after a preposition or to link it to a preceding noun ('… of grapes').

28.meaning: A noun meaning 'and the olive(s) / the olive tree' — the olive, used collectively for olives and the olive tree.
28.grammar: A definite collective noun prefixed with wa- ('and'). The l of 'al-' assimilates into the following z (pronounced 'az-zaytūn'). The -a ending is accusative, the case that commonly marks a direct object — the thing acted upon.
28.root: ز-ي-ت (z-y-t) — olive, olive oil

29.meaning: A noun meaning 'and the pomegranate(s)' — the pomegranate fruit and tree, used collectively.
29.grammar: A definite collective noun prefixed with wa- ('and'). The l of 'al-' assimilates into the following r (pronounced 'ar-rummān'). The -a ending is accusative, the case that typically marks the direct object of a verb.

30.meaning: An active participle meaning 'alike / resembling one another / similar in appearance' — things that look like each other.
30.grammar: An active participle (form VIII), 'one that resembles (another).' The mu- prefix forms the 'one being/doing.' The -an ending (tanwīn) marks it indefinite and accusative, frequently used here as a descriptive (circumstantial) term: '(being) alike.'

31.meaning: A noun meaning 'other than / not / different from' — used to negate or set apart, indicating something contrary to or distinct from what is mentioned.
31.grammar: A noun of exception/negation meaning 'other than,' prefixed with wa- ('and'). It is followed by another noun in the genitive ('other than …'). The -a ending here is accusative, the case marking a direct object or a noun governed in that position.

32.meaning: An active participle meaning 'mutually resembling / alike one another / similar' — things that correspond to and look like each other.
32.grammar: An active participle (form VI), a pattern of mutual/reciprocal action: 'resembling each other.' The mu- prefix forms the 'one being/doing.' The -in ending (tanwīn) marks it indefinite and genitive — the case taken after 'other than' (ghayr) or a preposition, or when linked to a preceding noun.

33.meaning: A command meaning 'look! / observe! / consider!' — an order directed at a group to direct their gaze or attention toward something and reflect on it.
33.grammar: An imperative (command) verb. The -ū ending directs the command at a masculine plural audience, 'you all (look!).' (The trailing alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention.) Often paired with the preposition 'to/at' to mean 'look at / consider.'

34.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
34.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

35.meaning: A noun with attached pronoun meaning 'its fruit / its produce' — the fruit or yield of a tree or plant. With the suffix: 'its fruit.'
35.grammar: A noun with a possessive pronoun. The -hi ending means 'its/his,' showing possession ('its fruit'). The -i vowel signals the genitive case (which is also why the pronoun appears as -hi rather than -hu) — the case taken after a preposition or when one noun is possessed by another.

36.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
36.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.

37.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'it bore fruit / it produced fruit' — when a tree or plant brings forth its fruit.
37.grammar: A perfect (past-tense) verb in the causative (form IV) pattern, here meaning 'to bring forth fruit.' It carries no separable subject suffix: the bare form, ending in the inherent short -a vowel of the stem, already denotes a third-person masculine singular subject, 'he/it (did).'

38.meaning: A noun with attached pronoun meaning 'its ripening / its becoming ripe' — the maturing of fruit to fullness. With the suffix: 'its ripeness.'
38.grammar: A verbal noun with a possessive pronoun, prefixed with wa- ('and'). The -hi ending means 'its,' showing possession ('its ripening'). The -i vowel marks the genitive case (which also causes the pronoun to appear as -hi) — the case taken after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun.

39.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
39.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

40.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
40.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

41.meaning: A demonstrative meaning 'that' addressed to a group of people (plural 'you'). It points to something at a distance — whether physical, or to a previously mentioned matter — and is directed at multiple listeners.
41.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun for something distant. The base 'dhā' carries the sense 'that', the 'li' is an element of distance, and the ending '-kum' tells you the speaker is addressing a plural 'you' — it specifies the audience, not the thing pointed at. It does not change for case.

42.meaning: Surely signs, tokens, or clear indications; evidences that point to a greater truth. The prefixed lām adds emphasis ('surely / indeed').
42.grammar: An emphatic particle 'la-' ('surely') joined to an indefinite feminine plural noun ('signs'). The -āt- is the sound feminine plural marker; the final -in (nunation) marks it indefinite. For this plural pattern the -in form serves for both the accusative and the genitive case.

43.meaning: For a people, for a folk or community; a group of human beings considered together. Joined to the preposition 'li' ('for / to').
43.grammar: The preposition 'li' ('for / to') plus an indefinite singular noun ('a people'). The -in ending (nunation) marks indefiniteness; it is the genitive form, required because nouns governed by 'li' stand in the genitive.
43.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a people/community

44.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'they believe / they have faith' — to trust and affirm with the heart, to hold something true and place one's security in it.
44.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb built on the form IV pattern, which here functions intransitively, 'to have faith / to believe' (not a causative making someone else believe). The yu- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they.' The full -ūna ending (indicative mood) presents the action as ongoing or habitual fact: 'they (do) believe.'

1.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'and they made / they set up / they appointed' — to make something into something, to render or establish it.
1.grammar: A perfect (past-tense) verb prefixed with wa- ('and'). The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (did).' (The trailing alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention.) The verb often takes two objects, in the sense 'to make X into Y.'

2.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to', 'for', or 'belonging to', attached to the name 'Allah'. It conveys 'to Allah' or 'for Allah'.
2.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to/for') pulls the following noun into the genitive case, which is why 'Allah' ends in '-i' (llāhi). The '-i' ending is the regular result of a noun governed by a preposition.

3.meaning: Associates, partners, or co-sharers — those set up as participants alongside another in ownership, authority, or worship. In theological usage it denotes rivals falsely placed beside Allah.
3.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of sharīk ('partner'), following the pattern faʿalāʾ. This pattern is a diptote, so it takes no nunation. The word is in the accusative case, marked by the short -a vowel on the word-final hamzah (آءَ); that hamzah is part of the plural pattern itself and cannot be split off as a separate ending. The accusative is the case typically used for the direct object of a verb ('they made/claimed partners') or after certain particles.

4.meaning: The jinn — a class of unseen beings created from smokeless fire, possessing free will and accountability like humans, capable of both good and evil. The word denotes that which is hidden or concealed from ordinary sight.
4.grammar: A collective noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -a is the accusative ending, marking it as the object of a verb or as a noun following certain particles.

5.meaning: 'And He created them' — a past-tense statement that the act of bringing into existence was done by a single masculine agent (He), with the created beings (them) as its object.
5.grammar: wa is the connector 'and'. khalaqa is a past-tense verb; the -a ending on the stem marks third-person masculine singular ('he'). The suffix -hum is the attached object pronoun 'them' (masculine plural).

6.meaning: 'And they fabricated/falsely attributed' — past tense for a plural group inventing or forging something untrue. The root carries the sense of tearing or piercing, hence concocting a baseless claim out of nothing.
6.grammar: wa is 'and'. kharaqa is the past-tense verb stem; the suffix -ū (written وۡا) marks third-person masculine plural ('they fabricated'). The written alif after the wāw is silent (a spelling convention for the plural ending).
6.root: خ-ر-ق (kh-r-q) — to tear, rend, pierce; to fabricate

7.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
7.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

8.meaning: Sons — male children or offspring.
8.grammar: A sound masculine plural of ibn ('son'). The full -īna ending (يۡنَ) is the oblique form of the masculine sound plural — used for both the accusative (object) and genitive cases — as opposed to the nominative -ūna (وۡنَ). The whole suffix -īna, not just the final vowel, carries the case marking.

9.meaning: 'And daughters' — female children or offspring.
9.grammar: wa is 'and'. banāt is the sound feminine plural of bint ('daughter'). The final -in is the indefinite ending with nunation (tanwīn). Sound feminine plurals do not distinguish the accusative from the genitive — both use this -ātin form — so here, coordinated with the preceding accusative object (banīna 'sons'), it is likewise accusative.

10.meaning: 'Without' or 'other than' — the preposition bi- joined to ghayr, a noun meaning 'other than / not / lacking', together conveying the absence of something ('with no …', 'wrongfully').
10.grammar: bi- is a preposition that takes the genitive; ghayr is a noun of exception/negation ('other than'). Its -i ending is genitive (required after bi-) and it also links to a following noun in a possessive 'of' relationship, so 'bi-ghayri X' means 'without X / other than X'.
10.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — otherness, difference, being other than

11.meaning: 'Knowledge.' A noun denoting sure, established knowing — to know a thing as it truly is. In its indefinite form it often appears in the sense 'any knowledge (at all).'
11.grammar: A noun with the -in ending (genitive with nunation, 'tanwīn'), marking it as indefinite ('any knowledge'). The genitive -i is the form used after a preposition such as 'of' or 'by' — e.g. 'of any knowledge.'
11.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; knowledge, certainty

12.meaning: An exclamation of glorification meaning 'far removed and utterly above all imperfection is He.' The verbal noun 'subḥān' declares that the One referred to is exalted beyond any deficiency, partner, or fault, and the attached 'Him' directs that declaration to a single masculine being.
12.grammar: A verbal noun used as an absolute exclamation, fixed in the accusative ending -a (an emphatic declaration, roughly 'I declare His utter transcendence'). The attached -hu is the possessive/object pronoun 'Him', referring to one masculine person.
12.root: س-ب-ح (s-b-ḥ) — to swim/glide away, hence to declare Allah free of all imperfection

13.meaning: 'And He is exalted/transcendent high above' — to be far above and beyond, used of Allah being utterly lofty and removed from any deficiency or false attribution.
13.grammar: wa is 'and'. taʿālā is a past-tense verb (form VI) functioning as an exclamation of glorification; its final long -ā marks third-person masculine singular ('He'). The form intensifies the root sense to 'be supremely high, transcendent'.
13.root: ع-ل-و (ʿ-l-w) — to be high, lofty, exalted

14.meaning: 'About what' / 'of that which' — the preposition 'ʿan' ('about, concerning, away from') merged with 'mā' ('what, that which').
14.grammar: A fusion of the preposition 'ʿan' ('about, concerning') with the relative/interrogative 'mā' ('what'); the 'n' of 'ʿan' assimilates into 'mā' to give 'ʿammā'. It introduces the thing being spoken about.

15.meaning: 'They describe/ascribe' — present-tense action of a plural group characterizing or attributing qualities to something, often implying claims that may be untrue.
15.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks third-person masculine plural ('they describe/ascribe'). The full -ūna ending also signals the indicative mood (a plain, factual statement).

1.meaning: The Originator who brings things into existence with no prior model — One who creates utterly afresh, fashioning the unprecedented out of nothing.
1.grammar: An intensive noun/adjective on the 'faʿīl' pattern, here in the nominative ending -u, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or a noun standing first in a possessive chain ('the Originator of …'). The pattern conveys an inherent, characteristic quality of creating without precedent.
1.root: ب-د-ع (b-d-ʿ) — to originate or innovate something wholly new

2.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
2.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

3.meaning: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
3.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.

4.meaning: A particle/adverb meaning 'in whatever manner,' 'from wherever,' or 'whenever' — it asks or denotes the how, where, or when of an action in an open-ended way.
4.grammar: An invariable interrogative/conditional adverb; it has no case ending and never changes form. It introduces the manner, place, or time of an action in a general, open sense ('in what way / from where / when').

5.meaning: 'It is / it comes to be' — the present-tense verb of being and becoming (from kāna). It expresses that something is the case, exists, or comes about.
5.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he/it is, becomes'. The ya- prefix means 'he/it', and the final -u is the indicative ending, marking a plain factual statement (as opposed to a command or a negated/subjunctive form).
5.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

6.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
6.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

7.meaning: 'A child / a boy / offspring' — a son or child, the offspring born to a parent.
7.grammar: A noun. The -un ending is nominative with tanwīn (nunation — the doubled 'n' sound marking an indefinite noun, 'a child'). The nominative case marks it as the subject of a sentence or as a noun whose existence is being affirmed or denied. The initial wa- here is part of the root (w-l-d), not the conjunction 'and'.
7.root: و-ل-د (w-l-d) — to give birth, beget; offspring

8.meaning: A two-part particle: the connector 'and' joined to 'lam', the negating word that turns a following present-tense verb into a completed past negation — 'and … did not'.

parts.en: did not (negates and puts the verb in the past)

8.grammar: Connector 'wa' ('and') plus the particle 'lam'. 'lam' negates a present-tense verb but shifts its meaning to the past, so 'lam + he finds' means 'he did not find'. It also puts the following verb into the jussive mood (clipping its ending).

9.meaning: A short (jussive) form of the verb 'to be / to become', meaning 'be' or 'does not become / is not'. It expresses being, existing, or coming to be in a clipped form that typically follows a particle such as a negator or a command.
9.grammar: Present-tense verb with the ta- prefix marking a second-person masculine singular ('you') or third-person feminine singular ('it/she') subject. The clipped final consonant (sukun, no vowel) is the jussive/apocopated mood, the form used after negative particles ('did not / was not') or as a command or prohibition.
9.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

10.meaning: A two-part phrase 'for Him' or 'to Him belongs,' expressing possession, ownership, or that something is due to one masculine being.
10.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('for/to/belonging to') with its vowel shifted to 'la-' before the pronoun. The attached -hu means 'Him', so the whole means 'for Him' or 'His'; the preposition signals possession or that something is owed or directed to that person.

11.meaning: A female companion, consort, or wife — a woman who accompanies or is paired with someone.
11.grammar: An active-participle noun with the feminine ending -at. The final -un is nominative case with nunation (tanwīn), marking an indefinite noun ('a companion') in the subject/predicate case — the form a noun takes as the subject or after 'there is'.
11.root: ص-ح-ب (ṣ-ḥ-b) — to accompany, befriend, keep company

12.meaning: 'And He created' — a past-tense statement that the act of originating was performed by a single masculine agent (He).
12.grammar: wa is 'and'. khalaqa is a past-tense verb; the final -a marks third-person masculine singular ('he created').
12.root: خ-ل-ق (kh-l-q) — to create, originate, shape

13.meaning: All, every, the whole of — totality. When followed by a singular it means 'every (one)'; when followed by a definite plural or whole it means 'all of.'
13.grammar: A noun of totality, almost always joined to a following noun in the genitive ('every … / all of …'). The final -a is the accusative case, the form used when the word functions as an object of a verb.

14.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
14.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
14.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

15.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
15.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

16.meaning: 'Of every / with all' — the preposition 'bi' ('with / in / by') joined to the word 'every / each / all', expressing comprehensiveness applied to whatever noun follows.
16.grammar: A preposition plus a noun. The prefix bi- ('with / in / by') always places the following noun in the genitive ('of') state. The final -i on 'kull' is that genitive ending, signalling the word is governed by the preposition. 'Kull' denotes totality — 'every (single)' or 'all'.

17.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
17.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
17.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

18.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'All-Knowing / fully aware' — one whose knowledge is complete, deep, and all-encompassing; as a divine attribute it denotes Allah's perfect knowledge.
18.grammar: An intensive adjective (the pattern faʿīl conveys 'thoroughly, abundantly'). The ending -un is the indefinite nominative — the nominative case marks it as the subject or the quality being affirmed, and the -n (nunation) signals 'a / an', i.e. indefinite. So it reads '(is) all-knowing'.

1.meaning: A demonstrative meaning 'that' — a pointing word that singles out something distant or already mentioned, addressed to a group of people ('that, O you [plural]').
1.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that', built from the base 'dhā' plus the distance-marker 'l-' and the plural-addressee particle '-kum' ('you all'). The final 'u' on '-kumu' is a connecting vowel used when the next word begins with a definite article. It does not change for case.

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
2.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

3.meaning: Your (plural) Lord — 'Rabb' means the Master, Owner, Sustainer, and Nurturer who creates, provides for, and brings a thing to its completion. It combines lordship with loving upbringing and care.
3.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The suffix '-kum' means 'your' (plural possessor). The '-u' on 'rabbu' before the suffix is the nominative case, marking the word as a subject or as a predicate standing on its own.
3.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, master, sustain, own

4.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
4.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

5.meaning: God / object of worship — a deity that is worshipped. The bare noun names the concept of a worshipped god.
5.grammar: A singular noun carrying an -a ending. This short -a typically marks the accusative (object) case; it is also the form a noun takes immediately after the absolute-negation particle 'lā' to mean 'no … (at all).'
5.root: أ-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, worship, being a deity

6.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
6.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

7.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
7.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

8.meaning: Creator, Originator, Maker — the one who brings things into existence and gives them their form. As a title of Allah it denotes the sole Author of all that exists.
8.grammar: An active participle ('one who creates') used as a noun. The final -u is the nominative ending, the case typically marking the subject of a sentence or a noun standing on its own. Often heads a possessive phrase ('Creator OF …').

9.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
9.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

10.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
10.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
10.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

11.meaning: 'So worship Him' — a directive to a group to serve, devote themselves to, and humbly submit in worship to Him.
11.grammar: fa- is a connector meaning 'so' or 'then', often drawing a consequence. The stem is a command (imperative) verb; the -ū ending addresses a masculine/mixed plural ('you all do it'). The final -hu is the object pronoun 'him/it', so the whole means 'so worship Him'.
11.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to worship, to serve, to devote oneself

12.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
12.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

13.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
13.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

14.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
14.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

15.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
15.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
15.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

16.meaning: A trustee, guardian, or disposer of affairs — one entrusted to manage, oversee, and take charge of matters on another's behalf. As a divine attribute it conveys Allah's complete care and management of all things.
16.grammar: An intensive noun of the faʿīl pattern. The final -un is nominative case with nunation (tanwīn), marking an indefinite noun ('a guardian') in the subject/predicate case. (The doubled w- reflects assimilation with a preceding word in recitation.)
16.root: و-ك-ل (w-k-l) — to entrust, rely upon, appoint as agent

1.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
1.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

2.meaning: 'It grasps/perceives Him' — present tense for a feminine or non-rational-plural subject overtaking, reaching, comprehending, or catching up with a masculine object (Him).
2.grammar: A present-tense verb (form IV, 'to attain/perceive'). The tu- prefix marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('it/she grasps') — also used for non-human plurals. The suffix -hu is the attached object pronoun 'him'.
2.root: د-ر-ك (d-r-k) — to reach, attain, overtake, perceive

3.meaning: Sights, visions, or eyes — the faculties of seeing, or the eyes as organs of perception. The plural of baṣar ('sight, vision').
3.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of baṣar, with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -u is the nominative ending, the case typically marking the subject of a sentence.
3.root: ب-ص-ر (b-ṣ-r) — to see, perceive, have insight

4.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
4.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

5.meaning: 'He grasps/perceives' — present tense for a single masculine agent overtaking, reaching, comprehending, or apprehending something.
5.grammar: A present-tense verb (form IV). The yu- prefix marks third-person masculine singular ('he grasps/perceives'). The final -u marks the indicative mood (a plain, factual statement).
5.root: د-ر-ك (d-r-k) — to reach, attain, overtake, perceive

6.meaning: Sights, visions, or eyes — the faculties or organs of seeing. The plural of baṣar ('sight, vision').
6.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of baṣar, with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -a is the accusative ending, the case typically marking the direct object of a verb.
6.root: ب-ص-ر (b-ṣ-r) — to see, perceive, have insight

7.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
7.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

8.meaning: The Subtle, the Most Gentle and Finely-Aware — one whose knowledge and kindness penetrate to the most delicate, hidden details, acting with imperceptible gentleness. A divine attribute combining subtlety of perception with graciousness of care.
8.grammar: An intensive adjective of the faʿīl pattern with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -u is the nominative ending, the case typically marking the subject or a noun standing on its own.
8.root: ل-ط-ف (l-ṭ-f) — to be subtle, gentle, kind, refined

9.meaning: 'The All-Aware', 'the Well-Acquainted' — the one possessing thorough, intimate knowledge of the inner reality of things, fully informed of what is hidden as well as what is open.
9.grammar: A definite intensive adjective (a 'one who is deeply X' pattern: thoroughly aware). The -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject of a sentence or a word standing as the main topic/predicate.
9.root: خ-ب-ر (kh-b-r) — knowledge, inner acquaintance, being informed

1.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.

2.meaning: "he/it came to you" — a past verb "came" with the pronoun "you" as the one reached, i.e. something arrived at or reached a group of people.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb in its base third-person masculine singular form ("he/it came"), with no extra subject suffix. The verb "to come" is intransitive, so the attached -kum is not a direct object but an indirect (dative) pronoun — "to you" (masculine plural), equivalent to "came to you (all)."

3.meaning: Insights, clear proofs, or means of perception — things that bring inner sight and discernment, enabling one to see truth clearly. The plural of baṣīra ('inner vision, insight').
3.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of baṣīra, following the diptote pattern. The final -u is the nominative ending, the case typically marking the subject or a noun standing on its own. (As a diptote, this plural pattern does not take nunation.)
3.root: ب-ص-ر (b-ṣ-r) — to see, perceive, have insight

4.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
4.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

5.meaning: 'Your Lord' (addressing a group). 'Rabb' is a rich term: the Master, Owner, Sustainer and Nurturer who creates, possesses, provides for, and brings a thing to its proper completion — far more than a mere ruler.
5.grammar: A noun ('Lord') with an attached possessive pronoun, forming a possessive pairing. 'Rabb' carries a doubled (geminated) 'b' — the shaddah — at its core. The '-i' vowel on 'rabb' is its case ending, determined by 'Lord's' own role in the sentence (not by the suffix); the attached '-kum' is the possessor ('your'), addressing a plural 'you', and as the possessed-to term it sits in the genitive.

6.meaning: A compound meaning 'then whoever' or 'so whoever'. It combines 'then/so' with the conditional/relative 'who', introducing whatever person meets a stated condition.
6.grammar: The connector fa- ('then/so', often answering or following a condition) joined to man ('whoever / the one who'), which refers to people and introduces a condition: 'whoever does X…'. man does not change its ending; the clause after it supplies the rest of the meaning.

7.meaning: 'He saw / gained sight / perceived clearly' — past tense for a single masculine agent coming to see or perceive, with the sense of attaining vision or insight.
7.grammar: A past-tense verb (form IV, which makes the root mean 'to come to see, gain sight'). The final -a marks third-person masculine singular ('he saw/perceived').
7.root: ب-ص-ر (b-ṣ-r) — to see, perceive, have insight

8.meaning: 'Then it is for his own self/soul' — introducing a consequence that the benefit accrues to a person's own self. The nafs is the inner self, soul, or person — the seat of one's individual being.
8.grammar: fa means 'then/so' (a connective showing result). li- is the preposition 'for/to (the benefit of)', which puts the following noun in the genitive. The -i ending is genitive (required after li-). The suffix -hi is the attached possessive pronoun 'his'.

9.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
9.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

10.meaning: 'He was/became blind' — past tense for a single masculine agent losing sight, literally or figuratively (failing to perceive truth).
10.grammar: A past-tense verb. The final -a (after the stem ʿamiy-) marks third-person masculine singular ('he was/became blind').
10.root: ع-م-ي (ʿ-m-y) — to be blind, to lack sight or insight

11.meaning: 'Then it is against it/her' — introducing a consequence that the harm or burden falls back upon the same party. The 'against' sense indicates a liability or detriment borne by the subject.
11.grammar: fa means 'then/so' (showing result). ʿalā is the preposition 'upon/against', here carrying the sense of detriment or liability. The suffix -hā is the attached pronoun 'it/her' (feminine singular), referring to a grammatically feminine antecedent such as nafs ('soul').
11.root: — (preposition + pronoun; no triliteral root)

12.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
12.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
12.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

13.meaning: I — the standalone pronoun used to declare or emphasize the speaker himself as the one in view.
13.grammar: A detached first-person singular pronoun ("I"). Being an independent pronoun, it has a fixed form with no case ending; it is used to state or stress who the subject is.

14.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
14.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

15.meaning: A keeper, guardian, or watchful overseer — one who preserves, protects, and keeps careful watch, maintaining a vigilant record over something.
15.grammar: bi- is a preposition ('with/over') which here often reinforces a negated predicate ('not a guardian over…'), and it puts the following noun in the genitive. ḥafīẓ is an intensive noun of the faʿīl pattern. The -in ending is genitive case with nunation (tanwīn), marking an indefinite noun governed by the preposition.
15.root: ح-ف-ظ (ḥ-f-ẓ) — to guard, preserve, protect, keep watch

1.meaning: 'And likewise / and in the same way / and thus' — a connective phrase pointing back to a manner just mentioned and saying 'in that very way…'. Built from 'and' + 'like' + 'that'.
1.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'; the prefix ka- means 'like/as'; 'dhālika' is the demonstrative 'that' (pointing to something distant or already mentioned). Because ka- acts like a preposition, the word after it stands in the genitive, though the demonstrative 'dhālika' keeps a fixed form and shows no visible case change. The whole means 'and just like that / and thus'.

2.meaning: 'We expound / vary / set forth in diverse ways' — to turn a thing about and present it from many angles, repeating and varying signs or proofs so they are made clear. The form intensifies the plain verb 'to turn/redirect' into 'to vary repeatedly, to dispose in different ways'.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb with the 'nu-' prefix meaning 'we'. The doubled middle consonant marks the intensive pattern, giving the sense of doing the action thoroughly or repeatedly. The '-u' ending is the default present-tense form for an action that is ongoing or habitual.

3.meaning: 'The signs / the verses' — the plural of 'sign,' referring to clear indicators, proofs, miracles, or the verses of revelation that point to truth.
3.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun ('the signs'), made definite by the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The sound feminine plural takes the -i ending when it is an object of a verb or linked after a preposition or possessor — that is, when it is grammatically governed rather than serving as the subject.

4.meaning: 'And so that they may say' — introducing a purpose ('in order that they say') for a plural group's act of speaking or uttering.
4.grammar: wa is 'and'. li- here is the particle of purpose ('so that/in order that'), which puts the verb in the subjunctive mood. The ya- prefix with the plural ending marks third-person masculine plural ('they say'); the ending appears as -ū (the subjunctive form, dropping the final -na of the indicative). The written alif after the wāw is silent.

5.meaning: You studied / you read and learned (a text). From a root for going over and reading a written text; the basic (Form I) verb means to study, read, or learn something, without any added 'teaching' or intensive sense.
5.grammar: A completed-action (past-tense) verb in the basic Form I pattern (middle letter not doubled). The suffix -ta marks a single male addressee: 'you (have) studied.' Past tense presents the action as already accomplished.
5.root: د-ر-س (d-r-s) — to study, read, learn (a text)

6.meaning: and so that We may make it clear / explain it plainly. Built on a doubled-letter stem meaning to render something distinct, evident, and fully spelled out, with an attached 'it' as the thing being clarified.
6.grammar: A present/imperfect verb of purpose. The prefix nu- means 'we.' The particle li- ('so that') puts the verb in the subjunctive, shown by the final -a vowel on the stem, expressing intended aim ('in order that We make clear'). The ending -hu is an attached object pronoun 'it/him.'

7.meaning: 'For a people / for a folk' — directed toward a community or group of human beings considered collectively.
7.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('for/to') joined to a noun 'people.' Because it follows a preposition, the noun takes the genitive, and the tanwīn (the -in ending) marks it as indefinite ('a people'). The whole phrase means 'for a people,' directing something toward that group.
7.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand/rise; a people, community

8.meaning: They know; they have knowledge, understanding, or awareness of something. The verb denotes possessing knowledge as an ongoing state.
8.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'). The ya- prefix marks the subject and the -ūna ending marks a masculine plural in the ordinary (indicative) present tense, describing ongoing or habitual knowing.

1.meaning: Follow! / adhere to and walk behind. A command to pursue, conform to, and take as a guide, from a root meaning to come after and accompany something step by step.
1.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a single male: 'follow!' The final consonant carries no case vowel (it is jussive in form), which is normal for a direct order. The initial i- is a connecting vowel that helps pronounce the cluster at the start.
1.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, come after, pursue

2.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

3.meaning: It has been revealed / inspired — divine communication has been sent down or conveyed (to someone). A passive verb: the focus is on the message being given, with the Giver understood rather than named.
3.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) passive verb (form IV). The opening vowelling marks it as passive ('it was/has been done to it'), and the ending denotes a third-person masculine singular subject — the thing revealed. Being passive, the doer (the Revealer) is left unstated. The long u of the prefix is formed by the damma plus the waw; the bare stem consonant carries -hi-.
3.root: و-ح-ى (w-h-y) — revelation, divine inspiration, conveying a message

4.meaning: 'To you' (addressing one person): indicating direction or motion toward a single individual — that toward which something moves or is directed.
4.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to, towards') with an attached pronoun; before a suffix ilā takes the form ilay-. The -ka ending is the pronoun 'you' for a single male addressee. Pronouns following a preposition stand in the genitive relationship, though their form does not visibly change for case.

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

6.meaning: The Lord belonging to a single male 'you' — Rabb is the Master, Owner, and Sustainer who creates, nurtures, and brings to maturity; here 'your Lord'.
6.grammar: The noun rabb (Lord, Sustainer) with the attached pronoun -ka, 'your' for one male. The -i ending before the pronoun is genitive, the case that typically links a word to a following possessor or follows a preposition (here showing the possession 'of you'). The doubled b (shadda) belongs to the root.

7.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
7.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

8.meaning: God / object of worship — a deity that is worshipped. The bare noun names the concept of a worshipped god.
8.grammar: A singular noun carrying an -a ending. This short -a typically marks the accusative (object) case; it is also the form a noun takes immediately after the absolute-negation particle 'lā' to mean 'no … (at all).'
8.root: أ-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, worship, being a deity

9.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
9.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

10.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
10.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

11.meaning: and turn away / avert yourself, disregard. A command to draw back from something and present one's side to it rather than engaging, from a root tied to a 'side' and to turning aside.
11.grammar: A command (imperative) to a single male: 'turn away!' The final consonant takes no case vowel (jussive form), which is standard for an order. The a- at the start is the command prefix of this verb pattern.
11.root: ع-ر-ض (ʿ-r-ḍ) — side, breadth; turning aside, presenting/averting

12.meaning: About / concerning; a particle marking the topic of inquiry or the thing one moves away from.
12.grammar: A preposition meaning 'about, concerning, away from'. Its base form is ʿan; the final -i here is a helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a connecting 'al-'. It governs the genitive case on whatever noun follows.

13.meaning: Those who associate partners with Allah — idolaters / polytheists who set up others alongside the one God in worship or devotion.
13.grammar: An active participle used as a noun, with 'the', in the masculine sound plural. The -īna ending marks the plural in the genitive/accusative case — the form used after a preposition or as the object of a verb.

1.meaning: 'and if' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle 'if'. This particular 'if' (law) introduces a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact condition: 'if (such-and-such had been the case)…', often implying it was not.
1.grammar: A conjunction plus a conditional particle. wa- means 'and'. law is a non-changing particle (no case ending) that sets up a supposition, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('… then certainly …').

2.meaning: A past-tense verb 'he willed / he wished / he so desired'. It denotes an act of will or volition bringing something about.
2.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third person masculine singular ('he'). The bare stem with no suffix is the basic 'he did' form. Its subject and object are typically supplied by context.

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
3.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

4.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
4.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

5.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'they associated partners / they set up partners (with Allah)' — to ascribe partners or equals to Allah, the act underlying idolatry and polytheism.
5.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb in a pattern meaning 'to make (someone) a partner'. The ending -ū marks a masculine-plural subject, 'they', so it reads 'they associated partners (with Allah)'.

6.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
6.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

7.meaning: We made you / We appointed you / We rendered you (such-and-such). From a root meaning to make, set, place, or designate; with an attached 'you,' it conveys 'We caused you to be' or 'We assigned you.'
7.grammar: A completed-action (past-tense) verb. The suffix -nā marks the doer as 'we'; the further suffix -ka is the object 'you (one male).' Past tense presents the making/appointing as already done.
7.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, set, place, render, appoint

8.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
8.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
8.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

9.meaning: Noun/intensive adjective meaning 'a guardian,' 'keeper,' 'protector,' or 'one who preserves and watches over' — one who guards carefully and keeps everything safe and accounted for.
9.grammar: An intensive noun/adjective (faʿīl pattern) denoting one who does the act thoroughly — a vigilant guardian. The final '-an' (tanwīn fatḥa) is indefinite accusative — the case often used for a direct object or, as commonly with this word, to express the capacity 'as a guardian.'
9.root: ح-ف-ظ (ḥ-f-ẓ) — to guard, preserve, protect, keep safe

10.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
10.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

11.meaning: 'You' — the standalone, independent pronoun for addressing a single male person directly.
11.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, second-person masculine singular. Unlike attached pronoun suffixes, it stands alone and is typically used to identify or emphasize the subject ('you [yourself]').

12.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
12.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
12.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

13.meaning: A guardian, trustee, or one put in charge to manage another's affairs; a disposer of matters, an agent responsible for and relied upon to handle things. The prefixed bi- often serves to reinforce a preceding negation ('not a guardian at all').
13.grammar: A noun in the pattern of an intensive agent ('one entrusted/relied upon'), preceded by the preposition bi- ('with/as'). The ending -in is genitive and indefinite (the 'n' is nunation, marking 'a/an'): the genitive case is required after the preposition bi-.

1.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
1.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

2.meaning: (that) you (all) insult / revile / verbally abuse. From a root meaning to speak ill of, curse, or hurl reproach at someone.
2.grammar: A present/imperfect verb addressed to a plural 'you.' The prefix ta- plus the ending -ū together mark a masculine plural subject. The -ū ending (with the normally-present final nūn dropped) signals that the verb is in a dependent mood, typically after a particle such as 'do not' or 'lest.'
2.root: س-ب-ب (s-b-b) — to insult, revile, curse, abuse

3.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
3.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

4.meaning: 'They call / invite / summon' — to call upon, invite, or summon (also to pray to or call out to); a present-tense verb with a masculine-plural subject.
4.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb, 3rd-person masculine plural ('they call/invite'). The ya- prefix with the full -ūna ending marks 'they (men) do' and shows the indicative mood — the plain statement form ('they do'), with its final nūn intact (contrast the jussive/subjunctive, where it drops).
4.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, summon, invite, pray

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

6.meaning: A noun used to mean 'besides', 'other than', 'apart from', or 'short of'. It points to something or someone set apart from, or lower/lesser than, a named party. Often used in the phrase 'besides Allah'.
6.grammar: 'dūn' functions as an adverb-like noun of place/relation. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, which appears because it follows a preposition (such as 'min', 'from') and because it links to a following noun ('other than …'). It commonly heads the construction 'besides/other than [someone]'.
6.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be low/beneath, to fall short; hence 'below, other than, besides'

7.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
7.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

8.meaning: so that they would then insult / lest they revile in return. The 'and/so' prefix carries a sense of consequence ('and then,' 'so that as a result'), joined to a verb of reviling done by 'they.'
8.grammar: A present/imperfect verb with the prefix ya- and ending -ū marking a masculine plural 'they.' The -ū (with the usual final nūn dropped) shows a dependent mood: the connector fa- ('so/then') introduces a result, putting the verb in the subjunctive ('so that they would revile').
8.root: س-ب-ب (s-b-b) — to insult, revile, curse, abuse

9.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
9.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

10.meaning: out of enmity / as hostile transgression. A noun denoting aggression, wrongful overstepping, and hostile excess against another.
10.grammar: An indefinite noun with the -an ending. This ending most often marks the accusative case, here functioning adverbially to express manner or cause — i.e., 'in/through enmity,' 'as an act of hostility.'
10.root: ع-د-و (ʿ-d-w) — to overstep, transgress; enmity, hostility

11.meaning: 'Without' or 'other than' — the preposition bi- joined to ghayr, a noun meaning 'other than / not / lacking', together conveying the absence of something ('with no …', 'wrongfully').
11.grammar: bi- is a preposition that takes the genitive; ghayr is a noun of exception/negation ('other than'). Its -i ending is genitive (required after bi-) and it also links to a following noun in a possessive 'of' relationship, so 'bi-ghayri X' means 'without X / other than X'.
11.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — otherness, difference, being other than

12.meaning: 'Knowledge.' A noun denoting sure, established knowing — to know a thing as it truly is. In its indefinite form it often appears in the sense 'any knowledge (at all).'
12.grammar: A noun with the -in ending (genitive with nunation, 'tanwīn'), marking it as indefinite ('any knowledge'). The genitive -i is the form used after a preposition such as 'of' or 'by' — e.g. 'of any knowledge.'
12.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; knowledge, certainty

13.meaning: 'Like that / thus / in this manner.' A comparison word meaning that something is done or is the case in the way just mentioned.
13.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like/as') prefixed to the demonstrative 'that'. Together they form a fixed adverbial expression, 'like that / thus', which does not change its ending with grammatical position.
13.root: — (a particle of comparison joined to a demonstrative; no root)

14.meaning: We made (something) seem fair / We adorned and beautified it to the eye. From a root meaning to decorate, embellish, and make attractive — here causing a thing to appear pleasing or alluring.
14.grammar: A completed-action (past-tense) verb on an intensive doubled-letter pattern (to beautify, make attractive). The subject suffix is -nā ('we'). Because the verb stem itself ends in nūn, that nūn and the nūn of -nā merge into one doubled nūn in writing (zayyan + nā → zayyannā), so only the long -ā is visibly left after it; the suffix is still 'we.' Past tense presents the adorning as already accomplished.

15.meaning: For each, for every — combines the preposition 'for/to' with 'each/every (one)'. Kull expresses totality taken one by one.
15.grammar: The noun kull ('each/every/all') preceded by the preposition li- ('for'). The -i ending is genitive, the case regularly required after a preposition, and which also lets kull link to a following noun ('each OF …').

16.meaning: A community, nation, or people — a body of people bound together by shared faith, way of life, or origin; one collective group.
16.grammar: A feminine noun. The final -in (genitive with 'nunation') marks it as indefinite ('a community') and links it to a preceding noun or preposition ('… of a community'). The feminine -t sound surfaces before the ending.

17.meaning: their deed / their work, action, conduct. A noun for a thing done or labour performed, with an attached 'their.'
17.grammar: A noun carrying the -a ending, which typically marks the accusative case — often the object of a verb ('the deed'). The attached -hum means 'their (of them, masc. plural),' showing possession of the deed.
17.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deed, labour

18.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
18.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

19.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
19.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

20.meaning: 'Their Lord' — the base 'rabb' means Lord, Master, Sustainer: the one who owns, nurtures, governs, and brings to maturity. As a divine title it conveys Allah as Creator and Sustainer of all.
20.grammar: The noun 'rabb' ('Lord, Sustainer') with the attached pronoun '-him' ('their'). The '-i' before the pronoun is the genitive case, the form used after a preposition or, as in a possessive linkage, to show belonging ('of/their').
20.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, master, sustain; lordship

21.meaning: their return / their place and act of returning. A noun naming the destination or event of going back, with an attached 'their' — i.e., the point to which they go back.
21.grammar: A noun of place/event (formed on the ma- pattern, meaning the locus or occurrence of an action) carrying the -u ending, which typically marks the nominative case — the subject or the thing being identified. The attached -hum means 'their (masc. plural).'
21.root: ر-ج-ع (r-j-ʿ) — to return, go back, revert

22.meaning: so He will then inform them / announce to them the truth of a matter. The 'so/then' prefix joins to a verb meaning to give weighty news or notify, with an attached 'them.' The doubled-letter stem suggests full, emphatic disclosure.
22.grammar: A present/imperfect verb on an intensive doubled-letter pattern (to inform fully). The prefix yu- marks a single male subject 'he,' and the final -u vowel on the stem signals the plain indicative mood (a straightforward statement, 'he informs'). The attached -hum is the object 'them.' The fa- prefix means 'so/then.'
22.root: ن-ب-أ (n-b-ʾ) — weighty news, tidings; to inform, announce

23.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
23.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

24.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
24.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
24.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

25.meaning: 'They do / they work, they act' — a present-tense verb of doing and working, covering deeds and actions carried out by a group.
25.grammar: Present/imperfect verb. The ya-…-ūna frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (do).' The -ūna ending also marks the indicative mood, the plain statement form, as opposed to command or negated-future forms.
25.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds
