1.meaning: and they swore / took a solemn oath. From a root tied to dividing and apportioning, and so to swearing — calling something to witness in a binding vow.
1.grammar: A completed-action (past-tense) verb. The ending -ū marks a masculine plural subject 'they.' (The written alif after it is silent.) Past tense presents the oath as already made.
1.root: ق-س-م (q-s-m) — to divide, apportion; to swear an oath

2.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
2.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
2.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

3.meaning: Utmost effort, the full extent or strength of something; with 'oaths' it means the most solemn, strenuous oaths one can swear. The word denotes exertion pushed to its limit.
3.grammar: A noun in the accusative state (final -a). This case is taken by an object of a verb or, as often with this word, by a noun used adverbially or in a binding (genitive) construction with what follows — conveying 'with the utmost of …'.
3.root: ج-ه-د (j-h-d) — to strive, exert utmost effort

4.meaning: Their oaths; the solemn sworn pledges belonging to them. (The same plural form also serves the unrelated sense 'right hands', from which the oath sense derives, since oaths were sealed with the right hand.)
4.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural joined to the possessive pronoun -him ('their'). The -i vowel before the pronoun reflects the genitive state — the form taken when the noun follows a preposition or is bound to a preceding noun ('… of …'); -him marks the owners as a male/mixed group.
4.root: ي-م-ن (y-m-n) — right hand; hence oath, and good fortune

5.meaning: An emphatic conditional opener combining an oath-like emphasis with 'if' — roughly 'most certainly, if (such-and-such happens)…', strongly stressing the condition and the response that follows.
5.grammar: Two particles fused together: an emphatic la- that signals a coming oath or strong assertion, plus in ('if') introducing a condition. Together they set up an emphatic 'if… then surely…' construction. Neither has a case ending; particles do not inflect.

6.meaning: A verb meaning 'she/it came to them' — the act of coming or arriving, directed toward a group of people. Built on the verb 'to come,' with the comers' goal ('them') attached.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb 'came.' The -t suffix is the feminine marker, showing the subject is grammatically feminine ('she/it came') or a feminine plural such as 'messengers/signs.' The attached -hum is the object pronoun 'them' (a group of males or mixed).

7.meaning: A sign, token, or mark — and especially a 'verse' of revelation. It denotes a clear indicator that points to a deeper truth: a miracle, a proof, or a portion of revealed text.
7.grammar: A feminine noun in the nominative case with tanwīn (the -un ending), marking it as indefinite ('a sign') and typically the subject or doer of a sentence. The nominative shows it is acting or being identified rather than acted upon.

8.meaning: they will most certainly believe / surely give faith. A verb of believing, of having faith and trusting, wrapped in a double emphasis ('they shall indeed, without fail, believe').
8.grammar: A present/imperfect verb on the pattern meaning 'to have faith / believe in.' The opening la- is an emphatic 'surely,' and the heavy ending -nna is an emphasis suffix that makes the statement a forceful assertion of what will certainly happen. Note the prefix yu- by itself only marks a third-person form ('he believes'); the masculine plural subject 'they' is the long-vowel plural ending -ūna, whose wāw drops out before the heavy nūn of emphasis (yuʾminūna + nna → yuʾminunna), leaving no separate plural letter visible in the stem. So the plural 'they' is carried within this emphatic form.
8.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, trust; to have faith, believe, feel safe

9.meaning: with it / by it — a preposition meaning 'with' or 'by means of' joined to a pronoun referring to a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing.
9.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition meaning 'with', 'by', or 'by means of'. The attached -hā is an object pronoun meaning 'it' or 'her', referring to something feminine in gender. Together they mean 'with it' or 'by means of it'.

10.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
10.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

11.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
11.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

12.meaning: the signs / the clear tokens, evidences, or verses. The plural of a word meaning a sign that points to a truth — a marker, proof, or miracle; also a verse of revelation.
12.grammar: A feminine plural noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The -u ending typically marks the nominative case — the subject of a sentence or the thing being named/identified.
12.root: أ-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, token, mark, evidence

13.meaning: 'With / in the presence of / near' — an adverb of place and relation meaning at, by, in the sight or estimation of someone. It indicates nearness, possession, or what holds in someone's view (as in 'with Allah' = in His sight).
13.grammar: An adverb of place that is always followed by a noun it relates to. It carries a fixed -a ending; this accusative-type vowel is characteristic of such adverbs of place and shows the word is functioning to locate something ('at, near, in the presence of').

14.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
14.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

15.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
15.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

16.meaning: What makes you (all) realize / what makes you aware...? A verb meaning to cause someone to sense, perceive, or become conscious of something, with an attached 'you (plural).' Often opens a rhetorical question.
16.grammar: A present/imperfect causative verb (to make someone perceive). The prefix yu- marks a third-person subject 'it/he,' and the final -u vowel signals the plain indicative mood (a straightforward 'makes [you] aware'). The attached -kum is the object 'you (masc. plural).'
16.root: ش-ع-ر (sh-ʿ-r) — to perceive, sense, become aware; awareness

17.meaning: that it / that she — a connector meaning 'that...,' introducing a reported fact or content clause, with an attached feminine 'it/she' as its subject. The base particle gives certainty and emphasis to the clause it opens.
17.grammar: An emphasizing particle meaning 'that...,' used to introduce a statement of fact (as in 'they know that...'). It grammatically governs a following noun in the accusative; here that noun is the attached pronoun -hā, 'it/she' (feminine), serving as the subject of the 'that'-clause.

18.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
18.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.

19.meaning: she/it came / arrived. A verb of coming, arriving, or presenting itself, in the feminine.
19.grammar: A completed-action (past-tense) verb. The suffix -t marks a single feminine subject: 'she/it came.' Past tense presents the arrival as already accomplished.
19.root: ج-ي-أ (j-y-ʾ) — to come, arrive, bring

20.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
20.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

21.meaning: 'They believe / they have faith' — to affirm something as true with trusting inner conviction and to feel secure in it. The verb carries both believing and being at peace through that belief; in religious use it is to commit oneself in faith.
21.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb, masculine plural. The yu-…-una frame means 'they (men, or a mixed group) do' the action now or habitually. The retained final -na marks the indicative (a plain, unqualified statement) — 'they believe' — as opposed to forms where that -na drops. The verb is Form IV (amana), used intransitively here meaning simply 'to believe / to have faith'.
21.root: ا-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, trust, faith

1.meaning: and We turn over / We overturn and cause to revolve. From a root meaning to flip, invert, and turn something this way and that. The doubled-letter stem suggests repeated or thorough turning.
1.grammar: A present/imperfect verb on an intensive doubled-letter pattern (to turn over thoroughly or repeatedly). The prefix nu- means 'we,' and the final -u vowel signals the plain indicative mood (a straightforward 'we turn over').
1.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — to turn, flip, overturn; heart

2.meaning: their hearts / their inmost faculties of feeling and understanding. The plural of a word for the heart as the seat of emotion and perception, with an attached 'their.'
2.grammar: A plural noun carrying the -a ending, which typically marks the accusative case — often the object of a verb. The attached -hum means 'their (masc. plural),' showing possession of the hearts.
2.root: ف-أ-د (f-ʾ-d) — the heart as seat of feeling/intellect

3.meaning: and their eyes / their faculties of sight, their gazes. The plural of a word for sight or the seeing eye, with an attached 'their.'
3.grammar: A plural noun carrying the -a ending, which typically marks the accusative case — often the object of a verb. The attached -hum means 'their (masc. plural),' showing possession of the sights/eyes.

4.meaning: 'Just as / in the same way that' — a phrase of comparison joining 'like / as' to 'what', meaning 'like that which...' or 'in the manner that...'.
4.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like / as') joined to mā ('what / that which'). Together they introduce a likeness or manner — 'just as...', 'in the same way that...' — comparing one thing or action to another.

5.meaning: A negating particle, 'not', used specifically to deny that an action happened in the past, even though it attaches to a present-tense verb form. It turns 'you do X' into 'you did not do X'.

parts.en: did not (negation of a completed act)

5.grammar: An indeclinable particle that governs the verb after it, putting that verb into the jussive (clipped) mood and giving it past-time meaning. In short: lam + a present-form verb = 'did not [verb]'.

6.meaning: 'They (masculine) believe' — to have faith in Allah; a present-tense verb with a masculine-plural subject.
6.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb, 3rd-person masculine plural ('they believe'). The yu- prefix with the -ū ending marks 'they (men) do'. The dropped final nūn (yu'minū, not yu'minūna) shows the jussive/subjunctive mood — used after conditional or negative-command particles. From form IV, 'to believe'.
6.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, trust; form IV: to believe, have faith

7.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
7.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

8.meaning: First, foremost — the one that comes before all others in time, order, or rank.
8.grammar: A noun/adjective meaning 'first', here in a form that does not take normal indefinite case-tanwīn (a 'diptote'). The -a ending is accusative, marking it as an object or, very often, as the leading term of a possessive phrase ('the first of …').
8.root: أ-و-ل (ʾ-w-l) — to be first, to return to a beginning

9.meaning: One time / once / an instance — a noun denoting a single occurrence of an act. Indefinite ('a time'), as shown by its two-vowel (tanwin) ending.
9.grammar: A feminine noun meaning 'a single time/occurrence'. The doubled-vowel ending (tanwin, here -in) marks it as indefinite ('a time', not 'the time'); the -i quality of that ending is genitive, signalling the word follows a preposition or links to another noun. It often expresses 'one time / once'.
9.root: م-ر-ر (m-r-r) — passing by; an instance or occurrence of something

10.meaning: and We leave them / We let them be, abandon them (to a state). From a root meaning to leave alone, forsake, or let remain, with an attached 'them.'
10.grammar: A present/imperfect verb. The prefix na- means 'we,' and the final -u vowel signals the plain indicative mood (a straightforward 'we leave'). The attached -hum is the object 'them.' This verb is used only in the present/command; it has no past-tense form of its own.
10.root: و-ذ-ر (w-dh-r) — to leave, let be, forsake

11.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
11.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
11.root: — (particle)

12.meaning: Their overstepping of bounds — rebellious excess, tyranny, and inordinate transgression that exceeds all proper limits, especially against the truth. The attached pronoun marks it as belonging to them.
12.grammar: A verbal noun (naming the act/state of overstepping bounds) with the attached possessive -him ('their,' for a group of males). The -i ending before the pronoun is genitive, marking possession ('… of theirs') or governance by a preceding preposition.
12.root: ط-غ-ي (ṭ-gh-y) — to overflow, exceed all bounds, be tyrannical

13.meaning: they wander blindly / stumble about in confusion and bewilderment. A verb describing being lost and groping aimlessly, unable to see one's way — perplexed and disoriented.
13.grammar: A present/imperfect verb. The prefix ya- with the ending -ūna marks a masculine plural 'they' in the plain indicative mood; the full -ūna ending (keeping its final nūn) signals a straightforward, ongoing statement ('they are wandering in bewilderment').
13.root: ع-م-ه (ʿ-m-h) — to wander blindly, be bewildered/perplexed

1.meaning: 'and if' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle 'if'. This particular 'if' (law) introduces a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact condition: 'if (such-and-such had been the case)…', often implying it was not.
1.grammar: A conjunction plus a conditional particle. wa- means 'and'. law is a non-changing particle (no case ending) that sets up a supposition, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('… then certainly …').

2.meaning: that we / indeed we — a connector meaning 'that...,' introducing a reported statement with emphasis, with an attached 'we' as its subject.
2.grammar: An emphasizing particle meaning 'that...,' used to introduce a statement of fact. It grammatically governs a following noun in the accusative; here that noun is the attached pronoun -nā, 'we/us,' serving as the subject of the 'that'-clause. (An extra connecting nūn appears between the particle and the pronoun.)

3.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'We sent down', 'We revealed', 'We caused to descend' — the form (with doubled middle letter) suggests a sending-down done gradually or emphatically, fittingly used of revelation.
3.grammar: This is a past-tense verb in an intensive pattern (the doubled middle consonant of nazzala). The '-nā' suffix is the attached subject marker meaning 'we', so the whole word reads 'We sent down'.
3.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, to come/send down

4.meaning: A prepositional phrase meaning 'to them' or 'toward them' (a group of males). It combines the preposition meaning 'to / toward / unto' with a pronoun referring to a third-person masculine plural group, signaling motion or direction ending at those people.
4.grammar: Built on the preposition ilā ('to, toward'), whose final long vowel shortens to -ay before an attached pronoun. The suffix -him means 'them' (a group of males). Attached pronouns do not inflect for case; their vowel is set by sound rules. Here the base -him is raised to -himu so the word can join smoothly onto a following word beginning with a connecting hamza (a phonological linking adjustment, not a case ending).

5.meaning: The angels — Allah's created beings of light who serve Him perfectly, never disobeying His commands, and carry out His will (including conveying revelation). A collective plural noun referring to them as a group.

parts.en: feminine plural ending (tā marbūṭa) + accusative vowel

5.grammar: A plural noun with the al- prefix ('the'). The word ends in tā marbūṭa (ة), here marking the feminine plural pattern, which itself carries the case vowel; bearing the accusative -a it is pronounced -ta. The accusative typically marks the word as the object of a verb or otherwise governed in that case.
5.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — to possess, have power; 'malak' = angel (alternatively analyzed as أ-ل-ك, ʾ-l-k, 'to send a message')

6.meaning: A past-tense verb with an attached object, meaning 'and he spoke to them' or 'and he addressed them'. The underlying action is speaking directly to someone, conversing with or addressing a person face to face.
6.grammar: wa- is the connecting word 'and'. The verb is the intensive (Form II) past tense kallama, 'he spoke to / addressed (someone)'; the doubled middle root letter and the -a ending mark a completed action done by a single third-person male ('he'). The object suffix -hum means 'them' (males), here raised to -humu to ease the join with a following word beginning with a connecting hamza.

7.meaning: 'The dead' — those who have died or are without life; the lifeless, as a group.
7.grammar: A definite plural noun/adjective ('the dead'). It is of a plural pattern that ends in a fixed long -ā, so its ending does not change with grammatical position; it refers collectively to those who are dead.

8.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'and we gathered / assembled / mustered'. The core action is bringing scattered people or things together into one place, herding or rounding them up.
8.grammar: wa- is 'and'. The stem ḥashara is a plain (Form I) past-tense verb. The suffix -nā attached to a past verb means the subject is 'we' — the doer is a first-person plural (often the royal/majestic 'We' when Allah speaks). The action is presented as completed.

9.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
9.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
9.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

10.meaning: All, every, the whole of — totality. When followed by a singular it means 'every (one)'; when followed by a definite plural or whole it means 'all of.'
10.grammar: A noun of totality, almost always joined to a following noun in the genitive ('every … / all of …'). The final -a is the accusative case, the form used when the word functions as an object of a verb.

11.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
11.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
11.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

12.meaning: An accusative noun/adverb meaning 'face to face', 'in direct confrontation', or 'in droves, group by group'. It conveys either things appearing right before one's eyes and confronting one directly, or things brought together in successive batches.
12.grammar: An indefinite noun used adverbially. Its final -an is the indefinite accusative, written with tanwīn (nunation) — a vowel-ending diacritic on the word itself, not a separately written suffix. Functioning adverbially, it describes the manner in which something occurs ('face to face', 'directly confronting', or 'in successive groups').
12.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — facing, front, receiving

13.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
13.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

14.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
14.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
14.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

15.meaning: A verb phrase meaning 'so that they would believe' or 'in order for them to believe'. The underlying act is having faith — accepting and trusting in a truth, especially faith in Allah and His message.
15.grammar: li- is the particle 'so that / in order that', which puts the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood (expressing purpose or intended result). The verb is the Form IV present yu'minu, 'to believe / have faith'. The plural ending normally -ūna loses its final -na to become -ū because of the subjunctive, and the doer is 'they' (a group of males).

16.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
16.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

17.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
17.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

18.meaning: '(that) he wills / wishes' — to will, intend, or so desire that a thing comes about.
18.grammar: A present-tense verb, third person masculine singular ('he wills'). The final -a is the subjunctive ending, which typically appears after particles meaning 'that/so that/until,' giving the sense 'that he should will.'

19.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
19.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
19.root: — (proper divine name)

20.meaning: But; however; rather. A particle of correction or contrast that cancels or qualifies a preceding statement and introduces what is actually the case.
20.grammar: A connective wa- ('and') joined to the emphatic particle lākinna. Lākinna belongs to the 'inna family: it governs the noun that follows it, putting it in the accusative case, and adds a sense of firm contrast — 'but in fact …'.
20.root: — (particle)

21.meaning: A noun phrase meaning 'most of them / the greater part of them' — the larger portion of a group.
21.grammar: An elative/comparative noun ('more/most, the greater number') on the 'afʿal' pattern. The -a ending marks the accusative case, the form used when the word is a verb's object. The attached -hum ('them') is in the possessive role, completing the sense 'the most of them'.
21.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — muchness, abundance, being many

22.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'they are ignorant' or 'they behave foolishly / know not'. Its sense covers both lacking knowledge and acting rashly or foolishly out of that lack.
22.grammar: A plain (Form I) present-tense verb. The ending -ūna marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they', males) and, being the full indicative ending, signals an ongoing or habitual action ('they are / keep being ignorant').

1.meaning: 'And likewise / and in the same way / and thus' — a connective phrase pointing back to a manner just mentioned and saying 'in that very way…'. Built from 'and' + 'like' + 'that'.
1.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'; the prefix ka- means 'like/as'; 'dhālika' is the demonstrative 'that' (pointing to something distant or already mentioned). Because ka- acts like a preposition, the word after it stands in the genitive, though the demonstrative 'dhālika' keeps a fixed form and shows no visible case change. The whole means 'and just like that / and thus'.

2.meaning: We made, rendered, set up, or appointed. A completed act of making or designating, done by a group or by a majestic 'We.'
2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb with the attached subject ending -nā, meaning 'we' did the action. 'Jaʿala' carries senses from 'to make/create' to 'to render X into Y' or 'to appoint.'
2.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, appoint, place

3.meaning: For each, for every — combines the preposition 'for/to' with 'each/every (one)'. Kull expresses totality taken one by one.
3.grammar: The noun kull ('each/every/all') preceded by the preposition li- ('for'). The -i ending is genitive, the case regularly required after a preposition, and which also lets kull link to a following noun ('each OF …').

4.meaning: A singular noun meaning 'a prophet' — one who receives revelation and tidings from Allah and conveys them to people. The word carries the sense of one given news from on high.
4.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The -in ending (tanwīn / nunation) marks the genitive case while indefinite ('a prophet'). The genitive typically appears after a preposition or when the noun is possessed by a following noun ('… of a prophet').
4.root: ن-ب-ء (n-b-ʾ) — news, tidings (a prophet conveys news from Allah)

5.meaning: 'An enemy / a foe' — one who is hostile or opposed; can refer to a single enemy or collectively to enemies.
5.grammar: A noun/adjective meaning 'enemy', on a pattern with a doubled final consonant. The -an ending (tanwīn) is accusative plus indefiniteness, the form used for the object of a verb or as a predicate after certain verbs (e.g. 'took/became an enemy').

6.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'devils / demons' — rebellious, malevolent beings (whether among jinn or humankind) who incite to evil. The root sense is of one who is remote from goodness and obstinately defiant.
6.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of shayṭān. It belongs to a class of nouns (the 'diptote' pattern) that does not take nunation; its single final -a vowel serves for both the accusative and the genitive case. The plain -a (not -u) shows it is not functioning as the subject of a sentence.
6.root: ش-ط-ن (sh-ṭ-n) — to be remote/rebellious; obstinate defiance

7.meaning: A noun with the definite article, meaning 'the mankind / humans / human beings' as a collective. The word evokes humans in their sociable, companionable nature, as opposed to hidden, unseen beings.
7.grammar: al- is the definite article 'the'. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… of mankind') or follows a preposition. The collective noun ins refers to humankind as a whole.
7.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — familiarity, sociability (humans as social beings)

8.meaning: A noun with the definite article, meaning 'and the jinn' — a class of unseen beings created from smokeless fire, possessing free will. The root sense is of that which is hidden or concealed from human sight.
8.grammar: wa- is 'and'; al- is 'the'. The -i ending is genitive, which typically follows a preposition or links the noun to a preceding one ('… of the jinn'). Jinn is a collective noun for the hidden beings.
8.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal, hide (the jinn being unseen)

9.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he inspires / reveals / whispers secretly'. Its core sense is conveying a message swiftly and covertly into someone's mind or heart — whether divine revelation or hidden suggestion.
9.grammar: A Form IV present-tense verb from a root whose final letter is a weak 'y'. The yu- prefix marks a third-person singular masculine subject ('he'), and the final long -ī is the weak root letter showing through; the verb is in the indicative (an ongoing or habitual act of inspiring/revealing).
9.root: و-ح-ي (w-ḥ-y) — to inspire, reveal, suggest swiftly and secretly

10.meaning: 'Some of them' / 'a part of them' — a noun meaning 'a portion, part, or some' joined to an attached pronoun 'them'. Often paired with itself to express 'one another / each other'.
10.grammar: A noun 'part/some' in the nominative case (the -u ending), which typically marks it as the subject or doer. The suffix -hum is a genitive (possessive) pronoun meaning 'their' (masculine plural); attached to a noun this way it sits in the possessor slot, giving 'some of them'.
10.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, portion, or some of a whole

11.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
11.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

12.meaning: 'Some (others)' / 'a part' — the same noun for 'a portion or some,' here left indefinite, often functioning as the counterpart in the 'one another' construction.
12.grammar: A noun 'part/some' in the genitive case with indefinite marking (the -in ending, called tanwīn). The genitive typically follows a preposition or links it to a preceding noun ('… of …'); the doubled -n sound marks it as indefinite ('a part / some').
12.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, portion, or some of a whole

13.meaning: An accusative noun meaning 'gilding / glittering ornament / gaudy embellishment'. It denotes showy, gilded decoration — beautified surface adornment, and by extension speech or things made falsely attractive.
13.grammar: The -a ending marks the accusative case, which typically identifies the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or otherwise the receiver of the action. The noun denotes ornate, gilded embellishment.

14.meaning: Speech, an utterance, a statement, or a saying — that which is said. It denotes the act or content of speaking.
14.grammar: A definite noun ('the speech'). The -i ending is the genitive case: it typically links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of …' relationship or follows a preposition.

15.meaning: 'delusion / deception / vain beguilement' — the deceiving of someone with empty, alluring appearances so that they are lulled into false confidence.
15.grammar: A noun with the -an ending (indefinite accusative, 'tanwīn'), which typically marks an indefinite 'a …' functioning as an object or, often, as a description of manner ('… as a delusion / deceptively'). It names the act/quality of beguiling deception.
15.root: غ-ر-ر (gh-r-r) — to deceive, delude, beguile; vanity

16.meaning: 'and if' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle 'if'. This particular 'if' (law) introduces a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact condition: 'if (such-and-such had been the case)…', often implying it was not.
16.grammar: A conjunction plus a conditional particle. wa- means 'and'. law is a non-changing particle (no case ending) that sets up a supposition, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('… then certainly …').

17.meaning: A past-tense verb 'he willed / he wished / he so desired'. It denotes an act of will or volition bringing something about.
17.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third person masculine singular ('he'). The bare stem with no suffix is the basic 'he did' form. Its subject and object are typically supplied by context.

18.meaning: 'Your Lord / your Master' — the word for 'Lord' (one who owns, sustains, nurtures and has authority over) combined with 'your' (a single addressee); rabb carries the layered sense of master, sustainer, and the one who brings to maturity.
18.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -u ending is the nominative case — the basic 'subject' state, used for the doer of an action or the topic of a sentence. The suffix -ka means 'your', addressed to a single masculine person. 'Rabb' bundles ownership, lordship, nurturing care, and sustaining authority into one term.

19.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
19.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

20.meaning: 'They did it' or 'they would have done it' — a completed action of carrying out, performing, or doing something, attributed to a group, with 'it' as the thing done.
20.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū marks a plural masculine 'they' as the doers. The attached -hu ('it/him') is the object — the thing that was done. So: 'they did it'.
20.root: ف-ع-ل (f-ʿ-l) — doing, acting, performing a deed

21.meaning: A command verb with an attached object, meaning 'so leave them / let them be / forsake them'. The underlying verb means to leave something alone, abandon it, or let it go.
21.grammar: fa- is 'so / then', drawing a consequence. dhar is an imperative (command) addressed to a single male ('you, leave!'); this very common verb is used only in present and command forms. The suffix -hum is the object 'them' (a group of males).
21.root: و-ذ-ر (w-dh-r) — to leave, let alone, forsake

22.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
22.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

23.meaning: They fabricate or invent falsely — to forge a lie, concoct something untrue and attribute it where it does not belong. The verb specifically names inventing falsehood and slander out of nothing.
23.grammar: Present-tense verb in the (form VIII) pattern, third-person masculine plural. The ya- prefix marks the third person and, together with the -ūna ending, yields 'they' (masculine plural) acting in ongoing/present time. The retained -na is the mark of the indicative ('they are fabricating / they fabricate').

1.meaning: A verb phrase meaning 'and so that ... may incline / lean toward'. The core verb describes a heart or inclination bending and tilting toward something, leaning in to it with desire or attention.
1.grammar: wa- is 'and'; li- is the purpose particle 'so that', which makes the following present verb subjunctive. The ta- prefix marks a third-person singular feminine subject ('it / she', here agreeing with a feminine noun). The verb's root ends in a weak letter appearing as the long final -ā; in the subjunctive this form shows no separate added ending.
1.root: ص-غ-و / ص-غ-ي (ṣ-gh-w/y) — to incline, lean, tilt toward

2.meaning: 'To Him' or 'toward Him' — the preposition expressing direction or endpoint ('to / toward') combined with a pronoun referring to a single masculine person, indicating motion or attention directed at him.
2.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base 'ilā shifts to 'ilay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -hi is the third-person masculine singular object of a preposition, 'him'; its -i vowel is the form the pronoun takes after the 'ay' sound.

3.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'hearts' — understood as the seat of understanding, emotion, intention, and the inner self, not merely the physical organ. The singular fu'ād suggests a heart that is enkindled or stirred.
3.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of fu'ād, 'heart'. The -u ending marks the nominative case, which typically identifies the subject — the one performing the action — or otherwise the noun being spoken about.
3.root: ف-ء-د (f-ʾ-d) — the heart; to be kindled, stirred

4.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
4.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

5.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
5.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

6.meaning: 'They believe / they have faith' — to affirm something as true with trusting inner conviction and to feel secure in it. The verb carries both believing and being at peace through that belief; in religious use it is to commit oneself in faith.
6.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb, masculine plural. The yu-…-una frame means 'they (men, or a mixed group) do' the action now or habitually. The retained final -na marks the indicative (a plain, unqualified statement) — 'they believe' — as opposed to forms where that -na drops. The verb is Form IV (amana), used intransitively here meaning simply 'to believe / to have faith'.

7.meaning: The noun 'the Hereafter / the next life / the world to come,' linked by 'with / for / in exchange for' (bi-). The base word means 'the last, the latter, the final' (state of affairs) and is used as the standing name for the everlasting life after this world.
7.grammar: A definite feminine noun ('the Hereafter') governed by the preposition 'bi-' ('with / for / in exchange for'). The '-i' ending is genitive: the case a noun takes after a preposition (or when linked to a preceding noun as '…of…'). Here it appears because the preposition 'bi-' requires the genitive form; the tā' marbūṭa of the stem is sounded as 't' before this ending.
7.root: ا-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — being last, coming after, the end

8.meaning: A verb phrase with an attached object, meaning 'and so that they may be pleased with it / find contentment in it / approve of it'. The core sense is being satisfied, accepting something gladly and willingly.
8.grammar: wa- is 'and'; li- is the purpose particle 'so that', putting the present verb in the subjunctive. The ya- prefix and the plural ending mark a third-person masculine plural subject ('they', males); because the root ends in a weak letter, the subjunctive plural appears as -aw rather than -ū. The suffix -hu is the object 'it / him'.
8.root: ر-ض-و / ر-ض-ي (r-ḍ-w/y) — to be pleased, content, satisfied

9.meaning: A verb phrase meaning 'and so that they may earn / commit / perpetrate'. The core verb means to acquire or commit something through one's own action — most often used of earning sins or wrongdoing.
9.grammar: wa- is 'and'; li- is the purpose particle 'so that', placing the present verb in the subjunctive. The verb is Form VIII (iqtarafa), 'to commit / acquire (by one's own doing)'. The plural ending, normally -ūna, drops its -na to -ū in the subjunctive, with the subject being 'they' (males).
9.root: ق-ر-ف (q-r-f) — to acquire, earn, commit (esp. wrongdoing)

10.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
10.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

11.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
11.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

12.meaning: An active participle (plural) meaning 'ones committing / perpetrators / earners'. It names those who are doing the committing or acquiring — the agents of the act, often of wrongdoing.
12.grammar: An active participle of Form VIII ('one who commits / acquires'). The masculine-plural ending -ūna marks the nominative case (the doers / those being described as the subject). A participle names the one performing the action rather than locating it in past or present time.
12.root: ق-ر-ف (q-r-f) — to acquire, earn, commit (esp. wrongdoing)

1.meaning: A pointed question meaning roughly 'so is it other than…?' — combining a 'then/so' connector, a questioning particle expressing surprise or rebuke, and the word 'other than / besides.'
1.grammar: A compound: the questioning particle a- (asking 'is it…?', often with a tone of astonishment or reproach) joined to the connector fa- ('then/so'), prefixed to the noun 'ghayr' (other/something else). The -a ending on ghayra is the accusative case, the form a noun takes as the object of an action or after certain particles.

2.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
2.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

3.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'I seek / desire / strive after'. The core sense is actively pursuing and looking for something, wanting and aiming for it.
3.grammar: A Form VIII present-tense verb from a root ending in a weak letter. The a- prefix marks a first-person singular subject ('I'), and the final long -ī is the weak root letter appearing in the indicative (an ongoing or general act of seeking).
3.root: ب-غ-ي (b-gh-y) — to seek, desire, strive after

4.meaning: An arbiter or judge — one appointed to decide between disputing parties and pronounce a binding ruling.
4.grammar: A noun denoting one who arbitrates. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative ('an arbiter'): this case typically marks the word as the object of a verb, and the doubled nasal -n (tanwīn) shows it is indefinite.
4.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, decide, govern; wisdom, sound judgment

5.meaning: And it / and he — a connective joined to the standalone pronoun 'he/it', often introducing a circumstantial clause ('while it…').
5.grammar: The prefix wa- ('and', or 'while' when introducing an accompanying circumstance) joined to the detached subject pronoun huwa, 'he/it' (masculine singular). The shadda on the wa- reflects assimilation of a preceding consonant onto it in connected speech. The pronoun is fixed in form and serves as the subject of its clause.

6.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
6.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

7.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'he sent down, he caused to descend, he revealed' — used especially of Allah sending down revelation, rain, or blessings from above.
7.grammar: A completed (past) action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the -a ending marks third-person masculine singular. The form IV (causative) pattern means 'to make something come down,' i.e., to send it down.

8.meaning: To you / towards you — directing an action or motion at the addressees.
8.grammar: A preposition meaning 'to/towards' with the attached pronoun -kum ('you all'). The pronoun takes the helping vowel -u (kumu) when followed by a word beginning with the definite article, simply to ease pronunciation; it does not change the meaning.

9.meaning: The Book, the Scripture — a written revelation; the term for a divinely revealed text.
9.grammar: A definite noun ('the Book') with attached 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb.
9.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; a writing, book

10.meaning: A passive participle meaning 'made distinct / set out in detail / fully explained'. It describes something laid out clearly, separated into its parts and elaborated point by point.
10.grammar: A passive participle of the intensive (Form II) verb faṣṣala, 'to set out in detail'. It describes a thing that has had the action done to it ('made detailed'). The -an ending (tanwīn / nunation) is the indefinite accusative, frequently used for a descriptive complement or a state in which something is found.

11.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
11.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.
11.root: — (relative pronoun)

12.meaning: We gave them / We granted them — a completed act of bestowing or conferring something upon a group, done by 'We'.
12.grammar: A past-tense verb of Form IV ('to give, bestow, grant'). The suffix -nā marks the doer as 'we'. The attached pronoun -hum(u) is the object, 'them' (a group); its vowel is lengthened to -humu to ease pronunciation before the next word. Altogether: 'We gave them'.
12.root: ء-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (Form IV) to give, bring, bestow

13.meaning: The Book, the Scripture — a written revelation; the term for a divinely revealed text.
13.grammar: A definite noun ('the Book') with attached 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb.
13.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; a writing, book

14.meaning: They know, have knowledge, are aware. Expresses ongoing or habitual knowing held by a group of males (or a mixed group).
14.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending means 'they' (a group of males). The full -ūna ending (rather than a shortened -ū) marks the indicative mood, signaling a plain statement of fact: 'they (do) know.'

15.meaning: 'That He …' — an emphatic particle meaning 'that / indeed' joined to the pronoun 'he'; it introduces and affirms a clause reporting something about a single masculine subject (most often Allah).
15.grammar: The emphatic particle 'anna' ('that, indeed') with the attached pronoun '-hu' ('he/it') as its subject. 'Anna' introduces a subordinate clause ('… that He …') and gives it certainty; '-hu' identifies a single masculine subject. (The pronoun is pronounced '-hu' here following the 'a' vowel.)

16.meaning: A passive participle meaning 'sent down / brought down (in stages)'. It describes something caused to descend, especially revelation sent down from on high.
16.grammar: A passive participle of the intensive (Form II) verb nazzala, 'to send down (gradually / in parts)'. It describes the thing acted upon ('that which is sent down'). The -un ending (tanwīn / nunation) marks the indefinite nominative, typically the subject or the thing being described as such.

17.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
17.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

18.meaning: The Lord belonging to a single male 'you' — Rabb is the Master, Owner, and Sustainer who creates, nurtures, and brings to maturity; here 'your Lord'.
18.grammar: The noun rabb (Lord, Sustainer) with the attached pronoun -ka, 'your' for one male. The -i ending before the pronoun is genitive, the case that typically links a word to a following possessor or follows a preposition (here showing the possession 'of you'). The doubled b (shadda) belongs to the root.

19.meaning: 'With the truth / by means of what is true and right.' Combines the preposition 'with/by' and 'the truth' — that which is real, established, correct, and rightfully due, as opposed to falsehood.
19.grammar: A noun governed by the attached preposition bi- ('with/by'). The -i ending is the genitive case, which is required after a preposition; here it links 'the truth' to 'with', giving 'with the truth'.
19.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, reality, that which is established and due

20.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
20.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

21.meaning: You must certainly be / never be — an emphatic form of the verb 'to be', stressing that one truly will (or, with a negative, truly must not) be in a certain state.
21.grammar: A present-tense form of the verb 'to be', addressed to 'you' (the prefix ta-). The heavy ending -anna (nūn of emphasis) gives a strong, insistent force — 'you most certainly are/must be' — and is the standard way Arabic stresses a command or warning attached to a verb.
21.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into being

22.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
22.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

23.meaning: 'The doubters / those who fall into doubt' — people characterized by harbouring uncertainty, wavering, or contesting the truth.
23.grammar: An active participle (form VIII, 'one who doubts') made definite by al- ('the'). The -ina ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative or genitive case — the form used for the object of a verb or after a preposition. It names a class of people by their action: 'the ones who doubt'.

1.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'and it was completed / fulfilled / came to its full measure'. The core sense is something reaching completion and perfection, being brought to its full and final state.
1.grammar: wa- is 'and'. tamma is a plain (Form I) past-tense verb, 'to be complete / fulfilled'. The suffix -t (a quiescent tā') marks a third-person singular feminine subject ('it / she'), agreeing with a feminine noun; the action is presented as completed.

2.meaning: A singular noun meaning 'word / utterance / decree'. Beyond a single 'word', it can denote a statement, a pronouncement, or a binding decree that is spoken and thereby takes effect.
2.grammar: A feminine singular noun (its tā' marbūṭa pronounced as a hard 't' here because a possessor noun follows). The -u ending marks the nominative case — typically the subject, or the noun being described — and it is the first term of a possessive pair ('the word of …').

3.meaning: A noun with an attached pronoun meaning 'your Lord' — the Lord/Master/Sustainer of a single person addressed. Rabb conveys an owner who creates, nurtures, sustains, and governs all that is under His care.
3.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord, Sustainer') carries the -i genitive vowel, which typically appears when the noun follows a preposition or is itself possessed by a following noun ('… of your Lord'). The suffix -ka means 'your', addressed to a single male.
3.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship; to nurture, sustain, master

4.meaning: Truthfulness, sincerity, the quality of being true and matching reality; here in the indefinite accusative, conveying 'in truth' or 'as a true thing'.
4.grammar: A noun (verbal noun/maṣdar) carrying nunation. The final -an is the indefinite accusative ending (tanwīn al-fatḥ): it commonly marks a word as a direct object, or functions adverbially to mean 'in/as a state of (truth)'.
4.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — truthfulness, sincerity, keeping faith with reality

5.meaning: Justice, fairness, equity; giving each thing its due and setting matters straight in perfect balance. Here in the indefinite accusative.
5.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and', joining this to what precedes. The noun ends in -an, the indefinite accusative ending (tanwīn al-fatḥ), which typically marks a direct object or an adverbial sense ('in/as justice').

6.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
6.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

7.meaning: A noun/participle meaning 'one who changes / alters / replaces.' It names the doer of changing — a substituter who exchanges one thing for another.

parts.en: one who … (prefix forming an active doer-noun)

7.grammar: An active participle (a doer-noun) from the intensive pattern, with the mu- prefix that marks 'the one who does' the action. The final -a is the accusative case ending, the form a noun takes as the object of a verb or after certain particles (such as 'there is no …').

8.meaning: Belonging to His words/utterances; 'kalimāt' is the plural of kalima, a spoken word, statement, or decree, attached to a possessive 'His'.
8.grammar: The prefix li- means 'to/for'. The -āt is the sound feminine plural marker. The case ending is -i (genitive), required after the preposition li-; the attached -hi is the possessive pronoun 'His', whose vowel is -i in harmony with the preceding genitive.

9.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
9.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

10.meaning: "the All-Hearing" — one who hears, perceiving all sounds completely and constantly; used as a divine name it denotes the One whose hearing is perfect and all-encompassing.
10.grammar: A definite intensive adjective/noun on the faʿīl pattern, which conveys a deep, enduring quality ('ever-hearing,' not merely 'hearing once'). The 'al-' prefix makes it definite ('the'). The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, the form a word takes when it is the subject of a sentence or a predicate/description following it.

11.meaning: The All-Knowing — one whose knowledge is complete, perfect, and all-encompassing; an intensive form stressing that knowing is an essential, constant attribute.
11.grammar: A definite noun/adjective in an intensive pattern (faʿīl) that stresses depth and permanence of the quality. The prefix 'al-' means 'the'; the final -u (ḍamma) marks the nominative case, which typically signals the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it.
11.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know

1.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
1.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

2.meaning: You obey, you comply with and submit to (someone's command); from a verb meaning to yield obedience.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form IV) in the jussive/apocopate mood. The tu- prefix marks 'you' (masculine singular). The bare ending (-ʿ with no final vowel) is the jussive form, used after particles like 'if' or negation/command particles, signalling a conditioned or non-indicative sense.

3.meaning: 'More' / 'greater (in number or amount)' — the comparative/superlative form built from 'much, many', meaning more numerous or more abundant.
3.grammar: A comparative adjective on the pattern afʿal ('more …'). The -a ending is the accusative case, the form a noun takes when it is an object or otherwise governed; this pattern does not take nunation. It is typically completed by 'than …'.

4.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
4.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
5.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

6.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
6.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

7.meaning: They will lead you astray, cause you to lose the way or fall into error; with an attached object 'you'.
7.grammar: A present-tense causative verb (Form IV, ʾaḍalla / yuḍillu 'to make go astray'). Two features mark Form IV rather than Form I: the prefix vowel is u (yu-, not the ya- of Form I), and the geminate stem carries kasra (-ḍill-). The -ū ending marks a masculine plural subject ('they'); the attached -ka is the object pronoun 'you' (masculine singular).
7.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — straying, losing the way, error

8.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

8.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

9.meaning: 'path, way, road' — a route or course; figuratively a cause or way of life one travels along. In construct ('the way OF ...').
9.grammar: A singular noun with the '-i' (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a following noun ('the way OF ...') or follows a preposition. It marks the word as connected to or possessed by what comes after.

10.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
10.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

11.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
11.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

12.meaning: They follow, pursue, or go after (something), tracking its path closely; from a verb meaning to follow in succession.
12.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form VIII) with the ya- prefix marking a third-person subject. The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural subject ('they') in the indicative mood, the form used for a plain, ongoing statement of fact.
12.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — following, succession, pursuit

13.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
13.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

14.meaning: Conjecture, supposition, opinion not grounded in certainty; a thought or assumption that may be doubt or mere likelihood rather than sure knowledge.
14.grammar: A definite noun: al- is 'the', and the final -a is the accusative ending (fatḥa), which typically marks the word as a direct object of a verb.

15.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
15.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

16.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
16.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

17.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
17.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

18.meaning: They guess, conjecture, or speak from mere estimation; from a verb meaning to surmise or speak falsely without sound basis.
18.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form I) with the ya- prefix. The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural subject ('they') in the indicative mood, used for an ongoing or habitual statement.
18.root: خ-ر-ص (kh-r-ṣ) — to conjecture, estimate, speak by guesswork

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: 'Your Lord' — the noun 'Lord' (Master, Sustainer, Owner, the One who nurtures and brings to completion) combined with 'your'. 'Rabb' carries the linked senses of ownership, authority, and ongoing care that raises a thing to its perfection.
2.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive. The -a ending is accusative, which typically marks the word as a direct object or governed element. The attached -ka means 'your', addressed to a single male.
2.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, nurturing care, ownership and mastery

3.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
3.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

4.meaning: 'I know' — a present-tense verb of knowing: to have certain knowledge or awareness of something.
4.grammar: A present/future (Form I) verb, first-person singular ('I'), marked by the prefix a-. This a- is the first-person agreement marker built into the conjugation, not a free-standing pronoun. The final -u marks the indicative — a plain statement of ongoing or habitual knowing.

5.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
5.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

6.meaning: He/it strays, goes astray, wanders from the right path or falls into error; the basic intransitive act of losing the way.
6.grammar: A present-tense intransitive verb (Form I) with the ya- prefix marking a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'). The doubled ل is the geminate (doubled) third radical of the root ض-ل-ل, not a Form II doubling; the ya- prefix vowel (a) contrasts with the yu- of the Form IV causative 'to make astray'. The final -u is the indicative ending, used for a plain present/future statement of fact.
6.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — straying, losing the way, error

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

7.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

8.meaning: "His way / His path" — the noun for a road, path, or way, here carrying the attached pronoun "His" (referring to Allah); idiomatically, the path or cause of Allah.
8.grammar: A masculine noun with the attached possessive pronoun "-hi" ("his/His"). The pronoun appears in its "-hi" form (with the "i" vowel), which is used when the noun is in the genitive — i.e., after a preposition or when linked in an "of"-type relation to a preceding word.

9.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
9.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

10.meaning: 'I know' — a present-tense verb of knowing: to have certain knowledge or awareness of something.
10.grammar: A present/future (Form I) verb, first-person singular ('I'), marked by the prefix a-. This a- is the first-person agreement marker built into the conjugation, not a free-standing pronoun. The final -u marks the indicative — a plain statement of ongoing or habitual knowing.

11.meaning: Those who are rightly guided, who have found and follow the true path; the active participle of accepting guidance, in the plural.
11.grammar: The prefix bi- means 'with/of/in', and l- is 'the'. This is an active participle (Form VIII, 'one who takes guidance'). The -īna ending is the sound masculine plural in the genitive/accusative (oblique) case, here genitive because governed by the preposition bi-.
11.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance, showing the right way

1.meaning: So eat! — a command to consume food, prefaced by a connective particle drawing a consequence ('so/then').
1.grammar: The connective particle 'fa-' ('so/then,' linking to a consequence) joined to a command (imperative) verb. The ending '-ū' directs the order at 'you all (masculine plural)' — a plural 'eat!'

2.meaning: From what / from that which — a fusion of the preposition 'from' with the relative 'what/which', introducing the thing or situation being referred to.
2.grammar: A merger of 'min' ('from') and 'mā' ('what/that which'); the 'n' of 'min' assimilates into the 'm' of 'mā', doubling it. The combination means 'from what ...' and typically introduces a following clause describing the thing referred to. Being particles, neither part takes a case ending.

3.meaning: It was mentioned, named, invoked, or called to remembrance; the passive sense of bringing something to speech or recall.
3.grammar: A past-tense passive verb (Form I), third-person masculine singular ('it was …'). The internal vowel pattern — u after the first radical, i after the second (dhukir-) — is the diagnostic of the Form I passive, with no agent named. The final -a is the third-person masculine singular past ending. A triliteral Form I has no internal affix, so the stem is not further divisible.
3.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — remembrance, mention, calling to mind

4.meaning: Name; the word by which a thing is called or identified. Here in the nominative, the subject form.
4.grammar: A noun. The final -u is the nominative ending (ḍamma), which typically marks the word as the subject of a sentence or the doer of an action. The initial alif is a connecting (elidable) hamza, pronounced 'is-' in isolation.
4.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — name, height, that by which a thing is raised/known

5.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
5.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

6.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
6.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

7.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
7.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

8.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
8.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
8.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

9.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in / by His signs' — the preposition bi- ('with/in/by') joined to āyāt ('signs, verses, tokens') and 'His'. Āyāt are signs or proofs pointing to Allah, including revealed verses and observable signs.
9.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in/by/with') governing the plural noun āyāt ('signs'), which takes the genitive -i ending because it follows a preposition; the attached -hi means 'His'. The genitive is the case used after prepositions and to show possession ('signs OF His'). The pronoun appears as -hi (rather than -hu) in harmony with the preceding -i vowel.

10.meaning: Believers, those who have faith — who trust, affirm, and find security in what they believe; the active participle of believing, in the plural.
10.grammar: An active participle (Form IV, 'one who believes/gives faith'). The -īna ending is the sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (oblique) case; with no preposition governing it, the form here is accusative, marking it as a direct object.

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
2.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

3.meaning: A compound particle meaning 'that … not,' 'lest,' 'so as not to.' It introduces a clause of something feared, intended-to-prevent, or negated after a verb.
3.grammar: A merging of the particle an ('that,' which introduces a verb in the subjunctive) with the negative lā ('not'); the 'n' of an assimilates into lā, giving allā. Together they mean 'that … not' and put the following verb into the subjunctive mood, often after verbs of fearing, wishing, or commanding.

4.meaning: '(that) you eat / consume' — to take in food, and by extension to devour or consume wealth or property. Addressed to a group ('you all').
4.grammar: A present-tense verb, second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The plural '-ū' ending (without the usual final '-na') shows the verb is in the subjunctive or jussive — typically after a particle of purpose, negation, or prohibition ('that you (not) eat').

5.meaning: From what / from that which — a fusion of the preposition 'from' with the relative 'what/which', introducing the thing or situation being referred to.
5.grammar: A merger of 'min' ('from') and 'mā' ('what/that which'); the 'n' of 'min' assimilates into the 'm' of 'mā', doubling it. The combination means 'from what ...' and typically introduces a following clause describing the thing referred to. Being particles, neither part takes a case ending.

6.meaning: It was mentioned, named, invoked, or called to remembrance; the passive sense of bringing something to speech or recall.
6.grammar: A past-tense passive verb (Form I), third-person masculine singular ('it was …').
