2.grammar: A past-tense (completed-action) verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he did'). The doubled middle letter marks the intensive/causative form ('to make something appear adorned'). The final '-a' is the standard past-tense vowel for 'he'.
2.root: ز-ي-ن (z-y-n) — to adorn, to beautify, to make attractive

3.meaning: A phrase meaning 'to many / for many (of them)'. The noun means 'a great number, many', and 'li-' marks the recipient or direction ('to/for').
3.grammar: A noun/adjective ('many') governed by the preposition 'li-' ('to/for'), which forces the genitive ending. The '-in' ending (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite and genitive — 'to many (people)'.
3.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — to be much, to be many, abundance

4.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
4.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

5.meaning: Those who associate partners with Allah — idolaters / polytheists who set up others alongside the one God in worship or devotion.
5.grammar: An active participle used as a noun, with 'the', in the masculine sound plural. The -īna ending marks the plural in the genitive/accusative case — the form used after a preposition or as the object of a verb.

6.meaning: Killing, slaying — the act/event of taking a life, expressed as a verbal noun ('the killing of...').
6.grammar: A verbal noun (the action named as a thing: 'killing, the act of slaying'). The final -a ending marks the accusative case — the form a noun takes when it is the direct object of a verb (e.g. the thing prompted or intended) or otherwise governed into that case.

7.meaning: A noun meaning 'their children / offspring'. The plural noun denotes sons and children generally; with the attached 'their', it means 'their children'.
7.grammar: A plural noun ('children') carrying the genitive '-i' ending (shown before the pronoun), which typically signals that it is possessed, follows a preceding noun, or comes after a preposition. The suffix '-him' is the attached possessive pronoun 'their'; its 'i'-vowel form follows the genitive '-i'.
7.root: و-ل-د (w-l-d) — to give birth, to beget; child, offspring

8.meaning: A noun meaning 'their associate-partners' — beings set up as partners (alongside Allah). With the attached 'their', it specifies whose alleged partners they are. Here the noun stands in the form typical of a subject.
8.grammar: A plural noun ('partners/associates') carrying the nominative '-u' ending (shown before the pronoun), which typically marks it as the subject — the one performing the action. The suffix '-hum' is the attached possessive pronoun 'their'; its 'u'-vowel form follows the nominative '-u'.
8.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, to partner, to associate

9.meaning: A purpose phrase meaning 'so that they may destroy / ruin them'. The base verb means 'to bring to ruin or cause to perish', and the attached 'them' is the object being ruined.
9.grammar: A present-tense verb with the prefixed 'li-' of purpose ('so that / in order to'), which puts the verb in the subjunctive mood. In this mood the plural 'they' ending is the shortened '-ū' (the usual final 'n' is dropped). The 'yu-' prefix and causative form give 'to bring to ruin', and the attached '-hum' is the object pronoun 'them'.
9.root: ر-د-ي (r-d-y) — to perish, to fall to ruin, to destroy

10.meaning: A purpose phrase joined by 'and', meaning 'and so that they may confuse / obscure (it) for them' — to make something doubtful, mixed-up, or unclear. The base verb means 'to cloak/confound'.
10.grammar: A present-tense verb opening with 'wa-' ('and') and the 'li-' of purpose ('so that'), which puts the verb in the subjunctive mood. In this mood the plural 'they' ending is the shortened '-ū' (the usual final 'n' is dropped). The base verb means 'to make confusing, to cloak in doubt'.
10.root: ل-ب-س (l-b-s) — to cover, to clothe; to confuse, to obscure

11.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
11.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
11.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

12.meaning: Their religion / way of life — the concept of dīn: the complete system of belief, worship, obligation, and obedience by which one lives and to which one is accountable; also rendered 'faith,' 'judgment,' or 'recompense' depending on context. Here joined to 'their.'

parts.en: religion, way of life, system of obedience and accountability

12.grammar: A noun with the attached possessive pronoun -hum ('their,' a group of men). The -a vowel before the pronoun reflects the accusative case — the form typically used when the noun is the direct object of a verb ('… their religion' as the thing acted upon).
12.root: د-ي-ن (d-y-n) — religion, obedience, judgment, requital, debt/accountability

13.meaning: 'and if' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle 'if'. This particular 'if' (law) introduces a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact condition: 'if (such-and-such had been the case)…', often implying it was not.
13.grammar: A conjunction plus a conditional particle. wa- means 'and'. law is a non-changing particle (no case ending) that sets up a supposition, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('… then certainly …').

14.meaning: A past-tense verb 'he willed / he wished / he so desired'. It denotes an act of will or volition bringing something about.
14.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third person masculine singular ('he'). The bare stem with no suffix is the basic 'he did' form. Its subject and object are typically supplied by context.

15.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
15.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

16.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
16.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

17.meaning: 'They did it' or 'they would have done it' — a completed action of carrying out, performing, or doing something, attributed to a group, with 'it' as the thing done.
17.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū marks a plural masculine 'they' as the doers. The attached -hu ('it/him') is the object — the thing that was done. So: 'they did it'.
17.root: ف-ع-ل (f-ʿ-l) — doing, acting, performing a deed

18.meaning: A command verb with an attached object, meaning 'so leave them / let them be / forsake them'. The underlying verb means to leave something alone, abandon it, or let it go.
18.grammar: fa- is 'so / then', drawing a consequence. dhar is an imperative (command) addressed to a single male ('you, leave!'); this very common verb is used only in present and command forms. The suffix -hum is the object 'them' (a group of males).
18.root: و-ذ-ر (w-dh-r) — to leave, let alone, forsake

19.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
19.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
19.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

20.meaning: They fabricate or invent falsely — to forge a lie, concoct something untrue and attribute it where it does not belong. The verb specifically names inventing falsehood and slander out of nothing.
20.grammar: Present-tense verb in the (form VIII) pattern, third-person masculine plural. The ya- prefix marks the third person and, together with the -ūna ending, yields 'they' (masculine plural) acting in ongoing/present time. The retained -na is the mark of the indicative ('they are fabricating / they fabricate').
20.root: ف-ر-ي (f-r-y) — fabricating, forging, inventing falsehood

1.meaning: And they said — to utter or declare in speech, with the action presented as completed by a group.
1.grammar: The prefix 'wa-' means 'and'. 'qāla' is the past-tense verb 'to say'; the '-ū' suffix marks a completed action done by 'they' (a masculine or mixed group). The stem shown here ('qālu') carries only the stem vowel before the suffix, with the plural '-ū' supplied by the separate ending. Past tense, so the speaking is presented as already finished.

2.meaning: Feminine singular demonstrative pronoun, 'this (one)' — pointing to a single nearby thing that is grammatically feminine.
2.grammar: A demonstrative ('this') for a single feminine thing close at hand, contrasting with the masculine 'hādhā.' Demonstratives in Arabic do not change for grammatical case; the form stays fixed whether subject, object, or after a preposition.

3.meaning: A noun meaning 'grazing livestock / cattle' — the herd animals such as camels, cattle, sheep, and goats. Stated indefinitely, it means 'cattle' or 'livestock'.
3.grammar: A plural noun ('cattle/livestock'). The '-un' ending (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite and in the nominative state — typically the role of a subject or the thing being described.
3.root: ن-ع-م (n-ʿ-m) — bounty, ease; grazing livestock (a blessing)

4.meaning: A noun joined by 'and', meaning 'and tillage / crops' — planted fields and their cultivated produce.
4.grammar: A noun ('tillage/crops') joined by the connector 'wa-' ('and'). The '-un' ending (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite and in the nominative state — typically the role of a subject or the thing being described. (The 'w' of 'wa' is here written doubled for recitation flow.)
4.root: ح-ر-ث (ḥ-r-th) — to till, to plow, to cultivate; crops

5.meaning: A noun used to mean 'forbidden / off-limits / restricted' — something declared prohibited or set apart so that access to it is barred. Its root sense is of withholding and prohibition.
5.grammar: A noun ('a forbidden/restricted thing') used predicatively to mean 'off-limits'. The '-un' ending (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite and in the nominative state — typically the role of a subject or the thing being described.
5.root: ح-ج-ر (ḥ-j-r) — to forbid, to restrict, to wall off, to withhold

6.meaning: 'Not' — a particle of negation. Depending on context it denies a present fact, forbids an action, or rules something out ('do not / there is no').
6.grammar: A negating particle, 'not / no'. It is used to deny or prohibit — negating present-tense statements, expressing 'there is no...', or, with a command form, forbidding an action ('do not...').

7.meaning: A present-tense verb with attached object, 'eats it / feeds upon it' — to consume something as food. The attached 'it/them' is the thing eaten.
7.grammar: A present/imperfect verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he/it does'). The 'ya-' prefix marks the 'he/it' subject, and the '-u' vowel (seen before the pronoun) marks the ordinary (indicative) mood — a plain statement of action. The attached '-hā' is the object pronoun 'it/them' (for a feminine or plural-of-things referent).
7.root: ط-ع-م (ṭ-ʿ-m) — to taste, to eat, to feed; food

8.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
8.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

9.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
9.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

10.meaning: 'We will / We wish' — to will, want, or choose for something to be; expresses volition.
10.grammar: A present-tense verb. The prefix means 'we'; the '-u' ending marks the plain indicative ('we will / we wish'). Its nūn carries a shadda (doubling) because the preceding connector 'man' ('whoever') merges into it, so it is sounded '-nn-'.
10.root: ش-ي-أ (sh-y-ʾ) — to will, to wish, to want

11.meaning: A phrase meaning 'according to their claim / by their assertion'. The noun denotes an allegation or unfounded claim, often one that is baseless; with the attached 'their', it means 'their (mere) claim'.
11.grammar: A noun governed by the preposition 'bi-' ('by/according to'), which forces the genitive '-i' ending (seen before the pronoun). The suffix '-him' is the attached possessive pronoun 'their' for a group; its 'i'-vowel form follows the genitive '-i'.
11.root: ز-ع-م (z-ʿ-m) — to claim, to allege, to assert (often baselessly)

12.meaning: And livestock — grazing herd-animals such as camels, cattle, sheep, and goats kept for milk, meat, riding, and burden. The 'and' joins this word to what precedes it.
12.grammar: A noun (a plural in form) carrying the -un ending, which marks the nominative case (the doer/subject or a thing simply being named) together with nunation (-un), the mark of an indefinite noun, i.e. 'some livestock,' not 'the livestock.' The wa- prefix is a connector meaning 'and.'
12.root: ن-ع-م (n-ʿ-m) — ease, blessing, well-being (whence grazing cattle as a gift/bounty)

13.meaning: She/it was made forbidden, prohibited, declared unlawful and off-limits — set apart as sacred or sanctioned against. The opposite of being made permissible.
13.grammar: A past-tense passive verb (Form II, its doubled middle root letter giving intensity): 'she/it was made forbidden' — passive because no doer is named, only that the thing was prohibited. The ending -at marks a third-person feminine singular subject. The internal u–i vowel pattern of the stem is the mark of the passive ('was forbidden' rather than 'forbade').
13.root: ح-ر-م (ḥ-r-m) — to forbid; declare sacred or inviolable

14.meaning: Their backs — the upper/outer surfaces (of animals, things, or the earth), with an attached 'their' referring to a previously mentioned group.
14.grammar: A plural noun with the -u ending, marking the nominative case (the word stands as a subject or as something being named). The attached -hā means 'her / its / their,' referring back to a feminine singular or a non-human plural already mentioned.
14.root: ظ-ه-ر (ẓ-h-r) — back, to appear/become manifest, outer surface

15.meaning: And livestock — grazing herd-animals such as camels, cattle, sheep, and goats kept for milk, meat, riding, and burden. The 'and' joins this word to what precedes it.
15.grammar: A noun (a plural in form) carrying the -un ending, which marks the nominative case (the doer/subject or a thing simply being named) together with nunation (-un), the mark of an indefinite noun, i.e. 'some livestock,' not 'the livestock.' The wa- prefix is a connector meaning 'and.'
15.root: ن-ع-م (n-ʿ-m) — ease, blessing, well-being (whence grazing cattle as a gift/bounty)

16.meaning: 'Not' — a particle of negation. Depending on context it denies a present fact, forbids an action, or rules something out ('do not / there is no').
16.grammar: A negating particle, 'not / no'. It is used to deny or prohibit — negating present-tense statements, expressing 'there is no...', or, with a command form, forbidding an action ('do not...').

17.meaning: 'They remember / make mention of,' i.e., to call to mind, invoke, or mention — both inward recollection and outward utterance, often of Allah.
17.grammar: A present-tense verb. The -ūna ending marks a plural masculine subject ('they') and signals the ordinary (indicative) present tense — an ongoing or habitual remembering and mentioning.
17.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, mention, call to mind

18.meaning: Name — the word or designation by which someone or something is called; in worship, the invoking of a name (especially Allah's) over an act.
18.grammar: A noun ('ism,' 'name'). The final '-a' (fatḥa) is the accusative case, the form typically used when the word is the direct object of a verb — the thing being acted upon.
18.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — height, loftiness; the source of 'ism' (name)

19.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
19.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

20.meaning: 'On it / upon it / over it' — the preposition 'alā ('on, upon, against') joined to the pronoun 'it/her', referring to a single feminine or grammatically feminine thing.
20.grammar: 'ʿalā' is a preposition meaning 'on/upon/over'; its ending shifts to -ay when a pronoun is attached. The suffix -hā is the object pronoun for a single feminine (or feminine-gender) thing. Together they mean 'on it'. Words after a preposition stand in the genitive, though attached pronouns like -hā do not visibly change form.

21.meaning: As a fabrication — the act of inventing a lie and falsely attributing it (especially to Allah); a baseless concoction passed off as truth.
21.grammar: A verbal noun in the accusative case shown by the -an ending (with nunation). The accusative here typically expresses the reason or manner of an action — i.e. doing something 'as / out of / by way of' a fabrication.
21.root: ف-ر-ي (f-r-y) — to fabricate, invent, forge (a lie)

22.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
22.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

23.meaning: He will repay them — to requite, recompense, or pay back in full, whether with reward or with punishment; the 'them' is the object receiving the recompense.
23.grammar: A present-tense verb made future by the prefix sa- ('will, shortly will'). The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'); the long -ī is the verb's stem-vowel. The attached -him is the object pronoun 'them' (a group of males or mixed group).

24.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
24.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.
24.root: — (particle + relative pronoun)

25.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
25.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
25.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

26.meaning: They fabricate or invent falsely — to forge a lie, concoct something untrue and attribute it where it does not belong. The verb specifically names inventing falsehood and slander out of nothing.
26.grammar: Present-tense verb in the (form VIII) pattern, third-person masculine plural. The ya- prefix marks the third person and, together with the -ūna ending, yields 'they' (masculine plural) acting in ongoing/present time. The retained -na is the mark of the indicative ('they are fabricating / they fabricate').
26.root: ف-ر-ي (f-r-y) — fabricating, forging, inventing falsehood

1.meaning: And they said — to utter or declare in speech, with the action presented as completed by a group.
1.grammar: The prefix 'wa-' means 'and'. 'qāla' is the past-tense verb 'to say'; the '-ū' suffix marks a completed action done by 'they' (a masculine or mixed group). The stem shown here ('qālu') carries only the stem vowel before the suffix, with the plural '-ū' supplied by the separate ending. Past tense, so the speaking is presented as already finished.

2.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: Bellies / wombs (of) — the inner cavity of the body; the abdomen, and by extension the womb that carries young. The form links to a following noun ('the bellies OF …').
4.grammar: A plural noun with the -i ending, marking the genitive case: it typically links to a following noun ('… OF …') as a possessor or comes after a preposition. The bare ending (no nunation) signals it is bound to a following word in a possessive chain.
4.root: ب-ط-ن (b-ṭ-n) — belly, interior, that which is inner/hidden

5.meaning: This (feminine) — a pointing word ('this one here') used for a single nearby thing that is grammatically feminine.
5.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun ('this') for a single feminine thing close at hand. It is fixed in form and does not change for case; it commonly precedes the noun it points to.

6.meaning: 'the grazing livestock / cattle' — a collective term for domesticated herd animals such as camels, cattle, sheep, and goats, valued as wealth and as a provision.
6.grammar: A definite noun ('the …') with the -i (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a preceding noun in a possessive 'of …' relationship or follows a preposition. It is itself a plural of naʿam (livestock).
6.root: ن-ع-م (n-ʿ-m) — softness, ease; grazing livestock, bounty/blessing

7.meaning: Purely (one's own) / exclusively reserved — set apart for one party alone, unmixed and unshared; the feminine form of 'pure, unalloyed, exclusive.'
7.grammar: A feminine active participle: the base is خَالِص (khāliṣ), and the tā' marbūṭa (ة) is the feminine suffix -at (its preceding -a is the connecting vowel of that suffix, not part of the stem). The -un ending marks the nominative case together with nunation (indefinite). It describes something 'purely / exclusively' belonging to or reserved for someone.
7.root: خ-ل-ص (kh-l-ṣ) — to be pure, unmixed, sincere, set apart

8.meaning: For our males — belonging to or designated for the male members of a group; combines 'for/to,' the plural 'males,' and 'our.'
8.grammar: A plural noun preceded by the preposition li- ('for, to, belonging to'), which always puts its noun in the genitive case — shown by the -i ending before the pronoun. The attached -nā means 'us / our.'
8.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — male; also remembrance/mention (a related sense of the root)

9.meaning: And forbidden / made unlawful — declared prohibited and off-limits; the passive-participle sense 'something that has been made forbidden.' The 'and' joins it to what precedes.
9.grammar: A passive participle (form II, 'made/declared ____') with the -un ending: nominative case plus nunation, marking it indefinite ('a forbidden thing'). The wa- prefix means 'and.'
9.root: ح-ر-م (ḥ-r-m) — to forbid, prohibit, treat as sacred/inviolable

10.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on, upon, over,' and by extension 'against' or 'incumbent upon.' It can mark something resting on top of, an obligation laid on someone, or being set over/above something.
10.grammar: An indeclinable preposition (its form never changes). It governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case, and conveys location 'on/upon,' or figuratively duty or opposition ('against').

11.meaning: Our spouses / our mates (of) — husbands or wives, pairs, partners; the plural 'spouses' bound to the possessor 'our.'
11.grammar: A plural noun with the -i (genitive) ending, marking it as either following a preposition or linked to/possessed by what follows; here the attached pronoun -nā ('our') is the possessor. The genitive is also the case used after particles like li- ('for') and ʿalā ('upon').
11.root: ز-و-ج (z-w-j) — pair, mate, spouse, to join in a pair

12.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
12.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

13.meaning: He/it comes to be, becomes, or proves to be — a linking verb of being, asserting that a subject is or turns out to be in a certain state.
13.grammar: A present-tense verb of 'being', 3rd-person masculine singular ('he/it is/becomes'). It stands in the jussive mood, marked by sukūn on the final nūn (the weak middle letter of the root having dropped); this conditional form typically means 'if he should be …' or 'let it be …'.
13.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

14.meaning: Dead / a carcass — a creature that has died (especially one not slaughtered); also used of lifeless carrion. The feminine indefinite form.
14.grammar: A feminine noun/adjective: the base is مَيۡت (mayt), and the tā' marbūṭa (ة) is the feminine suffix -at (its preceding -a is the connecting vowel of that suffix, not part of the stem). The -an ending marks the accusative case with nunation (indefinite). The accusative commonly marks the direct object of a verb or a predicate after certain verbs ('to be ___').

15.meaning: Means 'so they / then they' — the connector 'so/then' joined to the standalone pronoun 'they' (for a group of males or a mixed group). It draws a consequence and then names the subject.
15.grammar: The connecting particle fa- ('so/then', drawing a result or sequence from what precedes) attached to the detached subject pronoun hum ('they', masculine or mixed plural). As a standalone pronoun it has no case ending and serves as the subject of what follows.

16.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
16.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

17.meaning: 'Partners' / 'associates' / 'sharers' — the plural of 'partner', those who jointly share in something (such as property, ownership, or a claim).
17.grammar: A masculine plural noun (the broken plural of شَرِيك 'partner') on the pattern afʿilāʾ. The -u ending is the nominative case, marking it as the subject or the thing being identified ('partners'); this plural pattern does not take nunation.

18.meaning: He will repay them — to requite, recompense, or pay back in full, whether with reward or with punishment; the 'them' is the object receiving the recompense.
18.grammar: A present-tense verb made future by the prefix sa- ('will, shortly will'). The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'); the long -ī is the verb's stem-vowel. The attached -him is the object pronoun 'them' (a group of males or mixed group).

19.meaning: Their describing / their (false) attributing — the act of characterizing or ascribing a quality to something, often a wrongful labeling; with attached 'their.'
19.grammar: A verbal noun with the -a ending, marking the accusative case (typically the direct object of a verb, or the focus of an action). The attached -hum ('their') is the possessor, so it means 'their act of describing/ascribing.'
19.root: و-ص-ف (w-ṣ-f) — to describe, characterize, ascribe a quality

20.meaning: An emphasis particle fused with a pronoun, meaning 'indeed He' or 'truly He'. The particle inna strongly affirms and certifies the statement that follows ('it is certainly the case that…'), with 'He' as its subject.
20.grammar: The emphasising particle inna ('indeed/truly') with the attached pronoun -hu ('He'). inna affirms and strengthens the whole statement and grammatically takes a following noun or pronoun as its subject. The lengthened -hū is how this pronoun is pronounced after an -u vowel.

21.meaning: All-Wise: possessing perfect wisdom — placing everything in its right place with flawless knowledge, judgment, and purpose. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's consummate wisdom.
21.grammar: A masculine singular adjective/intensive noun on the faʿīl pattern, expressing a deep, settled quality of wisdom. The final -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite and nominative — the case used for a subject or, very often, a predicate describing the doer ('[He is] All-Wise').
21.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, to be wise

22.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'All-Knowing / fully aware' — one whose knowledge is complete, deep, and all-encompassing; as a divine attribute it denotes Allah's perfect knowledge.
22.grammar: An intensive adjective (the pattern faʿīl conveys 'thoroughly, abundantly'). The ending -un is the indefinite nominative — the nominative case marks it as the subject or the quality being affirmed, and the -n (nunation) signals 'a / an', i.e. indefinite. So it reads '(is) all-knowing'.

1.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.

2.meaning: 'he lost / suffered loss' — to forfeit or be deprived of something of value, ending in ruin or deficit; the opposite of profit and gain.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular: 'he lost / has lost.' The final -a is the standard ending marking a completed action done by 'he.'
2.root: خ-س-ر (kh-s-r) — loss, ruin, to be a loser

3.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
3.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

4.meaning: They killed / they slew — the past-tense act of putting to death, carried out by a group of people.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb. The suffix -ū marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they' did it). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention and is not pronounced.

5.meaning: Their children / their offspring — sons and daughters, descendants; the plural 'children' with attached 'their.'
5.grammar: A plural noun with the -a ending, marking the accusative case — most often the direct object of a verb (the ones to whom something is done). The attached -hum means 'their.'
5.root: و-ل-د (w-l-d) — to give birth; child, offspring

6.meaning: Out of foolishness / in folly — senseless, ignorant lack of sound judgment; rashness and lightness of mind.
6.grammar: A noun with the -an ending: accusative case with nunation (indefinite). This accusative typically explains the cause or manner of an action — i.e. doing something 'out of / in a state of' foolishness. (The small mark over the nun indicates a nasal pronunciation before the following letter.)
6.root: س-ف-ه (s-f-h) — foolishness, folly, weakness of judgment

7.meaning: 'Without' or 'other than' — the preposition bi- joined to ghayr, a noun meaning 'other than / not / lacking', together conveying the absence of something ('with no …', 'wrongfully').
7.grammar: bi- is a preposition that takes the genitive; ghayr is a noun of exception/negation ('other than'). Its -i ending is genitive (required after bi-) and it also links to a following noun in a possessive 'of' relationship, so 'bi-ghayri X' means 'without X / other than X'.
7.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — otherness, difference, being other than

8.meaning: 'Knowledge.' A noun denoting sure, established knowing — to know a thing as it truly is. In its indefinite form it often appears in the sense 'any knowledge (at all).'
8.grammar: A noun with the -in ending (genitive with nunation, 'tanwīn'), marking it as indefinite ('any knowledge'). The genitive -i is the form used after a preposition such as 'of' or 'by' — e.g. 'of any knowledge.'

9.meaning: And they forbade / made unlawful — the past-tense act, by a group, of declaring something prohibited and off-limits. The 'and' joins it to what precedes.
9.grammar: A past-tense verb (form II, an intensive/causative pattern: 'to declare/make forbidden'). The suffix -ū marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The silent alif after -ū is only a spelling convention. The wa- prefix means 'and.'
9.root: ح-ر-م (ḥ-r-m) — to forbid, prohibit, treat as inviolable

10.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
10.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

11.meaning: He provided/granted them sustenance — to bestow provision and the means of life upon someone, the giving coming from the Provider.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb. The '-a' on the stem marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he provided'), and the attached '-hum(u)' is the object pronoun 'them.' The base vowel of that pronoun is shifted to '-humu' to smooth the join with a following word.
11.root: ر-ز-ق (r-z-q) — provision, sustenance, the bestowing of livelihood

12.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
12.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
12.root: — (proper divine name)

13.meaning: As a fabrication — the act of inventing a lie and falsely attributing it (especially to Allah); a baseless concoction passed off as truth.
13.grammar: A verbal noun in the accusative case shown by the -an ending (with nunation). The accusative here typically expresses the reason or manner of an action — i.e. doing something 'as / out of / by way of' a fabrication.
13.root: ف-ر-ي (f-r-y) — to fabricate, invent, forge (a lie)

14.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
14.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
14.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

15.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
15.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

16.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
16.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.

17.meaning: 'they went astray / erred' — to lose the right way, to wander off into error or misguidance.
17.grammar: A past-tense verb with the -ū ending meaning 'they' (masculine plural). It conveys a completed action: 'they went astray / erred.'
17.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, lose the way, go astray

18.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
18.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

19.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
19.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
19.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

20.meaning: Rightly guided ones — those who have accepted and follow true guidance, walking the correct path; the plural of one who is guided.
20.grammar: An active participle (form VIII, 'one who takes/accepts guidance') in the sound masculine plural. The -īna ending marks the accusative or genitive case for such plurals — i.e. these people as the object of a verb, after a preposition, or as a predicate, rather than as the bare subject (which would be -ūna).
20.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance, to guide, to show the right way

1.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
1.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

2.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

3.meaning: He brought into being / He originated — to create and cause to grow or develop from nothing, to set in existence; a past-tense act by a single male subject.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb (form IV, a causative pattern: 'to cause to arise/grow, to originate'). With no attached subject pronoun, the bare form carries a built-in third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The final -a is part of the verb's stem.
3.root: ن-ش-أ (n-sh-ʾ) — to arise, grow, come into being; (IV) to originate, cause to grow

4.meaning: 'Gardens' — the plural of a lush, walled garden thick with trees whose foliage covers the ground. The root sense is concealment by dense greenery; it is the standard word for the gardens of Paradise.
4.grammar: An indefinite sound feminine plural noun ('gardens'). The '-in' (tanwīn) ending marks it as indefinite ('some gardens'), and for this plural form it stands in the oblique case (genitive or accusative), used after prepositions/possessives or as a direct object.
4.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal, hide (hence a dense garden)

5.meaning: Trellised / raised on supports — plants (such as vines) trained up onto frames or arbors; the feminine plural of 'something propped up and trellised.'
5.grammar: A passive participle ('made to be trellised') in the feminine sound plural (-āt). The -in ending marks the genitive case with nunation (indefinite) — the case used after prepositions or in a possessive link, here describing indefinite feminine-plural things.
5.root: ع-ر-ش (ʿ-r-sh) — trellis, arbor, raised structure, throne

6.meaning: A noun meaning 'other than / not / different from' — used to negate or set apart, indicating something contrary to or distinct from what is mentioned.
6.grammar: A noun of exception/negation meaning 'other than,' prefixed with wa- ('and'). It is followed by another noun in the genitive ('other than …'). The -a ending here is accusative, the case marking a direct object or a noun governed in that position.

7.meaning: Trellised / raised on supports — plants (such as vines) trained up onto frames or arbors; the feminine plural of 'something propped up and trellised.'
7.grammar: A passive participle ('made to be trellised') in the feminine sound plural (-āt). The -in ending marks the genitive case with nunation (indefinite) — the case used after prepositions or in a possessive link, here describing indefinite feminine-plural things.
7.root: ع-ر-ش (ʿ-r-sh) — trellis, arbor, raised structure, throne

8.meaning: And the date-palm — the palm tree that bears dates. The form carries 'and' plus 'the.'
8.grammar: A collective noun ('date-palms' as a class) with the definite article al- ('the') and the -a ending, marking the accusative case — typically the direct object of a verb. The wa- prefix means 'and'; the 'l' of al- assimilates into the following 'n' (so it is written/pronounced an-nakhl).

9.meaning: And the crops / the standing grain — cultivated plants and seed-produce, sown fields of grain. The form carries 'and' plus 'the.'
9.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the') and the -a ending, marking the accusative case — typically the direct object of a verb. The wa- prefix means 'and'; the 'l' of al- assimilates into the following 'z' (pronounced az-zarʿ).

10.meaning: Differing / varied — varying and diverse, not uniform; an active participle describing things that differ among themselves.
10.grammar: An active participle (form VIII, 'one that differs/varies') with the -an ending: accusative case with nunation (indefinite). The accusative often marks a descriptive state — describing something as being 'in a varied / differing' condition.
10.root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — to come after, differ, be at variance

11.meaning: Its produce / its fruit-yield (to eat) — the edible crop or harvest a plant brings forth; that which is eaten of it. With attached 'its.'
11.grammar: A noun with the -u ending, marking the nominative case (a subject or something simply being named). The attached -hu means 'his / its,' referring back to a masculine singular thing already mentioned.
11.root: أ-ك-ل (ʾ-k-l) — to eat; food, edible produce

12.meaning: And the olives / olive-trees — the olive and its tree. The form carries 'and' plus 'the.'
12.grammar: A collective noun ('olives / the olive' as a class) with the definite article al- ('the') and the -a ending, marking the accusative case — typically the direct object of a verb. The wa- prefix means 'and'; the 'l' of al- assimilates into the following 'z' (pronounced az-zaytūn).
12.root: ز-ي-ت (z-y-t) — olive, olive-oil

13.meaning: A noun meaning 'and the pomegranate(s)' — the pomegranate fruit and tree, used collectively.
13.grammar: A definite collective noun prefixed with wa- ('and'). The l of 'al-' assimilates into the following r (pronounced 'ar-rummān'). The -a ending is accusative, the case that typically marks the direct object of a verb.

14.meaning: 'Resembling / similar / alike.' An active participle describing something that bears a likeness to something else, things that match or correspond to one another in form or kind. The pattern carries a reciprocal sense, 'mutually resembling.'
14.grammar: An active participle of the reciprocal (form VI) verb, functioning as a noun/adjective. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative ('a resembling one'), the case used for objects of verbs and for descriptive/circumstantial terms; the doubled 'n' sound (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite.

15.meaning: A noun meaning 'other than / not / different from' — used to negate or set apart, indicating something contrary to or distinct from what is mentioned.
15.grammar: A noun of exception/negation meaning 'other than,' prefixed with wa- ('and'). It is followed by another noun in the genitive ('other than …'). The -a ending here is accusative, the case marking a direct object or a noun governed in that position.

16.meaning: An active participle meaning 'mutually resembling / alike one another / similar' — things that correspond to and look like each other.
16.grammar: An active participle (form VI), a pattern of mutual/reciprocal action: 'resembling each other.' The mu- prefix forms the 'one being/doing.' The -in ending (tanwīn) marks it indefinite and genitive — the case taken after 'other than' (ghayr) or a preposition, or when linked to a preceding noun.

17.meaning: 'Eat!' — a command addressed to more than one person, telling a group to eat or partake of food.
17.grammar: An imperative (command) verb. The -ū ending directs the command at a group ('you all, eat!'). This verb's command form drops its original first root letter, so the stem appears simply as kul-. The silent alif written after the wāw is a spelling convention for the plural ending.

18.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
18.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

19.meaning: A noun with attached pronoun meaning 'its fruit / its produce' — the fruit or yield of a tree or plant. With the suffix: 'its fruit.'
19.grammar: A noun with a possessive pronoun. The -hi ending means 'its/his,' showing possession ('its fruit'). The -i vowel signals the genitive case (which is also why the pronoun appears as -hi rather than -hu) — the case taken after a preposition or when one noun is possessed by another.
19.root: ث-م-ر (th-m-r) — fruit, yield, produce

20.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
20.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.
20.root: — (a time particle; no triliteral root)

21.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'it bore fruit / it produced fruit' — when a tree or plant brings forth its fruit.
21.grammar: A perfect (past-tense) verb in the causative (form IV) pattern, here meaning 'to bring forth fruit.' It carries no separable subject suffix: the bare form, ending in the inherent short -a vowel of the stem, already denotes a third-person masculine singular subject, 'he/it (did).'
21.root: ث-م-ر (th-m-r) — fruit, yield, bearing fruit

22.meaning: And give / hand over / bring — a command to deliver something to someone, to render it to its due recipient.
22.grammar: The conjunction wa- ('and') joined to a plural command verb of the causative (af'ala) pattern, meaning to make something come to someone, i.e. to give. The -ū ending marks a masculine-plural addressee being told to give.
22.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (causative) to give, bring

23.meaning: Its rightful due, the obligatory claim or right that belongs to it. The stem ḥaqq denotes truth, rightness, and a binding entitlement that someone or something is genuinely owed.
23.grammar: A noun with the attached pronoun '-hu' meaning 'its' or 'his'. The base carries an accusative '-a' vowel, which typically marks a word as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon), here joined to a possessor.
23.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, rightness, a binding entitlement or due

24.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
24.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
24.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

25.meaning: Its harvesting or reaping; the gathering-in of crops. The stem ḥaṣād refers to the act or time of cutting and collecting what has been grown.
25.grammar: A verbal noun with the attached pronoun meaning 'its' or 'his'. The '-i' vowel before the pronoun reflects the genitive (possessive/'of') case, which links the word to a possessor or follows a preposition.
25.root: ح-ص-د (ḥ-ṣ-d) — to reap, harvest, gather a crop

26.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
26.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

27.meaning: That you act wastefully or go to excess; to overstep the proper limit, squander, or be immoderate. It conveys spending or doing beyond what is right or needed.
27.grammar: A present-tense verb in a form that often follows particles of negation, prohibition, or purpose. The 'tu-' prefix plus '-ū' ending mean 'you (plural)'. The final short vowel is dropped (showing 'tusrifū' not 'tusrifūna'), which signals the verb is governed by such a particle (e.g. 'do not…' or 'so that…').
27.root: س-ر-ف (s-r-f) — to exceed the limit, waste, be extravagant

28.meaning: An emphasis particle fused with a pronoun, meaning 'indeed He' or 'truly He'. The particle inna strongly affirms and certifies the statement that follows ('it is certainly the case that…'), with 'He' as its subject.
28.grammar: The emphasising particle inna ('indeed/truly') with the attached pronoun -hu ('He'). inna affirms and strengthens the whole statement and grammatically takes a following noun or pronoun as its subject. The lengthened -hū is how this pronoun is pronounced after an -u vowel.

29.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
29.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

30.meaning: He loves / likes / holds dear. To have affection for and approval of something or someone.
30.grammar: A present-tense verb in the fourth pattern, third-person masculine singular ('he…'). The yu- prefix signals a single masculine subject, and the final -u ending marks the indicative mood, presenting the action as an established fact or ongoing reality.
30.root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b) — love, affection; to hold dear

31.meaning: Those who are wasteful or excessive; people who habitually overstep proper bounds, squander, or transgress moderation.
31.grammar: An active participle ('the ones who do X') with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The '-īna' ending marks a masculine sound plural in the accusative or genitive — the form used when such a word is an object or follows a preposition.
31.root: س-ر-ف (s-r-f) — to exceed the limit, waste, be extravagant

1.meaning: A connector meaning 'and', joined to the preposition 'from / of', introducing a portion or origin — 'and from' or 'and among'.
1.grammar: Two particles: wa- ('and') plus the preposition min ('from, of, among'). Min normally appears as 'min', but its final vowel shifts to 'mina' when the next word begins with the definite article, simply to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

2.meaning: 'the grazing livestock / cattle' — a collective term for domesticated herd animals such as camels, cattle, sheep, and goats, valued as wealth and as a provision.
2.grammar: A definite noun ('the …') with the -i (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a preceding noun in a possessive 'of …' relationship or follows a preposition. It is itself a plural of naʿam (livestock).
2.root: ن-ع-م (n-ʿ-m) — softness, ease; grazing livestock, bounty/blessing

3.meaning: Beasts of burden; animals large or capable enough to carry loads (such as for transport or labour). The word names livestock suited to bearing weight.
3.grammar: A feminine noun (the tā' marbūṭa is part of the stem). The '-an' tanwīn ending is the accusative indefinite, which marks a word as a direct object or as a specification, and often answers 'as what?' or 'of what kind?'.

4.meaning: And animals fit for slaughter or for furnishing — smaller livestock kept for their meat, wool, or hides (as opposed to those used for carrying). 'Farsh' suggests creatures low to the ground or spread out like a furnishing.
4.grammar: The prefix 'wa-' means 'and'. The '-an' ending is the accusative indefinite, marking the word as a direct object or as a category-specification ('as X').
4.root: ف-ر-ش (f-r-sh) — to spread out, lay low; a furnishing or that which is spread

5.meaning: 'Eat!' — a command addressed to more than one person, telling a group to eat or partake of food.
5.grammar: An imperative (command) verb. The -ū ending directs the command at a group ('you all, eat!'). This verb's command form drops its original first root letter, so the stem appears simply as kul-. The silent alif written after the wāw is a spelling convention for the plural ending.

6.meaning: From what / from that which — a fusion of the preposition 'from' with the relative 'what/which', introducing the thing or situation being referred to.
6.grammar: A merger of 'min' ('from') and 'mā' ('what/that which'); the 'n' of 'min' assimilates into the 'm' of 'mā', doubling it. The combination means 'from what ...' and typically introduces a following clause describing the thing referred to. Being particles, neither part takes a case ending.

7.meaning: A construction meaning 'He provided you / granted you sustenance' — to bestow provision (food, wealth, any good thing) upon someone. The provider is 'He'; 'you' are the recipients.
7.grammar: A past-tense verb for a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'); the final -a is the standard past-tense ending. The attached -kum ('you all') is the object; its vowel is raised to -kumu for ease before a following word beginning with the article.
7.root: ر-ز-ق (r-z-q) — provision, sustenance, bestowal of livelihood

8.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
8.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

9.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
9.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

10.meaning: 'You (plural) follow' — a verb meaning to come after, pursue, take as a guide, or obey and imitate; addressed to a group.
10.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form VIII), second-person masculine plural ('you follow'). The ta- prefix marks the addressee 'you'; the -ū ending marks a masculine plural 'you all'. The dropped final nūn (here -ū rather than -ūna) signals that the verb is in a subjunctive/jussive mood, typical after particles of negation, prohibition, or purpose.
10.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, come after, pursue

11.meaning: Footsteps, footprints, or paths — the steps and tracks left by walking; figuratively, the way or course someone treads.
11.grammar: A feminine sound plural ('footsteps, paths'; plural of khuṭwa). The -āt is the feminine plural marker; the final -i is the ending such plurals take in the genitive, which generally links the word to a following noun ('footsteps OF …') or follows a preposition.
11.root: خ-ط-و (kh-ṭ-w) — to step, stride, pace

12.meaning: The Shayṭān — Satan, the devil: a rebellious, evil being who tempts and misleads; the term suggests one who is far removed from goodness and burning in defiance.
12.grammar: A definite masculine noun ('the Satan / the devil'). The final -i is the genitive ending, which generally links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …') or follows a preposition.
12.root: ش-ط-ن (sh-ṭ-n) — to be remote (from good/mercy); a devil

13.meaning: An emphasis particle fused with a pronoun, meaning 'indeed He' or 'truly He'. The particle inna strongly affirms and certifies the statement that follows ('it is certainly the case that…'), with 'He' as its subject.
13.grammar: The emphasising particle inna ('indeed/truly') with the attached pronoun -hu ('He'). inna affirms and strengthens the whole statement and grammatically takes a following noun or pronoun as its subject. The lengthened -hū is how this pronoun is pronounced after an -u vowel.

14.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
14.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

15.meaning: A noun meaning 'enemy', 'foe', or 'adversary' — one who shows hostility or opposition. The single Arabic form can refer to one enemy or collectively to enemies.
15.grammar: A noun carrying the -un ending: nominative case (typically the subject, or the completing word after 'to be') combined with tanwīn, the indefinite '-n' that marks it as 'an enemy' rather than 'the enemy'.
15.root: ع-د-و (ʿ-d-w) — hostility, enmity, transgressing a limit

16.meaning: Clear, plain, and self-evident; that which makes things manifest. The form carries an active sense: not merely 'clear in itself' but 'making clear,' something that openly displays its nature and leaves no ambiguity.
16.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' word) on the form mufʿil, meaning 'one who/that which makes [something] clear.' The final -un is the indefinite nominative ending ('a …'), the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it.

1.meaning: Eight; the cardinal number 8.
1.grammar: A cardinal number (the tā' marbūṭa is part of the word's feminine form). The final '-a' vowel is the accusative, marking the word as a direct object (the thing counted or acted upon). Numbers like this take an opposite-gender form and are followed by the counted noun in the genitive ('eight of…').
1.root: ث-م-ن (th-m-n) — the notion of 'eight'; an eighth part

2.meaning: Pairs, mates, or kinds; a plural meaning 'spouses', 'counterparts', or 'paired sorts'. A single zawj is one of a pair, whether a mate, a partner, or one variety set alongside another.
2.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural. The '-in' ending is the genitive indefinite, the case used after prepositions, after a possessor, and notably after numbers (the counted thing comes in the genitive: 'X of pairs').
2.root: ز-و-ج (z-w-j) — to pair, couple, join one to another

3.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
3.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

4.meaning: The sheep; domesticated wool-bearing flock animals, taken as a collective kind.
4.grammar: A collective noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'); the 'l' assimilates into the following 'ḍ' (a 'sun letter'). The '-i' ending is genitive, used after a possessor ('of') or a preposition.

5.meaning: Two; the cardinal number 2 (in its masculine dual form), denoting a matched pair.
5.grammar: The number 'two' in dual form. The '-ayni' ending marks the dual in the accusative or genitive case — the shape used when the word is an object or follows a preposition. The initial 'i' is a helping vowel (a 'connecting hamza') that smooths pronunciation.
5.root: ث-ن-ي (th-n-y) — twoness, doubling, a second of a pair

6.meaning: A connector meaning 'and', joined to the preposition 'from / of', introducing a portion or origin — 'and from' or 'and among'.
6.grammar: Two particles: wa- ('and') plus the preposition min ('from, of, among'). Min normally appears as 'min', but its final vowel shifts to 'mina' when the next word begins with the definite article, simply to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

7.meaning: The goats; domesticated horned browsing flock animals, taken as a collective kind.
7.grammar: A collective noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The '-i' ending is genitive, the case used after a possessor ('of') or following a preposition.

8.meaning: Two; the cardinal number 2 (in its masculine dual form), denoting a matched pair.
8.grammar: The number 'two' in dual form. The '-ayni' ending marks the dual in the accusative or genitive case — the shape used when the word is an object or follows a preposition. The initial 'i' is a helping vowel (a 'connecting hamza') that smooths pronunciation.
8.root: ث-ن-ي (th-n-y) — twoness, doubling, a second of a pair

9.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
9.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

10.meaning: The two males? — the dual 'two males' carrying a prefixed questioning particle, so it asks 'is it the two males…?'. A male is a being of the masculine sex.
10.grammar: An interrogative particle 'a-' (here drawn out as 'ā' before the article) prefixed to a noun, posing a yes/no question. 'al-' is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'dh', a sun letter). The '-ayni' dual ending marks the accusative or genitive — the form used for an object or after a preposition.
10.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — the male, maleness; also remembering and mention

11.meaning: 'He forbade / made unlawful / declared sacredly off-limits.' To prohibit something firmly, to render it ḥarām — barred and inviolable, set outside what is permitted.
11.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) Form II verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he [did it],' a completed past action. The doubled middle root letter (Form II) gives an intensive/causative force — 'to make something forbidden/inviolable.'
11.root: ح-ر-م (ḥ-r-m) — prohibition, sacredness, inviolability

12.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'or', used especially to introduce the second part of a question ('…or…?'). The form 'ami' is the particle 'am' with a helping vowel -i added so it can be pronounced smoothly before a following word that begins with a connecting (elidable) alif.
12.grammar: 'am' is a coordinating particle that links alternatives, characteristically in an either/or question. The final -i here is not a case ending; it is a connecting vowel added to avoid an awkward consonant cluster when the next word begins with a silent (linking) alif.

13.meaning: The two females — a pair of female persons. The dual of unthā ('female'), made definite with 'the'.
13.grammar: The dual form of unthā, with the definite article al-. The -ayni ending marks exactly two and is the genitive/accusative form of the dual (its other form is -āni for the subject case). So it means 'the two females', in a position governed by a preposition or as object/possessed term.

14.meaning: Or rather…; as for…; or is it…? A particle that introduces an alternative or a fresh case for consideration, often pairing options ('this… or that…') or heading a topic ('as for X…').
14.grammar: A compound of the disjunctive particle 'am' ('or', used especially in questions to offer an alternative) with 'mā' ('what / that which'). Together they raise a further possibility, roughly 'or what about…' or 'or that which…'. Particles like these do not change their endings.

15.meaning: It (feminine) enclosed, contained, comprised, or wrapped around something. The verb conveys taking in and holding within.
15.grammar: A past-tense verb (Form VIII, which often gives a reflexive or self-involving sense — 'to wrap oneself around, comprise'). The '-at' ending marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('she' or 'it'). The opening 'i' is a helping vowel (connecting hamza).

16.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
16.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

17.meaning: Wombs; the bodily vessels in which offspring are carried before birth. By extension the same root conveys kinship and the ties of blood relationship.
17.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of 'raḥim' ('womb'). The '-u' ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject — the doer or topic of a sentence.
17.root: ر-ح-م (r-ḥ-m) — the womb; mercy and the bonds of kinship

18.meaning: The two females — a pair of female persons. The dual of unthā ('female'), made definite with 'the'.
18.grammar: The dual form of unthā, with the definite article al-. The -ayni ending marks exactly two and is the genitive/accusative form of the dual (its other form is -āni for the subject case). So it means 'the two females', in a position governed by a preposition or as object/possessed term.

19.meaning: Inform me!; tell me, give me news of it. A command to convey information or report something to the speaker.
19.grammar: A command verb (Form II, an intensive 'inform/announce') addressed to a plural 'you' via the '-ū' ending, with the attached object pronoun '-nī' meaning 'me'. The 'n' before '-ī' is a protective 'nūn' that links the verb to the pronoun.
19.root: ن-ب-أ (n-b-ʾ) — news, tidings; to announce or inform

20.meaning: With knowledge; by means of sure information or understanding. 'ʿilm' is firm, reliable knowing as opposed to guesswork.
20.grammar: The preposition 'bi-' ('with / by means of') attached to a noun. Any noun after a preposition takes the genitive, shown here by the '-in' ending (genitive indefinite).
20.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; knowledge, certain awareness

21.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
21.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

22.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
22.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
22.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

23.meaning: The plural of 'ṣādiq': 'truthful ones', 'those who speak the truth', 'the sincere and reliable'. It describes people whose words and conduct match reality.
23.grammar: 'ṣādiq' is an active participle ('one who is truthful'). The '-īna' ending is a 'sound' masculine plural marker; the '-ī-' form (rather than '-ū-') signals that the noun is functioning as an object or is governed by a preposition/particle, while the '-na' completes the plural ('the truthful ones').
23.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — truthfulness, sincerity, to speak truly

parts.en: or (in alternatives, esp. after a question)

17.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case or tense ending). It typically introduces the second branch of a two-part question or a balanced alternative, presenting the two as equally consequential.

18.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

19.meaning: Witnesses — those present who observe and can testify to what they saw; can also carry the sense of those who bear witness. Plural.
19.grammar: A broken plural on the fuʿalāʾ (فُعَلَاء) pattern, which is a diptote: it takes the -a ending for BOTH the accusative and the genitive and never takes tanwīn (the final 'n'). Because of this, the -a alone does not tell you the case — the word could be a direct object (accusative) or governed by a preposition ('of/among', genitive). Only when made definite or put into construct would it take the ordinary -i in the genitive.
19.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — to witness, observe, testify, be present

20.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
20.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

21.meaning: He enjoined, charged, or instructed you (plural); to give a binding directive or solemn counsel. The verb conveys laying a duty or earnest recommendation upon someone.
21.grammar: A past-tense verb (Form II, intensive 'to charge/enjoin'), third-person masculine singular ('he') by its base shape, with the attached object pronoun '-kum' ('you all'). The pronoun's final vowel appears as '-kumu' to ease into a following word.
21.root: و-ص-ي (w-ṣ-y) — to enjoin, charge, bequeath, counsel

22.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
22.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

23.meaning: A prepositional phrase meaning 'by this' or 'with this' — the preposition 'with/by means of' joined to the demonstrative 'this', pointing to something near or just mentioned.
23.grammar: A preposition bi- ('with', 'by') attached to the demonstrative pronoun hādhā ('this', masculine singular). The demonstrative is invariable in form here; the preposition indicates instrument or means ('by means of this') or association ('with this').

24.meaning: A compound meaning 'then whoever' or 'so whoever'. It combines 'then/so' with the conditional/relative 'who', introducing whatever person meets a stated condition.
24.grammar: The connector fa- ('then/so', often answering or following a condition) joined to man ('whoever / the one who'), which refers to people and introduces a condition: 'whoever does X…'. man does not change its ending; the clause after it supplies the rest of the meaning.

25.meaning: An elative adjective meaning 'more / most wrongdoing, unjust, or oppressive' — comparing degrees of ẓulm (placing things out of their rightful place, transgression).
25.grammar: An elative (comparative/superlative) noun on the pattern afʿal, meaning 'more/most unjust'. It ends in -u (nominative), the case typical of a subject or predicate.
25.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — wrongdoing, injustice, putting something where it does not belong

26.meaning: A combination meaning 'than whoever / than one who' or 'from whoever' — the preposition min ('from/than') merged with man ('who/whoever'). It links a comparison or origin to an unspecified person.
26.grammar: The preposition min ('from', and 'than' in comparisons) fused with the relative/indefinite pronoun man ('who(ever)'). The nūn of min assimilates into the mīm of man, so min + man becomes mimman. The whole final nūn belongs to man, not to min; the kasrah on it (-i) is a liaison (waṣl) vowel added to keep two unvowelled consonants (sukūns) from meeting before the next word. Read together: mimmani, 'than/from the one who'.
26.root: — (particles/pronoun; no root)

27.meaning: 'He fabricated, invented, forged (a lie); he concocted falsely' — made something up and falsely attributed it, especially a lie. A verb of deliberate fabrication.

parts.en: connecting (helping) vowel for the verb pattern
past-tense 3rd person masculine singular ending '-ā' (from a weak final root letter)

27.grammar: A past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he fabricated'). It is a Form VIII (ifta'ala) verb. The final '-ā' (written as alif maqṣūra) is how the past-tense '-a' ending appears when the root ends in a weak letter (w/y). The initial 'i-' is a helping vowel that lets the consonant cluster of this pattern be pronounced.
27.root: ف-ر-ي (f-r-y) — to fabricate, forge, invent (a falsehood)

28.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
28.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
28.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

29.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
29.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

30.meaning: A noun meaning 'a lie / falsehood' — a deliberately false statement, an untruth fabricated against the truth.
30.grammar: An indefinite noun ('a lie') with the accusative -an ending (tanwīn). The accusative commonly marks the object of a verb (e.g. fabricating a lie); the -an tanwīn shows it is indefinite.
30.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie, to declare false
