31.meaning: So as to lead astray; in order that he/it mislead or cause to wander from the right path. It expresses the purpose or result of leading someone into error.
31.grammar: The particle 'li-' ('so that / in order to') governs the verb, which is why it ends in '-a' (the subjunctive, used for purpose). The 'yu-' prefix marks a third-person 'he/it' subject in a causative form (Form IV: 'to make go astray').
31.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to go astray, lose the way, err

32.meaning: Mankind, humanity, people in general — the collective of human beings.
32.grammar: A definite noun ('the people') with the attached 'al-' ('the'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (a sun letter), which is why the 'n' is doubled — this is a pronunciation effect, not a separate piece. The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the one being acted upon) or the subject of certain particles.
32.root: ن-و-س (n-w-s) — to move/sway; by extension, people

33.meaning: 'Without' or 'other than' — the preposition bi- joined to ghayr, a noun meaning 'other than / not / lacking', together conveying the absence of something ('with no …', 'wrongfully').
33.grammar: bi- is a preposition that takes the genitive; ghayr is a noun of exception/negation ('other than'). Its -i ending is genitive (required after bi-) and it also links to a following noun in a possessive 'of' relationship, so 'bi-ghayri X' means 'without X / other than X'.
33.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — otherness, difference, being other than

34.meaning: 'Knowledge.' A noun denoting sure, established knowing — to know a thing as it truly is. In its indefinite form it often appears in the sense 'any knowledge (at all).'
34.grammar: A noun with the -in ending (genitive with nunation, 'tanwīn'), marking it as indefinite ('any knowledge'). The genitive -i is the form used after a preposition such as 'of' or 'by' — e.g. 'of any knowledge.'

35.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
35.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

36.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
36.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

37.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
37.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

38.meaning: 'He guides / leads on the right way' — to show someone the correct path, direct them rightly, or lead them to a goal, whether literally or in matters of belief and conduct.
38.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: the ya- prefix means 'he'. The verb ends in a long -ī (a weak final letter); in this indicative form the long vowel stands in place of the usual -u mood marker, still conveying a plain, ongoing statement ('he guides').
38.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance, showing the way, leading rightly

39.meaning: the people / the folk — a body of people, a community or group regarded collectively (here in the accusative form).
39.grammar: The l- prefix is the definite article 'the'. The final -a ending is accusative. Since the verb it follows is passive (and so takes no direct object), this accusative is adverbial — marking the circumstance or setting of the action ('before / in front of the people') rather than a thing being acted upon.
39.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to arise; a people standing together

40.meaning: The wrongdoers; those who commit injustice, oppression, or place things outside their right setting. Ẓulm is putting something where it does not belong and so transgressing against truth or against others.
40.grammar: An active participle ('the ones who do X') with the definite article 'al-' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'ẓ', a sun letter). The '-īna' ending marks a masculine sound plural in the accusative or genitive — the form used as an object or after a preposition.
40.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — injustice, wrongdoing, placing a thing wrongly

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: 'Not' — a particle of negation. Depending on context it denies a present fact, forbids an action, or rules something out ('do not / there is no').
2.grammar: A negating particle, 'not / no'. It is used to deny or prohibit — negating present-tense statements, expressing 'there is no...', or, with a command form, forbidding an action ('do not...').

3.meaning: I find, I come upon, I discover. The verb conveys encountering or locating something, and can also mean to find something to be the case.
3.grammar: A present-tense verb with the 'a-' prefix marking a first-person singular subject ('I'). The final '-u' ending is the indicative, the plain present form used to state a simple, ongoing, or general fact.
3.root: و-ج-د (w-j-d) — to find, come upon; to exist or be present

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
4.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

5.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
5.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

6.meaning: It has been revealed / inspired — divine communication has been sent down or conveyed (to someone). A passive verb: the focus is on the message being given, with the Giver understood rather than named.
6.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) passive verb (form IV). The opening vowelling marks it as passive ('it was/has been done to it'), and the ending denotes a third-person masculine singular subject — the thing revealed. Being passive, the doer (the Revealer) is left unstated. The long u of the prefix is formed by the damma plus the waw; the bare stem consonant carries -hi-.
6.root: و-ح-ى (w-h-y) — revelation, divine inspiration, conveying a message

7.meaning: 'To me / toward me.' It joins the preposition ilā, meaning 'to / toward,' with an attached first-person 'me,' expressing motion or direction toward the speaker.
7.grammar: A preposition meaning 'to / toward' with the attached pronoun 'me.' The base preposition is ilā, ending in a long vowel (written with alif maqsūra, ى). When the 'me' pronoun attaches, that final long vowel turns into yāʾ and merges with the pronoun's yāʾ, giving a doubled, stressed -ayya — the whole word reading ilayya, 'to me.'

8.meaning: Something made forbidden, prohibited, or rendered sacred and off-limits. The word names that which has been declared unlawful to do or to use.
8.grammar: A passive participle (Form II: 'a thing that has been forbidden'). The '-an' ending is the accusative indefinite, marking the word as a direct object (the thing acted upon) or a specification.
8.root: ح-ر-م (ḥ-r-m) — to forbid, prohibit; the sacred and inviolable

9.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
9.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

10.meaning: An eater; one who eats or partakes of food. An active participle naming the person who does the eating, the consumer of nourishment.
10.grammar: An active participle (the 'doer' form) meaning 'one who eats.' The final -in (tanwīn kasra) marks it as indefinite ('an eater') and in the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun as '… of …'.

11.meaning: He eats it / he partakes of it. A present-tense verb describing an ongoing or habitual act of eating, with an attached object 'it.'
11.grammar: A present/imperfect verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'), and the -u on the verb stem is the indicative mood, used for a plain ongoing or habitual action. The attached -hu is the object pronoun 'it/him.' The shaddah doubling the yā' reflects assimilation to a preceding word.
11.root: ط-ع-م (ṭ-ʿ-m) — eating, food, tasting

12.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
12.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.
12.root: — (particle)

13.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
13.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

14.meaning: '(That) He be / there be' — a form of the core verb 'to be/become', expressing existence or a state of being.
14.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he is/becomes' or 'there is'). The ya- prefix marks the 'he' subject. The final -a is the subjunctive ending, used after certain particles (e.g. 'that', 'so that', 'in order to') and giving the sense of a dependent or hoped-for action.
14.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to become

15.meaning: Carrion; a dead animal that has died of itself rather than being slaughtered. As a category it denotes the flesh of such an animal, regarded as unfit to eat.
15.grammar: A feminine noun. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥa) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case, the form typically used for the direct object of a verb or after certain particles.

16.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
16.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

17.meaning: Blood; the red fluid of a living body.
17.grammar: A noun. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥa) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case, typically the form a noun takes as the direct object of a verb.

18.meaning: Poured forth, spilled out, made to flow. A passive participle describing something (such as blood) that has been let out and made to stream.
18.grammar: A passive participle (the 'done-to' form) meaning 'that which has been poured out.' The final -an (tanwīn fatḥa) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case, often used when the word describes an accusative noun before it.

19.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
19.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

20.meaning: Flesh; meat, the soft tissue of a body. Often appears bound to a following noun as 'the flesh of …'.
20.grammar: A noun. The final -a here is the accusative case ending without tanwīn, which typically signals that the noun is the first part of a possessive pair ('the flesh OF …') joined to the following word.
20.root: ل-ح-م (l-ḥ-m) — flesh, meat

21.meaning: Swine; a pig. The animal whose flesh is named in dietary prohibition.
21.grammar: A noun. The final -in (tanwīn kasra) marks it as indefinite and in the genitive case, the form a noun takes when linked to a preceding noun as '… of …' or after a preposition.
21.root: خ-ن-ز-ر (kh-n-z-r) — (quadriliteral; pig); no triliteral root

22.meaning: A cluster of three elements: a connective 'so/then', the emphasis particle 'inna' that strongly affirms a statement ('indeed, truly'), and 'he/it'. Together: 'so indeed he / then truly it'.
22.grammar: 'fa-' is a connecting particle showing sequence or consequence ('so, then'). 'inna' is an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the sentence that follows and grammatically governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative. The attached 'hu' is that pronoun, 'he/it', here serving as the subject being emphasized.

23.meaning: An abomination / filth / defilement — rijs: something foul and impure, repugnant whether physically dirty or morally and spiritually corrupt; a thing to be shunned.
23.grammar: An indefinite noun ('a filth/abomination'). The ending -un is nominative with 'tanwīn' (the -n that marks an indefinite 'a/an'), the form used when the word is the subject or a predicate identifying what something is.
23.root: ر-ج-س (r-j-s) — filth, impurity, that which is foul

24.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
24.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

25.meaning: Transgression; a flagrant departure from obedience to Allah, stepping outside the bounds of His law. The word conveys rebellious deviance and moral corruption.
25.grammar: A verbal noun naming the act/quality of transgression. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥa) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case, often the form used to predicate or describe something ('…being transgression').
25.root: ف-س-ق (f-s-q) — departing from obedience, transgressing

26.meaning: A passive verb meaning 'it was raised aloud / proclaimed / dedicated'. The root sense is the lifting of the voice; it came to denote the loud invocation of a name over an animal at the moment of slaughter, hence 'to be dedicated/offered in the name of'. The passive form indicates the action was done to it by an unnamed agent.
26.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular, in the passive voice — Form IV (the active is ʾahalla, 'to raise the voice / dedicate'). The opening vowel u- on the hamza together with the internal i–a vowelling and the doubled final lām (uhilla) marks the Form IV passive 'it was [done]', so no doer is named; the final -a is the standard ending of a completed past-tense verb.
26.root: ه-ل-ل (h-l-l) — to raise the voice, proclaim aloud (also the appearing of the new crescent moon)

27.meaning: A two-part expression meaning 'to other than / for someone or something besides'. It combines the preposition 'to/for' with the noun 'other than, different from', conveying directing something toward a party distinct from the one expected.
27.grammar: A preposition (li- 'to/for') attached to the noun ghayr. Because li- governs the noun, ghayr takes the -i (genitive) ending, the case that regularly follows a preposition and links onward to a following noun ('other than … OF …').

28.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
28.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

29.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
29.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

30.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'so/then whoever'. It joins a clause to what precedes ('so', 'then') and introduces a conditional or general statement about any person who does something ('whoever, anyone who').
30.grammar: The prefix fa- is a connecting particle meaning 'so/then', linking this to a prior statement. man is a conditional/relative word for persons ('whoever'); its base form is man, and the final vowel here is read -i simply to ease pronunciation before a following consonant cluster, not a case ending.

31.meaning: A passive verb meaning 'he was compelled, driven by necessity, left with no choice'. The root conveys urgent need and constraint; the form means an outside pressure forced the person into something against preference.

parts.en: he was compelled / driven by necessity

31.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular, passive voice (Form VIII). It is a single stem with no detachable prefix: the opening alif is a connecting (waṣl) alif belonging to the Form VIII stem, and the passive is marked by the vowelling uḍṭurra (ḍamma on the first root letter ḍ, ḍamma on the infix ṭ, fatḥa on the doubled final rā), naming no compeller. The Form VIII infix tā has assimilated to ṭā before the emphatic root letter ḍ (so ḍtarara → iḍṭarra → passive uḍṭurra). The final -a is the regular completed past-tense ending.

32.meaning: 'Other than / different from / not'. A noun used to express difference or negation — 'something other than X', and so 'not-X'. It functions to exclude or contrast with what follows.
32.grammar: A noun of difference/exception. The -a ending marks the accusative case, the form it takes when it serves as a direct object or as a descriptive substitute standing in an object position; it governs a following noun in the genitive ('other than …'). That it takes case endings and tanwīn confirms it is a true noun, not a particle.
32.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — to be other, different; otherness, change

33.meaning: An active participle meaning 'one who seeks/craves wrongfully, who covets or rebels'. It describes a person who actively desires or pursues something out of bounds — overstepping through greedy or unjust seeking.
33.grammar: An active participle (the 'doer' pattern bāʿil → bāghin) functioning as a noun/adjective, masculine singular. The -in ending is 'nunation' in the genitive: it marks the word as indefinite ('a craver') and in the genitive case, the form taken after prepositions or in linkage.
33.root: ب-غ-ي (b-gh-y) — to seek/desire, often to crave or transgress wrongfully

34.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
34.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

35.meaning: An active participle meaning 'one who transgresses, oversteps, goes beyond the limit'. It describes a person who exceeds proper bounds, acting in hostility or excess.
35.grammar: An active participle (doer pattern, originally ʿādiy → ʿādin), masculine singular, used as a noun/adjective. The -in ending is indefinite nunation in the genitive case — marking 'a transgressor' and the case used after prepositions or in noun-to-noun linkage.
35.root: ع-د-و (ʿ-d-w) — to overstep, transgress, show enmity

36.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'so/then, indeed…'. It joins fa- ('so', 'then', marking a result or consequence) to inna, an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the statement that follows ('truly', 'verily').
36.grammar: fa- is a connective prefix signaling that what follows is a consequence or next step. inna is an emphatic particle that introduces a nominal sentence, puts its following noun in the accusative, and strengthens the assertion; it does not itself take a case ending.

37.meaning: 'Your Lord' — the noun 'Lord' (Master, Sustainer, Owner, the One who nurtures and brings to completion) combined with 'your'. 'Rabb' carries the linked senses of ownership, authority, and ongoing care that raises a thing to its perfection.
37.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive. The -a ending is accusative, which typically marks the word as a direct object or governed element. The attached -ka means 'your', addressed to a single male.
37.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, nurturing care, ownership and mastery

38.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'much-forgiving, ever-ready to forgive, one who veils and pardons faults again and again'. The form stresses abundance, so it conveys forgiveness as a constant, far-reaching quality.
38.grammar: An intensive adjective (the ghafūr 'doer-in-abundance' pattern), used as a divine attribute of Allah. The -un ending is nunation in the nominative case: it marks the word as indefinite and in the nominative, the case typically used for the subject or for a predicate that describes the subject.

39.meaning: Most merciful, ever-merciful; one whose mercy is constant and abundant. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's enduring, all-embracing compassion toward His creation.
39.grammar: An intensive adjective on the form faʿīl ('abundantly/constantly merciful'). The ending -un (tanwīn) is the nominative case with indefiniteness, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it ('[He] is most merciful').

1.meaning: A two-part phrase: the joining word 'and' plus the preposition 'on / upon / incumbent upon,' often used to express an obligation resting on someone.
1.grammar: The connector 'wa' ('and') joined to the preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon'). Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending; a noun governed by 'ʿalā' takes the genitive.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: 'They became Jews / adopted Judaism', or in the verb's wider sense 'they turned (back) in repentance'. A completed act by a group of taking on the way of the Jewish community.

parts.en: became Jews / turned back (past, masc. plural)

3.grammar: A past-tense verb from a hollow root. The whole form hādū is already 3rd-person masculine plural ('they turned/became Jews'): the long ū plus the final silent alif are the plural marker, so no separate ending is split off. The action is presented as completed; the root carries the idea of turning toward or returning, from which the sense 'to follow Judaism' derives.
3.root: ه-و-د (h-w-d) — turning back, returning; hence following Judaism

4.meaning: 'We forbade / made unlawful' — to declare something prohibited and off-limits, treating it as sacred or forbidden so that it may not be approached or used.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb in an intensive pattern (denoting decisive, complete prohibition). The suffix -nā marks the doer as 'we', so the whole means 'we made unlawful / we forbade'. Being past tense, it reports a completed act.
4.root: ح-ر-م (ḥ-r-m) — to forbid, to make sacred/inviolable; the forbidden and the sacrosanct

5.meaning: All, every, the whole of — totality. When followed by a singular it means 'every (one)'; when followed by a definite plural or whole it means 'all of.'
5.grammar: A noun of totality, almost always joined to a following noun in the genitive ('every … / all of …'). The final -a is the accusative case, the form used when the word functions as an object of a verb.

6.meaning: Possessor of / the one having — a relational word meaning 'owner of' or 'endowed with,' used to attach a quality or relationship to the noun it describes.
6.grammar: A relational noun meaning 'owner/possessor of,' which must be followed by another noun ('possessor OF …'). It declines for case: dhū (nominative), dhī (genitive), dhā (accusative). The form dhī (ending -ī) is its genitive, used when it follows a preposition or describes a preceding genitive noun. It never stands alone; it always governs a following noun.
6.root: — (a relational noun meaning 'possessor of'; no verbal root)

7.meaning: A claw or nail; the hard, curved growth on an animal's toe. By extension it can denote a clawed or undivided hoof.
7.grammar: A noun. The final -in (tanwīn kasra) marks it as indefinite and in the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when joined to a preceding noun as '… of …'.

8.meaning: A connector meaning 'and', joined to the preposition 'from / of', introducing a portion or origin — 'and from' or 'and among'.
8.grammar: Two particles: wa- ('and') plus the preposition min ('from, of, among'). Min normally appears as 'min', but its final vowel shifts to 'mina' when the next word begins with the definite article, simply to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

9.meaning: The cows; cattle, taken as a collective kind. The root also conveys 'splitting open', evoking the cow that cleaves the earth in ploughing.
9.grammar: A collective noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The '-i' ending is genitive, used after a possessor ('of') or following a preposition.
9.root: ب-ق-ر (b-q-r) — cattle, cows; also to split or cleave open

10.meaning: And the sheep / small grazing livestock (sheep and goats). A collective noun for flocks of small herd animals, here joined by 'and.'
10.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and'; al- is 'the.' The final -i is the genitive case ending, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun as '… of …'. As a collective noun it names the species as a whole.

11.meaning: 'We forbade / made unlawful' — to declare something prohibited and off-limits, treating it as sacred or forbidden so that it may not be approached or used.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb in an intensive pattern (denoting decisive, complete prohibition). The suffix -nā marks the doer as 'we', so the whole means 'we made unlawful / we forbade'. Being past tense, it reports a completed act.
11.root: ح-ر-م (ḥ-r-m) — to forbid, to make sacred/inviolable; the forbidden and the sacrosanct

12.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
12.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
12.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

13.meaning: Their fat (of the two). The body fat belonging to a pair, expressed with a dual possessive 'of the two of them.'
13.grammar: A plural noun 'fats' with an attached possessive pronoun -humā meaning 'of them two' (the dual, referring to exactly two owners). The noun itself is in the accusative here, typically the object form, though the case sits before the suffix.

14.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
14.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

15.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
15.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

16.meaning: It (she) carried, bore, or held. A past-tense verb of bearing a load or carrying something.
16.grammar: A past/perfect-tense verb. The -at ending marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('she/it'), used when the doer is grammatically feminine (or for non-human plurals treated as feminine).

17.meaning: Their backs (of the two). The backs belonging to a pair of animals, with a dual possessive 'of the two of them.'
17.grammar: A plural noun 'backs' with the attached possessive -humā, 'of them two' (dual). The noun carries the -u (nominative) marker, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence, before the suffix attaches.
17.root: ظ-ه-ر (ẓ-h-r) — back; to appear, become manifest

18.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative between two or more options, linking possibilities of which one applies.
18.grammar: A connecting particle meaning 'or'. Its base form is aw; the added -i is a 'helping' vowel given to the otherwise-silent final consonant to smooth the link to a following word that begins with a connecting (hamzat-waṣl) alif. It is not a case ending — particles do not take cases.

19.meaning: The entrails; the intestines or the gut, the convoluted inner viscera of the belly.
19.grammar: A plural noun preceded by the definite article al- ('the'). Its form ends in a long -ā; as one of the broken-plural patterns that do not take normal case endings, its shape stays fixed.
19.root: ح-و-ي (ḥ-w-y) — to coil, gather, contain

20.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
20.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

21.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
21.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

22.meaning: It became mixed, intermingled, or joined together. A past-tense verb describing two things blending or clinging together.
22.grammar: A past/perfect verb in the reflexive 'become-mixed' pattern (form VIII), where the action falls back on the subject. The final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'), with no suffix added.

23.meaning: With a bone; by means of, or attached to, a bone. A noun for the hard skeletal part, governed by the preposition 'with/by.'
23.grammar: The prefix bi- is a preposition ('with/by/at'). The final -in (tanwīn kasra) marks the noun as indefinite and in the genitive case, which is exactly the form a noun must take after a preposition.
23.root: ع-ظ-م (ʿ-ẓ-m) — bone; to be great, mighty

24.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
24.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

25.meaning: We requited them / paid them back. A past-tense verb of recompense — giving someone their due return, whether reward or punishment — with 'we' as doer and 'them' as object.
25.grammar: A past/perfect verb. The suffix -nā marks a first-person plural subject ('we'), and the attached -hum is the object pronoun 'them' (masculine plural). So the form means 'we recompensed them.'
25.root: ج-ز-ي (j-z-y) — recompense, requital, repaying in kind

26.meaning: Because of their transgression / for their insolent wrongdoing. 'Baghy' is overstepping the rightful bounds — rebellion, oppression, willful excess — here governed by 'with/because of' and owned by 'them.'
26.grammar: The prefix bi- here carries a causal sense ('because of / on account of'). The noun is in the genitive after the preposition, and the attached -him is the possessive 'their' (masculine plural); its vowel is -hi (rather than -hu) because it follows a kasra/yā'.
26.root: ب-غ-ي (b-gh-y) — to exceed bounds, transgress, oppress; to seek wrongfully

27.meaning: And indeed we: 'we' stated with emphasis. The particle inna strongly affirms and stresses the statement that follows, like saying 'truly' or 'most certainly'.
27.grammar: An emphasizing particle inna ('indeed, truly') with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā meaning 'we/us' (the doubled nūn shared between inna and the pronoun is written once as a shadda). After inna a pronoun takes this object-style form. The prefixed wa- means 'and'. The whole strongly asserts a statement about 'we'.

28.meaning: Surely truthful ones; those who speak the truth and are true to their word. An emphatic plural describing people characterized by honesty.
28.grammar: An active participle ('one who is truthful') made plural. The prefix la- adds emphasis ('surely, indeed'). The ending -ūna marks a sound masculine plural in the nominative case, the form used for the subject or predicate of a sentence.
28.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — truthfulness, sincerity, keeping one's word

1.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
1.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

2.meaning: They denied / rejected you — to charge someone with lying, to disbelieve and reject what they say; here a group does this to a single 'you'.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb in the intensive (form II) pattern, which conveys 'to declare false, treat as a liar'. The suffix '-ū' marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'), and the attached '-ka' is the object 'you' (masculine singular).
2.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie; (intensive) to call a lie, deny

3.meaning: So say! / Then say! A command to one person to utter or declare something, introduced by 'so/then.'
3.grammar: The prefix fa- means 'so/then,' linking to what precedes. 'Qul' is an imperative (a command) addressed to a single masculine person — 'say!' Its clipped form with a silent final consonant is normal for this command.

4.meaning: Your Lord. 'Rabb' means the Lord who creates, owns, sustains, nurtures, and governs all that He has made; combined with 'your' (plural) it addresses a group as 'the Lord of you all.'
4.grammar: A noun 'Lord' with the possessive -kum ('your,' addressing more than one person). The -u before the suffix is the nominative case marker, the form typically used when the word is the subject of a sentence.

5.meaning: Owner of / possessor of / endowed with — a word that does not stand alone but means 'the one who has' whatever noun follows it, ascribing that quality or possession to someone.

parts.en: possessor of, owner of, endowed with

5.grammar: A possessive noun meaning 'owner/possessor of', always followed by another noun in the genitive. The final -ū form here is the nominative case, used when this word names the subject or is the thing being described; it inherently requires a following noun to complete its sense ('owner OF …').
5.root: — (no triliteral root; an irregular noun of possession)

6.meaning: Mercy, compassion, tender loving-kindness — the deep, womb-like care that moves one to gentleness and pardon.
6.grammar: A singular feminine noun. The -in (tanwīn) ending is the indefinite genitive, used when the word follows a preposition or links to a preceding noun ('... of mercy'). It signals the word is being governed by something before it.
6.root: ر-ح-م (r-ḥ-m) — mercy, compassion; related to the womb and its nurturing care

7.meaning: Vast, wide, all-encompassing; ample and spacious. As a quality (often of mercy) it conveys boundless capacity that embraces and accommodates much.
7.grammar: An active participle used as an adjective, in the feminine form (marked by the -at). The prefix wa- is 'and' (its wāw doubled by assimilation to the preceding word). The stem itself begins with a wāw (root و-س-ع). The final -in (tanwīn kasra) marks it as indefinite and genitive, the case it takes to agree with a genitive feminine noun it describes.

8.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
8.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

9.meaning: It is turned back / repelled / averted. A present-tense passive verb: the action of pushing back or warding off is done to the subject, not by it.
9.grammar: A present/imperfect verb in the passive voice ('is being turned back'). The yu- prefix with the inner vowel pattern marks a third-person masculine singular passive ('it is …-ed'), and the final -u is the indicative mood used for a plain statement.

10.meaning: His might / His punishment; the force and severity He brings to bear. 'Ba's' denotes formidable power, hardship, or chastening might; with 'His' it ascribes that power to its owner.
10.grammar: A noun 'might/severity' with the possessive -hu ('his'). The -u before the suffix is the nominative case marker, the form a noun typically takes as the subject of a sentence.

11.meaning: About / concerning; a particle marking the topic of inquiry or the thing one moves away from.
11.grammar: A preposition meaning 'about, concerning, away from'. Its base form is ʿan; the final -i here is a helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a connecting 'al-'. It governs the genitive case on whatever noun follows.

12.meaning: 'The people / the folk' — a collective noun for a community, nation, or group of people regarded as a body. Often it carries the nuance of one's own people or a particular group sharing a trait.
12.grammar: A collective noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final '-i' is the genitive ending, which typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of …' relationship.
12.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand/rise; a people, community

13.meaning: Those who commit grave sins and crimes; wrongdoers who deliberately break Allah's law and cut themselves off in guilt. The word denotes hardened, culpable offenders, not those who err by accident.
13.grammar: An active participle (one who does the action) of Form IV, made definite by 'al-' ('the'). The '-īna' ending marks a masculine sound plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) case, so it names a group as the object of a verb or the complement of a preposition, rather than the subject.
13.root: ج-ر-م (j-r-m) — to commit a crime or grave sin

1.meaning: 'He/it will say' — a statement of future speech. Built from the present-tense verb 'he says' with the prefixed particle sa- ('will, shall, is going to'), marking an action expected to happen soon.
1.grammar: The prefix sa- places the verb in the near future ('will say'). The base verb is present-tense, third-person masculine singular: the ya- prefix means 'he', and the final -u ending marks the indicative mood (a plain, factual statement, as opposed to commands or subjunctive forms).

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'they associated partners / they set up partners (with Allah)' — to ascribe partners or equals to Allah, the act underlying idolatry and polytheism.
3.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb in a pattern meaning 'to make (someone) a partner'. The ending -ū marks a masculine-plural subject, 'they', so it reads 'they associated partners (with Allah)'.

4.meaning: A conditional particle introducing a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact supposition: 'if (it were the case that…)'. It typically presents a condition that is unfulfilled or merely imagined, often implying the result did not or would not happen.
4.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case ending). It signals a hypothetical 'if': it sets up a supposed condition whose consequence is then stated, frequently with the sense 'if X were so, then Y would be so' — often where X is contrary to fact.

5.meaning: A past-tense verb 'he willed / he wished / he so desired'. It denotes an act of will or volition bringing something about.
5.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third person masculine singular ('he'). The bare stem with no suffix is the basic 'he did' form. Its subject and object are typically supplied by context.

6.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
6.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

7.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
7.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

8.meaning: We associated others as partners with Allah; we set up rivals alongside Him in worship or lordship. This is the verb for the cardinal sin of shirk: ascribing divinity or Allah's exclusive rights to anyone else.
8.grammar: A past-tense (completed action) Form IV verb. The suffix '-nā' is the subject 'we', marking a first-person plural that has performed the act, so the whole word means 'we associated (partners)'.
8.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share or associate as a partner

9.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
9.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

10.meaning: Our fathers and forefathers; our ancestors. The word points to the line of male forebears whose example or tradition is often invoked.
10.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun with the possessive pronoun '-nā' ('our') attached. The plural ends in a hamza (written here on a 'wāw' seat as 'ؤ'), and the '-u' vowel on it before the pronoun is nominative, the case typically used when the noun is the subject (the doer) of a sentence.

11.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
11.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

12.meaning: 'We forbade / made unlawful' — to declare something prohibited and off-limits, treating it as sacred or forbidden so that it may not be approached or used.
12.grammar: A past-tense verb in an intensive pattern (denoting decisive, complete prohibition). The suffix -nā marks the doer as 'we', so the whole means 'we made unlawful / we forbade'. Being past tense, it reports a completed act.
12.root: ح-ر-م (ḥ-r-m) — to forbid, to make sacred/inviolable; the forbidden and the sacrosanct

13.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
13.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

14.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
14.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
14.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

15.meaning: 'Like that / thus / in this manner.' A comparison word meaning that something is done or is the case in the way just mentioned.
15.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like/as') prefixed to the demonstrative 'that'. Together they form a fixed adverbial expression, 'like that / thus', which does not change its ending with grammatical position.
15.root: — (a particle of comparison joined to a demonstrative; no root)

16.meaning: A verb meaning 'he denied / cried lies against / rejected as false' — to treat something or someone as a lie, refusing to accept it as true and openly rejecting it.
16.grammar: Past-tense verb (form II, intensive), third-person masculine singular ('he denied / rejected as false'). The doubled middle letter (kadhdhaba) gives the sense of actively declaring something false. The final -a is the past-tense ending for a masculine singular doer.
16.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie; (form II) to deny, to call a lie

17.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
17.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

18.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
18.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

19.meaning: 'Before them' in time — denoting what came earlier, the period or persons preceding a masculine plural group.
19.grammar: An adverb of time, 'before,' carrying the genitive ending -i because it is linked to a following possessor. The attached 'him' means 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group), giving 'before them.' The -i ending reflects that the word is governed in a possessive link.
19.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, come before; before/prior

20.meaning: 'Until / up to the point that; so that' — a particle marking a limit or goal. It expresses the end-point reached ('until') or the purpose aimed at ('so that, in order that').
20.grammar: A particle indicating a goal or limit. When followed by a present-tense verb it places that verb in the subjunctive mood (clipping its ending to -a), conveying 'until / so that' something comes about. Ḥattā itself is invariable.
20.root: — (particle)

21.meaning: They tasted; they experienced something directly and personally. Beyond literal tasting with the tongue, it commonly means to undergo and feel the full impact of something, such as a punishment or a consequence.
21.grammar: A past-tense (completed action) verb with the '-ū' ending marking a third-person masculine plural subject: 'they (men/people) tasted'. The action is presented as already done.
21.root: ذ-و-ق (dh-w-q) — to taste, to experience

22.meaning: Our might, force, or punishing power; the severity Allah brings against wrongdoers. The base word denotes formidable strength and harm, and is often used of a chastisement that cannot be resisted.
22.grammar: A noun with the possessive pronoun '-nā' ('our') attached. The '-a' vowel before the pronoun is accusative, the case typically used when the noun is the object of a verb (the thing acted upon).

23.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
23.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

24.meaning: An interrogative particle that turns a statement into a yes/no question, roughly "is it that…?" or "do…?". It can also carry a rhetorical or expectant tone rather than a literal request for information.
24.grammar: A question particle placed before a sentence to ask whether something is the case. It has no case ending and does not change form; it simply marks the words that follow as a yes/no question.

25.meaning: In your possession, presence, or keeping; available to you. The base word 'ʿinda' denotes being at, near, or held by someone, whether physically present or stored as knowledge or property.
25.grammar: An adverb of place meaning 'with/at', fixed in the accusative ('-a'), joined to the pronoun '-kum' ('you', for a group). Together it locates something as being present with or belonging to a group of people.
25.root: — (no triliteral root; locative particle)

26.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
26.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

27.meaning: 'Knowledge.' A noun denoting sure, established knowing — to know a thing as it truly is. In its indefinite form it often appears in the sense 'any knowledge (at all).'
27.grammar: A noun with the -in ending (genitive with nunation, 'tanwīn'), marking it as indefinite ('any knowledge'). The genitive -i is the form used after a preposition such as 'of' or 'by' — e.g. 'of any knowledge.'

28.meaning: Then you bring it out, produce it, or make it appear. The verb means to cause something to come forth from a hidden or contained state into the open, here with a connective 'then'.
28.grammar: A connective 'fa-' ('then/so') plus a present/subjunctive Form IV verb. The '-ū' marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'), and '-hu' is the object 'it/him'. The dropped final 'n' (subjunctive mood) shows the verb is governed by a preceding particle, often giving the sense 'so that you bring it out'.
28.root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — to go out, come forth

29.meaning: A combination of the preposition 'for / to' with the pronoun 'us', meaning 'for us' or 'to us / on our behalf'.
29.grammar: A preposition ('for / to') joined to the attached pronoun 'us'. The pronoun -nā always means 'us / our' regardless of position. Together they express benefit or direction toward the speakers ('for us').

30.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
30.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

31.meaning: You follow, pursue, or adhere to something; you take it as a path or guide and walk behind it. It implies following step by step, whether a person, teaching, or mere assumption.
31.grammar: A present-tense Form VIII verb. The '-ūna' ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all') and indicative mood, presenting the following as an ongoing or habitual action.

32.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
32.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

33.meaning: Conjecture, supposition, opinion not grounded in certainty; a thought or assumption that may be doubt or mere likelihood rather than sure knowledge.
33.grammar: A definite noun: al- is 'the', and the final -a is the accusative ending (fatḥa), which typically marks the word as a direct object of a verb.

34.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
34.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

35.meaning: You — the standalone pronoun for a group of people ('you all', masculine or mixed). It is used for emphasis or as the subject standing on its own.
35.grammar: A detached subject pronoun meaning 'you all' (second-person masculine/mixed plural). Unlike pronoun endings attached to verbs or nouns, this word stands alone — typically to emphasize the subject or to begin an equational sentence ('you [are]…'). Its form is fixed and does not change for case.

36.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
36.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

37.meaning: You guess, conjecture, or estimate without real knowledge; you speak from supposition. The verb carries the sense of merely surmising, often falsely, rather than relying on certainty or evidence.
37.grammar: A present-tense verb. The '-ūna' ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all') and indicative mood, presenting the guessing as an ongoing or habitual action.
37.root: خ-ر-ص (kh-r-ṣ) — to conjecture, estimate by guesswork

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: Then belonging to Allah; so it is Allah's. The phrase asserts that something pertains or belongs exclusively to Allah, introduced by a connective 'then/so'.
2.grammar: A connective 'fa-' ('then/so') plus the preposition 'li-' ('to/for/belonging to') attached to the name Allah. The '-i' ending on the name is genitive, the case required after a preposition; the combination expresses ownership or entitlement: '(it is) for/belonging to Allah'.

3.meaning: The proof, argument, or decisive evidence; a compelling case that establishes the truth and leaves the opponent without excuse. It is not a mere opinion but a binding demonstration.
3.grammar: A definite feminine noun ('al-' = 'the') ending in tā' marbūṭa, which is pronounced 't' here because a case vowel follows. The final '-u' is nominative, the case typically marking the subject of a sentence or the thing being described, so the form reads 'al-ḥujjatu'.

4.meaning: Reaching its goal, conclusive, and far-reaching; that which attains its full aim. Describing an argument or matter, it means one so complete and overwhelming that it leaves no room for dispute.
4.grammar: A definite feminine active participle ('one that reaches/attains'), with 'al-' ('the'). The tā' marbūṭa is sounded as 't' before the case vowel, and the feminine ending agrees with a feminine noun it describes. The final '-u' is nominative, the case used for a subject or for a describing word that matches such a noun.
4.root: ب-ل-غ (b-l-gh) — to reach, attain, arrive at

5.meaning: And if; so if. A connective 'and/so' joined to the conditional particle 'law', which introduces a hypothetical condition, typically one that is unreal or unfulfilled ('if [such-and-such had been the case]...').
5.grammar: Two particles: the connective 'fa-' ('and/so') and 'law' ('if'). 'Law' sets up a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact condition and normally expects a following clause (often introduced by 'la-') stating what would have resulted. Being particles, they take no case endings.

6.meaning: A past-tense verb 'he willed / he wished / he so desired'. It denotes an act of will or volition bringing something about.
6.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third person masculine singular ('he'). The bare stem with no suffix is the basic 'he did' form. Its subject and object are typically supplied by context.

7.meaning: He would surely have guided you; He would certainly have led you to the right way. The verb means to guide, direct, and show the correct path, here emphasised as a certain hypothetical outcome.
7.grammar: An emphatic prefix 'la-' ('surely') on a past-tense verb, with the object pronoun '-kum' ('you all'). The verb 'hadā' is third-person masculine singular ('He'); its final weak root letter is written as alif maqsūra (here in the archaic dotless style) and sounded as a long 'ā'. The 'la-' commonly answers a hypothetical 'if', giving 'He would surely have guided you'.

8.meaning: All together / one and all — an emphatic word meaning the entirety of a group, every last one without exception.
8.grammar: An emphatic plural used to stress totality ('all of them, every one'). The -īna ending is the sound masculine plural in its accusative/genitive form, agreeing with a plural noun it reinforces.

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: Bring it here! Produce it! Come on! A command used to summon something or someone forward, or to urge people to come or to present what they have.
2.grammar: An imperative verb (a direct command), fixed and invariable in form. It functions as an order to produce or bring something, and does not change for case; the same form is classically used whether addressing one person or many.

3.meaning: Your witnesses; those you call to testify or bear witness on your behalf. The base word names people who give testimony or stand as evidence-bearers.
3.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun with the possessive pronoun '-kum(u)' ('your', for a group). The '-a' vowel before the pronoun is accusative, the case typically marking the noun as the object of a verb (the ones being summoned).
3.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — to witness, testify, be present

4.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
4.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

5.meaning: 'they bear witness / testify' — a group giving firm testimony or attesting to the truth of something.
5.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix together with the -ūna ending means 'they' (masculine plural). The -ūna ending marks the ordinary, unrestricted present tense for a plural subject ('they bear witness / do testify').
5.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — to witness, testify, be present

6.meaning: An emphatic particle meaning 'that' (as in 'I know that...') or 'indeed/surely.' It introduces a statement and gives it certainty and emphasis, presenting what follows as an established fact.
6.grammar: An emphatic particle that introduces a noun-clause ('that...'). It puts the following noun into the accusative case and lends the whole statement a sense of certainty and assertion. It typically comes after verbs of knowing, saying, or informing.

7.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
7.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

8.meaning: 'He forbade / made unlawful / declared sacredly off-limits.' To prohibit something firmly, to render it ḥarām — barred and inviolable, set outside what is permitted.
8.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) Form II verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he [did it],' a completed past action. The doubled middle root letter (Form II) gives an intensive/causative force — 'to make something forbidden/inviolable.'

9.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
9.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

10.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
10.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

11.meaning: 'They bore witness' or 'they testified' — a completed act of testimony or affirmation by a group, also carrying the sense of being present at and attesting to something.
11.grammar: A past-tense (completed) verb. The -ū ending marks the subject as 'they' — a group of males or a mixed group. It states that the action of witnessing has already taken place.
11.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — to witness, testify, be present

12.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
12.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

13.meaning: He/she bears witness, testifies, or attests; he gives evidence. The verb means to affirm something one knows to be true, as a witness does.
13.grammar: A present-tense verb. With a singular subject this is read as third-person feminine ('she/it testifies') or second-person masculine ('you testify'). The silent (vowelless) final letter is the jussive mood, used after particles of negation or command, often giving 'does not testify' or 'let it testify'.
13.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — to witness, testify, be present

14.meaning: With them, in their company or possession — expressing accompaniment or togetherness. Maʿa denotes being alongside or in the presence of someone or something.
14.grammar: An adverb of accompaniment ('with') fixed in the -a form, joined to the pronoun -hum ('them'). Together they express that something is in the company or possession of a group.

15.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
15.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

16.meaning: '(You) follow / pursue / take as a path' — a verb meaning to walk after, conform to, and adopt something as one's way, in a form that intensively conveys 'to keep following'.
16.grammar: A present/jussive verb in the reflexive-intensive pattern (iftaʿala). The ta- prefix marks the second-person 'you (one male)'. The silent (vowelless) final consonant is the jussive mood, the form used after negative or conditional particles such as 'do not …' or 'if …'.
16.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, come after, pursue

17.meaning: Whims and cravings — inclinations, desires, or passions, especially the kind that pull a person toward what they merely want rather than what is true or right. This is the plural, 'desires'.
17.grammar: A broken (internal) plural of the noun hawā, formed on the pattern afʿāl. The final -a marks the accusative case — typically the direct object of a verb. (As a 'diptote', this kind of plural normally takes a plain -a without nunation even when indefinite.) The word denotes the pull of personal desire, often inclining away from truth.
17.root: ه-و-ي (h-w-y) — inclining, falling, the leaning of desire toward something

18.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
18.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

19.meaning: They denied / they cried lies; they declared (something or someone) to be false. An intensive verb meaning to reject as a lie, to disbelieve and brand untrue — directed by a plural 'they'.

parts.tr: kadhdhab (doubled dh; simplified transliterations may write 'kadhab')
parts.en: denied / branded as lies (past stem, intensive)

19.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in an intensive pattern (to treat as false, to repeatedly deny). The middle radical carries a shadda (doubling), which is exactly what marks this as the intensive form: kadhdhab- (not the simple kadhab-). The ending -ū marks the doers as 'they' — a plural, grammatically masculine group, so the whole reconstructs to kadhdhabū. Note that simplified transliterations sometimes omit the doubling and write 'kadhabū', but the doubled dh is essential to the form. The perfect tense denotes a completed action.
19.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie; in this form, to call a lie, to deny as false

20.meaning: By/in Our signs. Āyāt is the plural of āya — a sign, token, or evidence. Signs are pointers that indicate a greater reality. With the prefixed particle and pronoun it means 'with/in Our signs'.
20.grammar: A plural noun preceded by the preposition bi- ('with, in, by'), which requires the following noun to take the -i (genitive) ending. The attached -nā means 'our' when joined to a noun. The genitive here is governed by the preposition.
20.root: أ-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — sign, token, mark

21.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
21.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.
21.root: — (relative pronoun)

22.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
22.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

23.meaning: 'They believe / they have faith' — to affirm something as true with trusting inner conviction and to feel secure in it. The verb carries both believing and being at peace through that belief; in religious use it is to commit oneself in faith.
23.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb, masculine plural. The yu-…-una frame means 'they (men, or a mixed group) do' the action now or habitually. The retained final -na marks the indicative (a plain, unqualified statement) — 'they believe' — as opposed to forms where that -na drops. The verb is Form IV (amana), used intransitively here meaning simply 'to believe / to have faith'.

24.meaning: The noun 'the Hereafter / the next life / the world to come,' linked by 'with / for / in exchange for' (bi-). The base word means 'the last, the latter, the final' (state of affairs) and is used as the standing name for the everlasting life after this world.
24.grammar: A definite feminine noun ('the Hereafter') governed by the preposition 'bi-' ('with / for / in exchange for'). The '-i' ending is genitive: the case a noun takes after a preposition (or when linked to a preceding noun as '…of…'). Here it appears because the preposition 'bi-' requires the genitive form; the tā' marbūṭa of the stem is sounded as 't' before this ending.
24.root: ا-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — being last, coming after, the end

25.meaning: 'While they / and they' — the word 'wa' (here 'while' or 'and') joined to the standalone pronoun 'hum' ('they'), referring to a masculine plural group.
25.grammar: A connective 'wa' — often circumstantial 'while' — plus the independent subject pronoun 'hum' ('they'), used for a masculine plural group. As an independent pronoun it usually stands as the subject of a following statement.

26.meaning: 'In/with their Lord' — combining the preposition 'bi' (with, in, by) and 'rabb', meaning the Lord, Master, Nurturer, and Sustainer who owns, governs, and brings to maturity all that He has created; with the attached pronoun 'their'.
26.grammar: A preposition 'bi-' attached to the noun 'rabb', which then carries the possessive pronoun '-him' ('their'). Because it follows the preposition, the noun takes the genitive '-i' vowel (heard in 'rabbi'); after a word ending in '-i', the pronoun is voiced 'him' rather than 'hum'.
26.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, master, sustain, and lord over

27.meaning: They set up equals to Allah; they treat others as His peers, or they deviate from the truth. The verb spans 'to make something equal/a rival' and 'to turn aside', the sense turning on its context.
27.grammar: A present-tense verb. The '-ūna' ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they') and indicative mood, presenting the action as ongoing or habitual.
27.root: ع-د-ل (ʿ-d-l) — to be equal/just; to set equal; to turn aside

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: 'Come! / Come now!' — a call summoning people to approach or come forward, often used to invite a group toward a course of action.
2.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a group, masculine plural ('you all'). The -aw ending carries the plural 'you' addressees; the silent alif is a spelling convention written after this plural ending. It is an invitation to approach.

3.meaning: I recite, read aloud, or convey; I follow on by reading out. The verb means to deliver a text or message orally, especially the reciting of revelation.

parts.en: recite / read (root with elided final letter)

3.grammar: A present-tense verb with the prefix 'a-' marking a first-person singular subject ('I'). The root's final weak letter 'wāw' is elided (the full form is 'atlū'), and the '-u' is the indicative mood vowel that remains on the 'l'. The whole form means 'I recite / I will recite', presenting the act as current or about to occur.
3.root: ت-ل-و (t-l-w) — to recite, read out, follow

4.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
4.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

5.meaning: 'He forbade / made unlawful / declared sacredly off-limits.' To prohibit something firmly, to render it ḥarām — barred and inviolable, set outside what is permitted.
5.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) Form II verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he [did it],' a completed past action. The doubled middle root letter (Form II) gives an intensive/causative force — 'to make something forbidden/inviolable.'

6.meaning: Your (plural) Lord — 'Rabb' means the Master, Owner, Sustainer, and Nurturer who creates, provides for, and brings a thing to its completion. It combines lordship with loving upbringing and care.
6.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The suffix '-kum' means 'your' (plural possessor). The '-u' on 'rabbu' before the suffix is the nominative case, marking the word as a subject or as a predicate standing on its own.
6.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, master, sustain, own

7.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
7.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

8.meaning: A compound particle meaning 'that … not,' 'lest,' 'so as not to.' It introduces a clause of something feared, intended-to-prevent, or negated after a verb.
8.grammar: A merging of the particle an ('that,' which introduces a verb in the subjunctive) with the negative lā ('not'); the 'n' of an assimilates into lā, giving allā. Together they mean 'that … not' and put the following verb into the subjunctive mood, often after verbs of fearing, wishing, or commanding.

9.meaning: You (plural) associate / set up a partner — to ascribe partners or equals to a deity, treating another as sharing in what belongs to Allah alone.
9.grammar: A present/imperfect Form IV verb (base أَشْرَكَ, imperfect stem -shrik-, 'to make a partner/associate'). The tu- prefix marks second-person address and the -ū ending marks a plural (male/mixed) subject: 'you all associate.' The verb is tushrikū, not the indicative tushrikūna: the missing final nūn marks a non-indicative mood (here typically after the prohibitive lā or in a jussive context). The trailing alif is a silent orthographic alif (alif al-fāriqah) written after plural -ū.
9.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — partnership, sharing; to associate partners (with Allah)

10.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
10.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

11.meaning: A thing; something or anything. With a negation it commonly amounts to 'nothing at all.'
