11.grammar: A singular masculine noun, indefinite ('a thing'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative, often used here as an object or an adverbial 'in any respect / at all.'
11.root: ش-ي-أ (sh-y-ʾ) — thing, to will

12.meaning: And toward the two parents — directing kindness and good treatment to one's mother and father (the pair of parents).
12.grammar: A dual noun, 'the two parents,' preceded by the preposition bi- ('with/to/toward') and the article 'the,' all joined by wa- ('and'). A dual noun ends in -āni in the nominative but in -ayni in the oblique (the shared genitive/accusative case); after the preposition bi- it is genitive, hence the -ay…ni form here. It denotes exactly two.
12.root: و-ل-د (w-l-d) — to give birth, beget; parent and offspring

13.meaning: Good treatment, excellence, doing what is beautiful and right — acting toward others with kindness, generosity, and the highest moral excellence (iḥsān), going beyond mere duty to genuine goodness.
13.grammar: A verbal noun (the act of doing good). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥ) marks the indefinite accusative; it often functions adverbially or as an object, conveying 'doing good' or '[show] good treatment' — describing the manner or content of an action.
13.root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — to be good, beautiful, excellent

14.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
14.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

15.meaning: 'You (plural) kill, slay, put to death.'
15.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb addressed to a masculine plural 'you.' The dropped final -n (giving -ū not -ūna) shows a dependent mood (subjunctive/jussive), the form used after particles of prohibition ('do not…'), negation, purpose, or condition.

16.meaning: A noun meaning 'your children' or 'your offspring' — the plural 'children' attached to a possessive 'your' addressed to a group.
16.grammar: A plural noun in a possessive construction. The -a ending is accusative, the case typically marking the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon). The attached -kum means 'your', addressed to a group, so the whole means 'your children'. The awC-ā-C shape is a broken-plural pattern.
16.root: و-ل-د (w-l-d) — to give birth, to beget; offspring

17.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
17.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

18.meaning: Destitution, dire poverty, and want; the fear of having too little to live on. The word denotes a state of being penniless or facing financial ruin.
18.grammar: A verbal noun (the name of an action/state) from Form IV. The '-in' ending is nunation in the genitive case: the extra 'n' marks it as indefinite ('a poverty'), and the 'i' vowel is the case typically used after a preposition or to link it to a preceding noun.
18.root: م-ل-ق (m-l-q) — to be destitute, run out of provision

19.meaning: 'We' — the standalone pronoun for a speaker including others (or a single speaker of majesty). It stands alone to name or emphasize the subject 'we'.
19.grammar: A detached (standalone) personal pronoun, first-person plural, 'we'. Such independent pronouns are used to state or emphasize the subject, often highlighting 'we' as the ones who do or are something.

20.meaning: We provide for you; We grant you sustenance. The verb means to supply provision and the means of life, here with Allah as the Giver and a group as recipients.
20.grammar: A present-tense verb. The prefix 'na-' marks a first-person plural subject ('we'), and the object pronoun '-kum' is 'you all'. The indicative '-u' on the verb stem presents the providing as a real, ongoing reality.
20.root: ر-ز-ق (r-z-q) — to provide sustenance, bestow provision

21.meaning: And them; and them too. A connective 'and' joined to an isolated object pronoun built on 'iyyā', a word used to carry a 'them/him/you' when it must stand as the object without attaching directly to a verb.
21.grammar: A connective 'wa-' ('and') plus a standalone object pronoun: 'iyyā' is a support word that lets the suffix '-hum' ('them') function as an object on its own. The combination singles out 'them' as the object, often for emphasis or when the object is placed before its verb.
21.root: — (pronoun; no triliteral root)

22.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
22.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

23.meaning: You (plural) approach, draw near to, or come close to something — physically nearing it or, by extension, engaging in or attempting it.
23.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix marks a second-person subject ('you'), and the -ū ending makes it masculine plural ('you all'). With the short, vowelless ending (rather than -ūna), this jussive/subjunctive form is the shape used after particles of prohibition or command — i.e. the form for 'do not approach' or 'so that you approach'.

24.meaning: Gross indecencies and shameful deeds; acts of flagrant immorality whose ugliness is plain, especially sexual sins. The word names sins that exceed all bounds of decency.
24.grammar: A definite broken (irregular) plural noun ('al-' = 'the'). The final '-a' is accusative, the case typically marking the noun as the object of a verb (the things done, forbidden, or approached).
24.root: ف-ح-ش (f-ḥ-sh) — to be excessive, grossly indecent

25.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
25.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

26.meaning: It became apparent, visible, or open; it came out into the open. The verb means to show or manifest plainly, and can also carry the sense of being outward or external as opposed to hidden.
26.grammar: A past-tense (completed action) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The 3ms past form carries no overt subject suffix; the final fatḥa is the inherent vowel of the verb's own pattern, not a subject-marking ending. It presents the becoming-apparent as something that has happened.
26.root: ظ-ه-ر (ẓ-h-r) — to appear, become manifest, be outward

27.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'min' ('from / out of / some of') joined to the pronoun 'it' (feminine). Together: 'from it / out of it / of it,' indicating a source or a portion taken from a feminine thing.
27.grammar: A preposition 'min' with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('it/her'), referring to a feminine noun. 'Min' indicates origin, source, or a part taken from a whole; the attached pronoun is in the object form required after a preposition.

28.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
28.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
28.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

29.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'it was hidden, concealed, or inward' — to be on the inside, out of sight, beneath the surface, as opposed to what is open and visible.
29.grammar: A third-person masculine singular verb in the past (perfect) tense; the bare -a ending marks 'he/it' as the doer of a completed action. Built on the simple Form I pattern faʿala.
29.root: ب-ط-ن (b-ṭ-n) — belly, interior, what is hidden/inward

30.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
30.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

31.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb addressed to a masculine plural 'you.' The dropped final -n (giving -ū not -ūna) shows a dependent mood (subjunctive/jussive), the form used after particles of prohibition ('do not…'), negation, purpose, or condition.

32.meaning: 'The soul / self / life' — the living person or inner self; by extension a human life.
32.grammar: A singular feminine noun made definite by 'al-' (the); the 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (a 'sun letter'), which is why the 'n' is doubled in pronunciation (an-nafs). The final '-a' marks the accusative — the state a noun takes when it is the object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or otherwise governed into that case. It denotes the self, the soul, or a living person.

33.meaning: A feminine singular relative pronoun: 'the one which / that which / who' (referring to a single feminine thing). It introduces a descriptive clause that tells us more about a preceding feminine noun.
33.grammar: A relative pronoun, feminine singular, fixed in form (it does not change for case). It links a feminine noun to a following clause describing it, the equivalent of English 'which,' 'that,' or 'who.'

34.meaning: 'He forbade / made unlawful / declared sacredly off-limits.' To prohibit something firmly, to render it ḥarām — barred and inviolable, set outside what is permitted.
34.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) Form II verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he [did it],' a completed past action. The doubled middle root letter (Form II) gives an intensive/causative force — 'to make something forbidden/inviolable.'

35.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
35.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

36.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
36.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

37.meaning: 'With the truth / by means of what is true and right.' Combines the preposition 'with/by' and 'the truth' — that which is real, established, correct, and rightfully due, as opposed to falsehood.
37.grammar: A noun governed by the attached preposition bi- ('with/by'). The -i ending is the genitive case, which is required after a preposition; here it links 'the truth' to 'with', giving 'with the truth'.
37.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, reality, that which is established and due

38.meaning: A demonstrative meaning 'that' addressed to a group of people (plural 'you'). It points to something at a distance — whether physical, or to a previously mentioned matter — and is directed at multiple listeners.
38.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun for something distant. The base 'dhā' carries the sense 'that', the 'li' is an element of distance, and the ending '-kum' tells you the speaker is addressing a plural 'you' — it specifies the audience, not the thing pointed at. It does not change for case.

39.meaning: A verb meaning 'He firmly enjoined, charged, or instructed (you) as a binding duty' — to give an earnest, solemn commandment or counsel, with an attached object 'you (plural)'.
39.grammar: An intensive Form II past-tense verb (waṣṣā), third-person masculine singular 'he', with the doubled middle consonant signalling emphasis/thoroughness; the suffix -kum is the attached object pronoun 'you all (men, or a mixed group)'.
39.root: و-ص-ي (w-ṣ-y) — to enjoin, charge, bequeath, give binding counsel

40.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
40.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

41.meaning: 'so that you may…,' 'in the hope that you…' — a particle expressing purpose, expectation, or hopeful anticipation, fused with 'you (plural).' It introduces a hoped-for or intended outcome; when used of Allah it conveys the desired result rather than uncertainty.

parts.en: so that / perhaps / in hope that

41.grammar: An emphatic particle of hope/purpose belonging to the 'inna' family, which attaches a pronoun as its subject. The particle's fixed form ends in '-a,' and the suffix '-kum' is 'you (plural),' giving 'so that you (all) may…'

42.meaning: 'You understand / use reason' — to comprehend, think, and grasp matters with the intellect; to apply sound reasoning.
42.grammar: The prefix 'ta-' marks a 2nd-person present-tense verb, and the '-ūna' ending makes the subject a masculine-inclusive plural 'you all.' The '-ūna' is the indicative marker, signalling a plain factual or ongoing statement.
42.root: ع-ق-ل (ʿ-q-l) — to reason, understand, be intelligent

1.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
1.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

2.meaning: You (plural) approach, draw near to, or come close to something — physically nearing it or, by extension, engaging in or attempting it.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix marks a second-person subject ('you'), and the -ū ending makes it masculine plural ('you all'). With the short, vowelless ending (rather than -ūna), this jussive/subjunctive form is the shape used after particles of prohibition or command — i.e. the form for 'do not approach' or 'so that you approach'.

3.meaning: 'Wealth, property, possessions' — money or goods one owns; that in which a person has standing means.
3.grammar: A masculine singular noun in the accusative case, shown by the -a ending; the accusative typically marks a word as the direct object of a verb or otherwise governed (e.g. after certain particles).

4.meaning: 'The orphan' — a child whose father has died (in the case of humans) before reaching maturity; one bereft of a parent's protection.
4.grammar: A definite masculine singular noun ('the orphan') in the genitive case, shown by the -i ending; the genitive typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the orphan') or follows a preposition.
4.root: ي-ت-م (y-t-m) — orphanhood, being bereft of a parent

5.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
5.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

6.meaning: A combination meaning 'by/with that which…' or 'in the way that…' — the preposition 'with/by' joined to a feminine relative pronoun 'that which, she who'.
6.grammar: A preposition bi- ('with, by, by means of') prefixed to allatī, the singular feminine relative pronoun ('the one who/which'); the relative pronoun is invariable and here stands in the genitive as object of the preposition. It introduces a description, roughly 'with that which is …'.

7.meaning: A standalone pronoun meaning 'she' or 'it' (feminine). Arabic has no neuter, so 'it' for a feminine noun is expressed with this word. Used independently for emphasis or to stand as the subject of a sentence.
7.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person feminine singular. It stands on its own (not attached to another word) and most often functions as the subject of a nominal sentence ('she/it is …'). Its form is fixed and does not take case endings.

8.meaning: 'Better, finer, more excellent / best, finest' — the comparative-superlative form of 'good, beautiful', meaning surpassing in goodness or beauty.
8.grammar: A comparative/superlative adjective on the pattern 'afʿal' ('more/most …'). The final -u marks the nominative case, the form used when the word is the subject or predicate of a sentence ('… is better/best'). As a comparative of this pattern it does not take the indefinite tanwīn.

9.meaning: 'Until / up to the point that; so that' — a particle marking a limit or goal. It expresses the end-point reached ('until') or the purpose aimed at ('so that, in order that').
9.grammar: A particle indicating a goal or limit. When followed by a present-tense verb it places that verb in the subjunctive mood (clipping its ending to -a), conveying 'until / so that' something comes about. Ḥattā itself is invariable.

10.meaning: It reaches or arrives at — to attain a point or destination, to come fully to its mark.
10.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'). The final -a is the subjunctive ending, signalling that the verb depends on a preceding particle such as 'until', 'so that', or 'that'.
10.root: ب-ل-غ (b-l-gh) — to reach, attain, arrive; eloquence (full attainment of expression)

11.meaning: 'His full strength / prime of maturity' — the age at which a person reaches sound, settled adulthood and full vigor of body and judgment; with the attached pronoun 'his'.
11.grammar: A noun carrying the attached possessive pronoun -hu 'his'. The noun is accusative in function (e.g. as the goal of 'until he reaches …'), but that case is not separately visible here: because the stem ends in a doubled consonant (-dd), a short -a is inserted as a connecting/linking vowel before the suffix, so the -a you hear is a phonological helper, not the case marker.
11.root: ش-د-د (sh-d-d) — strength, firmness, intensity

12.meaning: 'And fulfill! / keep, honor in full' — a command to carry out an obligation completely, to keep a promise or pay a due in full. Prefixed 'wa' adds 'and.'
12.grammar: 'And' (wa) plus a command (imperative) verb to a masculine plural 'you.' The verb is from a causative (Form IV) pattern meaning 'to fulfill completely/loyally'; the '-ū' ending directs the order to a group ('you all fulfill!').
12.root: و-ف-ي (w-f-y) — fulfilling, completing, keeping in full

13.meaning: 'The measure' — the act or standard of measuring out a quantity (especially of grain or goods), and the measuring-vessel itself.
13.grammar: A definite masculine singular noun in the accusative case, shown by the -a ending; the accusative typically marks the direct object of a verb (e.g. 'give full measure').
13.root: ك-ي-ل (k-y-l) — to measure out (by volume), a measure

14.meaning: 'And the balance / the scales' — the instrument for weighing, and by extension the principle of just weight and equilibrium.
14.grammar: The conjunction wa- ('and') plus a definite masculine singular noun in the accusative case, shown by the -a ending; the accusative typically marks the direct object of a verb. The mīzān pattern (mifʿāl) denotes an instrument — here a thing used for weighing.

15.meaning: In/with justice and equity — 'qisṭ' is fair, balanced dealing: giving each their due in full measure, without wronging anyone.
15.grammar: A masculine noun ('justice, equity') governed by the preposition 'bi-' ('in/with') and made definite by 'al-' ('the'). The final -i ending is genitive, the case a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship.

16.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
16.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

17.meaning: A verb meaning 'We impose as a duty / We burden (someone) with a charge' — to assign a task or obligation that requires effort, with 'We' as the doer.
17.grammar: A Form II present-tense verb; the nu- prefix marks the first-person plural 'we' as the doer, and the -u ending marks the ordinary (indicative) present, describing an ongoing or habitual action. The doubled middle consonant gives the causative sense 'to make (someone) bear'.
17.root: ك-ل-ف (k-l-f) — to charge with, impose a burden/obligation

18.meaning: A 'self' or 'soul' — the living person, the inner self, and by extension a human being or life. It can mean one's very self, one's soul, or simply 'a person/a life'.
18.grammar: A feminine noun. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative case, which typically marks the word as the object of a verb ('a soul / a person' as the thing acted upon).
18.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — soul, self, breath, living being

19.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
19.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.
19.root: — (particle)

20.meaning: A noun meaning 'its capacity', 'its scope', or 'what is within its power' — the full extent of ability or means that something possesses. From a word for room, breadth, or ability, with a possessive 'its'.
20.grammar: A noun with the accusative -a ending, the case typically marking the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon). The attached -hā means 'its' or 'her', so the whole means 'its capacity'. The accusative here signals it as what a verb falls upon.
20.root: و-س-ع (w-s-ʿ) — to be wide, spacious, to have room or capacity

21.meaning: 'And when...' — a linking phrase joining 'and' to 'when', used to introduce a circumstance or a recurring situation: 'and whenever / and at the time that...'.
21.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to idhā ('when'). Idhā is a particle pointing to a time or condition, generally referring to something expected or recurring in the future ('when / whenever' it happens), and it normally introduces a following clause that states what occurs at that time.

22.meaning: 'You (plural) said' — to say, speak, or utter. The verb covers any act of stating or declaring something in words.
22.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The suffix -tum marks the masculine plural 'you (all)' as the doers of a completed action — it signals both the past tense and that the speakers being addressed are a group. (This is a hollow verb: its middle root letter is a wāw, which surfaces as a long ā in the base form qāla but reduces to a short u, giving qul-, before a consonant-initial suffix like -tum.)
22.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, to speak, to utter

23.meaning: A command meaning 'so be just, act with fairness / give each its due' — to hold to equity and balance; here prefaced by 'so/then'.
23.grammar: The connective particle fa- ('so, then') plus a Form I masculine plural imperative; the -ū ending commands 'you all' to do the act. It orders a group to act justly.

24.meaning: 'and if' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle 'if'. This particular 'if' (law) introduces a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact condition: 'if (such-and-such had been the case)…', often implying it was not.
24.grammar: A conjunction plus a conditional particle. wa- means 'and'. law is a non-changing particle (no case ending) that sets up a supposition, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('… then certainly …').
24.root: — (particles; no triliteral root)

25.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

25.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.
25.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existence; to be

26.meaning: A demonstrative meaning 'this one' or 'the one' — a pointing word ('that/this') used to single out a person or thing. It often combines with the question particle to form 'who is it that…?'
26.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun ('this/that one'). It does not take case endings; the final -ā is part of the fixed word. It functions to point out or identify someone or something.

27.meaning: Kinship / nearness of relation — closeness in family ties; a near relative or the bond of being related. Built from the sense of 'nearness.'
27.grammar: A feminine singular noun ending in alif maqṣūra (-ā). This fixed -ā ending does not change for case, so it can serve in any grammatical position; the word denotes kinship or close relationship.

28.meaning: 'And by/with the covenant' — a solemn, binding pledge or compact; the preposition 'with/by' joined to the word for covenant.
28.grammar: The conjunction wa- ('and') and preposition bi- ('with, by') prefixed to a masculine singular noun; the -i ending is genitive (required after the preposition bi-), typically linking to a following noun ('… the covenant OF …') or simply governed by the preposition.
28.root: ع-ه-د (ʿ-h-d) — covenant, pledge, compact, undertaking

29.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
29.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

30.meaning: A command addressed to a group: 'fulfil!', 'discharge in full!', 'pay back completely!'. The verb conveys giving something its complete, undiminished due — meeting an obligation fully without falling short.
30.grammar: An imperative (command) verb directed at a group of people. The -ū ending marks the command as plural masculine: 'all of you, do this!'. The form is causative/intensive (Form IV), giving the sense of bringing a thing to full completion.
30.root: و-ف-ي (w-f-y) — to fulfil completely, to give in full measure, faithfulness

31.meaning: A demonstrative meaning 'that' addressed to a group of people (plural 'you'). It points to something at a distance — whether physical, or to a previously mentioned matter — and is directed at multiple listeners.
31.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun for something distant. The base 'dhā' carries the sense 'that', the 'li' is an element of distance, and the ending '-kum' tells you the speaker is addressing a plural 'you' — it specifies the audience, not the thing pointed at. It does not change for case.

32.meaning: A verb meaning 'He firmly enjoined, charged, or instructed (you) as a binding duty' — to give an earnest, solemn commandment or counsel, with an attached object 'you (plural)'.
32.grammar: An intensive Form II past-tense verb (waṣṣā), third-person masculine singular 'he', with the doubled middle consonant signalling emphasis/thoroughness; the suffix -kum is the attached object pronoun 'you all (men, or a mixed group)'.
32.root: و-ص-ي (w-ṣ-y) — to enjoin, charge, bequeath, give binding counsel

33.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
33.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

34.meaning: 'so that you may…,' 'in the hope that you…' — a particle expressing purpose, expectation, or hopeful anticipation, fused with 'you (plural).' It introduces a hoped-for or intended outcome; when used of Allah it conveys the desired result rather than uncertainty.

parts.en: so that / perhaps / in hope that

34.grammar: An emphatic particle of hope/purpose belonging to the 'inna' family, which attaches a pronoun as its subject. The particle's fixed form ends in '-a,' and the suffix '-kum' is 'you (plural),' giving 'so that you (all) may…'

35.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (all) take heed, bear in mind, call to remembrance' — to reflect and let something sink in as a reminder.
35.grammar: A present-tense Form V verb (tafaʿʿala type, whose stem ta- is dropped by assimilation after the present-tense prefix). The ta- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks 'you all' as the doers in the ordinary (indicative) present, describing ongoing or habitual action.
35.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, mention, call to mind

1.meaning: And that — a linking expression introducing a fact or clause ('and that …'); it combines 'and' with a particle that sets up and emphasises the statement that follows.
1.grammar: A connective made of wa- ('and') plus anna ('that'). Anna introduces a noun clause — a fact being asserted — and gives it emphasis, roughly 'and (it is the case) that …'. As a governing particle, anna puts the noun right after it into the accusative case.

2.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
2.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

3.meaning: 'My path / My way' — a road or way; with the attached pronoun 'my'. Often used figuratively for a way of life or course to be followed.
3.grammar: A masculine singular noun with the attached first-person possessive pronoun -ī 'my'; this suffix both marks possession and absorbs the case ending, so the noun's case is not separately shown.

4.meaning: An adjective meaning 'straight', 'upright', or 'standing firm' — perfectly direct and even, without crookedness or deviation; the well-balanced, correct course.
4.grammar: A Form X (istafʿala) active participle — the mustafʿil pattern — built on the root q-w-m and used here as an adjective ('straight, upright'). The -an (accusative indefinite, tanwīn) ending marks it as indefinite and in the accusative, the case taken when it describes a noun in that case or functions as an object/predicate.
4.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, be upright, straight

5.meaning: A command meaning 'so follow it / pursue and adhere to it' — to walk behind and conform to something; here 'so' + 'follow' + the object 'it'.
5.grammar: The connective particle fa- ('so, then') plus a Form VIII masculine plural imperative ('you all, follow!'), with the attached object pronoun -hu 'it/him'. Form VIII here gives the sense of diligently following/pursuing.
5.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, come after, pursue

6.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
6.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

7.meaning: 'You (plural) follow' — a verb meaning to come after, pursue, take as a guide, or obey and imitate; addressed to a group.
7.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form VIII), second-person masculine plural ('you follow'). The ta- prefix marks the addressee 'you'; the -ū ending marks a masculine plural 'you all'. The dropped final nūn (here -ū rather than -ūna) signals that the verb is in a subjunctive/jussive mood, typical after particles of negation, prohibition, or purpose.
7.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, come after, pursue

8.meaning: 'The paths / the ways' — the plural of a road or way; the various routes or courses one might take.
8.grammar: A definite broken (irregular) plural noun in the accusative case, shown by the -a ending; the accusative typically marks the direct object of a verb. The l- of 'the' assimilates into the following s- in pronunciation (al-subul → as-subul).

9.meaning: A verb meaning 'so it became scattered / split apart and diverged' — to break up into separate, parting directions (intransitive — the subject itself comes apart); prefaced by 'so/then'.
9.grammar: The connective particle fa- ('so, then') plus a Form V past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular 'it'; the bare -a ending marks a completed action by 'he/it'. Form V (tafaʿʿala) is reflexive/intransitive here, conveying that the subject itself became dispersed or split into parts (not that it caused something else to scatter).
9.root: ف-ر-ق (f-r-q) — to separate, divide, split apart

10.meaning: A preposition 'bi' ('with / by / in / for') joined to the attached pronoun 'you all', yielding 'with you' or 'for you (plural)'. The exact shade — attachment, instrument, or benefit — depends on the verb it accompanies.
10.grammar: A preposition plus an attached pronoun. 'bi' is a versatile preposition (with, by, in, for), and -kum is the genitive/object pronoun 'you all' (masculine plural). Pronouns following a preposition always take this attached (genitive) form.

11.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

11.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

12.meaning: "His way / His path" — the noun for a road, path, or way, here carrying the attached pronoun "His" (referring to Allah); idiomatically, the path or cause of Allah.
12.grammar: A masculine noun with the attached possessive pronoun "-hi" ("his/His"). The pronoun appears in its "-hi" form (with the "i" vowel), which is used when the noun is in the genitive — i.e., after a preposition or when linked in an "of"-type relation to a preceding word.
12.root: س-ب-ل (s-b-l) — way, path, road

13.meaning: A demonstrative meaning 'that' addressed to a group of people (plural 'you'). It points to something at a distance — whether physical, or to a previously mentioned matter — and is directed at multiple listeners.
13.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun for something distant. The base 'dhā' carries the sense 'that', the 'li' is an element of distance, and the ending '-kum' tells you the speaker is addressing a plural 'you' — it specifies the audience, not the thing pointed at. It does not change for case.

14.meaning: A verb meaning 'He firmly enjoined, charged, or instructed (you) as a binding duty' — to give an earnest, solemn commandment or counsel, with an attached object 'you (plural)'.
14.grammar: An intensive Form II past-tense verb (waṣṣā), third-person masculine singular 'he', with the doubled middle consonant signalling emphasis/thoroughness; the suffix -kum is the attached object pronoun 'you all (men, or a mixed group)'.
14.root: و-ص-ي (w-ṣ-y) — to enjoin, charge, bequeath, give binding counsel

15.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
15.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

16.meaning: 'so that you may…,' 'in the hope that you…' — a particle expressing purpose, expectation, or hopeful anticipation, fused with 'you (plural).' It introduces a hoped-for or intended outcome; when used of Allah it conveys the desired result rather than uncertainty.

parts.en: so that / perhaps / in hope that

16.grammar: An emphatic particle of hope/purpose belonging to the 'inna' family, which attaches a pronoun as its subject. The particle's fixed form ends in '-a,' and the suffix '-kum' is 'you (plural),' giving 'so that you (all) may…'

17.meaning: 'you become mindful and guard yourselves,' 'you are God-conscious' — to shield oneself through reverent awareness of Allah, guarding against wrongdoing and His displeasure. This is the verb of taqwā: a protective, careful piety, not merely 'fear.'
17.grammar: A present/future-tense verb of the self-protective (form VIII) pattern. The 'ta-' prefix marks 'you,' and the '-ūna' ending marks a plural masculine subject ('you all') in the ongoing/indicative mood — the full '-ūna' (rather than shortened '-ū') signals the plain indicative, stating an action as a fact or expected reality.
17.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, shield, protect (basis of taqwā)

1.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
1.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

2.meaning: 'We gave / granted / brought'. To hand over or bestow something upon someone; to come to someone with a gift or grant.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb in the causative (form IV) sense 'to bring/grant to someone'. The '-nā' suffix is the doer 'we' in completed past time. It often takes two objects — the recipient and the thing given.
2.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (form IV) to give, bring

3.meaning: Mūsā (Moses), the prophet — a proper name.
3.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin. It is indeclinable — its final long 'ā' does not change to show case — so one and the same form serves whether it acts as subject, object, or follows a preposition.

4.meaning: The Book, the Scripture — a written revelation; the term for a divinely revealed text.
4.grammar: A definite noun ('the Book') with attached 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb.
4.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; a writing, book

5.meaning: 'As a completion / in full measure' — the bringing of something to its full, perfect, entire state; completeness or fulfillment.
5.grammar: An indefinite masculine singular noun in the accusative case, marked by the -an ending (tanwīn); this often functions adverbially — 'as a completion / by way of completing' — explaining the purpose or manner of an action.
5.root: ت-م-م (t-m-m) — to be complete, whole, perfect; completion

6.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
6.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
6.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

7.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
7.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

8.meaning: A verb meaning 'he did good / acted well, excellently' — to do what is beautiful, fine, and right; also 'he was good (at something)'.
8.grammar: A Form IV (afʿala) past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular 'he'; the bare -a ending marks a completed action by 'he'. Form IV here gives the sense of doing/making good, acting with excellence.

9.meaning: 'And as a detailed exposition / a making-distinct' — the laying out of something clearly, point by point, in full detail.
9.grammar: The conjunction wa- ('and') plus an indefinite masculine verbal noun (Form II maṣdar) in the accusative case, marked by the -an ending (tanwīn); the accusative often functions adverbially here — '(as) a detailing/explaining'. The Form II pattern (tafʿīl) stresses doing the act thoroughly, part by part.
9.root: ف-ص-ل (f-ṣ-l) — to separate, distinguish, set out in detail

10.meaning: For every, for each, belonging to all of. Combines the preposition 'for/to' with the word for 'every/all.'
10.grammar: The preposition li- ('for/to') joined to kull ('every/each/all'). The -i ending on kull is genitive, the case required after a preposition. The combination conveys 'for every / to each.'

11.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
11.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
11.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

12.meaning: Joined to 'and': 'and a guidance' — guidance meaning right direction, the showing of the correct path, that which leads aright.
12.grammar: A noun preceded by the connector 'wa' ('and'). It is a 'defective' noun whose third root letter is a weak yāʾ, written here as a final alif maqṣūra (ى); the indefinite ending '-an' (tanwīn) sits on that final letter. Such nouns keep the same form across the nominative, accusative, and genitive cases.
12.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, show the way

13.meaning: 'And as a mercy' — compassion, tenderness, and active kindness shown to others; relief and grace bestowed.
13.grammar: The conjunction wa- ('and') plus an indefinite feminine singular noun in the accusative case, marked by the -an ending (tanwīn) on the closed tā'; the accusative often functions adverbially here — '(as) a mercy' — or marks it as a direct object.

14.meaning: A compound particle of hopeful expectation, meaning roughly 'perhaps', 'so that', or 'in the hope that'. It expresses a wished-for or anticipated outcome — when used of people, an expectation that they might do or become something. The attached pronoun specifies the ones concerned: 'they' (a group).

parts.en: perhaps / so that / in hope that

14.grammar: The particle laʿalla governs a following noun or pronoun in the accusative-style attachment; the suffix -hum is the attached pronoun 'they/them', here naming the group about whom the hope or expectation is expressed.

15.meaning: A noun meaning 'a meeting, encounter, or coming face-to-face,' prefixed with 'in/with.' It denotes the act of two parties meeting, often used for the encounter with one's Lord.

parts.en: genitive ending (because of the preceding preposition)

15.grammar: A noun governed by the attached preposition bi- ('in / with'). The final -i is the genitive case ending, which is the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a following noun ('… of …').
15.root: ل-ق-ي (l-q-y) — to meet, encounter, come face-to-face

16.meaning: 'Their Lord' — the base 'rabb' means Lord, Master, Sustainer: the one who owns, nurtures, governs, and brings to maturity. As a divine title it conveys Allah as Creator and Sustainer of all.
16.grammar: The noun 'rabb' ('Lord, Sustainer') with the attached pronoun '-him' ('their'). The '-i' before the pronoun is the genitive case, the form used after a preposition or, as in a possessive linkage, to show belonging ('of/their').
16.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, master, sustain; lordship

17.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believe / have faith' — to place trust and secure conviction in, especially in Allah and what He has revealed; to hold something firmly true.
17.grammar: A Form IV (afʿala) present-tense verb; the yu- prefix with the -ūna ending marks 'they (masculine plural)' as the doers in the ordinary (indicative) present, describing ongoing or habitual action.
17.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, trust; to be safe, to have faith

1.meaning: A phrase meaning 'and this (one)' — the pointing word 'this' (for something near, masculine/neutral) joined to 'and'.
1.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to the demonstrative hādhā ('this'), used to point to something near at hand (masculine singular). A demonstrative like this has a fixed ending and does not change for grammatical case; it can stand as a subject or be linked to a following noun ('this ___').

2.meaning: A book, scripture, or written record — that which is written. It denotes a written document, and in the religious sense a revealed Scripture sent down from Allah.
2.grammar: A noun ('a book') with the -un ending, the nominative indefinite case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence. The form names a written or revealed text without specifying which.

3.meaning: 'We sent it down / revealed it'. Past-tense verb from anzala ('to send down, cause to descend'), with the 'We' of majesty as subject and 'it' as object. Characteristically used of revelation sent down from above.

parts.en: sent down / caused to descend (causative stem)

3.grammar: A past-tense verb of the causative pattern (af ʿala: 'to make come down'). The suffix -nā marks a first-person plural subject, 'we'. The attached -hu is the object 'it/him'. In divine speech the plural 'We' conveys majesty, not number.
3.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to come down, descend; (causative) to send down

4.meaning: 'blessed; full of and bestowing blessing'. The passive participle of bāraka ('to bless'), describing something endowed with abundant, lasting good (baraka) and a source of it.
4.grammar: A passive participle ('blessed') on the pattern mufāʿal. The ending -un (tanwīn with -u) is the indefinite nominative: it marks the word as indefinite and as standing in the subject/predicate position, e.g. describing something as 'a blessed (thing)'.
4.root: ب-ر-ك (b-r-k) — to be/become blessed; abundant, enduring good

5.meaning: A command meaning 'so follow it / pursue and adhere to it' — to walk behind and conform to something; here 'so' + 'follow' + the object 'it'.
5.grammar: The connective particle fa- ('so, then') plus a Form VIII masculine plural imperative ('you all, follow!'), with the attached object pronoun -hu 'it/him'. Form VIII here gives the sense of diligently following/pursuing.
5.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, come after, pursue

6.meaning: A command addressed to a group: 'guard yourselves / be mindful and on your guard.' The verb conveys taqwā — protecting oneself by being conscious of Allah and shielding oneself from wrongdoing and its consequences.
6.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a plural 'you (all).' The -ū ending marks the masculine plural addressees ('you all'). The pattern (form VIII, from waqā 'to protect') gives the sense of taking protective care for oneself.
6.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, shield, protect oneself

7.meaning: 'so that you may…,' 'in the hope that you…' — a particle expressing purpose, expectation, or hopeful anticipation, fused with 'you (plural).' It introduces a hoped-for or intended outcome; when used of Allah it conveys the desired result rather than uncertainty.

parts.en: so that / perhaps / in hope that

7.grammar: An emphatic particle of hope/purpose belonging to the 'inna' family, which attaches a pronoun as its subject. The particle's fixed form ends in '-a,' and the suffix '-kum' is 'you (plural),' giving 'so that you (all) may…'

8.meaning: '(that) you may receive mercy / be shown mercy' — to be treated with compassion and mercy by another. Addressed to a group, with the doer of the mercy unnamed.
8.grammar: A present-tense passive verb, second-person masculine plural ('you all are shown mercy' — the subject receives the action rather than doing it). The full '-ūna' ending is the indicative, marking a plain ongoing statement; it often follows a particle expressing hoped-for result ('so that you may be shown mercy').

1.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
1.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

2.meaning: You (all) say / utter — referring to speaking or saying words, addressed to a group. In context it is the form used after a particle so that it reads 'do not say' / 'that you may say'.
2.grammar: Present-tense verb, second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The ta- prefix marks the second person; plurality is supplied by the -ū ending. The plain ending here (without final -na) is the form a verb takes after certain particles such as 'do not' or 'so that', signalling command-prohibition or purpose.

3.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
3.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

4.meaning: 'It was sent down / revealed': the act of being caused to descend, used especially of revelation brought down from Allah. The passive form puts the focus on the thing sent down rather than on the sender.
4.grammar: A past-tense passive verb in Form IV (anzala 'to send down' → unzila 'was sent down'). The prefix is only the u- vowel carried on the connecting hamza; the nūn that follows is the first root letter (of ن-ز-ل), not part of the prefix. The internal vowel pattern u–i marks it as passive ('was/were sent down'), with no named doer. The final -a marks the subject as 'he/it', a single masculine thing, and signals completed action.
4.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down; (Form IV) to send down

5.meaning: 'The Book / Scripture / what is prescribed in writing' — a written record or ordinance; the decreed, written prescription. Often denotes revealed Scripture or, by extension, a fixed written decree.
5.grammar: A verbal noun on the fiʿāl pattern ('that which is written') with the definite article al- ('the'). The -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate.

6.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
6.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

7.meaning: 'Two groups / two parties' — the dual of a band, faction, or company of people; specifically two such groups.
7.grammar: A feminine noun in the dual (meaning exactly two) bearing the -ayni ending; this dual ending is used when the word is in the accusative or genitive — i.e. as an object, or after a preposition, or linked to a preceding noun.
7.root: ط-و-ف (ṭ-w-f) — to go around, encircle; a band/group

8.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
8.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

9.meaning: 'Before us / prior to us' — earlier in time than 'us'; an adverb of time joined to the pronoun 'us'.
9.grammar: The time-word qabl ('before') with the attached pronoun -nā 'us'; the -i ending is genitive, the regular case for such adverbs when governed (here by the attached pronoun), giving 'before us'.
9.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, come before; priority, frontness

10.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
10.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

11.meaning: 'We were' — the past tense of the verb 'to be,' establishing a past state or condition for a group including the speaker. It is the basic verb of existence and of 'being something.'
11.grammar: The past tense of 'to be' in the first-person plural ('we were'). The subject suffix is -nā ('we'); its nūn is written with a shadda (نَّ) because it merges with the final nūn of the verb stem kun-, and the alif spells the long -ā. A hollow verb, its middle weak letter drops in this form. It sets up a past state, and what follows describes how 'we' were.
11.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into being, existence

12.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

12.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

13.meaning: 'Their study / their reading and learning' — the act of poring over and studying texts so as to master them; with the attached pronoun 'their'.
13.grammar: A feminine verbal noun (Form III maṣdar, dirāsa, with its tā' opened before a suffix) in the genitive case (the -i), carrying the attached possessive pronoun -him 'their (masculine plural)'; the genitive typically follows a preposition or links the noun to a preceding word ('… OF their study').
13.root: د-ر-س (d-r-s) — to study, learn, read repeatedly

14.meaning: Heedless, unaware, oblivious ones — people who are inattentive and neglectful, letting something slip from their notice or care. The opening lam is an emphatic particle conveying 'surely, certainly,' stressing the truth of the statement.
14.grammar: An active participle in the masculine sound plural. The -īna ending marks the plural in the accusative/genitive (object or 'of/to') case, the form used when the word is an object of a verb or follows certain particles, as opposed to the subject ending -ūna. The prefixed la- adds emphasis ('surely').

1.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
1.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

2.meaning: You (all) say / utter — referring to speaking or saying words, addressed to a group. In context it is the form used after a particle so that it reads 'do not say' / 'that you may say'.
2.grammar: Present-tense verb, second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The ta- prefix marks the second person; plurality is supplied by the -ū ending. The plain ending here (without final -na) is the form a verb takes after certain particles such as 'do not' or 'so that', signalling command-prohibition or purpose.

3.meaning: A conditional particle introducing a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact supposition: 'if (it were the case that…)'. It typically presents a condition that is unfulfilled or merely imagined, often implying the result did not or would not happen.
3.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case ending). It signals a hypothetical 'if': it sets up a supposed condition whose consequence is then stated, frequently with the sense 'if X were so, then Y would be so' — often where X is contrary to fact.

4.meaning: That We … — an emphatic linking particle 'that' fused with the pronoun 'We.' 'Anna' introduces and asserts a fact ('that indeed …'), and the attached 'We' names the doer (a majestic or plural 'We').
4.grammar: An emphatic particle 'anna' ('that, indeed') with the attached pronoun -nā 'we.' This family of particles takes a following noun/pronoun in the accusative as its subject, so -nā here functions as that subject: 'that We …'. It firmly introduces a stated fact.

5.meaning: 'It was sent down / revealed': the act of being caused to descend, used especially of revelation brought down from Allah. The passive form puts the focus on the thing sent down rather than on the sender.
5.grammar: A past-tense passive verb in Form IV (anzala 'to send down' → unzila 'was sent down'). The prefix is only the u- vowel carried on the connecting hamza; the nūn that follows is the first root letter (of ن-ز-ل), not part of the prefix. The internal vowel pattern u–i marks it as passive ('was/were sent down'), with no named doer. The final -a marks the subject as 'he/it', a single masculine thing, and signals completed action.
5.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down; (Form IV) to send down

6.meaning: 'Upon us' / 'over us' / 'against us' — the preposition ʿalā ('on, over, upon') with an attached 'us'. It conveys something resting on, incumbent upon, or bearing against the group.
6.grammar: A preposition (ʿalā, 'upon/over') with an attached pronoun, first person plural (-nā, 'us'). When a pronoun is attached, ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay-. Such prepositional phrases put their pronoun in the object/genitive role.

7.meaning: 'The Book / Scripture / what is prescribed in writing' — a written record or ordinance; the decreed, written prescription. Often denotes revealed Scripture or, by extension, a fixed written decree.
7.grammar: A verbal noun on the fiʿāl pattern ('that which is written') with the definite article al- ('the'). The -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate.

8.meaning: 'We would surely have been' — a past-tense 'to be' verb with an attached 'we,' carrying a sense of a hypothetical outcome ('we would have been'). The opening lam emphasizes the statement, often as the answer to a condition ('if … then surely we would have been').
8.grammar: A past-tense form of the verb 'to be' (kāna) with the subject suffix -nā ('we'). When -nā attaches, the long vowel of the stem drops and the stem-final n merges with the n of the suffix, which is why the two are written together as a single doubled n (shadda) in -nnā. The -nā morpheme means the doers are 'we.' The leading la- is the emphatic particle that typically introduces the result clause of a conditional ('… then we would surely have been …').
8.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

9.meaning: Comparative/elative adjective from guidance: 'more rightly guided, better guided, more on the straight path.' It weighs one party against another in nearness to true guidance.
9.grammar: An elative (comparative/superlative) adjective on the pattern afʿal, formed from a 'weak' root, hence the long final -ā. As an elative it conveys 'more …' or 'most …' and does not change for case in this fixed shape.

10.meaning: From them / among them — the preposition min ('from, out of, part of') joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
10.grammar: The preposition min ('from / among / part of') with the attached third-person masculine plural pronoun -hum ('them'). Pronouns after a preposition are in the genitive; the combination expresses origin, partition ('some of them'), or belonging to that group.

11.meaning: A two-part connector: fa- means 'so', 'then', or 'and so', linking what follows as a result or consequence; qad before a past-tense verb intensifies it, conveying 'certainly', 'indeed', or 'already' — stressing that the action has truly and definitely occurred.
11.grammar: fa- is a connecting particle meaning 'so' or 'then', often marking a result. qad is a particle of emphasis; placed before a completed (past-tense) verb it affirms that the action has definitely or already happened. Neither part takes a case ending.

12.meaning: "he/it came to you" — a past verb "came" with the pronoun "you" as the one reached, i.e. something arrived at or reached a group of people.
12.grammar: A past-tense verb in its base third-person masculine singular form ("he/it came"), with no extra subject suffix. The verb "to come" is intransitive, so the attached -kum is not a direct object but an indirect (dative) pronoun — "to you" (masculine plural), equivalent to "came to you (all)."
12.root: ج-ي-ء (j-y-ʾ) — to come, arrive

13.meaning: A clear proof, a plain piece of evidence, something self-evidently manifest that makes the truth obvious. As a noun it denotes a clarifying sign or demonstration that removes doubt.
13.grammar: A feminine singular noun. The final -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a clear proof') and in the nominative case, the form used for the subject of a sentence. The feminine -a(t) ending is built into the word.

14.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
14.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

15.meaning: 'Your Lord' (addressing a group). 'Rabb' is a rich term: the Master, Owner, Sustainer and Nurturer who creates, possesses, provides for, and brings a thing to its proper completion — far more than a mere ruler.
15.grammar: A noun ('Lord') with an attached possessive pronoun, forming a possessive pairing. 'Rabb' carries a doubled (geminated) 'b' — the shaddah — at its core. The '-i' vowel on 'rabb' is its case ending, determined by 'Lord's' own role in the sentence (not by the suffix); the attached '-kum' is the possessor ('your'), addressing a plural 'you', and as the possessed-to term it sits in the genitive.

16.meaning: A connective 'and' plus 'guidance' — 'and guidance': right direction, the showing of the correct way, that which leads one rightly.
16.grammar: The prefix wa- is the connective 'and'. 'hudā' is a noun meaning 'guidance'; because it ends in a special shortened alif, its indefinite ending appears as -an (written with tanwīn over the preceding letter). This -an is the indefinite marker; on such alif-ending nouns the case is not separately shown, so the word can stand as subject, object, or predicate alike.

17.meaning: 'And a mercy' — raḥma is tender compassion that actively moves one to kindness, relief, and care. The wa- prefix adds 'and'. It is the same quality central to the divine names ar-Raḥmān and ar-Raḥīm.
17.grammar: The wa- prefix is 'and'. The word ends in a tāʾ marbūṭa (ة), the feminine ending: read in full it carries the -un here as -tun, while at a pause it is softened to -h. The final -un marks the noun as indefinite ('a mercy') and nominative, the subject form.

18.meaning: A compound meaning 'then whoever' or 'so whoever'. It combines 'then/so' with the conditional/relative 'who', introducing whatever person meets a stated condition.
18.grammar: The connector fa- ('then/so', often answering or following a condition) joined to man ('whoever / the one who'), which refers to people and introduces a condition: 'whoever does X…'. man does not change its ending; the clause after it supplies the rest of the meaning.

19.meaning: An elative adjective meaning 'more / most wrongdoing, unjust, or oppressive' — comparing degrees of ẓulm (placing things out of their rightful place, transgression).
19.grammar: An elative (comparative/superlative) noun on the pattern afʿal, meaning 'more/most unjust'. It ends in -u (nominative), the case typical of a subject or predicate.
19.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — wrongdoing, injustice, putting something where it does not belong

20.meaning: A compound meaning 'than one who / than whoever' — combining the preposition of comparison 'than' with the relative pronoun 'who', used to compare a person against others.
20.grammar: The preposition 'min' (here 'than', used after elatives) followed by the indeclinable relative 'man' ('who'). The final nūn of 'min' undergoes regressive assimilation into the following mīm of 'man', producing a doubled mīm; the resulting shadda sits on the mīm of 'man'. Both words are indeclinable particles and take no case ending.

21.meaning: A verb meaning 'he denied / cried lies against / rejected as false' — to treat something or someone as a lie, refusing to accept it as true and openly rejecting it.
21.grammar: Past-tense verb (form II, intensive), third-person masculine singular ('he denied / rejected as false'). The doubled middle letter (kadhdhaba) gives the sense of actively declaring something false. The final -a is the past-tense ending for a masculine singular doer.
21.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie; (form II) to deny, to call a lie

22.meaning: 'With/in the signs of…' — the preposition bi- joined to a plural noun meaning 'signs', 'tokens', or 'verses': evidences that point to a truth beyond themselves.
22.grammar: bi- is a preposition meaning 'with/in' and always takes the genitive. āyāt is a sound feminine plural; its -i ending here is genitive, the case required after the preposition, and it typically also links to a following noun ('signs OF …').
22.root: ء-ي-ي / ء-و-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, mark, or token

23.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
23.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

24.meaning: 'And he turned away / shunned / averted himself' — to turn aside from something, to disregard or recoil from it. The verb conveys an active turning-away or barring of oneself (and others) from a thing.
24.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he …'). The bare -a ending is the basic past-tense form meaning the single male doer completed the action. The prefixed wa- means 'and.'
24.root: ص-د-ف (ṣ-d-f) — turning away, shunning, averting

25.meaning: From it / about it / away from it — a preposition meaning 'from' or 'off of', attached to a feminine 'it'.
25.grammar: 'ʿan' is a preposition conveying departure or removal — 'away from / off of / concerning'. The attached -hā is 'it/her', referring to a single feminine thing. Prepositions like this put the following pronoun in the genitive.

26.meaning: 'We will recompense / requite / repay' — to pay back in kind, to give a fitting return for deeds, whether reward or penalty. The prefixed sa- marks near future ('we will'), and the subject is 'we.'
26.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The na- prefix means the doers are 'we'; the attached sa- prefix marks the near future ('will'). The verb is built on a root meaning to repay in kind.
26.root: ج-ز-ي (j-z-y) — recompense, requital, repaying in kind

27.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
27.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

28.meaning: 'They turn away / shun / avert themselves' — to recoil from something and refuse to face it, deliberately keeping away from it.
28.grammar: A present-tense verb. The 'ya-' prefix together with the '-ūna' ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they') performing an ongoing or habitual action. The full '-ūna' ending (rather than a shortened '-ū') signals the plain indicative — a simple statement of what they do.
28.root: ص-د-ف (ṣ-d-f) — turning away, shunning, averting

29.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

29.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

30.meaning: Our signs / verses. The plural of āya — a sign, token, or miraculous proof, and also a verse of revelation — with the attached 'our'.
30.grammar: A feminine plural noun ('signs / verses') with the possessive pronoun -nā ('our'). The sound feminine plural ending -āt shows -i, the case used for the genitive (linked to a following word or after a preposition) and the accusative (object of a verb); attaching -nā ('our') also places it in a possessive relationship. So it means 'signs belonging to Us'.

31.meaning: Evil, harm, or grievousness — the bad or distressing aspect of something; in a possessive link, 'the worst of …' or 'a grievous …'.
31.grammar: A singular masculine noun in the accusative (-a ending), which typically marks an object of a verb or the first term of a possessive link ('the evil OF …'). The sense is 'grievous / worst kind of.'
31.root: س-و-ء (s-w-ʾ) — evil, harm, to be bad

32.meaning: The punishment, torment, or chastisement — severe penalty or suffering inflicted as retribution.
32.grammar: A singular masculine noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending is the genitive, which typically links it to a preceding noun ('… of the punishment') or follows a preposition.

33.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
33.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

34.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
34.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
34.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

35.meaning: 'They turn away / shun / avert themselves' — to recoil from something and refuse to face it, deliberately keeping away from it.
35.grammar: A present-tense verb. The 'ya-' prefix together with the '-ūna' ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they') performing an ongoing or habitual action. The full '-ūna' ending (rather than a shortened '-ū') signals the plain indicative — a simple statement of what they do.

1.meaning: An interrogative particle that turns a statement into a yes/no question, roughly "is it that…?" or "do…?". It can also carry a rhetorical or expectant tone rather than a literal request for information.
1.grammar: A question particle placed before a sentence to ask whether something is the case. It has no case ending and does not change form; it simply marks the words that follow as a yes/no question.

2.meaning: They look toward, watch for, or await; a present-tense act of a group either gazing at something or expecting/waiting for it to happen.
2.grammar: A present/ongoing verb. The ya- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ("they"). The full -ūna ending also signals the indicative mood, used for stating an action that is happening or habitual.

3.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
3.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

4.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
4.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

5.meaning: 'That it comes to them / that it should come to them' — a 'to come, to arrive, to reach' verb with an attached 'them,' expressing the coming or arrival of something upon people. The final -a vowel reflects a subjunctive mood, typically after a particle like 'that' or 'until.'
5.grammar: A present-tense verb with the ta- prefix marking a third-person feminine singular subject ('it/she comes'). The final -a is the subjunctive mood ending, the form taken after particles meaning 'that,' 'so that,' or 'until.' The suffix -hum(u) is the object 'them' (the -u is a connecting vowel before the next word).

6.meaning: The angels — the heavenly beings created by Allah to carry out His commands. A definite plural noun referring to that order of spiritual creatures.
6.grammar: A definite plural noun (a 'broken' plural of malak, 'angel'), treated grammatically as feminine. The prefixed al- means 'the.' The final -u marks the nominative case, the form used for the subject of a sentence.
6.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — possession, dominion; also linked to أ-ل-ك (ʾ-l-k) 'to convey a message'; malak = angel

7.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
7.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

8.meaning: He/it comes, brings, or arrives — to come or to bring (something) about. The form points to an action not yet completed (present or future).
8.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it comes'). The ya- prefix (a single, undoubled yāʾ) marks a single male/thing subject. The final -a (in -iya) is the subjunctive ending, which appears after certain particles meaning 'that', 'until', or 'so that', giving the sense '… that he come' or '… until he comes'.

9.meaning: 'Your Lord / your Master' — the word for 'Lord' (one who owns, sustains, nurtures and has authority over) combined with 'your' (a single addressee); rabb carries the layered sense of master, sustainer, and the one who brings to maturity.
9.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -u ending is the nominative case — the basic 'subject' state, used for the doer of an action or the topic of a sentence. The suffix -ka means 'your', addressed to a single masculine person. 'Rabb' bundles ownership, lordship, nurturing care, and sustaining authority into one term.

10.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
10.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

11.meaning: He/it comes, brings, or arrives — to come or to bring (something) about. The form points to an action not yet completed (present or future).
11.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it comes'). The ya- prefix (a single, undoubled yāʾ) marks a single male/thing subject. The final -a (in -iya) is the subjunctive ending, which appears after certain particles meaning 'that', 'until', or 'so that', giving the sense '… that he come' or '… until he comes'.
11.root: ء-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come, arrive, bring

12.meaning: Some, a part, a portion — a piece or subset of a larger whole. As a noun it points to 'some of' a group or thing rather than all of it.
12.grammar: A singular noun meaning 'a part / some.' The final -u marks the nominative case, used for the subject of a sentence; it is commonly followed by a noun in the 'of' (genitive) form to mean 'some of …'.
12.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, portion, some

13.meaning: Signs, tokens, or evident proofs; also used for the discrete verses of revelation. An āya is a marker that points beyond itself to a deeper truth or to its Author.
