13.grammar: A feminine plural noun ('signs/verses'). The sound-feminine plural takes -i in both the genitive and accusative; the -i ending here links it to a following noun ('… of …') or marks it as the object of a verb or preposition.

14.meaning: A noun with an attached pronoun meaning 'your Lord' — the Lord/Master/Sustainer of a single person addressed. Rabb conveys an owner who creates, nurtures, sustains, and governs all that is under His care.
14.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord, Sustainer') carries the -i genitive vowel, which typically appears when the noun follows a preposition or is itself possessed by a following noun ('… of your Lord'). The suffix -ka means 'your', addressed to a single male.
14.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship; to nurture, sustain, master

15.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
15.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
15.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

16.meaning: he brings / he comes with — a third-person verb meaning to bring something forward or cause it to come, often by fetching or producing it.
16.grammar: A present/future tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person singular masculine doer ('he/it'). Built on a weak root ending in a long vowel, it carries the sense of bringing or coming forth. The form expresses an ongoing or habitual action.

17.meaning: Some, a part, a portion — a piece or subset of a larger whole. As a noun it points to 'some of' a group or thing rather than all of it.
17.grammar: A singular noun meaning 'a part / some.' The final -u marks the nominative case, used for the subject of a sentence; it is commonly followed by a noun in the 'of' (genitive) form to mean 'some of …'.

18.meaning: Signs, tokens, or evident proofs; also used for the discrete verses of revelation. An āya is a marker that points beyond itself to a deeper truth or to its Author.
18.grammar: A feminine plural noun ('signs/verses'). The sound-feminine plural takes -i in both the genitive and accusative; the -i ending here links it to a following noun ('… of …') or marks it as the object of a verb or preposition.

19.meaning: A noun with an attached pronoun meaning 'your Lord' — the Lord/Master/Sustainer of a single person addressed. Rabb conveys an owner who creates, nurtures, sustains, and governs all that is under His care.
19.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord, Sustainer') carries the -i genitive vowel, which typically appears when the noun follows a preposition or is itself possessed by a following noun ('… of your Lord'). The suffix -ka means 'your', addressed to a single male.
19.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship; to nurture, sustain, master

20.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
20.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

21.meaning: He/it benefits, profits, or brings advantage to someone; to be of use.
21.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he' or 'it'). The final -u ending is the indicative mood, used for a plain, ongoing or habitual statement of fact ('benefits / is benefiting').
21.root: ن-ف-ع (n-f-ʿ) — benefit, usefulness, profit

22.meaning: A 'self' or 'soul' — the living person, the inner self, and by extension a human being or life. It can mean one's very self, one's soul, or simply 'a person/a life'.
22.grammar: A feminine noun. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative case, which typically marks the word as the object of a verb ('a soul / a person' as the thing acted upon).
22.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — soul, self, breath, living being

23.meaning: 'Its / her faith' — the noun for faith or believing trust, with an attached possessive 'its/her.' Faith (īmān) is inner belief and trusting affirmation, especially in Allah and what He has revealed.
23.grammar: A verbal noun ('faith') with the possessive suffix -hā ('its/her'). The -u before the suffix marks the nominative case, the form used for the subject of a sentence. The suffix -hā refers back to a feminine or non-human singular owner.
23.root: ا-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, trust, faith; to believe / feel safe

24.meaning: A negating particle, 'not', used specifically to deny that an action happened in the past, even though it attaches to a present-tense verb form. It turns 'you do X' into 'you did not do X'.

parts.en: did not (negation of a completed act)

24.grammar: An indeclinable particle that governs the verb after it, putting that verb into the jussive (clipped) mood and giving it past-time meaning. In short: lam + a present-form verb = 'did not [verb]'.
24.root: — (particle; no triliteral root)

25.meaning: A short (jussive) form of the verb 'to be / to become', meaning 'be' or 'does not become / is not'. It expresses being, existing, or coming to be in a clipped form that typically follows a particle such as a negator or a command.
25.grammar: Present-tense verb with the ta- prefix marking a second-person masculine singular ('you') or third-person feminine singular ('it/she') subject. The clipped final consonant (sukun, no vowel) is the jussive/apocopated mood, the form used after negative particles ('did not / was not') or as a command or prohibition.
25.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

26.meaning: 'She / it believed' — the past tense of 'to believe, to have faith, to affirm trustingly.' It signals the coming-to-belief of a single feminine or non-human subject.
26.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person feminine singular. The -at ending means a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) subject completed the action ('she/it believed'). The verb is the form built on the 'faith/security' root with a lengthened first vowel.
26.root: ا-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, trust, faith; to believe / feel safe

27.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
27.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

28.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'before / beforehand / previously,' pointing to a moment or state that precedes something else in time. When used with the final vowel -u (qablu), it stands cut off from an explicit following noun, conveying 'before(hand)' or 'previously' in an absolute sense — the thing it is 'before' is understood rather than stated.
28.grammar: An adverb of time. The final -u ending here is the indeclinable (mabnī) form taken when the word is severed from a following genitive: rather than 'before X,' it means 'before(hand)' on its own, with the reference point left implicit.
28.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to come before, precede, be in front; to receive/accept

29.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
29.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

30.meaning: 'It earned / acquired, gained' — said of deeds and their consequences; the root means to gain or acquire something, especially the moral 'earnings' of one's actions.
30.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -t (sukūn-marked -at) suffix marks a third-person feminine singular subject, 'she/it.' The past tense presents the action as completed.
30.root: ك-س-ب (k-s-b) — to earn, acquire, gain (esp. deeds)

31.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
31.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

32.meaning: 'Of its / her faith' — the noun for faith with an attached possessive 'its/her,' in the 'of/from' form. Faith (īmān) here is the inner belief and trusting affirmation belonging to someone.
32.grammar: A verbal noun ('faith') with the possessive suffix -hā ('its/her'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of …'). The suffix -hā refers to a feminine or non-human singular owner.
32.root: ا-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, trust, faith; to believe / feel safe

33.meaning: Good — that which is beneficial, virtuous, and excellent; goodness as a thing one can do or possess, and what is better or preferable.
33.grammar: A noun (also serving as the 'better/best' form). The final -an (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case — the case used for the direct object of a verb ('to do good') and for similar governed roles.

34.meaning: 'Say!' — a command to utter or declare something aloud, addressed to a single male.
34.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to one male: 'say!'. Its natural form ends in a silent consonant (qul), but here a short -i vowel is added simply to smooth pronunciation before a following word that begins with a connecting sound; it carries no case meaning of its own.

35.meaning: 'Wait! / Await! / Watch and expect!' — a command addressed to a group, telling them to wait, look out for, or expectantly anticipate something.
35.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a plural 'you.' The -ū ending directs the order to more than one person ('all of you, wait!'). It is built on a reflexive/intensive pattern of the root, giving the sense of actively awaiting or watching for something.

36.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
36.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

37.meaning: Ones who wait / those who watch and expect — people in a state of awaiting or anticipating something. As a participle it names the doers of waiting.
37.grammar: An active participle in the masculine sound plural. The -ūna ending marks the plural in the nominative (subject) case — the form used when the word is the subject or predicate of a sentence, as opposed to the object form -īna. Built on a reflexive/intensive pattern, it means 'those engaged in awaiting.'

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: 'They split up / divided / separated (it)' — the past tense of a verb meaning to break something into parts, to cause division or to make distinctions/factions. The intensive form stresses a thorough splitting apart.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means the doers are 'they' (more than one male, or a mixed group). The doubled middle letter marks the intensive form, conveying a forceful or repeated splitting/dividing.

4.meaning: Their religion / way of life — the concept of dīn: the complete system of belief, worship, obligation, and obedience by which one lives and to which one is accountable; also rendered 'faith,' 'judgment,' or 'recompense' depending on context. Here joined to 'their.'

parts.en: religion, way of life, system of obedience and accountability

4.grammar: A noun with the attached possessive pronoun -hum ('their,' a group of men). The -a vowel before the pronoun reflects the accusative case — the form typically used when the noun is the direct object of a verb ('… their religion' as the thing acted upon).
4.root: د-ي-ن (d-y-n) — religion, obedience, judgment, requital, debt/accountability

5.meaning: A compound meaning 'and they were' or 'and they used to' — it sets a state or habit in the past. The verb 'to be/become' here establishes an ongoing past condition, often paired with a following verb to express habitual action.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb ('to be') in the third-person masculine plural — the -ū ending means 'they' did/were. It commonly conveys a continued past state or habit, especially when followed by another verb. The wa- prefix means 'and.'
5.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into being

6.meaning: Into factions, parties, sects — separate groups and partisan camps into which people split apart. An indefinite plural.
6.grammar: An indefinite broken plural noun. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative, the case typically used for a direct object or to express the state/result into which something is brought ('… into factions').
6.root: ش-ي-ع (sh-y-ʿ) — to follow, to spread; faction, party

7.meaning: 'You are not' — a negating 'to be' verb addressed to a single male, denying that he is or does something ('you are not …').
7.grammar: A special verb that negates 'to be' (from laysa). The suffix -ta marks the second-person masculine singular subject ('you,' one male). Together it states 'you are not.' Such verbs put their following predicate into the object (accusative) form.

8.meaning: From them / among them — the preposition min ('from, out of, part of') joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
8.grammar: The preposition min ('from / among / part of') with the attached third-person masculine plural pronoun -hum ('them'). Pronouns after a preposition are in the genitive; the combination expresses origin, partition ('some of them'), or belonging to that group.

9.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
9.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

10.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
10.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
10.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

11.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
11.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

12.meaning: 'Their affair / matter / command' — the noun amr (a matter, affair, command, or decision) with an attached possessive 'their.' It can mean the business, situation, or decision-making that concerns a group.
12.grammar: A singular noun with the possessive suffix -hum ('their'). The -u before the suffix marks the nominative case, the form used for the subject of a sentence. The suffix -hum refers to a masculine or mixed plural owner.
12.root: ا-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — command/order; affair, matter

13.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
13.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

14.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
14.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

15.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
15.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

16.meaning: 'He will inform them / tell them news of' — a verb meaning to convey weighty news or important information, with an attached 'them.' The intensive form stresses a full and significant announcing.
16.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he …'). The yu- prefix marks 'he' on this derived (causative/intensive) pattern. The suffix -hum is the object 'them.' Built on the root for 'momentous news,' it means to inform someone of significant tidings.

17.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
17.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

18.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
18.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
18.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

19.meaning: They do / they were doing — a verb of general doing or acting, performing a deed.
19.grammar: A present-tense verb in the basic Form I. The ya-…-ūna frame marks a 3rd-person masculine plural subject ('they'), and the -ūna ending is the indicative mood (a plain statement). The verb is the general one for doing, making, or carrying out an action.
19.root: ف-ع-ل (f-ʿ-l) — doing, making, performing an act

1.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
1.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

2.meaning: He/it came, arrived, or came about — the act of coming into presence or of something occurring.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb with no prefix and no personal suffix, naming a completed act by a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it came'). All three letters here are root letters: jā spells the first radical plus the lengthened weak middle radical, and the final hamza (ء) is the third root consonant — not an ending. The fatḥa (-a) on that hamza is simply the past-tense vocalization for a 'he' subject sitting on the last root letter; there is no separable suffix.

3.meaning: 'With / for the good deed' — the noun ḥasana (a good deed, a fine thing, a benefit) made definite ('the') and governed by the preposition bi- ('with/for/by'). It denotes a beautiful or beneficial act or reward.
3.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the prefixed preposition bi- ('with/for') and the article al- ('the'). The final -i marks the genitive case, which is required after a preposition. The feminine -a(t) ending is built into the word.

4.meaning: So for him / then his is; a linking word 'so/then' joined to 'for him,' expressing that something belongs or accrues to a single male — 'so to him belongs…'
4.grammar: A cluster of particles: the connector fa- ('so, then, and as a result') + the preposition la- ('for, belonging to') + the pronoun -hu ('him'). Together they assign possession or entitlement to a single male: 'so for him (is)…'

5.meaning: Ten / tenfold — the cardinal number ten. As a noun of number it can head a phrase meaning 'ten of …' or 'ten times the like.'
5.grammar: A number-noun ('ten'). The final -u marks the nominative case, used for the subject or predicate of a sentence; it is typically followed by the counted thing in the 'of' (genitive) form.

6.meaning: 'Its / their likes, the equivalents of it' — the plural of mithl ('a like, an equal, a similar one') with an attached possessive 'its/her.' It denotes things comparable or equal to something.
6.grammar: A 'broken' plural noun ('likes, equivalents') with the possessive suffix -hā ('its/her'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, the form taken after a preposition or when the noun is linked to another ('… of …') — here also because it follows a number. The suffix -hā refers to a feminine or non-human owner.

7.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
7.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

8.meaning: He/it came, arrived, or came about — the act of coming into presence or of something occurring.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb with no prefix and no personal suffix, naming a completed act by a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it came'). All three letters here are root letters: jā spells the first radical plus the lengthened weak middle radical, and the final hamza (ء) is the third root consonant — not an ending. The fatḥa (-a) on that hamza is simply the past-tense vocalization for a 'he' subject sitting on the last root letter; there is no separable suffix.

9.meaning: 'With / for the evil deed' — the noun sayyi'a (a bad deed, an evil or harmful thing) made definite ('the') and governed by the preposition bi- ('with/for/by'). It is the counterpart of the 'good deed.'
9.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the prefixed preposition bi- ('with/for') and the article (written al- but pronounced as-sayyi'a because the s is a 'sun letter' that absorbs the l). The final -i marks the genitive case, required after a preposition. The feminine -a(t) ending is built in.

10.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
10.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

11.meaning: 'He / it will be recompensed, repaid, requited' — the passive of the verb meaning to be given a fitting return for one's deeds. The subject is the one receiving the recompense, not the one giving it.
11.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in the passive voice, third-person masculine singular ('he/it is/will be …'). The yu- prefix with the internal vowel pattern marks the passive, so the subject is the receiver of the action ('is repaid') rather than the doer. Built on the root for repaying in kind.
11.root: ج-ز-ي (j-z-y) — recompense, requital, repaying in kind

12.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
12.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.
12.root: — (particle)

13.meaning: 'Its / her like, the equal of it' — the singular noun mithl ('a like, a counterpart, an equivalent') with an attached possessive 'its/her,' denoting something matching or comparable to a thing.
13.grammar: A singular noun ('a like/equal') with the possessive suffix -hā ('its/her'). The -a ending marks the accusative case — the form used for the object of a verb or in an adverb-like sense ('to the like of it'). The suffix -hā refers to a feminine or non-human owner.

14.meaning: 'While they / and they' — the word 'wa' (here 'while' or 'and') joined to the standalone pronoun 'hum' ('they'), referring to a masculine plural group.
14.grammar: A connective 'wa' — often circumstantial 'while' — plus the independent subject pronoun 'hum' ('they'), used for a masculine plural group. As an independent pronoun it usually stands as the subject of a following statement.

15.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
15.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

16.meaning: They are wronged / treated unjustly — to suffer ẓulm, the placing of something out of its right place: injustice, oppression, being deprived of one's due. The passive form names being on the receiving end of wrongdoing.
16.grammar: Present-tense passive verb, third-person masculine plural. The yu- prefix (with the internal vowelling) marks the third person and the passive 'are being …', and the -ūna ending makes it 'they' (masculine plural) as the ones undergoing the action: 'they are wronged'. The -na is the indicative marker.

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: 'Indeed I / truly, as for me' — an emphatic opening particle (inna, 'indeed/truly') fused with an attached 'I.' It introduces a statement about oneself with stress and certainty.
2.grammar: The emphatic particle inna ('indeed, truly') with the attached pronoun -ī ('I/me'), joined by a buffer -n- (giving -nanī). Inna stresses and affirms the sentence it opens. The final -ī suffix is the first-person singular ('I'), the thing inna is making a statement about.
2.root: — (particle with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

3.meaning: He has guided me — He showed the speaker the right way and led to it, with the attached object meaning 'me'. The verb conveys both pointing out the correct path and bringing someone onto it.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he …'); the bare stem ending in the long ā marks completed action. The attached -nī is the object pronoun 'me' (nūn + yāʾ, the -n- being the connecting consonant before the object pronoun). So the form states that a single masculine subject performed the act of guiding upon the speaker.

4.meaning: 'My Lord' — the Master, Sustainer and Nurturer, claimed in close personal relation by the speaker.
4.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord') with the attached pronoun -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' ending merges with the case-vowel of the noun, so a single long -ī is heard. The sense is 'the Lord who is mine'.
4.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord/master, to nurture and sustain

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
5.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

6.meaning: 'A path / road / way'. It denotes a clear, open road that one travels — often used figuratively for a course of life or conduct.
6.grammar: The '-in' ending (tanwīn) marks the word as indefinite ('a path / some way') and in the genitive case. The genitive typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').

7.meaning: Straight, upright, level — describing a path or course that runs directly to its goal without deviation or crookedness. As an active participle it names the thing that 'stands straight' of itself.
7.grammar: An active participle of the form 'mustafʿil' (Form X), meaning 'one that is/keeps straight'. The final -in is the genitive case with nunation (the -n marking it as indefinite, 'a …'); the genitive typically appears after a preposition or links to a preceding noun as a description 'of a straight …'.

8.meaning: 'A religion / a way of life' — a binding system of devotion, obedience, and accountability that one lives by (see the fuller sense of 'dīn').
8.grammar: An indefinite noun. The -an ending (accusative with tanwīn, the 'n' sound) marks it as the object of an action or as a specifying complement — often translatable as 'as a religion.'

9.meaning: Upright, well-established, correct and self-sustaining — a quality of being firmly set right and enduring, often describing a religion or order that is sound and steadfast.
9.grammar: A noun/adjective on the pattern 'fiʿal'. The final -an is the accusative case with nunation ('a …', indefinite); the accusative commonly marks a description or state attached to something, or a direct object. Its sense is that of something firmly straight and self-maintaining.

10.meaning: A religious way or creed — the distinct path of belief and practice followed by a community or tradition. It denotes the whole 'fold' or confession one belongs to, more than a single doctrine.
10.grammar: A feminine noun (the tā' here pronounced 'milla(t)'). The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the direct object of a verb or a noun set in apposition ('namely, the creed of …'). It refers to a body of religion as a defined way of life.
10.root: م-ل-ل (m-l-l) — to dictate, lay down (a way/creed)

11.meaning: The proper name Ibrāhīm (the Prophet Abraham).
11.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin. The -a ending here serves for both accusative and genitive because the name is a diptote — a class of nouns that refuses tanwīn (no -an/-in) and uses a single -a for these two cases. So this one -a covers 'Ibrāhīm' whether as an object or as 'of Ibrāhīm'.
11.root: — (proper name)

12.meaning: 'Upright in faith, naturally inclined to pure monotheism' — one who turns away from all false worship toward sincere devotion to the one Allah; a term for steadfast, primordial monotheistic faith.
12.grammar: A singular indefinite noun/adjective (an intensive 'faʿīl' pattern). The -an ending is accusative plus nunation: it marks indefiniteness ('a/an') and the accusative case, the form used for an object, a descriptive term, or a circumstantial state ('… as one upright in faith').
12.root: ح-ن-ف (ḥ-n-f) — to incline away (from error) toward pure monotheism

13.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
13.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

14.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

14.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

15.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
15.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

16.meaning: Those who associate partners with Allah — idolaters / polytheists who set up others alongside the one God in worship or devotion.
16.grammar: An active participle used as a noun, with 'the', in the masculine sound plural. The -īna ending marks the plural in the genitive/accusative case — the form used after a preposition or as the object of a verb.

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
2.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

3.meaning: My prayer — the ritual worship of standing, bowing and prostrating before Allah, here possessed by the speaker ('my'). It names the formal act of devotion (ṣalāh).
3.grammar: A feminine noun ('ṣalāh', here in its connected form 'ṣalāt-') with the attached possessive -ī meaning 'my'. Before a possessive the noun loses its own case-tip, and -ī marks first-person singular ownership ('my prayer').

4.meaning: And my acts of worship/devotion — particularly rites of sacrifice and ritual offering. The word covers the prescribed observances by which one draws near to Allah, here belonging to the speaker.
4.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and'. The noun 'nusuk' denotes acts of worship and ritual sacrifice; the attached -ī is the first-person possessive 'my'. Before the possessive the noun shows no separate case-ending.

5.meaning: And my living — my life, the state and span of being alive. Built as a 'place/time/source of life' noun, it points to one's life as a whole, here ascribed to the speaker.
5.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and'. 'maḥyā' is a noun of place/state from the verb 'to live' ('a living, a life'). The attached -ya is the possessive 'my' (it takes the form -ya after the long final ā). So the whole means 'and my living/life'.

6.meaning: And my dying — my death, the event and fact of ceasing to live. Formed as a 'place/time of death' noun, it denotes one's death generally, here belonging to the speaker.
6.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and'. 'mamāt' is a noun of place/time from the verb 'to die' ('a dying, death'). The attached -ī is the first-person possessive 'my'; before it the noun shows no separate case-ending.

7.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to', 'for', or 'belonging to', attached to the name 'Allah'. It conveys 'to Allah' or 'for Allah'.
7.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to/for') pulls the following noun into the genitive case, which is why 'Allah' ends in '-i' (llāhi). The '-i' ending is the regular result of a noun governed by a preposition.

8.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'my': the One who owns, sustains, nurtures, and governs — combining mastery, ownership, and loving cultivation. With the attached 'my' it is an intimate address, 'my Lord.'
8.grammar: A noun, rabb, with the first-person possessive (the original 'my' yāʾ being reduced to a final -i, so 'my Lord'). The word denotes the Master who creates, owns, and lovingly sustains. Used as a heartfelt vocative, calling upon one's Lord.
8.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

9.meaning: The worlds, all created realms — the totality of beings and peoples; in 'Lord of the worlds,' the whole of creation across all its kinds.
9.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the worlds') with 'al-' ('the'). The '-īna' ending marks a masculine sound plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) form — the form used after a preposition, in an 'of' linkage, or as a direct object.
9.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; a 'world' as a sign by which the Creator is known

1.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
1.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

2.meaning: A partner, associate, or sharer — one who shares in something (ownership, authority, or worship) alongside another. In matters of the divine it denotes any being set up as a co-deity beside Allah.
2.grammar: A noun on the pattern 'faʿīl' meaning 'a sharer/partner'. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the direct object of a verb (e.g., the thing denied or affirmed) or the noun governed by a negating particle. The sense is one who partakes or shares with another.
2.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, associate as partner

3.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
3.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

4.meaning: And with that / and by that — a linking phrase pointing back to a previously mentioned matter. It joins a new statement and indicates the means or reference: 'with/by this very thing'.
4.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and'; bi- means 'with/by/in'. 'dhālika' is the masculine singular demonstrative 'that' (pointing to something distant or just-mentioned). Demonstratives do not change for case here; the -a is part of the fixed word. Together: 'and with/by that'.

5.meaning: 'I was commanded', 'I have been ordered / instructed'. It expresses that the speaker is the recipient of a command — someone else has issued an order and the speaker is bound by it.

parts.en: passive vowel: the action was done to the subject

5.grammar: Past-tense passive verb. The -tu ending means the subject is 'I', and the opening u-vowel makes it passive ('I was commanded' rather than 'I commanded'). The action is presented as completed.

6.meaning: And I — the standalone first-person singular pronoun 'I,' here joined by 'and.' As a detached pronoun it stands on its own (typically as subject), unlike the attached endings.
6.grammar: Prefix 'wa' = 'and.' 'anā' is the independent (detached) pronoun 'I,' used for emphasis or to begin/identify the subject; it does not take a case ending and is fixed in form.

7.meaning: First, foremost — the one that comes before all others in order, time, or rank. It marks the initial or leading member of a set.
7.grammar: A noun/adjective of the elative-type pattern 'afʿal' ('first'). The final -u is the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or a predicate ('… is the first'). It identifies the foremost in sequence or standing.
7.root: ء-و-ل (ʾ-w-l) — to be first, to precede

8.meaning: The ones who submit/surrender — those who give themselves wholly to Allah in willing obedience and peace (the Muslims). As an active participle it names people characterized by this submission.
8.grammar: The prefix al- is 'the'. The stem is the Form IV active participle 'one who submits/surrenders'. The ending -īna is the sound masculine plural in the genitive/accusative state (the form used after prepositions, as object, or when linked to a preceding noun); its nominative counterpart would be -ūna. So: 'the ones who submit'.

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: 'Is it other than…?', 'shall (it be) other than…?' — a questioning expression built from the question particle 'is/shall?' and the word for 'other than / besides'. It challenges whether anything besides the named thing could be intended.
2.grammar: A yes/no question particle attached to the noun 'other than'. The -a ending is accusative, the case that often marks a word as a direct object or otherwise governed into this case (here the questioned object). The opening 'a-' turns the phrase into a question.
2.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — otherness, difference, being other than

3.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
3.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

4.meaning: I seek, I desire, I pursue — to want and go after something earnestly. The verb conveys actively looking for or aspiring to a thing.
4.grammar: A present/imperfect verb in the first-person singular: the a- prefix means 'I'. It denotes ongoing or intended action ('I seek / I am seeking / should I seek'). The final weak-letter -ī belongs to the root and stays in this base (indicative) form.

5.meaning: A lord, master, owner — one who possesses, sustains, and has full authority over something or someone, caring for and bringing it to completion. Of Allah it conveys the Sustainer who creates, owns and governs all.
5.grammar: A noun 'rabb'. The final -an is the accusative case with nunation ('a lord', indefinite); the accusative typically marks a direct object or a noun specifying a state/role ('… as a lord'). The word fuses the ideas of ownership, lordship and nurturing care.

6.meaning: And it / and he — a connective joined to the standalone pronoun 'he/it', often introducing a circumstantial clause ('while it…').
6.grammar: The prefix wa- ('and', or 'while' when introducing an accompanying circumstance) joined to the detached subject pronoun huwa, 'he/it' (masculine singular). The shadda on the wa- reflects assimilation of a preceding consonant onto it in connected speech. The pronoun is fixed in form and serves as the subject of its clause.

7.meaning: The Lord of — owner, master and sustainer who creates, possesses and governs. Of Allah it names the One who brings up and maintains all that exists.
7.grammar: The noun 'rabb' with the final -u marking the nominative case (subject or predicate: '… is the Lord'). Standing before a following noun it carries the sense 'Lord of …'. It combines ownership, authority and nurturing care.

8.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
8.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

9.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
9.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
9.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

10.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
10.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

11.meaning: He/it earns, acquires, gains — to gather to oneself, especially the consequences of one's own deeds, whether good or bad. The verb stresses what a person brings upon themselves by their actions.
11.grammar: A present/imperfect verb. The ta- prefix marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('she/it …') or a second-person masculine singular ('you …'); context decides which. The final -u is the indicative ('plain present') ending, signalling ongoing or habitual action: 'earns / is earning'.
11.root: ك-س-ب (k-s-b) — to earn, acquire, gain

12.meaning: A noun meaning 'all, every, each, the whole of.' It expresses totality — when joined to a following noun it means 'every (one)' or 'the entirety of' that thing.
12.grammar: A noun of totality with the final -u ending (nominative). The -u typically marks it as the subject or the thing being spoken about. It normally attaches to a following noun to mean 'every / all of' it.
12.root: ك-ل-ل (k-l-l) — totality, wholeness, comprehensiveness

13.meaning: A noun meaning 'soul, self, person, living being.' It denotes the inner self or the whole individual — the seat of life and identity, and by extension a 'person' as a single unit.
13.grammar: A noun with the -in ending (with nunation): the genitive indefinite ('a soul'). This form appears after prepositions or in an 'of' linkage with a preceding noun (such as 'every soul').
13.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — soul, self, breath; the inner being

14.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
14.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

15.meaning: 'On it / upon it / over it' — the preposition 'alā ('on, upon, against') joined to the pronoun 'it/her', referring to a single feminine or grammatically feminine thing.
15.grammar: 'ʿalā' is a preposition meaning 'on/upon/over'; its ending shifts to -ay when a pronoun is attached. The suffix -hā is the object pronoun for a single feminine (or feminine-gender) thing. Together they mean 'on it'. Words after a preposition stand in the genitive, though attached pronouns like -hā do not visibly change form.

16.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
16.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

17.meaning: It bears, carries, or takes on (a burden) — especially to carry the weight of sin or responsibility. The verb conveys shouldering a load of guilt or accountability.
17.grammar: A present/imperfect verb. The ta- prefix marks a third-person feminine singular ('she/it …') or second-person masculine singular ('you …') subject. The final -u is the indicative ending, marking ongoing/general action: 'bears / carries'. The verb specifically evokes carrying a load of sin.

18.meaning: A bearer of burden, a burdened soul — one (especially a person) who carries a load, above all the weight of their own sins. As an active participle it names the one doing the bearing.
18.grammar: A Form I feminine active participle, 'a bearer of burden', a single word whose initial wāw is the first radical of the root (not a conjunction). It is feminine because the implied subject 'soul' (nafs) is grammatically feminine. The final -un is the nominative case with nunation ('a …', indefinite), typically marking the subject.

19.meaning: A burden, load, or weight of sin — the heavy charge of guilt and accountability that a person carries for their wrongdoing.
19.grammar: A noun 'wizr' on the pattern 'fiʿl'. The final -a is the accusative case, typically marking the direct object of a verb ('carries a burden') or the thing acted upon. The word denotes a load, especially the weight of sin.
19.root: و-ز-ر (w-z-r) — to bear a burden/sin

20.meaning: 'Another / other' — a feminine word for one that is different from, or additional to, one already mentioned; a second or further (feminine) one.
20.grammar: A feminine singular adjective/noun meaning 'other, another', the feminine counterpart of ākhar. It ends in a fixed long -ā (alif maqṣūra) and does not change its ending for case; it commonly describes or stands for a feminine noun such as 'a group/party'.
20.root: أ-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be later/other; that which comes after or differs

21.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
21.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

22.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
22.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

23.meaning: 'Your Lord' — Rabb denotes the Master, Owner, Sustainer, and Nurturer who creates, possesses, and brings each thing to its completion; joined to 'your' (plural).
23.grammar: A noun 'Lord' in the genitive case (the -i ending), which typically follows a preposition or links it to a preceding noun ('… of …'). The suffix -kum is the possessive 'your' addressed to a group.
23.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship: nurturing, mastering, owning, sustaining

24.meaning: Your return, your place or time of coming back — the point to which you ultimately go back. With the attached 'your (plural)', it names the destination of a group's return.
24.grammar: A noun of place/time ('mafʿil' pattern) meaning 'place or act of returning'. The -u is the nominative case (subject/predicate: '… is your return'). The attached -kum is the second-person masculine plural possessive 'your (all of you)'. Together: 'your return / your place of return'.
24.root: ر-ج-ع (r-j-ʿ) — to return, go back

25.meaning: 'Then He will inform / tell you' — a verb of announcing weighty news or disclosing what was unknown, with 'He' as the informer and 'you (plural)' as those informed; preceded by 'then/so', linking it to what comes before.
25.grammar: A present-tense verb in the intensive pattern (faʿʿala: 'to inform thoroughly'), prefixed with fa- ('then/so') which connects it to a preceding statement as a result. The yu- prefix marks 'he'; the -u ending is the indicative mood, marking a plain, ongoing or future fact. The attached -kum is the object 'you (a group)'.
25.root: ن-ب-أ (n-b-ʾ) — momentous news, to announce/inform

26.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
26.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.
26.root: — (particle + relative pronoun)

27.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
27.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
27.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

28.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
28.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

29.meaning: 'You (all) differ / disagree' — from a verb meaning to differ, dispute, or hold conflicting views. The form addresses a group: 'you all differ from one another.'
29.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in a pattern meaning 'to differ among one another.' The ta- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks the subject as 'you all' (a group). The -na at the end signals the ordinary (indicative) present form used for a plain statement.
29.root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — to come after, differ, be at variance

1.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
1.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

2.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

3.meaning: He made you, He appointed/rendered you (plural) — to bring into a state or set in a role. The verb can mean 'to make/create' or 'to designate as', with the attached object 'you (all)'.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he …'); the bare stem with the open ending marks completed action. The attached -kum is the second-person masculine plural object pronoun 'you all'. So: 'He made/appointed you (all)'.

4.meaning: Successors, deputies, inheritors — those who come after others and take their place, holding a position handed on to them (as stewards or vice-gerents on the earth). It is the plural of 'khalīfah'.
4.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural on the pattern 'khalāʾif', plural of 'khalīfah' ('successor, deputy'). The final -a is the accusative case, here typically the direct object or the role assigned ('made you successors'). Such 'diptote' plurals take -a rather than -an even when indefinite. It denotes those who succeed and take others' place.
4.root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — to come after, succeed, leave behind

5.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
5.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

6.meaning: "and he raised / he lifted up / he elevated" — built on the verb meaning to raise high, to lift, to elevate in rank or position.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb in the 'he' form (third-person masculine singular). The final -a is the normal past-tense vowel. The leading wa- is the connector 'and'.

7.meaning: Some of you, a portion of you — singling out one part of a group in relation to another.
7.grammar: A noun 'a part / some' with the attached plural pronoun -kum ('you all'), forming a possessive link ('some of you'). The -a ending on the noun marks the accusative case, which typically signals that the word is the object of a verb.

8.meaning: 'Above / over / on top of.' An adverb of place meaning the higher position relative to something else; it can also mean 'superior to' or 'beyond.'
8.grammar: An adverb of place that is normally attached to a following noun ('above …'). Its fixed -a ending is the form such place-words take when they govern the noun that follows them.
8.root: ف-و-ق (f-w-q) — to be above, surpass, exceed

9.meaning: 'Some (others)' / 'a part' — the same noun for 'a portion or some,' here left indefinite, often functioning as the counterpart in the 'one another' construction.
9.grammar: A noun 'part/some' in the genitive case with indefinite marking (the -in ending, called tanwīn). The genitive typically follows a preposition or links it to a preceding noun ('… of …'); the doubled -n sound marks it as indefinite ('a part / some').
9.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, portion, or some of a whole

10.meaning: "degrees / ranks / levels / steps" — the plural of daraja, a step or grade in an ascending scale; it denotes ranks, levels, or stages of elevation.
10.grammar: A feminine plural noun (the -āt ending marks sound feminine plural). The final -in (with nunation/tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('degrees, ranks') and in the accusative/genitive case — the form used as an object or after a preposition.
10.root: د-ر-ج (d-r-j) — step, grade, to ascend by degrees

11.meaning: 'So that He may test / try you' — a verb of testing and proving, here directed at the purpose of an action; 'to put you to trial' so as to bring out what you truly are.
11.grammar: A present-tense verb governed by the purpose particle li- ('so that / in order to'), which puts the verb into the subjunctive — shown by the final -a on the stem (yabluwa) expressing intended purpose. The y- prefix marks 'he'; the attached -kum is the object 'you (a group)'.
11.root: ب-ل-و (b-l-w) — to test, try, put to the proof

12.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
12.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
12.root: — (particle)

13.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
13.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

14.meaning: 'He has given / granted you' — a verb of bestowing, with 'He' as the giver and 'you (plural)' as the recipients; to hand over and grant something so that the receivers come to have it.
14.grammar: A past-tense verb in the causative pattern (afʿala: 'to give/bring to'). The third-person masculine singular subject 'he' is carried within the bare verb form (ending in the long -ā). The attached -kum is the object pronoun 'you (a group)' — the ones given to.
14.root: ء-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; in this causative form, to bring/give

15.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
15.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

16.meaning: 'Your Lord' — the noun 'Lord' (Master, Sustainer, Owner, the One who nurtures and brings to completion) combined with 'your'. 'Rabb' carries the linked senses of ownership, authority, and ongoing care that raises a thing to its perfection.
16.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive. The -a ending is accusative, which typically marks the word as a direct object or governed element. The attached -ka means 'your', addressed to a single male.
16.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, nurturing care, ownership and mastery

17.meaning: Swift, quick, fast — describing one who is rapid in carrying out something. Used of Allah, it conveys that an action (such as reckoning) is accomplished with utter speed.
17.grammar: An adjective in the intensive 'faʿīl' pattern (denoting a strong, inherent quality). The final -u (ḍamma) marks the nominative case; with no tanwīn here it is in a possessive construction, 'swift of …,' linking it to a following noun.

18.meaning: The punishment, penalty, requital — the consequence imposed for wrongdoing. The word stresses a recompense that comes at the 'heels' of, and in answer to, one's deeds.
18.grammar: The prefix al- is 'the'. The stem 'ʿiqāb' is a verbal noun meaning 'punishing, penalty'. The final -i is the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… of the punishment') or follows a preposition. It denotes penalty as the sequel to misdeeds.
18.root: ع-ق-ب (ʿ-q-b) — to follow at the heels; requite, punish

19.meaning: A linkage of 'and' with the emphatic particle inna ('truly, indeed') plus 'he' — meaning 'and truly he…', opening a clause with firm assurance about the person referred to.
19.grammar: 'wa' is the connector 'and'. 'inna' is an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the statement and grammatically governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative. The attached -hu ('he/him') is the subject of the inna-clause, expressed in object form as inna requires.

20.meaning: Surely most forgiving — abundantly and repeatedly forgiving, One who covers over and pardons sins again and again. The intensive form stresses the fullness and constancy of the forgiving.
20.grammar: The prefix la- is an emphatic 'surely/indeed' (often answering or stressing a statement). The stem is the intensive adjective 'faʿūl' ('much-forgiving'). The final -un is the nominative case with nunation, typically marking a predicate ('… is surely Most-Forgiving'). It conveys constant, abundant forgiveness.
20.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to forgive, cover over, pardon

21.meaning: Most Merciful / ever-compassionate — one whose mercy is deep, constant, and abundantly bestowed; an intensive form stressing enduring tenderness and care. The '-un' nunation marks it as indefinite nominative.
21.grammar: An intensive adjective (faʿīl pattern) conveying a lasting, abundant quality. The '-un' (nunation on the ḍamma) marks it as indefinite and in the nominative case, typically used for a subject or predicate ("is most merciful").
21.root: ر-ح-م (r-ḥ-m) — mercy, compassion
